SUV5PudsyI.text:
• Termination-based constrained RL is simple, scalable, and avoids online optimization, making it attractive for safety-critical robots.
• Problem: on terminal-navigation tasks, constraints tightening near the goal cause "feasibility collapse" in this method class.
• Survival-weighted objectives make dwelling outside the goal preferable, yielding high constraint compliance but low task completion.
• Authors formalize this pathology for goals located near regions where constraints become active.
• Key idea: add a dense per-step success signal via an auxiliary value critic to PPO.
• Improves task completion while keeping safety constraint compliance; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Validated on a 6U-CubeSat in simulation and a floating-platform testbed with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

Glj2RSQIS4.text:
• Problem: symmetry-based policy learning needs known group actions, often unavailable in pixel-based POMDPs.
• Prior methods rely on environment-specific preprocessing, limiting portability across tasks and observation modalities.
• Key idea: MIRROR learns symmetry group operations jointly on observations and actions from offline data.
• Method explicitly enforces group axioms while discovering nonlinear symmetry operations directly from interaction data.
• Setup: four Robosuite tabletop tasks, compared against GAN baselines including LaLiGAN.
• Results: best on 3/4 symmetry metrics, 61% lower compatibility error than LaLiGAN.
• Equivariant BC beats vanilla BC on all tasks, gains up to 9.66%, zero-shot transfer to Kinova GEN3.

XY8QpMSxvq.text:
• Problem: reward-centric RL needs hand-crafted scalar rewards; can embodied behavior emerge without explicit environment rewards?
• Key idea: generate actions by minimizing free energy, i.e., deviations from priors over preferred states.
• Method 1: model-based free-energy planner using learned world models and trajectory optimization for predictive control.
• Method 2: model-free free-energy controller trained with deep policy optimization instead of reward maximization.
• Setup: continuous locomotion, autonomous driving, and underactuated control environments, all without environment-defined rewards.
• Results: goal-directed sparse-reward control, stable locomotion from homeostatic priors, collision-averse driving; abstract reports no numbers.
• Novelty: minimal self-supervised free-energy objectives as an alternative paradigm to reward-centric reinforcement learning.

9SnXCYklB0.text:
• Problem: existing VLAs output purely kinematic commands, degrading performance on real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks.
• Contact-rich tasks require regulating both motion and how the robot yields to external forces.
• Key idea: CompVLA jointly predicts motion and stiffness matrices from RGB images and language instructions.
• Method: a dedicated Compliance Expert augments the conventional VLA architecture.
• The Compliance Expert outputs time-varying stiffness and virtual displacement profiles, executed via geometric impedance control.
• Results: highest average success across diverse contact-rich tasks; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• CompVLA outperforms vanilla and compliance-aware VLA baselines; ablations confirm each component is essential.

USCrYWxsUc.text:
• Problem: text-to-motion generators trained on retargeted human data produce motions humanoid controllers cannot execute.
• Retargeted data ignores tracking controller nuances: balance, contact, actuation limits, and controller-specific failure modes.
• Key idea: TEXEDO applies test-time scaling, sampling many motions from a frozen pre-trained text-conditioned generator.
• Dynamic feasibility verifier, distilled from whole-body tracking rollouts, predicts whether each motion is physically executable.
• Semantic verifier scores text-motion alignment in a learned co-embedding space, selecting the best motion among feasible candidates.
• Evaluated in large-scale simulation and real-world deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid.
• Consistently improves tracking fidelity and text alignment without retraining or needing a stronger generator.

DyO8vc0zYK.text:
• Problem: robot formations must reach goals, avoid collisions, and keep shape, but these requirements often conflict.
• Key idea: treat them as prioritized constraints, where safety outranks recoverable errors like temporary formation deformation.
• Method: CTDE priority-conditioned actor-critic; decentralized actors use local observations plus online safety and formation budgets.
• Training: a multi-head centralized critic predicts navigation return, safety violation, and formation degradation from a shared representation.
• Critic estimates update the online budgets and drive a hierarchical advantage for policy optimization.
• Setup: VMAS formation-navigation scenarios with static and dynamic obstacles, plus deployment on a fleet of omnidirectional AGVs.
• Result: teams avoid collisions, deform when needed, recover formation, and keep navigating; the abstract reports no numbers.

xL2eR7x00h.text:
• Equivariant robot learning needs symmetry groups specified in advance; discovering them from controlled transition data remains unaddressed.
• Challenge: actions transform under their own representation, and behaviour-policy data distributions need not be symmetric.
• Key idea: valid transitions form a submanifold; every symmetry generator must be tangent to it.
• Estimating local normal frames depends on geometry, not density, giving robustness to nonlinear dynamics and biased policies.
• Two estimators: model-free local-PCA (TMT-KNN) and denoiser-based (TMT-NN), plus a discrete manifold-consistency test.
• Continuous benchmarks: TMT-NN recovers ground-truth generators where Jacobian and distribution-matching baselines fail.
• Discrete benchmarks: TMT-NN candidates approach the denoiser noise floor; ratio metrics misleadingly favour near-identity baselines.

mday00WZFr.text:
• Problem: divergent components of motion (DCMs) aid legged balance but only exist for reduced models like inverted pendulums.
• Key idea: recast DCMs as Koopman eigenfunctions learned from closed-loop data, without committing to a kinematic model.
• Novelty: unlike typical Koopman analysis of conserved, persistent dynamics, the method deliberately searches for unstable eigenpairs.
• Method: encode DCM observables from real-robot measurement histories, needing neither simulation ground truth nor full-state estimation.
• Regularization: learned eigenfunctions are coupled to control inputs through the DCM recursion, keeping them control-relevant.
• Result: Koopman DCMs learned from one hour of robot data improve tracking of reference walking patterns.
• Outlook: Koopman DCMs combined with MPC could enable learning state-based viability constraints for legged balancing.

33H7BChFgI.text:
• Problem: estimating relative 6-DoF pose between two image groups, for cross-sequence relocalization and multi-camera rig odometry.
• Each group has known intra-group geometry from visual odometry or rig calibration, already fused by pretrained multi-view backbones.
• Gap: current models treat all views as an unstructured set, missing explicit cross-group reasoning.
• Key idea: G2G keeps the foundation model frozen and adds lightweight modules bridging the two groups.
• Modules: perceiver resampler, cross-group bridge with merged self-attention, and multi-frame pose head, about 32M parameters.
• Trainable parameters are under 6% of the full model, supervised only by relative poses.
• State-of-the-art on four datasets, including cross-season real-world and zero-shot sim-to-real, versus fully retrained baselines.

317SZV2vuS.text:
• Problem: vision-based legged locomotion fails catastrophically under occlusion, reflections, and illumination changes.
• Key idea: explicitly model perception reliability and fall back to proprioception on out-of-distribution visual inputs.
• Method: two-stage teacher-student learning; teacher learns both perception-driven and proprioceptive fallback behaviors.
• Student predicts exteroceptive features with uncertainty, suppressing them when inputs appear out-of-distribution.
• Setup: real-world tests on Unitree Go2 quadruped with a RealSense D435 depth camera.
• Results: normal vision enables parkour over large gaps, elevated platforms, and narrow beams (abstract gives no numbers).
• Under heavy occlusion and strong illumination changes, the robot maintains stable, robust locomotion.

xaGVjPTxtr.text:
• Problem: UMI enables robot-free data collection, but its demonstrations are poorly suited to large-scale VLA training.
• Dual gap: fisheye wrist views mismatch pretrained VLMs, and human trajectories may violate robot embodiment limits.
• Key idea: VISTA adapts UMI data via fisheye-aligned visual grounding plus embodiment-conditioned trajectory validation.
• UMI-VQA provides vision-language supervision directly on wrist-mounted fisheye observations, beyond standard-view VQA.
• Validation scores demos by continuity, self-collision risk, and execution fidelity, keeping physically plausible trajectories.
• Two-stage VLA training uses adapted VQA data and validated trajectories; scores predict real-robot deployment success.
• Beats π0.5, LingBot-VLA, and Wall-X in simulation and real tasks; pipeline, datasets, and model to be released.

1JcOSLXzHB.text:
• Problem: social navigation metrics treat pedestrians as independent obstacles, ignoring group formations like queues and gatherings.
• Gap: trajectories keeping safe individual distance can still bisect queues or cut through a gathering's core.
• Key idea: model social structure as an intention-driven graph and measure trajectory intersections with it.
• Method: three group-structural compliance metrics, one each for gatherings, queues, and walking groups.
• Setup: CARLA-based procedural generation of pedestrian formations anchored to urban semantic features.
• Results: evaluated vision foundation models and online RL agents, showing geometric skill and structural compliance diverge.
• New: real-world dataset tests confirm persistent compliance gaps; full generation pipeline released for extension.

J8pJIDI6rM.text:
• Problem: generative imitation policies are limited by scarce expert demonstrations.
• Preference fine-tuning can use suboptimal rollouts but usually needs expensive human annotations.
• Key idea: PGPG generates preference labels automatically, with no human-in-the-loop supervision.
• Method: ordered coverage alignment measures rollout progress against a few expert demonstrations to derive pseudo-preferences.
• Added enhancements make progress-guided preferences more reliable, removing the need for hand-designed reward functions.
• Results: outperforms supervised fine-tuning baselines on challenging long-horizon manipulation tasks; the abstract reports no numbers.
• New: unsupervised alignment framework that works with both diffusion and flow-matching policies.

sS9FjkKKsm.text:
• Problem: legged RL rewards entangle task, operational limits, gait preference, and terrain adaptation in one objective.
• Key idea: assign each function its own mechanism instead of one complex, hand-tuned reward.
• Method: rewards for task, constraints for limits, energy minimization for gait, perception for terrain adaptation.
• No gait priors: air-time, contact-count, and foot-clearance targets removed; gaits emerge naturally.
• Ablations: removing any single component exposes a distinct failure mode, so all four are needed.
• Results: comparable terrain traversal, 56% lower cost of transport, 96% fewer limit violations versus complex-reward baseline.
• Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer to Unitree Go2 using LiDAR-based elevation mapping; videos at tinyurl.com/locomposition.

PjzSYChBzg.text:
• Problem: reactive navigation policies lack foresight; modular imagination pipelines accumulate errors and slow inference.
• Key idea: a latent world-action model that jointly learns action generation and short-horizon visual foresight.
• Method: shared Diffusion Transformer with asymmetric joint diffusion, producing long-horizon actions plus short-horizon latent foresight.
• Dual-stream conditioning fuses episode-level ego-motion history with sequential visual observations for smooth trajectories.
• Unified goal alignment lets one policy handle Image-Goal, Point-Goal, and No-Goal exploration.
• Results on ClutterScenes and InternScenes: success rates improve 15.7% on Image-Goal and 3.3% on Point-Goal.
• Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer reaches 85% average success across diverse indoor and outdoor environments.

wLgEYxjqid.text:
• Problem: dexterous grasps must serve free-form task instructions, contact functional regions, and stay executable on high-DoF hands.
• Task: generate grasps from multi-view images, 3D object geometry, and open-vocabulary language instructions.
• Data: OpenDexVerse, built with a Coverage-to-Alignment recipe combining large-scale breadth with high-quality functional alignment.
• OpenDex-Scale: optimization-generated grasps with vision-language annotations; OpenDex-Align: teleoperation plus category-level transfer.
• Model: shared semantic-geometric latent space fusing language-conditioned multi-view perception with 3D geometric structure.
• Affordance prediction and grasp generation act as complementary supervision, grounding functional regions while producing task-consistent grasps.
• Results: gains in task generalization, functional alignment, feasibility, inference speed, and real-robot success (abstract gives no numbers).

JhdmNwpT4o.text:
• Problem: humanoid teleoperation is mostly validated on compact robots, rarely with real payloads.
• Full-size humanoids have larger inertia and tighter balance, making tracking sensitive to VR noise and drift.
• HEFT: a teleoperation framework for full-size humanoids tracking motions while carrying heavy real payloads.
• Privileged Motion Guidance learns from noisy VR references, guided by physically plausible reconstructed references.
• Windowed Payload Curriculum with expert-guided payload caps builds robust heavy-payload tracking during training.
• Deployed on L7, a 175cm, 65kg humanoid, teleoperated with commodity VR trackers.
• Tracks turns, forward/backward walking and squats while carrying payloads up to 24kg.

lsfM8TzuH2.text:
• Problem: unclear which pretraining signals make video world model latents useful for predicting robot actions.
• Method: unified inverse-dynamics probing across image SSL, video SSL, autoencoders, diffusion, and shortcut-forcing dynamics models.
• Key finding: temporal video pretraining, not pixel reconstruction fidelity, drives action-relevant latent structure.
• Models with strong pixel decoding can show near-zero action recoverability from their latents.
• Video-pretrained self-supervised encoders achieve the best Pareto trade-off between visual fidelity and action prediction.
• V-JEPA vs VideoMAE: natural-video temporal context drives most gains, latent prediction adds less; CALVIN masks this.
• Inverse-dynamics supervision substantially improves robustness to visual corruption, regularizing latent geometry beyond clean-setting performance.

fHzDEYENPF.text:
• Problem: motion prediction for pedestrians, bicycles, cars, and buses must be accurate and interpretable for safe navigation.
• Gap: state-of-the-art predictors are black-box, without explicit traffic regulations or behavioral constraints.
• Key idea: TraCS augments existing forecasting backbones with interpretable, probabilistic first-order logic compliance reasoning.
• Agentic code generation translates natural-language traffic regulations into probabilistic logic for motion prediction.
• A reactive data-streaming inference engine efficiently updates compliance landscapes as scenes evolve.
• A learned neural confidence rating attenuates the compliance signal to prevent overconfident misguidance.
• On Argoverse 2, TraCS consistently improves state-of-the-art backbones; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

Nxn1pyNZpE.text:
• Problem: existing benchmarks poorly evaluate VLMs' embodied abilities across diverse navigation and manipulation tasks.
• Current evaluation metrics are constrained, preventing thorough, fine-grained assessment of VLM-driven robot capabilities.
• Key idea: RMMBench, a unified benchmark combining high- and low-level embodied tasks in one framework.
• Robots must follow language instructions and execute long-horizon tasks in continuous spaces.
• Setup: 70 core navigation-manipulation use cases, from localized manipulation to long-horizon composite navigation.
• Main result: leading VLMs still struggle significantly with spatial localization accuracy in mobile manipulation.
• Takeaway: stronger spatial perception during long interactions is needed; benchmark enables fine-grained future research.

Wv9xF5Ii7L.text:
• Problem: policy gradients on flow matching policies require costly, fragile backpropagation through the multi-step noise-to-action ODE.
• Key idea: FlowDPG distills critic gradients directly into the velocity field during training, bypassing BPTT entirely.
• Update combines demonstration-driven velocity for action feasibility with critic-driven correction steering toward higher value.
• Method: DDPG-style actor-critic framework designed specifically for flow matching policies, enabling stable real-world policy improvement.
• Theory: FlowDPG update formally linked to vanilla Deterministic Policy Gradient via three explicit approximations.
• Setup: real-world long-horizon, multi-stage, dual-arm AirPods assembly task.
• Results: 92% end-to-end success, outperforming value-conditioning, auxiliary-module adaptation, and adjoint-based critic-gradient RL baselines.

4dqRAd2sNp.text:
• Problem: flow-matching VLA policies need iterative ODE solving at inference, limiting robot control frequency.
• Key idea: rectified flow training makes one-step and multi-step Euler integration equivalent at the global optimum.
• Method: empirical comparison of one-step versus multi-step sampling in existing flow-matching VLAs, without modification.
• Setup: six flow-matching VLA policies, evaluated with their standard multi-step refinement versus single-step generation.
• Result: one-step generation largely matches multi-step sampling; multi-step refinement gives no consistent advantage at scale.
• Condition: equivalence holds when models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity, as theory predicts.
• What's new: low-latency single-step policies come free, with no retraining, distillation, or auxiliary objectives.

Y55iJjxMsh.text:
• Problem: VLA agents must generalize to novel recombinations of semantic and physical task requirements.
• Existing holistic policies entangle semantics and physics in one latent, hurting generalization and physical feasibility.
• Key idea: energy-based compositional diffusion policy with separate semantic and physical energy terms.
• Multimodal inputs are factorized into grounded semantic factors, modeled as implicit semantic energies.
• Physical constraints like motion smoothness and kinematic manipulability are explicit differentiable energies.
• Energies are combined to guide trajectory generation toward task success and physical feasibility.
• Consistent gains in real-world and benchmark tests, plus ablations; abstract gives no numbers; code promised.

qHndjmxgs1.text:
• Problem: whole-body mobile manipulation needs coordinated base and arm control under constantly shifting camera viewpoints.
• Gap: existing policies use 2D or sparse 3D features and merge arm and base into one action vector.
• Key idea: inject geometry only where depth is reliable, and attend to it only where needed.
• Method: a lightweight Fourier encoder turns per-pixel 3D coordinates into geometric tokens, with no extra 3D backbone.
• Gated fusion conditioned on depth validity enriches foundation-model features while preserving their pretrained semantic priors.
• A hybrid diffusion decoder separates arm and base actions, using sparse cross-attention and causal temporal modeling.
• Results: 79.3% mean success on ManiSkill-HAB, 23.7% over the strongest baseline, with consistent real-world gains.

5fZzu1zWzG.text:
• Problem: human robot demonstrations contain mistakes, retries, and corrections, usually discarded as noisy or suboptimal data.
• Insight: these imperfect segments reveal when execution deviates and how task feasibility can be restored.
• Gap: existing reward and value models assume monotonic progress, missing local execution errors and corrective behaviors.
• Key idea: ReTVL learns mistake-sensitive value functions using sparsely annotated retry events as supervision.
• Method: combines global progress calibration with local pairwise preferences around retry keypoints to capture degradation-and-recovery.
• Use: the learned value reweights demonstration chunks for behavior cloning, suppressing harmful errors while keeping useful corrections.
• Results: on real-robot manipulation, finer-grained values and better imitation than progress-based baselines; abstract reports no numbers.

mg7X6SFE75.text:
• Problem: finetuned VLAs behave unpredictably out-of-distribution, so runtime failure detection is essential for safe deployment.
• Existing detectors need costly action sampling, restrictive architectural assumptions, or access to failure rollouts.
• VLA-FAIL: lightweight, broadly applicable framework combining two novel detectors with minimal overhead and no failure data.
• LLMD flags out-of-distribution states via token-wise Mahalanobis distance of last-layer features to training data.
• ACC exploits receding-horizon overlap, detecting failures when consecutive action chunks become inconsistent.
• New metric AUCPDT jointly scores precision, recall, and detection time, independent of threshold choice.
• Real-world and simulation results: combined detectors catch complementary failures early, often beating far costlier baselines.

19iADsbO9A.text:
• Problem: pretrained VLAs are vision-driven and fail in contact states with occlusion, depth ambiguity, or force errors.
• Key idea: LIFT adds contact reactivity to a pretrained VLA via late force injection, preserving general manipulation knowledge.
• Method: grafts a reactive action expert, initialized from pretrained action weights, beside the original action expert.
• Recent 6D end-effector force enters via causal force memory and zero-initialized cross attention, refreshing actions mid-execution.
• Online DAgger mixes offline task-alignment data with human-corrected rollouts to handle policy-dependent contact distribution shift.
• Evaluated on towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement; learns faster and outperforms vision-only post-training.
• Ablations: reactive force memory and online corrective data are both important; abstract reports no numbers; code public.

EWEKI0rF6v.text:
• Problem: driving planners from vision/video-action models ignore explicit scene geometry like drivable space and obstacles
• Key idea: give planning explicit geometric priors over both present observations and future scene evolution
• Built on a streaming video geometry foundation model extracting ego-aligned, multi-scale geometry tokens from current frames
• Q-Former-style geometry world model predicts latent future tokens, supervised by future depth and conditioned on ego state
• Geometry-oriented action model iteratively aggregates present and future geometry tokens to refine trajectory proposals
• Evaluated on NavSim v1 and v2, reporting state-of-the-art closed-loop performance and improved safety
• New: future geometry prediction replaces pixel-level forecasting as a compact, planning-aligned world model abstraction

w1x9MHo93E.text:
• Problem: open-world mobile manipulation needs vast data; teleoperation and UMI collection are too costly at scale.
• Key idea: WANDA synthesizes large, diverse training data for mobile manipulation from a single real demonstration.
• Reconstructs background Gaussian splats and robot-object interaction trajectories from source RGBD observations as a world substrate.
• Rearranges contact-rich interaction segments into new spatial layouts, chained via whole-body motion planning.
• Corrective State Expansion diversifies robot and object states across trajectory stages for long-horizon robustness.
• Scene generalization: trajectories synthesized in 3D worlds generated from everyday photos, rendered with splats plus Isaac Sim.
• Policies trained on synthetic data show strong spatial and scene generalization in simulation and real-world tasks.

aKjXDWnmzc.text:
• Problem: GPU simulators handle kinematic trees, but robots with kinematic loops need workarounds like mimic joints.
• Key idea: Kamino natively supports closed kinematic loops and strongly coupled constraints in massively parallel GPU simulation.
• Method: constrained forward dynamics solved as a nonlinear complementarity problem with a state-of-the-art optimization algorithm.
• Contacts resolved with high fidelity, without simplified or convexified approximate contact models.
• Setup: implemented in Python with NVIDIA Warp, integrated into the Newton physics framework.
• Result: trained a feasible walking RL policy for DR Legs, a biped with six nested loops.
• Scale: 4096 parallel environments simulated on a single GPU, enabling large-scale RL for loop-heavy robots.

loMfT7cfYl.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation needs adaptive compliance, but real data is costly and simulation struggles with contact dynamics.
• Prior sim-to-real methods need real-world adaptation or fall back on isotropic, non-adaptive compliant controllers.
• Key idea: split force regulation into a sim-transferable directional part and a manually tunable magnitude part.
• Policy predicts a task frame and per-axis control gains, adapted from a pre-trained VLA model.
• Trained by imitation learning purely on automatically generated simulation demonstrations, with no real-world data.
• Admittance controller combines predictions with human-set stiffness and target wrench at deployment.
• Real-world tests on microwave, peg-in-hole, whiteboard wiping, door opening show strong success and disturbance robustness.

VxUazHdUwe.text:
• Problem: efficient-inference studies for robot models measure per-step cost, ignoring closed-loop effects of embodied execution.
• Techniques studied include quantization, pruning, and asynchronous inference for reducing per-step cost and inter-action latency.
• Key idea: TISED, an analytical framework decomposing task-level effects of inference speedups.
• TISED unifies diverse optimization techniques and analyzes their effects on both static and dynamic embodied tasks.
• Paradox 1: on static tasks, optimization can lengthen end-to-end completion time despite lower per-step latency.
• Paradox 2: on dynamic tasks, moderate lightweighting can raise success rate above the unoptimized baseline.
• Paradox 3: monotonicity and sweet-spot location of both effects shift with hardware configuration.

JV472m0zgq.text:
• Problem: robot manipulation policies need massive, diverse demonstrations; collecting real robot data is costly and limited.
• Key idea: convert egocentric human manipulation videos into robot-format data to pretrain vision-language-action models at scale.
• Method: action retargeting, robot-arm visual synthesis, and multi-level quality curation over curated and in-the-wild videos.
• Scale: 18,561 hours of synthesized robot data across 15 robot morphologies, the largest ego-to-robot dataset to date.
• Setup: RoboTwin2.0 extended with disentangled perturbations in visual appearance, scene layout, embodiment, and task semantics.
• Results: joint pretraining on Ego2Robot plus robot data consistently improves out-of-distribution generalization, confirmed on real robots.
• What's new: first evidence that ego-to-robot synthesis provides pretraining benefits at scale, beyond small per-task policies.

98pbD92mEI.text:
• Problem: imitation-learning driving planners suffer distribution shift between expert logs and self-induced deployment states.
• In Transformer planners, shift causes ego-attention concentration, incomplete scene understanding, and unsafe mode selection.
• Key idea: TRIAD, a three-level robustness formulation covering channel, scene, and decision levels.
• Channel-level: constrained ego-state attention prevents over-reliance on a few state channels.
• Scene-level: offline VLM guidance keeps interaction-critical agent and route-relevant map evidence in the ego query.
• Decision-level: multimodal supervision reshaped by a CVaR-style tail-risk score; VLM and risk terms are training-only, adding no inference overhead.
• nuPlan test14-hard: NR-CLS 73.39 and R-CLS 67.12, beating CAR Planner's 72.94 and 64.90.

vA3t8YK04w.text:
• Diffusion policies with linearly composed scores promise modular, compositional, interpretable multi-task robot learning.
• Problem: standard training does not encourage specialization, so components learn redundant, uninterpretable copies.
• Composed predictions then average over duplicate factors, undermining the architecture's core premise.
• Key idea: a drop-in score-decorrelation auxiliary loss grounded in projective composition theory.
• Method encourages orthogonal component noise predictions with minimal architectural change and little compute overhead.
• Across multiple benchmarks, it reduces double counting and improves held-out compositional generalization (abstract reports no numbers).
• New: behaviorally meaningful component specialization without sacrificing multitask performance.

A9AQjk3dAt.text:
• Problem: embodied agents' high success rates overstate their real instruction-following ability.
• Cause: low scene entropy; one valid task per scene makes language redundant for policies.
• RoboFollow benchmark: each training scene supports up to 16 kinematically distinct task branches.
• Four-level protocol (L0–L3) perturbs layout and semantics: spatial relations, attributes, trajectories, logic.
• Confound control: simple objects, trained actions only, separate Intent and Execution scores.
• Results: SOTA VLA/VA models score high at L0 but fail under minimal L1–L3 perturbations.
• Stronger VLMs, QA co-training, LangForce, CFG fail to close the gap; real-robot tests confirm.

AIInkHZlvB.text:
• Problem: contact-rich insertion needs visual alignment plus tactile adjustment, but chunk policies fuse touch through one pathway.
• Existing visuotactile fusion implicitly mixes persistent contact states, abrupt contact events, and future contact consequences.
• Key idea: PACE splits one shared tactile stream into three distinct temporal roles with separate pathways.
• Persistent contact states condition chunk generation; abrupt events correct generated chunks; consequence prediction shapes training representations.
• Real robot: 90.7% average success across five insertion tasks, beating vision-only and fusion baselines by 44+ points.
• ManipulationNet: 88.7% success over six geometry-clearance configurations, including industrial-grade 0.1-mm clearance.
• Ablations confirm complementary roles; principle generalizes across feedback signals and policy backbones.

VTSUekrCnH.text:
• Problem: carry multiple free-rolling spheres on a wheel-legged quadruped's back, with no fences, grippers, or stops.
• Identical spheres lack persistent identity; their ordering can change independently at every history frame.
• History-concatenation encoders enforce only shared permutation symmetry across history, mismatching this per-frame symmetry.
• Under equal PPO budgets, MLPs, branch-wise encoders, and HCDS plateau at or below two spheres.
• HCDS progresses only with randomised ball-slot assignment, suggesting it exploits slot indices as a shortcut.
• Per-Frame Deep Sets pools within each frame before temporal readout; proven invariant and universally approximating.
• PFDS reaches five spheres with 100% no-drop transport in simulation across all five random seeds; distilled to 16x16 tactile map.

x05Rf7L7H4.text:
• Problem: behavior cloning weights all demonstration states equally, though few states make small errors catastrophic.
• Key idea: define state criticality as worst-case value loss from bounded perturbations of the expert action.
• Method: SCRIM trains an adversarial disturbance policy and value critic around a fixed imitation policy.
• Output: each demonstration state gets a score for how vulnerable task success is to small action errors.
• Uses: reweighting behavior-cloning losses toward critical states, and curating compact, high-value demonstration subsets.
• Setup and results: on simulated and real manipulation, SCRIM improves success and preserves performance with much less data.
• What's new: interpretable, policy-aware criticality scores revealing which demonstration moments matter most; abstract reports no specific numbers.

fuB1LcFk9g.text:
• Robotic disassembly for remanufacturing needs uncertain perception, prerequisite sequencing, contact-rich manipulation, and failure recovery.
• VLA models mostly target tabletop tasks; scarce disassembly data cannot cover environment and product distribution shifts.
• Key idea: human corrections expose the policy's own failure states, offering targeted improvement signals.
• PACER converts correction trajectories and in-process robot evidence into weights or advantages for training.
• It preserves the native VLA training objective rather than treating corrections as ordinary demonstrations or coarse outcomes.
• Setup: 70 human correction trajectories across seven positions, real UR5e motherboard disassembly, five component classes.
• Results: 33% success-rate improvement over direct SFT, extending VLA correction learning to industrial disassembly.

qF26obIUEX.text:
• Problem: humanoid loco-manipulation needs long-horizon locomotion-interaction coordination and generalization across diverse objects and noisy observations.
• Prior reference-motion or task-reward methods show promise but often fail to generalize across objects.
• Key idea: EVOLVE expands a single successful demonstration to diverse objects via simulation-based demonstration editing.
• Method: structured transformations edit robot keypoint trajectories, tracked by a task-agnostic whole-body controller using sparse keypoints.
• A high-level egocentric visuomotor policy is trained on successful edited rollouts for real-world deployment.
• Simulation: generalizes across object size, shape, pose and initialization, beating reference-based and reference-free baselines.
• Real world: zero-shot deployment succeeds; abstract reports no numeric results, so check the paper for exact figures.

4M7C3PsA78.text:
• Problem: open-world mobile manipulation VLM agents see targets but fail to reacquire, approach, and stop at graspable poses.
• Diagnosis: supervision-interface mismatch; teachers use privileged low-level traces, students act from egocentric images and skills.
• Key idea: AIDA-OWMM collects demonstrations directly in the deployed VLM agent's interface.
• Method: active target-acquisition demos annotated with object-centric spatial reasoning targets, using compact memory and high-level skill calls.
• Result: OWMM benchmark full-task success rises from 7.65% (exact legacy baseline) to 71.76%.
• Largest gains after object retrieval: pick readiness, object pickup, goal search, and final task completion.
• Supervision format transfers beyond OWMM, improving EmbodiedBench navigation results; code will be publicly released.

QsmD0Pq7uP.text:
• Problem: robot demos and structured human data are expensive to collect and tied to specific embodiments.
• Idea: learn task intent from unstructured internet human videos, and learn robot control in simulation.
• Intent model predicts short-horizon scene changes from the current observation, running in closed loop.
• Embodiment-specific tracking policy, trained in massively-parallel simulation, converts predicted intent into robot actions.
• Shared intent interface lets one intent model drive both a dexterous hand and a parallel-jaw gripper.
• Stirring, wiping, and binning use only internet video and transfer zero-shot to novel scenes and objects.
• Push-T and cable routing learned from just 1 hour each of self-collected smartphone video.

XQGBZwsuXt.text:
• Goal: full-scale humanoid sprinting above 7 m/s with aggressive high-speed cornering and up to 25° trunk lean.
• Problem: above ~4 m/s, foot impacts cause high-frequency yaw-rate oscillations that corrupt proprioceptive history.
• Yaw-rate tracking rewards fight natural gait oscillations, and one shared style prior degrades low-speed skills.
• Method: causal multi-head attention encodes high-frequency temporal feedback instead of flat-history MLP policies.
• Heading-direction reward supervises only low-frequency velocity direction, enabling agile turns without suppressing natural oscillations.
• Skill-conditioned multi-adversarial-motion-prior discriminators tie style rewards to the commanded skill, preserving gait fidelity.
• Ablations confirm each component is essential; validated in simulation and real-robot sprinting and cornering deployment.

rEmMzoUnpn.text:
• Problem: RL humanoid policies can still output unsafe actions, causing instability or falls.
• Challenge: high-dimensional dynamics, contact-rich interactions, and disturbance sensitivity make humanoid safety hard.
• Key idea: residual reinforcement learning acts as an implicit safety filter for humanoid control.
• Method: the nominal policy optimizes task performance; a residual policy learns safety corrections on top.
• Benefit: decoupling avoids tuning competing performance, safety, and robustness rewards within one policy.
• Setup: evaluated on challenging humanoid balance tasks against the nominal policy and a learned safety-filter baseline.
• Results: better performance-safety Pareto trade-off, improving safety while keeping competent performance; abstract reports no numbers.

XKZ7YJEfr4.text:
• Problem: learning from human demos often requires multiview cameras, depth sensors, or custom hardware.
• Existing methods also limit policy execution to third-person or egocentric camera viewpoints.
• Key idea: WARPED synthesizes realistic wrist-view observations and actions from monocular egocentric RGB human videos.
• Vision foundation models initialize the interactive scene from egocentric RGB recordings alone.
• A hand-object tracking pipeline retargets hand and object trajectories to a robot end-effector.
• Gaussian Splatting renders photorealistic wrist-view images that directly train visuomotor policies.
• Results: matches teleoperation-trained policies on five rigid and one articulated task, with 5-8x less collection time.

AilV1LyfXF.text:
• Problem: using video generation models for control needs costly test-time video generation or from-scratch action heads.
• Key idea: treat robot actions as single-patch tokens inside a pretrained video diffusion transformer's latent space.
• Method: linear projection maps each action timestep to VAE patch dimensions, sharing patchify layers and backbone.
• Training mixes three diffusion objectives: video-only, joint video+action with block-causal attention, and action-only.
• Video objective uses robot and human videos to build dynamics priors in the shared backbone.
• Inference: single DDIM step generates action chunks from noise at 84 ms, skipping full video generation.
• Results: strong simulation and real-robot performance at substantially lower inference cost than joint video-action policies.

mMRhLrwLFx.text:
• Problem: humanoid control degrades under target-domain dynamics shifts from terrain, payload, or actuator changes.
• Prior work: zero-shot domain randomization lacks specialization; calibration, residual learning, or retraining are heavy.
• Key idea: few-shot adaptation by aligning an inverse dynamics model with target-domain dynamics.
• Method: train privileged oracle policy, then distill into deployable Planner-IDM student via DAgger.
• Deployment: freeze planner, finetune only IDM on about 2 minutes of target-domain rollouts.
• What's new: supervised IDM finetuning on observed action-observation pairs, needing no rewards or optimal demonstrations.
• Results: outperforms in-context and end-to-end baselines; real humanoids execute diverse high-precision whole-body tasks.

mw8BgE8ADo.text:
• Problem: VLAs control robots semantically but lack explicit foresight of how actions change the scene.
• World-Action Models add foresight via predicted futures, but costly pixel-level video generation is highly redundant.
• Key idea: LaWAM conditions policies on compact latent visual subgoals instead of reconstructed future video.
• Method: train latent action model in pretrained vision foundation model feature space, yielding Latent World Model.
• Its forward decoder is repurposed to predict future observation features, guiding dynamics-aware action generation.
• Results: 98.6% success on LIBERO, 91.22% on RoboTwin, plus strong real-world manipulation performance.
• Efficiency: 187 ms per action chunk, up to 24× lower latency than pixel-space WAMs.

0w0ylGezd5.text:
• Problem: collecting diverse, contact-rich robot data across embodiments, viewpoints, and scenes is a major bottleneck for manipulation.
• Human egocentric videos offer abundant interactions, but each covers only one body, camera path, and scene.
• Key idea: AnyWorld expands one human interaction into many robot-native rollouts, without paired human-robot demonstrations.
• Method: a world model factorizes interactions into action, camera, and target-embodiment controls that can be recomposed independently.
• Training: large-scale human interaction pretraining, then mixed-embodiment fine-tuning, preserving dynamics and object interactions across recompositions.
• Results: controllable recomposition works; generated data improves manipulation on RoboCasa GR1 and a real IRON humanoid.
• What's new: one factorized model turns human videos into scalable cross-embodiment data; the abstract reports no numbers.

Sh0dG0HwVK.text:
• Problem: high-quality robot demos are costly, while abundant suboptimal or out-of-distribution data often hurts co-trained policies.
• Key idea: noise-dependent data usage, a new co-training axis that extracts only useful signal from suboptimal data.
• Method: suboptimal data contributes only at high and low diffusion times; clean data trains all noise levels.
• Theory: robot actions follow a spectral power law, yielding locality and global-to-local hierarchy in optimal diffusion policies.
• Setup: four suboptimal data types (noisy, sim-to-real, task mismatch, large mixtures) across six tasks.
• Results: outperforms co-training baselines by up to 33% when scaled to Open X-Embodiment heterogeneous data.
• What's new: a principled, simple way to make arbitrary suboptimal demonstrations usable for diffusion policy imitation learning.

r8MOxo93Mv.text:
• Problem: 3D manipulation policies rely on RGB-D geometry, but commodity sensors corrupt depth on transparent, reflective, or thin objects.
• Finding: modern 3D policies hit a sharp depth-noise cliff, even when trained on matched noisy depth.
• Insight: corrupted depth entangles with token coordinates and geometry features consumed by the action expert.
• Key idea: NISE, a 3D policy architecture that learns trustworthy geometry features despite imperfect depth.
• Method: Geometric Cross-View Self-Supervision shapes shared policy features using calibrated multi-view depth during training.
• Method: Gaussian Marginalized 3D Attention propagates position uncertainty into attention instead of treating lifted tokens as exact.
• Results: improves robustness in simulation with sensor-realistic corruption and on real transparent/reflective tasks while preserving clean-depth performance.

rwx9GCSVjH.text:
• Problem: generalist visual-navigation policies output direction as unitless trajectories, lacking the metric distance controllers need.
• Gap: scalar lifters scale uniformly; monocular-depth policies inherit depth errors near obstacles and at close range.
• Key idea: PathLift, a per-waypoint depth-conditioned adapter that lifts pre-trained navigation policies into metric paths.
• Method: uses sensor-grade depth to fit per-waypoint magnitude and lateral residuals to a canonicalized prior.
• Setup: diverse visual-navigation policies tested in simulation and on a real wheeled robot with stereo and LiDAR.
• Results: consistently improves closed-loop navigation and real-world success; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• What's new: one feed-forward pass yields depth-feasible metric paths without test-time optimization.

HT8whUVp22.text:
• Strongest robot foundation models are closed-weight, reachable only via managed fine-tuning APIs without weights or gradients.
• Such APIs allow only imitation, ruling out reinforcement learning and other closed-loop policy improvement methods.
• This hurts agile, contact-rich humanoid manipulation, where latency, tracking dynamics, and novel states cause failures.
• One of the first real-humanoid studies of managed-API adaptation, using Gemini Robotics On-Device (GROD).
• Direct API fine-tuning beats a leading open-weight VLA on identical demos but falls short of mastery.
• CLIFT converts deployment-time reward feedback into API-compatible supervised data, needing no weights, gradients, likelihoods, or losses.
• GROD reaches near-perfect success after two CLIFT flywheel cycles, never opening the model box.

aspenN9eir.text:
• Problem: pretrained flow/diffusion robot policies fail outside their training distribution during real-world deployment.
• Existing fixes need large data collection or on-robot RL, which is slow, costly, and unsafe.
• FlowDAgger adapts frozen generative policies from a handful of human interventions, entirely in latent space.
• Key idea: action inversion maps each expert action back to the noise producing it under the base policy.
• Inversion uses reverse-time integration plus local refinement; a lightweight latent policy then learns to steer the base model.
• Tested in simulation and real bimanual and single-arm tasks, adapting action-head VLAs and world-action models.
• Beats supervised fine-tuning and latent-space RL baselines while preserving pretrained skills on held-out tasks (abstract gives no numbers).

JQvRoFU5aS.text:
• Problem: VLA policies drift off nominal trajectories during manipulation, even when tasks remain physically feasible.
• Deviations push policies into unfamiliar states, where direct re-planning often destabilizes action sequences.
• Key idea: B2FF uses future visual conditioning in foresight-driven VLAs as a recovery interface.
• Before execution, the VLA imagines a milestone bank of familiar future states from the clean initial observation.
• At recovery, a recoverability-aware selector picks a milestone and enforces it as a fixed visual goal.
• On failure-injected LIBERO, B2FF raises baseline average success from 56.3% to 74.0% with aligned recovery timing.
• New: pre-imagined milestones guide recovery without fine-tuning the low-level action generator.

Gkka9VEhWb.text:
• Whole-body humanoid manipulation of bulky, deformable, shared-load objects needs distributed contact sensing and explicit force regulation.
• Most imitation policies treat contact force implicitly; human demos lack robot actions, teleoperation lacks natural force regulation.
• WT-UMI: wearable whole-body tactile interface, worn by humans or mounted on humanoids, capturing tactile images, forces, and poses.
• Force-conditioned pose correction converts human poses into contact-aware robot targets, learned from limited teleoperation data.
• Force-supervised planner predicts end-effector pose chunks and contact-force trajectories, feeding a tactile-based admittance controller.
• Evaluated on five contact-rich tasks: deformable objects, bulky rigid objects, and human-humanoid collaboration.
• Outperforms four policy baselines in success rate and contact-position tracking error; abstract reports no specific figures.

4ar3F6Obiq.text:
• Problem: generative planners are mostly single-robot or produce multi-robot trajectories sequentially with iterative conflict post-processing.
• Key question: can coordinated multi-robot trajectories be generated feed-forward by one generative model?
• Roken: a unified diffusion transformer jointly generating trajectories satisfying individual safety and global connectivity constraints.
• Each robot is a token: self-attention models inter-robot interaction; cross-attention to map tokens encodes environment layout.
• Bayes-motivated auxiliary tasks, local occupancy reconstruction and long-horizon waypoints, add multi-scale spatiotemporal supervision.
• Trained on mixed team sizes; handles single-robot, multi-robot, and conditional generation with fixed robot tokens.
• Results: high success in cluttered connectivity-constrained navigation, beating its data-generating expert; abstract reports no numbers.

lY47GBfn32.text:
• Motion imitation enables humanlike humanoid locomotion, but high-quality mocap datasets like AMASS are scarce and expensive.
• Video-derived datasets like Humanoid-X scale up but suffer floating, penetration, and foot skating artifacts.
• PHUMA: a physically reliable humanoid locomotion dataset combining motion capture and internet video.
• Two-stage pipeline: physics-aware curation filters bad motions, then physics-constrained retargeting maps them to humanoids.
• Result is a 73-hour, physically reliable corpus for training motion tracking policies.
• PHUMA-trained policies achieve higher tracking success rates than those trained on AMASS or Humanoid-X.
• Policies transfer zero-shot to a real Unitree G1, showing scalable data without sacrificing physical realism.

bXQv3Kn5qL.text:
• Problem: vision-and-language navigation needs both high-level semantic understanding and precise spatial structure.
• Key idea: decouple low-level spatial state estimation from high-level MLLM semantic planning.
• Explicit metric world representation replaces oversimplified textual maps, keeping rich, consistent spatial information.
• The MLLM queries and reasons over this representation to make navigation decisions.
• Counterfactual reasoning elicits MLLM capacity; the world representation keeps actions physically valid.
• New zero-shot state of the art: 48.8% SR on R2R-CE, 46.2% on RxR-CE.
• Sim-to-real transfer works across diverse robot embodiments, showing robust real-world deployment.

qQs6JndxfZ.text:
• Problem: LLM robot plans are fluent but often violate syntactic and semantic constraints needed for execution.
• Existing fixes trade off: soft methods lack guarantees, while symbolic planners like LLM+P discard LM commonsense.
• Key idea: Meta-Ctrl guarantees encoded constraints via constrained decoding while preserving the base LM's plan quality.
• Meta-tokens, a compact grounded-action vocabulary, enforce syntax per token and preconditions, goals, ordering per action.
• Exact factorization cuts constrained-decoding memory from 107 TB to under 2 GB.
• Small open-weight LM reaches highest reported subgoal success on WAH-NL (LoTa-Bench), beating GPT-4, plus strong EAI results.
• Real tabletop robot: every generated plan satisfies its preconditions and goals by construction.

Lp94sPpAo0.text:
• Problem: robots rarely use sound to find manipulation targets, despite rich acoustic cues about location and material.
• New benchmark: acoustic-aware manipulation tasks where robots must localize and identify sound sources to choose targets.
• Tasks demand active exploration guided by auditory cues, combining sound source localization and timbre identification.
• Key idea: S2A2 fuses visual features with acoustic spatial and spectral signal information for imitation learning.
• Framework is policy-agnostic, implemented with ACT, Diffusion Policy, VQ-BeT, and π0 backbones.
• Simulation: S2A2 performed best on tasks requiring both sound position and timbre; abstract reports no numbers.
• Real-robot experiments confirm the proposed tasks and framework transfer to real-world manipulation.

8iFziu27Yy.text:
• Problem: manipulation benchmarks like LIBERO and robosuite assume ground-supported robots, ignoring aerial manipulation dynamics.
• Aerial manipulation faces disturbances, coupled arm-floating base dynamics, and constrained degrees of freedom.
• Key idea: AM-Bench, a modular simulation suite and benchmark for multirotor aerial manipulation policy learning.
• Includes fully actuated and underactuated embodiments, plus 12 tasks spanning contact, transport, and constrained interaction.
• Configurable disturbances model aerodynamic effects and actuator saturation, with standard low-level controllers and baseline policies.
• New: system-level evaluation of how embodiment, control, disturbances, and policy choices interact, beyond end-to-end success.
• Studies reveal policy performance under aerial conditions, policy-control interface effects, and embodiment differences; abstract gives no numbers.

xMysKLF2hX.text:
• Problem: evaluating robot policies usually needs real rollouts, simulators, or world models, which are costly and error-prone.
• Simulator and world-model evaluators accumulate prediction errors that compound over long evaluation horizons.
• Key idea: off-policy evaluation estimates policy return directly from offline robot trajectories, with no new rollouts.
• Method: RoboFQE combines fitted Q-evaluation, a pretrained vision foundation model, and learned terminal success annotation.
• No behavior-policy density estimation needed, bridging standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation.
• Results: accurate discounted-return estimates and preserved policy rankings across simulated and real-world tasks (abstract reports no numbers).
• Outperforms video world models on long-horizon tasks; pretrained encoders beat from-scratch, and learned success labels cost little accuracy.

DBLXUxxslN.text:
• Problem: sparse-reward RL avoids reward shaping but often needs heavy curriculum engineering, long training, or many demonstrations.
• Key idea: combine scalable RL, high-throughput GPU simulation, and demonstration-based auto-curricula to tackle these bottlenecks.
• Method: FlashRFCL uses reverse-forward curriculum learning, building on prior reverse-forward curriculum work.
• Setup: evaluated on a variety of high-dimensional robotic tasks trained in massively parallel GPU simulation.
• Main result: solves these tasks using just one demonstration per task, with no reward shaping.
• Speed: trains faster than prior work, though the abstract reports no exact speedup figures.
• New: extensive ablations show how each design choice affects training speed and final performance.

ult1vxdeUb.text:
• Most visuomotor policies and pretrained VLAs ignore touch, relying only on vision and proprioception.
• Prior tactile methods need special hardware, separate encoders, or non-image backbones, breaking pretrained 2D pipelines.
• Key insight: the bottleneck is how contact is delivered, not the contact information itself.
• Visible Touch renders contact signals into the camera image frame, requiring no architectural changes.
• Includes an open-source, low-cost magnetic contact sensor built from off-the-shelf parts via CAD-to-mold.
• LIBERO: BC-Transformer gains 16 points; miniVLA gains 29 points average success rate.
• Real world: π0.5 gains 30 points on four contact-rich tasks; contact representation matters most.

0cK9Wf9Eeq.text:
• Problem: real-world dexterous manipulation still depends heavily on human supervision and hand-engineered algorithms.
• Key idea: automate robotics research via a repeatable physical loop: reset, execute, verify, refine.
• ENPIRE: harness for coding agents with Environment, Policy Improvement, Rollout, and Evolution modules.
• Agents analyze logs, consult literature, and rewrite training infrastructure and algorithm code to fix failures.
• Works across heuristics, tool calling, behavior cloning, offline and online RL, plus RoboCasa simulation.
• Results: agents autonomously reach 99% success on PushT, pin-box organizing, and zip-tie cutting.
• New: parallel robot-fleet acceleration, measured by Mean Robot Utilization and Mean Token Utilization metrics.

k6kMJCL22t.text:
• Problem: HJ reachability gives safety guarantees but scales poorly to high-dimensional nonlinear robotic systems.
• Gaps: grid solvers hit dimensionality limits; neural PDE solvers need gradients; RL approaches train unstably.
• Key idea: discrete-time Bellman-Isaacs value propagation learns reachable and reach-avoid tubes without explicit PDE gradients.
• Method: bang-bang optimal control yields teacher actions from value probes, turning adversarial learning into supervised learning.
• Stability: windowed temporal curriculum trains values backward from terminal boundary, each window seeding the next.
• Results: accurate value functions on benchmarks up to 80 dimensions, more stable than existing learning-based solvers.
• Scale: F1-tenth safety filter with 16,000+ dimensional inputs generalizes zero-shot and runs real-time on RC car.

8TvqhVkrMd.text:
• Problem: VLAs with continuous action experts generalize poorly to unseen, out-of-distribution language instructions.
• Cause: language is far less diverse than vision and action data, inviting visual shortcuts.
• Randomly initialized action experts produce noisy gradients that corrupt the VLM and underuse its language ability.
• Key idea: Bayesian factorization into a language-agnostic vision-action prior and a language-conditioned VLA likelihood.
• Stage 1 pretrains the action expert on vision-action pairs from a frozen VLM.
• Stage 2 injects language through gated fusion, preserving the learned visuomotor prior.
• Works with π- and GR00T-style architectures, giving consistent gains on unseen instructions and compositional tasks.

RwGNm8fUxX.text:
• Problem: VLN agents "succeed" by stopping within 3 meters, ignoring final orientation and target visibility.
• The paper formalizes this flaw as the Last-3-Meter Grounding Gap between region arrival and object grounding.
• Three new instance-centric metrics measure proximity precision, target visibility, and final-view grounding.
• REALM: plug-and-play, architecture-agnostic module separating fine target approaching from long-horizon navigation.
• Visibility-aware stopping strategy reduces premature termination and improves final viewpoint alignment with the target.
• New REVERIE-AIM dataset: object-instance goals plus 180K short-horizon samples for final-stage approaching.
• Across four VLN backbones, REALM consistently improves proximity precision and visual grounding success.

8QEFjWSgyu.text:
• Problem: robot planners encode observations by appearance, not task-relevant functionality, limiting generalization to novel robot-object interactions.
• Key idea: reason about what objects enable (e.g., movable), not what they look like (e.g., cart).
• Method: A4D maps visual observations into a shared latent space structured around affordances.
• Proximity to affordance embeddings infers object functionalities and quantifies uncertainty in the inference.
• New: uncertainty-triggered affordance discovery expands the latent space when existing affordances are insufficient.
• Setup: evaluated on several planning tasks involving diverse and unseen affordances.
• Results: 94% accuracy, beating state-of-the-art by 15+ points; new affordances ~70% to 90%+ with <10% data; 100x faster inference.

KDuIgyXUtd.text:
• Dexterous hands get motion intent from teleoperation or policies, but commands rarely specify the needed contact decisions.
• DexFLEX: a contact-aware foundation controller turning fingertip-motion drafts into contact-consistent joint commands.
• Key idea: treat drafts as evidence about intent, not trajectories to copy exactly.
• Draft-Dream-Select proposes short-horizon motion chunks, predicts contact outcomes, and picks the most stable command-following candidate.
• Mixes pure-prior proposals for recovery with draft-seeded proposals for responsiveness, then decodes into joint targets.
• Evaluated on degraded-command simulation, real-world shared control, and visuomotor policy learning, using one controller without retraining.
• Real teleoperation success rises from 29.2% to 78.3%; policy learning reaches 46.7%, 3.5x direct joint prediction.

hgRIVs5QZU.text:
• Problem: embodied world models generate long manipulation videos frame by frame, making pixel-space rollouts slow.
• Naive frame dropping fails because policies need sparse task events: approach, contact, grasp, release.
• Key idea: SKIP generates only task-relevant keyframes, then densifies them through event-preserving interpolation.
• Method: robot-aware multimodal keyframe selection, sparse video diffusion, learned gap predictor, action-conditioned interpolator.
• On LIBERO, SKIP is 4.16x faster than dense generation and cuts aggregate FVD by 89.0%.
• Replacing all real demos with SKIP videos drops pi0.5 success only 1.3 pp in simulation, 6.7 pp on a real robot.
• Dense frame-by-frame generated data collapses policy success by 48-58 pp, so SKIP makes generated rollouts usable training data.

7qMRpmvhZL.text:
• Problem: VLA manipulation models are fragile to small real-world perturbations, especially lighting changes.
• FLARE: optimized physical spotlight attack, black-box, drops baseline task success rates to zero.
• Pitfall: naive augmentation-based adversarial training teaches VLAs to discard color as noise.
• Defended models become shape-biased, revealed by a diagnostic grayscale evaluation where they still succeed.
• Consequence: benign color-dependent real-world task success falls to at most 47.5%, below the undefended baseline.
• ChromaGuard: chroma-preserving adversarial training that keeps color perception while resisting illumination attacks.
• On a physical 6-DoF robot: 97.5% benign and 92.5% attacked success on color-dependent tasks.

bjPoaczBRX.text:
• Problem: pre-trained manipulation policies fail unless mobile base is placed within their training distribution.
• Task: predict SE(2) base pose for a fixed policy from one ego-centric RGB-D frame plus instruction.
• Prior work learns per-task, instruction-agnostic success likelihoods, limiting cross-task generalization and language disambiguation.
• Key idea: MoFlo learns language- and observation-conditioned transport from current base pose to policy-compatible pose.
• Method: single multi-task model trained via conditional flow matching with x1 (endpoint) prediction.
• Results: 80% mean success on five RoboCasa kitchen tasks, outperforming prior policy-mobilization baselines.
• New: language disambiguation among same-category fixtures, validated on real mobile manipulator, beating a representative baseline.

Gr9nFtFTjn.text:
• Diffusion Policy controls robots well, but iterative denoising is too costly for resource-constrained edge devices.
• AgileDP introduces integer-based quantization of diffusion policies for efficient on-board deployment.
• Challenge one: activation distributions shift drastically across denoising timesteps, so fixed quantization grids fail.
• Fix: lightweight network maps timestep to dynamic activation quantization scales, without extra training overhead.
• Challenge two: low-magnitude action regions suffer large relative quantization error; magnitude-aware reweighted distillation targets them.
• Evaluated on 7 tasks across 3 benchmarks; 4-bit precision performs comparably to full-precision models.
• Achieves up to 8.5x speedup and 3.2x memory savings, validating practical on-board robot deployment.

0DopZPPLvw.text:
• Problem: tactile sensors are heterogeneous, so models trained on one sensor fail on others.
• This limits scaling contact-rich manipulation policy learning from diverse tactile data.
• Key idea: Heterogeneous Tactile Transformer learns shared tactile representations across different sensor types.
• Method: sensor-specific encoders feed a shared transformer trunk, pretrained with masked reconstruction plus cross-modal alignment.
• New HPT dataset: 1.6M synchronized paired frames across four vision- and array-based tactile sensors.
• Evaluated on tactile perception and real-world manipulation; representations transfer to new tasks and unseen sensors.
• Dataset, code, and model checkpoints will be released upon publication.

ShBMWDRPVu.text:
• Problem: pixel video models waste capacity on appearance; action models need embodiment-specific labels, limiting scalability.
• Key idea: μ0 forecasts smooth 3D traces of interaction points: objects, tools, hands, contact regions.
• Traces give a compact, embodiment-agnostic motion interface, learnable without any robot action labels.
• TraceExtract auto-labels diverse videos: keypoint selection, globally aligned 3D traces, hierarchical language captions.
• Model: pretrained vision-language backbone plus modular trace expert predicting B-spline control points per query.
• Outperforms trace prediction models and tokenized VLM methods on both 2D and 3D trace prediction.
• Frozen μ0 plus action experts yields policies competitive with action-pretrained VLAs like π0.

hwTNqrJmuQ.text:
• Problem: VLA policies assume the initial view is actionable, but wrist-view targets are often partially or fully occluded.
• Insight: many manipulation failures stem from lacking a task-ready observation, not from insufficient manipulation skill.
• Key idea: Seek-before-Act, a plug-in framework that actively acquires the right viewpoint before downstream manipulation.
• Method: from instruction and wrist RGB, generative foresight imagines target-revealing views, then lifts them to 3D.
• Planning: collision-aware motion toward viewpoints improving visibility, reachability, and manipulability; semantic verification triggers closed-loop replanning.
• Results: simulation and real-world tests show substantially higher success under occlusion, clutter, noise, and scene changes (abstract gives no figures).
• New: task-conditioned visual foresight for active viewing, compatible with existing VLA policies and model-based planners.

HfHTPpDBYr.text:
• Problem: human teaching covers some task features well, others poorly, leaving learned rewards underspecified.
• Prior work detects poorly supervised features but asks humans to re-teach, burdening those who already struggled.
• Key idea: the robot uses knowledge of its own uncertainty to ask smarter, targeted preference questions.
• Method: an informed prior focuses active preference queries on features that still need resolving.
• Each query includes an explanation directing human attention to exactly those uncertain features.
• Simulation: informed prior beats standard active preference learning by up to 30.8% with few queries.
• User study: prior and explanations each significantly improve reward recovery and amplify each other.

y5Z5ccS0Bv.text:
• Problem: scalable sim for manipulation needs fine-grained functional object compositions, not just coarse scene layouts.
• Key idea: recast composition generation as disentangled reconstruction followed by relative pose recovery.
• CoGen combines 2D and 3D generative models to produce instance-disentangled meshes with coarse initial poses.
• GPRM refines relative poses using joint geometric and physical guidance; a VLM verifier selects the best candidate.
• Setup: new benchmark spanning eight contact-geometry classes, compared against state-of-the-art 3D generators.
• Results: better asset quality and relation matching, with collision rate reduced below 1%.
• New: synthesized data for policy learning shows diversity scaling in both simulation and real-world deployment.

NCeeEHy8d5.text:
• Problem: steering learned robot policies at test time toward unanticipated user preferences, without retraining.
• Gap: end-to-end methods need fine-tuning or expert guidance; neuro-symbolic edits can yield physically infeasible plans.
• Key idea: ReStruct reconfigures task structure inside a neural automaton policy to follow new preferences.
• Policy splits into a high-level state-machine skeleton plus a low-level residual continuous controller.
• Preferences encoded as automata, merged into the skeleton via synchronous product; controller stays frozen.
• Skeleton action priors update accordingly, enabling physically-aware control under the modified task structure.
• Sim and real-world results: handles object-centric to temporal-logic preferences, beating VLAs by up to 25%.

NWlhQeCX3L.text:
• Problem: fly a quadrotor through a moving narrow gap, needing centimeter-level alignment and precise timing.
• Setting is state-free: policy maps onboard visual and inertial measurements directly to thrust and body-rate commands.
• Challenge: success lies on a thin feasible manifold; small timing, pose, or visibility errors cause collision.
• Key idea: train visuomotor policies from scratch by backpropagating through differentiable quadrotor dynamics and smooth task costs.
• New: first dynamic narrow-gap traversal learned without privileged state, teacher, planner, or distillation.
• Simulation: pathwise gradients beat score-function gradients, reaching 99.3% success after minutes on one GPU.
• Real world: direct sim-to-real transfer with onboard sensing only, 80% success over 10 trials from varied starts.

Tk20sRMzhv.text:
• Problem: rehab robots prescribe kinematic trajectories, not the muscle activations believed to drive neuromotor recovery.
• Challenge: muscle activity is hysteretic and stochastic, sEMG is noisy, and interventional datasets are costly.
• Key idea: personalizable transformer maps desired sEMG muscle activations to prescribed contact force trajectories on end-effector robots.
• Method: RoPE encoder-decoder learns user-specific neuromotor latents, with flow matching sampling plausible, distribution-constrained trajectories.
• Setup: 16 healthy participants, 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, testing generalization to held-out tasks and users.
• Results: under 8% mean trajectory error, effectively instantaneous deterministic inference, sub-second distribution sampling.
• New: minutes of user-specific fine-tuning further cut error, enabling activation-targeted prescription within a therapy session.

QwpnI3BlwT.text:
• Problem: VLA pretraining as behavior cloning ignores goal-reaching nature and temporal task progress of robot learning.
• Key idea: PRTS reformulates VLA pretraining as goal-conditioned RL, treating language instructions as goals.
• Contrastive RL learns embeddings whose inner product approximates log-discounted goal occupancy, i.e., goal reachability.
• Dense reachability supervision comes from offline trajectories, requiring no reward annotations.
• Role-aware causal mask folds this into the VLM backbone with negligible overhead over behavior cloning.
• Pretrained on 167B tokens; SOTA on LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv, and 14 real tasks.
• Largest gains on long-horizon, contact-rich, and zero-shot novel-instruction tasks via goal-reachability awareness.

SMBnET3Mz9.text:
• Problem: learning robot skills from human videos lacks fair comparison due to differing assumptions, hardware, setups.
• Key idea: RoboReel, a unified benchmark for evaluating policies learned from human video observation.
• Contents: real-world human demo videos, simulated robot trajectories, and evaluation environments across ten manipulation tasks.
• Four test suites probe robustness to visual distractors, long-horizon task completion, and other axes.
• Evaluates over seven state-of-the-art LfO algorithms, including the authors' new VLA-based variants.
• Studies how different representation choices affect learning-from-observation performance across model categories.
• Finding: long-horizon and low-tolerance tasks remain challenging for all current LfO models.

4RLjGPEfpH.text:
• Problem: VLA models struggle to transfer zero-shot to unseen robot embodiments; evaluations lack consistent definitions and controls.
• Key idea: separate strict zero-shot transfer (target never seen) from pretrain-exposed transfer (target seen only in pretraining).
• Setup: controlled benchmark with 14 held-out target embodiments, simulation plus real-world validation, isolating embodiment from task changes.
• Method: systematically studies state-action representations, pretraining embodiment diversity, auxiliary co-training, and target-embodiment exposure.
• Results: local end-effector state-action representations improve cross-embodiment transfer by about 15 percentage points.
• Results: greater source embodiment diversity adds about 18 points; auxiliary co-training adds about 7 points.
• New: just 5% target data in pretraining adds 13.4 points, so report strict and pretrain-exposed transfer separately.

IjnCc1OZnJ.text:
• Problem: robotic foundation models exploit spurious scene correlations, failing under shifted tables, dim lighting, or new distractors.
• This shortcut learning is well studied in vision but underexplored in robotic foundation models.
• Key idea: Artificial Foveated Perception (AFP) focuses policies on task-relevant visual regions, like human foveal vision.
• AFP is a lightweight, policy-agnostic module predicting task-conditioned masks over objects, robot, and action-critical regions.
• Masks enable preprocessing, token filtering, attention modulation, or auxiliary grounding losses without changing core policy architecture.
• Results across state-of-the-art VLA and World Action Models: faster fine-tuning, less overfitting, better robustness; abstract gives no numbers.
• Ablations over integration modes and mask usage attribute gains to directing learning toward task-relevant regions.

Vv1WXMkSTD.text:
• Problem: robotics teams invest heavily in data infrastructure, assuming loading and augmentation bottleneck imitation learning training.
• Key idea: systematically profile end-to-end LeRobot policy training to test whether data loading truly limits speed.
• Method: compare standard loaders against a custom Rust engine using Apache Arrow zero-copy and copy-on-write caching.
• Setup: consumer hardware, LeRobot ecosystem, multiple image spatial resolutions, measuring per-step training time breakdowns.
• Result: data path consumes only 1–4% of per-step training time across all reachable configurations.
• Result: large isolated micro-benchmark data speedups yield zero measurable wall-clock improvement in full training.
• New: real slowdowns come from format flaws like unindexed video decoding; optimize upstream, e.g., visual feature caching.

xyFvvMLQRo.text:
• Problem: mapless navigation methods assume fixed goals, but real-world goals often change online during execution.
• Setting: online chained-goal navigation, where goals are redirected or newly emerge without explicit transition signals.
• Insight: evolving goals demand continued exploration or strategic revisitation, creating conflicting memory requirements.
• Key idea: GLST decomposes latent beliefs into global-local spatial and long-short temporal memory representations.
• Method: goal-conditioned rewards balance exploration and exploitation as goals evolve over long horizons.
• Results: beats baselines in simulation across diverse terrains and is validated on Spot; abstract reports no figures.
• New: chained-goal navigation formulation, memory-decomposition framework, and open-source code for benchmarking.

2NBZAh51If.text:
• Problem: flow-matching policies must satisfy deployment constraints absent from demonstrations, like collision-free paths or grasp orientations.
• Guidance uses gradients at noisy intermediates, which need not point toward clean feasible actions.
• Projection is efficient but executes actions the policy would never draw itself.
• Key idea: projection gives a cheap, clean, feasible signal; the only mistake is executing it.
• Method: sample, project to nearest feasible point, resample biased toward it, iterate; no auxiliary network needed.
• Evaluated on 2D diagnostic, 7-DoF shelf pick-and-place, and zero-shot Franka deployment; extends to arbitrary costs.
• Stays closest to policy while satisfying constraints; highest real-world safe-success on obstacle avoidance (abstract gives no numbers).

xm8LPYlbxA.text:
• Problem: robots must learn safety from experience, since risky behaviors often cannot be specified in advance.
• Evidence from demonstrations, interventions, near misses, and failures is only local, hard to use for long-horizon planning.
• Existing goal-conditioned planners compose short behaviors but assume safety-relevant costs are already known.
• Key idea: CoGeL learns a soft safety signal and embeds it directly into the goal-reaching distance.
• What's new: safety shapes planning geometry itself, not a separate classifier, hard mask, or post-hoc filter.
• Theory: bounded geometry changes from safety errors, waypoint composition, and calibrated limits on expected violations.
• Results: substantially fewer unsafe events across navigation tasks while preserving long-horizon goal-reaching; abstract reports no numbers.

Mnggg9cnbh.text:
• Problem: cameras fail in low light and high dynamic range, while sparse single-channel LiDAR mismatches RGB-pretrained vision models.
• Key idea: Cyclops translates sparse non-repetitive scanning LiDAR intensity into RGB video for camera-free, all-day perception.
• Method: a frozen pretrained module densifies sparse intensity projections into a geometrically rich source condition.
• Latent Bridge Matching then transports dense intensity latents to RGB using a learned velocity field in few ODE steps.
• Temporal attention injects prior-frame context, and a differentiable terminal reward optimizes the velocity field to reduce flicker.
• Results: synthesized RGB beats LiDAR baselines and real cameras on segmentation, lane detection, and colorization (abstract reports no numbers).
• What's new: LiDAR acts as an illumination-invariant RGB camera, letting off-the-shelf RGB models work even near dark.

R1fgJZLFnx.text:
• Problem: legged loco-manipulation needs stable grasps under uncertain external forces while coordinating whole-body motion.
• Gap: tactile sensing is rarely used in dynamic whole-body control; existing policies simply grasp firmly.
• Key idea: a unified RL policy controls legs, arm, and gripper using tactile plus proprioceptive feedback.
• Method: tactile array data from compliant grippers is encoded into a compact latent fused with proprioception.
• Grasp stability rewards teach tracking body velocity and end-effector trajectories while moderating force and preventing slip.
• Setup: zero-shot sim-to-real on Unitree Go2 with WidowX 250 arm, tested under gradual loads and sudden releases.
• Results: 47% lower grasping force and under 1% object drop rate in dynamic tactile-informed loco-manipulation.

Tk1gtgOESR.text:
• Problem: universal humanoid motion tracking must handle highly diverse human motions in human environments.
• Mixture-of-experts policies are popular here, using dynamic routing to boost policy expressiveness.
• Insight: dynamic routing causes misestimated divergence between old and updated policies during policy-gradient updates.
• Consequence: updates become overly conservative or excessively large, yielding suboptimal policies.
• Key idea: MAPO alternately optimizes the router and the experts, avoiding divergence misestimation.
• Results: about 1.8x higher reward than an MoE policy trained with an existing policy-gradient method.
• MAPO achieves the highest tracking success rate and the lowest error on most metrics among compared methods.

7cfCazwFp6.text:
