• Problem: diffusion-based VLAs execute action chunks open-loop, so they react poorly to moving objects or changing contacts.
• Key idea: VLA-Feedback pairs low-frequency diffusion planning with high-frequency observation feedback in a two-timescale architecture.
• Method: stop denoising before the final stage, then refine the chunk online at control frequency.
• Refinement uses observation-conditioned denoising velocity updates, avoiding reruns of the full vision-language diffusion model.
• Setup: evaluated on both stationary and non-stationary (dynamic) robotic manipulation tasks.
• Results: preserves static-task performance and improves robustness in dynamic scenes; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• What's new: real-time closed-loop correction inside diffusion denoising while keeping the planner's expressiveness.

GMAZdF34n5.text:
• Problem: world-model VLA policies use reconstruction objectives, favoring pixel fidelity over task-relevant state evolution for control.
• Key idea: predict future world states in a pretrained latent space instead of reconstructing future pixels.
• Latent predictions give compact, semantically grounded, dynamics-aware context for action generation.
• Method: Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with shared causal self-attention in a single sequence model.
• Unifies environment understanding, latent world-state prediction, and action generation in one framework.
• Setup and results: state-of-the-art in simulation and real robots; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Strongest gains on long-horizon, interaction-rich, dynamically perturbed tasks; latent prediction serves as control-aligned objective.

CqkIkio00K.text:
• Problem: users' valued outcomes and preferences in assistive robotics are unknown, individual, and context-dependent.
• Constraint: costly policy execution, biomechanical measurement, and feedback collection severely limit queries and optimization iterations.
• Key idea: SFIHILO jointly learns a forward outcome model and inverse individual reward from preferences over outcomes.
• Method: forward model predicts user outcomes from policies, enabling active querying that accelerates inverse reward learning.
• Queries score expected uncertainty reduction across forward and inverse beliefs, targeting a regional preference boundary.
• Setup: simulations varying user heterogeneity, outcome dimensionality, precision, noise levels, and nonstationarity; final policy needs no extra trials.
• Results: significantly better inverse-learning sample efficiency than mutual information baselines, preserving forward accuracy; no numbers reported.

EfgCnZgmvN.text:
• Problem: visuomotor control and dynamics models are trained separately and struggle to exploit heterogeneous robot, human, and simulated data.
• Key idea: 3D object motion trajectories serve as a shared interface linking robot actions and dynamics modeling.
• Method: object motion and robot actions co-evolve as variables under a single masked generative objective.
• The mask pattern sets both the pretraining supervision regime and the deployment inference mode within one model.
• Hindsight-relabeled motion contexts and a contrastive loss separate task intent from scene geometry, with no manual instructions needed.
• Setup: pretrained on public robot demos, human videos, and simulation; the same parameters serve every inference mode.
• Results: consistently beats specialized SOTA baselines in motion-conditioned control, dynamics modeling, and few-shot task adaptation.

PHNhlZK2uS.text:
• Problem: vision-based drone policy training is bottlenecked by slow rendering in existing batch quadrotor simulators.
• Key idea: HyperDrone, a batch quadrotor simulator built around high-performance rendering on modern GPU ray-tracing cores.
• Method: custom ray-tracing engine renders RGB and depth observations across many parallel environments.
• Configurable fidelity: reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and physically based rendering (PBR).
• Results: over 20x faster than state-of-the-art batch simulators, millions of FPS on consumer-grade GPUs.
• Speed holds even at highest fidelity while simulating realistic 3D scenes.
• Demo: yaw-control policy trained purely in simulation, transferred to a real Crazyflie running fully onboard.

SBGylS4zwM.text:
• Problem: end-to-end bio-lab automation needs robots that manipulate liquids and operate automated liquid-handler platforms.
• Gap: AutoBio and LabUtopia focus on rigid instruments or chemistry, with limited fluid modeling fidelity.
• Key idea: LiquidLab benchmark jointly evaluates physical liquid manipulation and automated liquid-handler operation.
• Setup: sixteen tasks spanning direct liquid manipulation, platform operations, and long-horizon wet-lab protocols.
• Method: parallel SPH fluid simulation on Genesis enables large-scale liquid simulation on a single GPU.
• New: success judged by particle-level volumetric criteria instead of pose proxies.
• Results: four imitation-learning and VLA policies remain unreliable, failing at millimeter-scale labware staging and free-surface control.

mlF6DhhBNF.text:
• Problem: video-action models lose video foundation models' compositional priors after finetuning on robot action data.
• The authors call this discrepancy the video-action generalization gap and study it systematically.
• Evaluating a broad VAM design space, standard design choices show no pattern explaining generalization.
• Key idea: Temporal Ratio, an attention measure of action-head reliance on future latents versus current frame.
• Higher Temporal Ratio predicts stronger compositional generalization; it rises during planning and drops during precise manipulation.
• Method: inference-time adaptive guidance amplifies compositional video conditioning when the policy attends to future rollouts.
• Results: reduces the OOD-ID compositional gap on LIBERO and real-world tasks; the abstract reports no numbers.

bC8Sv8wTTL.text:
• Problem: inference-time steering of generative robot policies typically verifies candidate actions with vision only, missing contact cues.
• Vision alone fails in contact-rich manipulation, where success hinges on subtle local interactions like contact force.
• Key idea: ViTaL frames visuo-tactile steering as bi-level optimization combining visual mode selection with tactile refinement.
• High level: visual sampling-and-verification picks long-horizon behavior; low level: tactile-guided diffusion editing refines short-horizon actions.
• Method: learned visuo-tactile latent world model with semantically aligned visual and tactile verifiers for outcome-based steering.
• New: text-conditioned tactile reward scoring predicted tactile futures directly in latent space.
• Results on three real-world contact-rich tasks: +51% over base policy, +33% over unimodal, +20% over naive fusion.

6TXMWx1Wih.text:
• Problem: imitation learning relies on costly, unguided teleoperation, yielding much data that barely improves policy performance.
• Gap: existing curation methods filter datasets after collection, so they cannot prevent wasted uninformative demonstrations.
• Key idea: GUILD actively decides which data to collect next to maximize downstream policy performance.
• Method: iterative loop alternating task proposal and data collection with data evaluation for closed-loop feedback.
• Task proposal: vision-language model priors suggest relevant environments, object configurations, and goals to collect.
• Data evaluation: predictive data attribution estimates each trajectory's influence on performance in the target deployment setting.
• Results: in simulation and on real robots, it improves sample efficiency over passive collection, baselines, and experienced roboticists.

UMHg65UHcY.text:
• Problem: open-vocabulary 3D affordance detection, localizing interaction regions on point clouds from novel text descriptions.
• Gap: MLLM segmentation tokens are semantically rich but spatially poor, since autoregression ignores spatial neighborhoods.
• Key idea: after generation, inject multi-scale geometric features from a frozen pre-trained 3D VQVAE encoder into output tokens.
• Method: each token queries its paired voxel scale via cross-attention, with a learned gate controlling injection strength.
• Enhanced tokens form a spatially-aware affordance prompt via semantic-conditioned attention, decoded with per-point features into masks.
• Results: state-of-the-art on open-vocabulary affordance detection, about 10% absolute gain in instance-level mIoU.
• Real robot experiments confirm zero-shot transfer to novel objects; novelty is post-generation voxel-token fusion.

gQFYIM5dJy.text:
• Problem: sequential manipulation policies fail on novel combinations of familiar instruction components under sparse data.
• Exhaustively collecting demonstrations for every instruction tuple is combinatorially expensive and impractical.
• Key idea: study compositional generalization through instruction-space coverage rather than raw task count.
• Method: decompose the gap into marginal instruction, instruction-compositional, and context-action shifts.
• Result: structured subsets covering a quarter of task space recover strong out-of-distribution performance.
• Sparse training fails from instruction steering; one demo per task lifts OOD success from 0.4% to 54.7%.
• New takeaway: data collection should prioritize dependency and relational coverage over exhaustive task expansion.

NnFdATGR3L.text:
• Problem: imitation-learning manipulation policies assume clean backgrounds and lack obstacle-aware motion generation in clutter.
• Key idea: ObstaDiff, a decomposed diffusion-policy framework with a lightweight obstacle-aware visual encoder.
• Encoder extracts a structured target–obstacle–background representation of the scene.
• Alignment policy generates end-effector trajectories toward a target-centered bottleneck pose while reasoning about obstacles.
• Setup: 61 real-robot greenhouse trials testing target-pose, obstacle-layout, and target-appearance generalization.
• Results: 75.41% average task success and 8.20% average obstacle collision rate, beating imitation-learning baselines.
• What's new: explicit obstacle-aware representations improve diffusion-policy generalization in cluttered agricultural scenes.

PNSqN6Bng7.text:
• Problem: terminal success labels rarely reveal which local decision caused a failed language-conditioned VLA trajectory.
• Key idea: DCCP turns world-model imagined futures into localized action preferences instead of whole-trajectory supervision.
• Mines decision-sensitive states using progress curvature and action-token entropy to target critical choices.
• Perturbs only the first action chunk under a shared visual-language prefix; a progress scorer rates short branches.
• High-margin branch differences train a local DPO-style loss; trajectory-level GRPO preserves full-task improvement.
• Simulation: LIBERO, LIBERO-BDDL, MimicGen-D0 average success rises from 75.6% (WMPO) to 80.1%.
• Real RM65, four tasks: success 70.6% to 78.8%, semantic commitment errors 13.1% to 7.5%.

pTqOGquuCh.text:
• Problem: safe navigation needs semantic awareness, since different object categories require different safety clearances.
• Challenge: VLM confidence scores are poorly calibrated, making raw predictions unreliable for safety-critical planning.
• Gap: existing conformal prediction assumes fixed label sets and stationary data, unsuitable for open-world exploration.
• Key idea: CoSMO converts VLM embeddings into calibrated coverage sets and safety-aware obstacle dilations.
• What's new: supports a dynamically expanding hazard vocabulary with coverage guarantees even under distribution shift.
• Setup: evaluated on Matterport3D (MP3D) scenes against a geometry-only navigation baseline.
• Results: 61.6% fewer semantic collisions, with formal coverage maintained even under delayed expert feedback.

T3IOHvur0R.text:
• Problem: World Action Models generalize better than VLAs but are slow, needing costly denoising per inference chunk.
• WAMs learn from abundant unlabeled video, handling novel motions and environments better than standard VLA policies.
• Prior acceleration caches computation only within a single chunk's denoising trajectory, missing cross-chunk redundancy.
• Key insight: during smooth behaviors, residuals at the same denoising step correlate strongly across consecutive chunks.
• Method: C³ache, training-free, caches and reuses residuals across inference chunks at matching denoising steps.
• Setup: evaluated on robotics benchmarks using a Fast-WAM backbone.
• Results: up to 2.5X faster total wall-clock inference with negligible drop in task success rate.

9uM5JbXz4T.text:
• Problem: video world models evaluate policies on nominal imaginations, missing rare high-impact outcomes without prohibitively many samples.
• Key idea: StressDream steers diffusion world model imaginations toward text-specified high-impact yet plausible outcomes at inference time.
• Method: optimizes the initial diffusion noise instead of retraining, targeting events like task failures described in text.
• Semantic objective: a Vision-Language Model reasons about generated videos, providing informative gradients toward nuanced, scene-dependent target events.
• Plausibility objective: keeps optimized noise in-distribution, preventing drift toward implausible, out-of-distribution imaginations.
• Setup: evaluated with state-of-the-art video world models for autonomous driving and robotic manipulation.
• Results: identifies actions whose plausible futures include failures, enabling robust policy evaluation and improvement; abstract reports no numbers.

wXv81vB0Xt.text:
• Generative control policies can scale test-time compute via more denoising steps (sequential) or more samples (parallel).
• Existing fixed conservative schedules over-compute in easy states and under-allocate compute in difficult ones.
• Optimal allocation is state-, task-, and policy-dependent, e.g., broad exploration early, precise refinement near contact.
• ELASTIC frames compute allocation as a meta-MDP over a frozen pretrained diffusion or flow policy.
• An RL-trained meta-policy picks sequential steps and parallel samples per denoising iteration, without GCP training data.
• In simulated manipulation with diffusion policies, ELASTIC Pareto-dominates fixed and single-axis baselines at matched compute.
• On real robots with pi0.5 VLA, it matches best-of-10 success while cutting wall-clock latency by 34%.

rIyIQWvpST.text:
• Problem: low-cost passive leader arms lack restoring forces, leaving redundant joints unconstrained and demonstrations inconsistent.
• Key idea: "Hardware-as-Regularization", where mechanical compliance acts as a physical prior on joint-space trajectories.
• Method: passive joint with adjustable mechanical clutch and 3D-printed spiral spring returning joints to user-defined zero-point.
• No active actuators needed; compliance is adjustable and adds no extra cognitive load for operators.
• Setup: compared against a naive passive arm and an active virtual spring system for data collection.
• Results: drastically lower joint-angle variance than the naive arm, matching the active system's trajectory consistency.
• Downstream policies match active-setup success rates, eliminating manual drift compensation at a fraction of the cost.

wYLEzeAKFI.text:
• Problem: classical reachability methods like Hamilton-Jacobi and set propagation scale poorly with state dimension.
• Sampling-based methods offer finite-sample probability-mass guarantees, but accuracy's dependence on geometry, dynamics, and sampling is unclear.
• Key idea: cast sampling-based reachable-set recovery as geometric support estimation over initial set, dynamics, and sampling law.
• Positive reach of the initial set's complement plus Lipschitz dynamics upgrade mass coverage to Hausdorff accuracy r.
• Upper bound: recovery needs O~((e^{3LT}/r)^n) samples, exponential in state dimension n and horizon T.
• Minimax lower bound Ω((e^{LT}/r)^n) for any estimator: exponential dimension and horizon dependence are intrinsic.
• Experiments on nonlinear systems show adversarial sampling improves constants but cannot change the exponential scaling.

51YZMUGRUA.text:
• Problem: real-world robot policy testing is faithful but costly; simulation scales but is biased by sim-to-real gap.
• Existing simulation-augmented evaluation estimates only population-averaged performance, hiding scenario-specific failures and safe deployment conditions.
• SCAPE predicts scenario-conditioned real-world performance from few paired sim-real samples plus large-scale simulation rollouts.
• Method: corrects sim-to-real bias in simulation labels before training predictor; conformal prediction calibrates uncertainty.
• Setup: autonomous driving and quadruped velocity tracking, sim-to-sim experiments plus a physical Unitree Go2 deployment.
• Results: error cut 4.9%/34.7% (driving), 14.5%/27.7% (quadruped) versus neural/aggregate statistical baselines.
• Also: better sample-efficiency, narrower calibrated intervals, stronger out-of-distribution generalization, enabling fine-grained deployment strategies.

iOU9zkASbg.text:
• Problem: robot policies are ranked using few costly hardware trials, so statistical noise can produce wrong rankings.
• Fixed-batch comparisons across multiple policies are especially error-prone without rigorous uncertainty control.
• Key idea: AnyRank, a sequential policy-ranking method combining sequential testing with multiple-hypothesis testing.
• Adaptively allocates hardware trials to policies that are hardest to separate statistically.
• Gives valid partial rankings at any stopping time, bounding the probability of an incorrect ranking.
• Optionally uses priors from held-out hardware trials or world-model rollouts to prioritize evaluations.
• Simulation and real-world benchmarks: up to 50% fewer hardware trials than rigorous baselines, avoiding heuristic ranking errors.

UVJPDRCmlf.text:
• Problem: safe, real-time manipulation of ropes and cloth under model and sensing uncertainty with intermittent contact.
• Key idea: pair a GPU-parallel differentiable simulator with real-time robust MPC to certify safety.
• Simulator uses contact smoothing, enabling efficient gradient-based planning through intermittent, contact-rich interactions.
• Method: GPU-parallel output-feedback robust MPC plans with the simulator to satisfy constraints despite uncertainty.
• Conformal prediction calibrates visual-feedback and perception-error bounds, yielding reachable tubes for high-probability safe control.
• Setup: obstacle avoidance, routing, folding, and smoothing of ropes and cloth, in simulation and hardware.
• Results: millisecond-speed planning beating baselines in safety, speed, and success; simulator also accelerates model-based RL.

e9ZYAwJqFR.text:
• Problem: VLA prompts are reused every replanning step, so text repeatedly steers closed-loop robot control.
• Prior attacks target low-level actions or persistence across images, not final physical task outcomes.
• New failure mode: prompts that appear to specify the intended task but redirect the final outcome.
• Formalized as command-preserving trajectory redirection: one fixed prompt, all policy and environment components unchanged.
• Constraints: prompt stays close to the benign instruction, omitting target words and correction language.
• Method: on-policy prompt search using rollouts to find perturbations whose behavior tracks attacker targets.
• Results: near-benign prompts redirect VLA rollouts to attacker targets in simulation and on hardware.

2LNbCnzTQk.text:
• Problem: embodied agents rely on hand-designed module compositions; architecture choices depend on researcher intuition.
• Question: does Agent Architecture Search, proven for text agents, transfer to perceptual embodied agents via simulator rollouts?
• AgentCanvas: typed-graph runtime hosting embodied executors as editable node-and-wire programs with simulator-aware execution and logs.
• KDLoop: coding-agent search cycling proposal, critique, experiment, distillation, with triggered reflection after stalls.
• Setup: 3 AAS variants × 4 executors spanning navigation, embodied QA, and language-conditioned manipulation.
• Results: search yields deployable, directional success-rate gains; one high-scoring candidate rejected for data leakage.
• New limits vs text AAS: rollout noise masks signals, local edit basins, only partial episode-level credit assignment.

9seU2kEIxR.text:
• Problem: simulated human models for intervention learning don't match how real people actually intervene.
• Finding: humans intervene when agent progress stalls, and their corrective actions are often suboptimal.
• New progress-based intervention model better rank-correlates with real-user algorithm rankings, enabling realistic simulated benchmarking.
• Key idea: Q-OIL adds optimistic RL bonuses on intervention transitions to revisit informative states.
• Method uses decoupled critics to avoid over-optimism, plus imitation-learning regularization.
• Setup: evaluated against competitive learning-from-intervention baselines in simulation and real-world robotic tasks.
• Results: Q-OIL achieves 10-50% higher success than baselines, grounding learning in realistic human behavior.

xXHKqL5u5P.text:
• Problem: sim-and-real co-training treats simulators as fixed data sources, using uniform, retrieval, or manual expert alignment.
• Key idea: Active Generative Simulation, optimizing simulator data distributions to maximize downstream real-world policy performance.
• Method: MetaGenSim trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to discover high-utility simulation parameter distributions.
• No human heuristics needed; evaluated on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks against uniform and retrieval baselines.
• Results: 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation; matches expert manual alignment.
• Distributions curated with a lightweight proxy policy transfer effectively to VLA fine-tuning.
• Exploits partial sim-real alignment via atomic skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact matches are unavailable.

qd6clCx6QY.text:
• Problem: behavior cloning research lacks large open datasets, reproducible training, and cheap, reliable evaluation without physical robots.
• Key idea: ABC, a fully open-source stack covering data, hardware, training, simulation, and evaluation for manipulation.
• ABC-Data: largest open bimanual teleoperation dataset, 3,500 hours, over 130K episodes, 195 diverse tasks.
• Also releases accessible hardware setup, training infrastructure, simulation pipeline, and 280 hours of sim-teleop data.
• Sim-real co-training recipe yields correlated simulation and real-world evaluation, enabling design choices to be tested without robots.
• Compares training recipes and architectures for Diffusion Transformers and VLA models, grounded in real-world evaluations.
• Resulting policies perform dexterous tasks like box folding and extracting credit cards from wallets.

y1uP4arjzC.text:
• Problem: standard CBFs are myopic, enforcing safety only now, risking future states with no feasible safe control.
• MPC enforces constraints over a horizon but needs costly online optimization every step, limiting real-time use.
• Key idea: BarrierFormer encodes rollout-level CBF constraints into training a learned safe policy.
• A causal transformer outputs residual corrections to a nominal controller and autoregressively predicts future rollouts.
• A barrier critic checks CBF violations along rollouts; a safety teacher supplies barrier-consistent supervision actions.
• Inference maps observation-action history directly to actions, enabling real-time predictive safety without online optimization.
• Beats RL, diffusion, MPC, and transformer baselines on safety, success, and latency; abstract reports no numbers.

o03EddNo6r.text:
• Problem: image policies are pretrained but brittle to shifts; 3D policies are robust but trained from scratch.
• Prior multi-modal policies still encode 3D with from-scratch encoders, keeping this asymmetry.
• Key idea: represent 3D as image-shaped pointmaps so pretrained 2D backbones encode both modalities.
• Method: RGB and pointmap streams fused by a unified diffusion transformer with per-modality modulation.
• Setup: 13 LBM dexterous sim tasks, 5 RoboTwin bimanual tasks, 4 real-world YAM tasks.
• Results: beats strong RGB-only baseline on LBM under distribution shift, and beats π0.5 on RoboTwin and YAM.
• New: unified 2D+3D co-training recipe that brings 2D pretraining priors to 3D manipulation inputs.

PW8egEb2no.text:
• Problem: evidence that diffusion models learn data-manifold geometry comes mostly from images, where true geometry is unknown.
• Key idea: use constrained inverse kinematics, where each constraint's configuration-space manifold has analytically known intrinsic dimension.
• Setup: one conditional diffusion model per robot, 6-DoF UR5 and 7-DoF Franka, across seven constraint families.
• Constraint families span discrete IK branches to continuous self-motion manifolds, giving direct geometric ground truth.
• Result: intrinsic dimension estimated from the score function matches analytical degrees of freedom on both robots.
• Result: linear latent-space interpolation yields solutions staying close to the correct constraint manifold.
• New: constrained IK as a controlled benchmark for probing geometry learned by diffusion models.

d0ltfevDaD.text:
• Problem: world-action models rely on frozen reconstruction-trained encoders, poorly suited for robot control.
• Goal: learn physically-grounded, control-relevant representations for visuo-tactile world-action models.
• Key idea: MDF++ learns multisensory latent representations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone.
• Method: multi-task learning exploits cross-modal correlations, preventing feature collapse from naive joint training.
• Model jointly generates actions and predicts future visual and tactile observations.
• Setup: contact-rich manipulation tasks, including real-world bolt screwing and nut mating.
• Results: outperforms world-action models built on frozen pretrained representations by up to 50%.

ZwUhb2fAWb.text:
• Problem: autonomous drifting needs fast dynamics adaptation as tire temperature, friction, wear, and load transfer shift.
• Model errors vary in scale across state channels and driving regimes, making fixed squared-error objectives brittle.
• Key idea: decoupled profiled-likelihood objective avoids unstable joint training of dynamics parameters and residual variances.
• Method: bidirectional transformer with learned query token maps long state-control histories to vehicle model parameters.
• Single forward pass runs above 100Hz, integrated into an existing MPC framework for online control.
• Setup: full-scale drifting tests on a modified Toyota Supra and Lexus LC500 under varied conditions.
• Results: up to 2.4x lower RMS path-tracking error than hand-tuned physics and neural-network baselines.

GVDQtVONA1.text:
• Problem: real-robot imitation data is costly and gives only one action label per visited state.
• Key idea: crowdsource Multiple Actions per State (MAPS), expanding datasets in "width," not just trajectories.
• Method: web-based 3D interface sends visited robot states to remote annotators, no hardware needed.
• Annotators: non-experts provide alternative valid keyframe goal-pose actions, during or after standard data collection.
• Setup: imitation policies trained on MAPS data across five real-world manipulation tasks.
• Results: going from one to ten actions per state boosts success 35.6% (keypose), 33.0% (trajectory).
• Novelty: software-mediated crowd annotations as a scalable digital layer densifying real-robot supervision and sample efficiency.

sitHOFsi2x.text:
• Problem: monocular RGB human videos are abundant but hard to use for dexterous robot manipulation data.
• Barriers: estimating hand-object interactions and bridging the human-to-robot embodiment gap.
• Key idea: Do as I Do reconstructs and retargets RGB human videos to multi-fingered robot hands.
• Method: reconstruct hand-object interactions, then retarget into real-world executable robot action sequences.
• Setup: works on egocentric and exocentric in-the-wild videos, evaluated on ground-truth datasets and online clips.
• Results: outperforms prior state of the art in hand-object estimation and dexterous trajectory extraction.
• New: yields robot-complete data from disparate videos, plus a playbook for collecting human manipulation data.

TH0fdttVB0.text:
• Problem: assistive robots should adapt how they perform tasks, like applied force, to individual user preferences.
• Language-conditioned policies need costly style labels and give poor fine-grained control over continuous behaviors.
• Key idea: use language to reason over preferred behaviors rather than generate actions directly.
• Method: learn a structured latent space organizing behaviors by differences between the corresponding trajectories.
• A foundation model interprets a user's preference prompt and selects a latent value producing the desired behavior.
• Evaluated in simulation and real-world tactile tasks, such as force-sensitive manipulation like folding laundry or cleaning furniture.
• Results: more precise preference adaptation with significantly fewer labels than language-conditioned policies; abstract gives no numbers.

psNqjklVOK.text:
• Problem: scaling humanoid motion tracking across huge datasets is costly with model-free RL, distillation, or cluster compute.
• Key idea: amortize learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of shared dynamics.
• World model learns from logged rigid-body simulator transitions, co-trained with the tracking policy in one loop.
• Policy gets analytic gradients via backpropagation-through-time over short, fast imagined rollouts.
• 3 hours on one GPU beats a SOTA tracker trained 7 days on 128 GPUs, over 1000x fewer GPU-hours.
• Only 25 failures on 129,514 motions versus baseline's 179; zero failures after 9.8 hours on two GPUs.
• Error stays stable from 1 to 264 motion-hours; policy transfers to real Unitree G1, including acrobatics.

cauTGdv8L0.text:
• Problem: generative behavior cloning policies never check whether candidate actions actually reach task-relevant future states.
• Key idea: couple action generation with an action-conditioned dynamics model predicting future observations.
• Challenge: naive coupling is circular, since futures guide actions yet depend on the actions being generated.
• Method: DAP co-samples actions and futures via flow extrapolation between policy and dynamics flow matching models.
• The two flows correct each other each step, converging to a self-consistent action-future pair.
• Results: best average success on 4 simulated and 3 real tasks, +47.0% sim, +34.0% real relative.
• Robustness: with corrupted future estimates, DAP recovers via iterative refinement, while fixed-future baselines degrade or fail.

VVdYxLGhxH.text:
• Offline RL critics overestimate values at out-of-distribution actions, and these errors cannot be corrected without interaction.
• Prior methods like IQL stay in-distribution but obtain optimism by regressing an upper expectile with asymmetric loss.
• DIQL keeps in-distribution learning but uses a categorical distributional critic to represent action-value distributions.
• Optimistic targets come from simply selecting an upper quantile of the learned value distribution.
• Quantile level adapts per state: well-supported states get more optimism, weakly supported states stay conservative.
• On four OGBench robot task suites, DIQL outperforms state-of-the-art offline RL methods; abstract gives no exact numbers.
• On Robomimic, DIQL naturally extends to offline-to-online fine-tuning for robot manipulation tasks.

8klpl3FXjN.text:
• Problem: physics simulators generalize but lack fidelity; neural world models are expressive but data-hungry and brittle.
• Key idea: residual world model keeps simulator physics priors and learns only the sim-to-real gap.
• Challenge: residual training needs simulator floating base state and contact forces matched to recorded hardware states.
• Method: Unsupervised Actuator Networks learn residual corrections without torque sensing or motion capture.
• New proprioceptive state estimator aligns initial contact forces and base velocities during open-loop hardware trajectory playback.
• Alignment ensures the residual captures true physics discrepancies, not artifacts of inconsistent simulator initialization.
• Results: actuator-feasible policies, more robust sim-to-real transfer, efficient humanoid locomotion, precise end-effector force control; abstract reports no numbers.

S0rbnmOkit.text:
• Problem: material, contents, and softness are hard to infer from vision but revealed through touch.
• Challenge: tactile signals are transient and sparse, making informative events hard to extract and use.
• Key idea: learn task-agnostic object representations from tactile exploration as semantic context for manipulation.
• Method: a token learner selects representative tactile segments from long-horizon exploration sequences.
• Contrastive alignment with descriptive text embeddings yields a latent space capturing multiple physical properties.
• Results: 90% property estimation accuracy on seen and unseen objects.
• Rearrangement, pouring, box opening: 85% average success versus 36% for policies without object context.

hSRtOgnkTM.text:
• Problem: manipulation across the air-water interface, like dishwashing, bathing, water sampling, is hard for robots.
• Water distorts visual cues through turbidity, reflection, and refraction, and it damages electronics.
• Key idea: fuse vision with tactile and immersion-depth signals from a sensorized waterproof gripper.
• Method: imitation learning transformer policies trained with submerged-domain visual augmentations to reduce overfitting.
• Results: full policy reaches 71% mean success versus 41% for the best no-tactile variant.
• Gains are largest under difficult visuals such as floating foam and strong glare.
• New: combines visual robustness with multimodal tactile and depth sensing for submerged manipulation.

zsHXQqYhFn.text:
• Problem: manipulation policies often fail in final millimeters, missing pose offsets, boundaries, and pre-contact alignments.
• Insight: semantically invariant encoders suppress correspondence cues that closed-loop contact-rich control needs.
• Diffusion features offer strong dense correspondence priors but are stochastic, slow, and drift for direct use.
• Robot-DIFT: Manifold Distillation turns noisy diffusion Teacher into deterministic single-pass Student preserving its feature manifold.
• S2-FPN fuses coarse-to-fine Student decoder features into tokens exposing semantics and fine contact detail.
• Beats vision-language, self-supervised, geometry, and diffusion baselines on RoboCasa, LIBERO-10, and real robots; abstract gives no numbers.
• Backbone/readout swaps show S2-FPN unlocks, rather than replaces, the diffusion correspondence prior.

79jC3quhGp.text:
• Problem: human-robot collaboration systems rely on hand-engineered pipelines, limiting scalability and flexibility for new tasks.
• Key idea: end-to-end imitation-learned vision-language-action (VLA) models can support implicit collaborative manipulation.
• Evaluated two state-of-the-art VLAs and characterized key factors affecting real-world collaborative performance.
• New failure mode: demonstration action leakage, where action chunks cross latent task transitions, causing premature assistance.
• Leakage worsens with longer execution horizons, e.g., robot handing over tools before the person is ready.
• Method: inference-time steering suppresses erroneous assistive actions while preserving overall policy performance.
• 16-participant assembly study: steering enables longer horizons, faster collaboration, fewer failures versus shorter-horizon policy.

A9tBpzFsWI.text:
• Problem: deep feature matchers are too computationally expensive for visual localization on edge devices.
• Bottleneck: interleaved intra- and inter-image layers force K full network runs per query, preventing caching.
• Key idea: cacheable matching, deferring inter-image interaction to final layers of existing matchers.
• Method: offline-cacheable Context Blocks for database images; only lightweight Interaction Blocks run online.
• E-SToRE: entropy-guided spatial token reduction and expansion prunes tokens before cross-image interaction.
• Evaluated on HPatches, ScanNet, MegaDepth, and ETH3D benchmarks.
• Results: over 2x lower effective compute; E-SToRE adds 10-14% savings with negligible accuracy loss.

W443fVglzC.text:
• Problem: planetary rovers on steep deformable terrain face slip, sinkage, and sim-to-real gaps from unmodeled wheel-soil effects.
• Constraint: rover operations allow little trial-and-error, so deployment-time adaptation must be highly data-efficient.
• Key idea: TERRA seeks deployment data that exposes task-relevant model errors, then corrects them online.
• Method: adapts a simulation-trained world model using a reward-weighted prediction loss, focusing on performance-relevant errors.
• A learned loss predictor estimates where future relevant errors occur, guiding exploration within MPC.
• Simulation: about 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe out-of-distribution pretraining, beating exploration baselines.
• Real world: ERNEST rover recovers coordinated active-suspension locomotion on a deformable Mars-simulant slope in 3-5 trials.

QLhHHolka7.text:
• Contrastive RL excels at goal-conditioned locomotion but struggles in interaction-rich object manipulation tasks.
• Key insight: contact and grasping cause dynamic mode changes that standard CRL energy functions represent poorly.
• Manipulation is formulated as a piecewise-smooth Markov process with piecewise nonlinear, multi-modal reachability structure.
• Interaction-weighted Resampling (IWR) resamples data before, during, and after interactions to preserve mode boundaries.
• Evaluated on 2D dynamic control, robotic manipulation, and robot air hockey interaction-centric environments.
• IWR improves sample efficiency and performance, averaging 19.8% gains over prior CRL methods in simulation.
• Sim-to-real yields the first real goal-conditioned air hockey agent, raising success from 25% to 60%.

xXnpKl2IgD.text:
• Problem: generating articulated 3D objects requires capturing both geometric diversity and kinematic constraints simultaneously.
• Gap: point cloud generators ignore kinematics; prior articulated methods assume predefined kinematic skeletons.
• Key idea: ArticFlow, flow matching learning an action-controllable velocity field from noise to target point sets.
• Method: latent flow maps noise to shape-prior code; point flow moves points conditioned on action and prior.
• Setup: evaluated on PartNet-Mobility and MuJoCo Menagerie, covering tools, eyeglasses, robotic arms, and quadrupeds.
• Results: one model interpolates novel shapes, handles unseen actions validly, beats per-instance baselines on reconstruction error.
• New: generated point clouds yield functional URDFs in simulation, enabling skeleton-free, simulation-ready asset creation.

hSZ0lT7TCp.text:
• Problem: users lack simple ways to steer VLA robot actions in real time toward their intent.
• Key idea: flow control steers VLA action generation using generic, crude inputs like a keyboard.
• Works out-of-the-box on existing VLAs, with no retraining or fine-tuning required.
• Outputs stay within the VLA's learned expert action distribution, giving high-quality, intent-faithful actions.
• Steering is accurate and responsive, and robust to suboptimal user inputs.
• Users reach significantly higher success rates and faster task completion; the abstract reports no exact numbers.
• New: fine-tuning VLAs on flow-control trajectories improves the autonomous policy itself.

0jY75QYDMn.text:
• Problem: humanoid loco-manipulation VLAs need costly teleoperation demos; sim-trained VLAs have transferred poorly to real humanoids.
• Key idea: LEGS hybrid simulator composites mesh robot and objects over photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting backgrounds.
• Backgrounds reconstructed from handheld scene captures; two-stage color calibration aligns renders to the deployment camera.
• Procedural motion-primitive generator synthesizes labeled demonstrations at scale, with no human teleoperation needed.
• Setup: Unitree G1, three pick-and-place tasks of rising whole-body difficulty, VLAs psi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.6.
• Results: LEGS-only policies match or beat teleop-trained policies in every experiment and outperform mesh-only baselines.
• New: motion decoupled from appearance enables re-rendering for new scenes and objects at over 15x lower cost.

Y6pog6YGIX.text:
• Problem: robots need interaction-relevant physical properties like friction, stiffness, and sinkage from vision before contact.
• Challenge: visually similar regions can behave differently physically; point estimates and semantic classes hide distinct regimes.
• Key idea: Gaussian-mixture posterior over physical parameters, conditioned on continuous visual embeddings instead of semantic classes.
• Method: past interaction estimates become mixture components, retrieved and weighted by embedding similarity to each query region.
• Extras: support-aware fusion with a generative prior for sparse history, plus learned embedding refinement for better retrieval.
• Setup: high-fidelity autonomous racing simulation with unknown low- and high-friction surface regions; the abstract reports no numbers.
• Results: multimodal beliefs, rejects unrelated history, no map discretization, controller-rate speed, improves over repeated laps.

rTX0zr5FjT.text:
• Problem: imitation policies must capture multimodal actions, run in real time, and exploit many sensors.
• Diffusion, flow matching, and IMLE policies each satisfy these requirements only partially.
• Key idea: single-pass multisensory policy trained with a calibrated batch-global RS-IMLE objective.
• New insight: RS-IMLE rejection degenerates at policy-scale batch sizes; calibration restores effective rejection.
• Method: temporal encoder fuses RGB, depth, tactile, audio, proprioception; linear-attention Performer generates actions.
• Real robots (Unitree Go2 with 7-DoF arm, UR5): 10–25 pp over diffusion at 30–50 Hz.
• CALVIN ABCD: about 31 pp over diffusion, 24 pp over flow matching, 20–70x lower jerk.

vVIVf2E7KG.text:
• Problem: high-speed off-road navigation needs dynamics models capturing complex robot-terrain interactions.
• Prior learned models condition on perception too simplistically, ignoring the spatial structure of dynamics.
• Key idea: condition each dynamics prediction on BEV perception features queried around the predicted state.
• Each rollout step uses local geometric and semantic terrain cues at the vehicle's anticipated location.
• New benchmarking approach evaluates dynamics models on challenging off-road datasets collected across all seasons.
• Improves worst-case prediction by 23.8% versus physics-based and learned baselines.
• Hardware tests at 10+ m/s on challenging courses cut maximum cross-track error by 34.9%.

aPosmVaV9y.text:
• Problem: long-horizon manipulation needs memory, but conditioning on full histories causes spurious correlations and worse performance.
• Existing fixes compress history via expensive VLM queries in-the-loop, slowing deployment and adding compute cost.
• Key idea: move VLM reasoning to train-time, learning a lightweight latent memory called the workspace token.
• Method: a VLM labels task-salient current and historical information as supervision targets.
• These targets are distilled into the workspace token using a set-reconstruction decoder loss.
• Setup: token serves as drop-in observation replacement for policies, evaluated in simulation and on real hardware.
• Results: solves memory-intensive tasks without in-loop VLMs; lighter and outperforms baselines (no numbers in abstract).

bqXyS2gKba.text:
• End-to-end driving planners perform well but stay opaque, limiting observability and trust.
• Key idea: apply mechanistic interpretability via Sparse Autoencoders trained on planner internal activations.
• Setup: simple single-camera end-to-end path planning model; SAEs trained on its internal activations.
• Unsupervised clustering of SAE latents recovers driving intent with 98.3% accuracy, aligned with route, speed, braking.
• Counterfactual image edits show features respond to traffic light state and stop sign presence.
• Steering individual SAE latents monotonically changes lateral displacement, curvature, and braking outputs.
• Adapter trained on SAE latents cuts trajectory selection error by 3.44%, beating an adapter without them.

4pwzyVBjXY.text:
• Problem: robots in drifting environments cannot afford full state estimation and replanning at every step.
• Question: given a limited compute and energy budget, when along the horizon should a robot replan?
• Setting: time-varying MDPs with a known bound on how fast transition dynamics drift.
• Method: skip-update scheme with maximum-likelihood transition estimates and finite-horizon policies, reused between updates.
• Theory: dynamic regret bound showing regret growth during skips, tied to TVMDP properties and skip lengths.
• New: an online, regret-guided rule that adaptively allocates the replanning budget, derived directly from the bound.
• Results: beats budgeted baselines on simulated Mars-rover slip navigation and real Crazyflie quadrotor flights; abstract gives no numbers.

bL51SsKShM.text:
• Problem: real-world generalist policy evaluation needs manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites.
• Key idea: ScaleEvals evaluates policies reset-free through continuous autonomous play, without per-rollout human intervention.
• Method: VLM AutoPrompter generates grounded tasks and rubrics; AutoGrader scores progress from multimodal observations.
• Skill tags, difficulty normalization, soft-win Bradley-Terry, and tag-stratified ANOVA yield rankings plus capability diagnostics.
• Setup: five generalist policies evaluated across 1,750 real-world trajectories.
• Results: 3x rollouts per hour per station; AutoGrader agrees with humans 90.7%; rankings correlate 0.92 with manual evaluation.
• New: evaluation as a continuously running system, exposing capability gaps that aggregate success rates hide.

z47bcul4Zk.text:
• Problem: VLA language-to-behavior mapping is brittle; similar instructions can yield drastically different robot behaviors.
• Human instructions and zero-shot language models often fail to reliably steer VLAs toward task success.
• Key idea: interactively search for language sequences that improve closed-loop VLA task performance.
• Method: distill found sequences into a test-time language feedback policy (LFP) plus an improvement-prediction head.
• Conformalized improvement head prevents harmful steering when the LFP would underperform the original instruction.
• Works on any frozen pretrained VLA, with no fine-tuning or access to original training data.
• Results: +24.7% simulation, +65.0% hardware on seen environments, with emergent recovery behaviors.

aZ2Ojk8zxd.text:
• Problem: sparse-reward tabletop manipulation makes RL sample-inefficient and prone to unsafe, off-manifold exploration.
• Key idea: use an action-chunked imitation policy as a local task-space progress estimator, not a controller.
• Method: controller-aware action-to-motion mapping converts predicted chunks into short-horizon end-effector references.
• RL receives dense progress rewards toward these references; the sparse environment reward remains the dominant objective.
• Pretraining: imitation-guided look-ahead relaxes conservative value penalties for actions predicted to make task-space progress.
• Setup: simulation and real-robot experiments, compared against prior RL and IL–RL baselines.
• Results: better early sample efficiency, fewer safety violations, and equal or better final success; abstract reports no numbers.

hWuk4y2AeR.text:
• Problem: long-horizon multi-object rearrangement, where policies suffer compounding errors and must preserve future feasibility.
• Search reasons about future consequences but becomes expensive in high-dimensional continuous action spaces.
• Key idea: DISCO distills long-horizon tree search into a deployable policy-value model over continuous actions.
• Method: progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation; learned policy proposes actions, learned value scores task progress.
• GPU-parallelized simulation enables periodic distillation of MCTS plans, iteratively improving proposals and value estimates.
• New: no simulator-based search needed at test time; the learned policy-value model deploys directly.
• Results: outperforms behavior cloning, RL, and search baselines in simulated and real-world rearrangement; abstract reports no numbers.

5b4j0e21aJ.text:
• Problem: scaling RL to loco-manipulation is bottlenecked by slow, manual dense reward shaping.
• Key idea: use Sample-based MPC in simulation as an automated, rapidly tunable expert demonstrator.
• SMPC generates massive offline datasets that solve the exploration problem for RL.
• Off-policy offline-to-online RL then trains using purely sparse task rewards, no manual reward tuning.
• High-level RL agent pairs with a low-level dynamic stability controller for robust whole-body behavior.
• Learned policies align with true task objectives and surpass the SMPC teacher; abstract reports no numbers.
• Sim-to-real deployment demonstrated on arm-equipped Spot quadruped and Unitree G1 humanoid.

3Ex2nEGqHP.text:
• Problem: shared task-agnostic whole-body controllers break down when composing many learned humanoid skills over long horizons.
• Humanoid Hanoi: new benchmark sequencing pickup, locomotion, and placement to rearrange stacked boxes.
• Key idea: expand the shared WBC's closed-loop coverage instead of specializing it per skill.
• Method: rollout aggregation adds each skill's domain-randomized closed-loop rollouts to shared-WBC training.
• Baselines compared: skill-specific WBC fine-tuning and residual low-level adaptation, both task-agnostic strategies.
• Setup: evaluated in simulation and on Digit V3 hardware; abstract reports no quantitative success rates.
• Finding: rollout aggregation gives best long-horizon robustness; low-level controller consistency matters as much as skills.

2Y1Osh6gOU.text:
• Problem: cable and rope manipulation is hard because linear deformable objects deform in complex ways.
• Prior imitation learning needs thousands of demonstrations per task and cable type, limiting scalability and generalization.
• Key idea: sim-to-real reinforcement learning for multi-stage cable routing using GPU-parallelized deformable cable simulation.
• Training across thousands of parallel simulations helps policies generalize across diverse cable geometries and deformation patterns.
• Deployment: Simulation In the Loop execution, localized RL policies, and robust cable state estimation bridge the gap.
• Real-world results: higher success rates and about 2x shorter cycle times than prior state-of-the-art learning methods.
• Claimed first successful sim-to-real transfer of RL policies for multi-stage cable routing.

RS2INStAhX.text:
• Problem: imaging Earth-like exoplanets needs 10 milliarcsecond resolution and 10^-9 contrast, hard for single telescopes.
• Key idea: recast distributed-aperture telescope phasing as high-dimensional visuomotor optomechanical robot control.
• Method: recurrent visuomotor policies trained with PPO act directly on interferometric focal-plane science images.
• Setup: end-to-end training on the full 45-DOF, fifteen-segment problem proved ineffective.
• Fix: fifteen per-segment three-actuator skill policies, composed at inference into a single 240-step rollout.
• Result: target-conditioned variant suppresses flux in designated dark-hole regions by roughly two orders of magnitude.
• Result: coarse-to-fine variant co-phases two segments from 2 arcsec in median 15 steps, ~10^5x faster.

QHIz2k4E88.text:
• Problem: RL post-training for VLA models needs massive real-world interaction, impractical on physical robots.
• Learned world models as simulators suffer hallucination and long-horizon error accumulation, misleading policy optimization.
• Key idea: WoVR regulates how RL interacts with imperfect imagined dynamics instead of assuming faithful world models.
• Method: controllable action-conditioned video world model improves stability of closed-loop imagined rollouts.
• Keyframe-Initialized Rollouts reduce effective error depth; World Model-Policy co-evolution keeps simulator aligned with policy.
• Results: stable long-horizon imagined rollouts, superior LIBERO performance, consistent real-world gains across multiple robot platforms.
• New: shows world models become practical RL simulators for VLAs when hallucination is explicitly controlled.

FK33gnkKgF.text:
• Problem: representations learned by RL legged locomotion policies are poorly understood, especially their link to hardware motion.
• Key idea: measure effective rank of the policy network Jacobian, conditioned on gait phase rather than globally.
• Phase-conditioned rank reveals representation structures that a single global rank measure completely hides.
• Observation and layer normalization with residual connections add over one extra rank dimension to swing versus stance states.
• This swing-stance rank allocation is mostly absent in vanilla shallow MLPs trained with PPO.
• Proposed diagnostics and recommendations cut joint jitter up to 2x, in simulation and on a physical Spot.
• New insight: how policies distribute capacity across the gait cycle predicts policy health and sim-to-real transfer.

tfC6LMD02z.text:
• Problem: specializing robotics foundation models to new tasks from few demos without eroding broad capabilities.
• Key idea: steer a frozen base policy using the difference between two lightweight proxy policies.
• Reference proxy imitates the frozen base on target-task observations; task proxy starts from it, trained on demos.
• Their difference gives a calibrated velocity-space residual steering the base sampler at every denoising step.
• Authors identify conditions where this residual isolates the task-induced change, and validate them empirically.
• Evaluated on 8 real-world and 4 simulation manipulation tasks using the π0.5 base policy.
• Average +53% absolute success, 0-to-1 gains, beating LoRA, specialists, residual policies, and steering baselines.

El4EDBhqCG.text:
• Problem: natural-language robot instructions are often ambiguous, incomplete, or underspecified, complicating intent inference.
• LLM-driven multi-turn clarification dialogues can introduce systematic failures in interactive robot planning.
• Key idea: frame clarification as Bayesian active learning over grounded Signal Temporal Logic task specifications.
• LLMs propose candidate STL specifications and phrase informative contrasts as natural-language clarification questions.
• Bayesian optimization tracks uncertainty over user intent, selecting queries that maximize information gain.
• The converged STL specification feeds a formal planner, producing verifiable robot trajectories.
• Across four simulated and real domains: higher task satisfaction, fewer clarification rounds, smaller LLMs rival reasoning models.

ODfnFGIIe3.text:
• Problem: navigation under partial observability fails when robots lack informative observations along their planned trajectories.
• Prior work adapts the robot through belief-space planning or extra sensing, which is costly and brittle in observation-poor regions.
• Key idea: augment the environment instead by placing a small budget of fiducial markers where the task needs them.
• Insight: a few well-timed observations along the trajectory stop uncertainty from accumulating where estimation errors would break control.
• Method: SCoDA, a conditional diffusion model learning marker layouts conditioned on map, trajectory, disturbances, and execution profile.
• Its shielded sampler reasons where pose corrections should occur, steering samples toward task-relevant, finite-budget layouts.
• Results: higher reliability and faster completion than strong baselines in simulation and hardware; the abstract reports no numbers.

CSYA6oHdlE.text:
• Deep unfolding speeds up iterative optimizers but has rarely scaled to large semidefinite programs common in robotics.
• Unrolling COSMO causes quadratic-memory linear-solve backprop and unstable PSD projection gradients under repeated eigenvalues.
• A matrix-free implicit differentiation rule uses only matrix-vector products, cutting memory from O(n²) to O(n).
• A Daleckii–Krein Fréchet-derivative backward rule keeps PSD projection gradients well-defined with repeated eigenvalues.
• These enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm-starts for a full-update conic solver.
• Evaluated on covariance steering via SCP, max-cut, Lovász theta, robust estimation, and control SDPs/SOCPs.
• Learned policies beat state-of-the-art solvers, up to 50x faster, with over 30x SCP speedup versus COSMO.

Alu9eLT93i.text:
• Problem: vision-only control faces noisy, occluded perception and shared onboard compute limiting real-time planning horizons.
• Key idea: distill privileged long-horizon MPC into lightweight short-horizon MPC with vision-inferred cost parameters.
• Teacher: full-state, field-of-view-aware multi-trajectory MPC in simulation, guaranteeing the agent stays within view.
• Student: recurrent network maps noisy, occluded perception context to MPC cost parameters, recovering teacher behavior.
• Setup: vision-based autonomous racing, evaluated in simulation and on real hardware using only onboard track perception.
• Results: generalizes to unseen tracks, nears teacher lap times, cuts per-step computation by over 90%.
• Novelty: modular, perception-agnostic student–teacher framework learning MPC objectives online from vision.

ZyLuLA1Tsy.text:
• Problem: VLA models suit field robotics, but edge SWaP-C limits make deployment hard; compressing them is essential.
• Pruning is well studied for LLMs and VLMs but largely unexplored for Vision-Language-Action models.
• Surprising finding: pruning VLAs causes drastic performance drops and more safety violations.
• Spectral analysis reveals structural properties of VLA weights that explain this fragility to pruning.
• GLUESTICK computes a one-time correction by interpolating dense and pruned weights, applied per layer at inference.
• It is training-free, agnostic to the pruning algorithm, and adds minimal overhead while preserving sparsity benefits.
• Results: recovers up to 100% success rate, near-dense safety, saves up to 5.36 GB, 1.75x speedup.

mwJwAQ0CXT.text:
• Problem: mobile multi-robot collaboration is hard; centralized policies scale poorly, decentralized ones need alignment or communication.
• Key idea: pretrained VLA visuomotor priors enable reactive decentralized collaboration from each robot's local observations alone.
• Method: CHORUS adapts a single shared VLA backbone to control diverse, multi-embodiment robot teams.
• Inference: each robot runs an independent CHORUS copy, conditioned on its own observations and robot-identifying prompt.
• Setup: real-world tasks include mobile tape measurement, library book handovers, and laundry basket lifting.
• Results: 64-point gain over decentralized from-scratch models, 40-point better reactivity, beats centralized baselines.
• What's new: one policy for all robots, no per-robot policies or inter-robot communication at inference.

GqqwqejrTq.text:
• Problem: home mobile manipulators treat each task as new, repeating failures across rooms and visits.
• Gap: scene representations omit interaction knowledge, video buffers bloat, VLM planners never persistently update knowledge.
• Key idea: "learning from doing," memory that is spatially grounded, queryable, interaction-updatable, and visually fine-grained.
• Method: compact 3D scene graph linked to learned interaction-derived properties and keyframes preserving visual detail.
• Use: task planner avoids repeated failures, reuses object locations, recovers visual context for long-horizon decisions.
• Setup: evaluated on multiple tasks in simulation and on a real mobile manipulator against representative baselines.
• Results: persistent interaction-grounded memory significantly improves long-horizon success; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

DEPCm83K5I.text:
• Problem: transferring abundant human demonstrations into robot dexterous manipulation policies remains challenging.
• CHORD: RL framework for long-horizon manipulation of rigid and articulated objects guided by human demonstrations.
• Key idea: object-centric contact wrench space guidance compares human and robot motions via forces induced on objects.
• Similarity is measured by induced instantaneous object motions, making RL more scalable for contact-rich manipulation.
• New benchmark: 4739 bimanual dexterous tasks built from motion-capture datasets and reconstructed in-house videos.
• Results: 82.12% average success on 1831 benchmark tasks; 90.77% on whole-body manipulation from hand-only demos.
• Generalizes from third-person demonstrations; policies transfer to real robots in open-loop and closed-loop settings.

802PZFmFGd.text:
• Problem: robot control tasks vary in sensing and compute demands, yet controllers allocate resources for worst-case phases.
• Mode-switching controllers save resources but traditionally require laborious, expert-driven design for every new task.
• Key idea: use LLMs to automatically synthesize efficient mode-switching control architectures, called LEMCA.
• Method: controller designs are interpretable programs, iteratively refined by LLMs within an evolutionary search loop.
• LLMs edit modes, sensory-compute allocations, and transitions; fitness comes from MSC-compatible RL synthesis in simulation.
• Results: across diverse control benchmarks, LEMCA designs consistently surpass the Pareto frontier of monolithic controllers.
• What's new: automated, low-effort path to resource-efficient controllers by reclaiming waste during easy task phases.

8T3FxlYk9K.text:
• Problem: diffusion/transformer dexterity policies are data-hungry, compute-heavy, and unreliable for multi-fingered hands.
• Reactive policies with fixed-horizon action chunking force a rigid trade-off between temporal coherence and reactivity.
• Key idea: Unified Behavioral Models treat skills as coupled dynamical systems of visual flow and action flow.
• Unlike world models, UBMs act as pseudo planners, predicting full-horizon robot behavior and imagined visual flow.
• Method: Koopman-UBM uses a structured latent linear system, making it efficient and temporally coherent by construction.
• Online replanning triggers automatically when predicted and observed visual flow diverge beyond a threshold.
• Across 7 simulated and 4 real tasks, matches or beats baselines with faster inference and occlusion robustness.

Kakzp9Lr9V.text:
• Problem: deformable objects have high-dimensional, partially observable states and long-horizon, topology-changing dynamics with many valid modes
• Key idea: in-context imitation learning lets one human demonstration specify the desired folding mode
• No gradient updates at test time; policy infers spatial execution and step ordering directly from the demonstration
• Method stage 1: temporal contrastive pretraining learns deformation-aware visual representations of cloth state
• Method stage 2: demonstration-conditioned flow-matching transformer policy predicts actions executing the intended manipulation mode
• Setup: trained entirely in simulation, then transferred zero-shot to real robots without real data or finetuning
• New: one-shot generalization across diverse folding modes; abstract reports no numbers, see instant-fold.github.io

xombt7ofur.text:
• Problem: RGB-only video world models produce rollouts that look right per frame but lack consistent 3D geometry.
• Key idea: add large-scale 3D supervision without disturbing strong pretrained video diffusion priors.
• Calibration pipeline: learned stereo depth plus joint factor graph pooling episodes per robot for shared kinematics.
• DROID-3D: recalibrated DROID with dense metric depth, under 0.7px reprojection error on 90% of episodes.
• DepthWorld: Stable Video Diffusion world model jointly predicting multi-view RGB and depth via spatial latent tiling.
• Pretrained VAE stays unchanged, so depth is absorbed without retraining the video autoencoder.
• Depth supervision boosts RGB prediction by +1.48 dB PSNR over an equal-budget RGB-only baseline.

OJkazbkLtE.text:
• Problem: demonstrations show robots how to act, not why, so robots misjudge which task features matter.
• Misaligned feature representations cause wrong behaviors; language suits semantically defined features better than demonstrations.
• Prior language-based editing only adds features, yielding over-specified or narrow feature sets, especially across sequential edits.
• FLEX uses language models to iteratively refine robot feature representations from natural language corrections.
• Three operations: Add missing features, Generalize overly specific features, Mask irrelevant features.
• Evaluated on 2D navigation, 7-DoF Franka tabletop manipulation, and a real-world study with naturalistic human corrections.
• Results: all three operations needed; FLEX achieves higher normalized reward with compact, transferable representations (abstract gives no exact numbers).

zDGliNPeBL.text:
• Problem: large world models capture hard-to-simulate dynamics but are too costly to differentiate for RL.
• Key idea: decouple forward simulation from gradient computation using coupled global and local world models.
• Method: large world model rolls out accurate trajectories; lightweight latent surrogate approximates local dynamics for gradients.
• This yields a novel decoupled first-order gradient (FoG) method for efficient first-order policy optimization.
• Setup: real-world robotic tasks of increasing complexity, from PushT to ego-centric object manipulation and grasping.
• Results: significantly better sample efficiency than PPO on real-world PushT, similar trends on harder tasks, zero-shot deployment.
• New: policies trained entirely inside data-driven world models in image space, without hand-crafted physics simulators.

nBwRDRUdMc.text:
• Problem: real-world paths get blocked by everyday clutter like chairs and toys, so robots must clear them.
• Prior interactive navigation relies on heavy simulation training or per-scenario instructions on which objects to handle.
• Such methods generalize poorly to novel objects, new environments, and context, like fragile versus empty carts.
• New formulation: open-world interactive navigation, where robots must decide how to handle arbitrary obstacles.
• Key idea: zero-shot framework using vision-language models for explicit affordance reasoning before task planning.
• Method: the VLM decides whether to push, pick up, or avoid each object, then produces a high-level plan.
• Results: on a real mobile manipulator indoors and outdoors, it substantially outperforms baselines without task-specific training.

LwMNsyCnCk.text:
• Problem: language-conditioned navigation policies and reasoning usually need costly human language and reasoning annotations.
• Key idea: Action Self-Distillation (ASD) learns language-conditioned navigation reasoning without any human labels.
• One open-source VLM serves as both self-teacher and student policy, leveraging its world knowledge.
• Teacher sees privileged trajectory feedback, inferring the navigation goal plus goal-oriented reasoning.
• Student uses onboard observations only, predicting ego-frame trajectories plus scene semantics, plan, and reasoning.
• Tested on 13 real-world tasks: +30% success indoors, +30% multi-stage, 95% outdoors versus strongest baseline.
• New: privileged trajectory feedback enables scalable self-distillation for generalist navigation without human annotations.

jQAOksG9Bd.text:
• Problem: sequential robot skill learning without past trajectories, task losses, or task-specific heads, routing, adapters.
• Identifies skill-coupling collapse: individual skills still succeed, but reliability across related skills deteriorates.
• Key idea: Sleeping Robots, a wake-sleep framework learning new skills awake, consolidating the shared policy offline asleep.
• Memories: frozen critics with state buffers for RL; frozen actor snapshots with observation buffers for imitation.
• Sleep consolidation combines surrogate-objective gradients via Nash bargaining, plus adaptive anchoring and local excitability for stability.
• Meta-World MT5: 64% higher average success, 2.0x pairwise reliability over strongest non-oracle baseline.
• SurgicAI: better average success and backward transfer than continual imitation baselines; competitive pairwise reliability.

RExYYVsLbT.text:
• Problem: robot navigation planning needs scene geometry and traversability; classic methods depend on accurate 3D occupancy maps.
• Gap: learned costs overfit scene layout or lack geometry, and mostly give uninformative image-level scalar costs.
• Key idea: Plann3r predicts 3D-grounded pixel-level planning costs as geodesic distances to any arbitrary subgoal pixel.
• Works on any image set, giving dense costmaps instead of a single scalar per image.
• VGGT-Nav, offline phase: Plann3r iteratively generates subgoals and global costmaps for reference images during mapping.
• VGGT-Nav, execution phase: Plann3r localizes and plans locally, producing costmaps that condition a learned control policy.
• Results: abstract reports large gains over planning and navigation baselines, without numbers; real-world demos show sim-to-real transfer.

KHjJ1z5m4y.text:
• Problem: world action models predict actions and future states, but full-frame video prediction is computationally expensive.
• Question: what minimal state representation keeps the planning and supervision benefits of future prediction?
• Key idea: BoxWAM replaces dense future frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant objects.
• Method: the model imagines object-centric future motion, capturing key physical changes caused by robot actions.
• Setup: evaluated on robotic manipulation tasks against video-based world action models; the abstract omits specific benchmarks.
• Results: substantially lower training and inference cost with improved action prediction; the abstract reports no numbers.
• What's new: compact object-centric states as an efficient alternative to video-based world action modeling.

xyRbF93MWh.text:
• Problem: dynamic navigation relies on obstacle predictions with uncertain, non-stationary errors causing rare safety-critical failures.
• Gap: CBF safety filters reject unsafe controls but cannot tell when the planning mode itself becomes unsafe.
• Key idea: CERT-Replan uses calibrated barrier risk as an early-warning signal that triggers replanning.
• Method: online conformal calibration of horizon-indexed prediction residuals yields uncertainty radii for obstacle safety margins.
• A one-step filter guards the next control; CVaR of predicted barrier violations monitors the whole MPC rollout.
• When risk exceeds budget, it switches speed profile, corridor, or homotopy class instead of patching the plan.
• Results: 83.3% fewer collisions, 32.4% fewer filter interventions versus filter-only baseline; hardware-in-the-loop shows onboard feasibility.

PAX622BSf6.text:
• Problem: rearrangement plans must satisfy symbolic goals and geometric feasibility, which symbolic models rarely capture.
• Key idea: learn hidden geometric action preconditions from motion-policy feedback instead of hand-encoding them.
• Method: relational graph neural network heuristic learned over a simple symbolic abstraction, supervised by a motion policy.
• Search: learned heuristic guides greedy best-first search to find feasible rearrangement plans.
• Generalization: transfers out-of-distribution to more objects, longer plans, and new object arrangements.
• Results: about 10x fewer motion policy queries than classical heuristic search and TAMP baselines.
• What's new: same architecture, training recipe, and search adapt across multiple robotic rearrangement domains.

MjpidVjNMS.text:
• Articulated objects like doors, bolts, and drawers impose kinematic constraints that neural policies often violate during manipulation.
• Impedance control helps, but choosing task-appropriate 6x6 impedance gains for learned robot policies remains difficult.
• Key idea: use a generative policy's sampling diversity to infer feasible and constrained end-effector twist subspaces.
• PCA on twists from trajectories sampled for one observation yields the feasible subspace and shapes the impedance gains.
• Gains are estimated once and held fixed; configuration-dependent cases use a larger, configuration-independent subspace.
• Tested on simulated and real-world single- and multi-DoF articulated objects against isotropic impedance control.
• Consistently reduces constraint-violating contact loads while maintaining task execution; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

mG3eBTsBiG.text:
• Problem: existing VLA action tokenizers optimize reconstruction, giving codes with weak semantic supervision for the backbone.
• Key idea: treat action tokenization as semantic interface learning between multimodal reasoning and executable robot control.
• Method: lightweight encoder, Semantic Residual Quantization (SRQ), and decoder, shared across diverse robotic arm embodiments.
• SRQ: first level learns coarse motion intent via Masked Action Modeling; deeper levels preserve fine-grained residual details.
• Alignment: contrastive alignment to a pretrained foundation model, plus next-frame vision-language feature prediction.
• Setup: pretrained on 2.4M trajectories (2.0B frames); frozen tokenizer supervises a mixed discrete-continuous VLA.
• Results: top real-world aggregate, strong RoboTwin 2.0; beats FAST by +13.5% grounding, +8.25 long-horizon.

Afq9dTKP09.text:
• Problem: ROI visual bottlenecks aid data-efficient visuomotor learning but usually need external labels like gaze or affordances.
• Label-free action-derived crops fix event timing, proxy points, and scale, misaligning when evidence lies elsewhere.
• Key idea: Seeker learns task- and state-conditioned attention purely from action supervision, no spatial labels.
• Method: iteratively updates a query over frozen DINO features, producing progression-aware ROIs.
• Learned ROI drives RGB cropping, mask-guided background augmentation, and point-cloud filtering.
• Real robots: in-domain success rises from 48.3% to 76.7% versus the best baseline.
• Under lighting/background shifts, success improves from 20.0% to 60.0%, also beating baselines in simulation.

60tPXLIFyM.text:
• Problem: multi-robot control in cluttered spaces faces robot-robot collisions, obstacle collisions, and unreachable motions.
• Failures can arise at task or motion level, so both must be optimized jointly.
• Challenges: complex low-level trajectory parameterization and ambiguous credit assignment between planning levels.
• Key idea: hybrid bi-level framework using waypoints as a simple, expressive motion trajectory representation.
• Method: curriculum training with modified RLVR propagating motion-feasibility feedback from motion planner to task planner.
• Setup: BoxNet3D-Obs benchmark with dense obstacles and up to nine robots.
• Results: consistently higher task success than motion-agnostic and VLA-based baselines; abstract reports no exact figures.

QBAA8svAIK.text:
• Problem: federated RL struggles when clients have heterogeneous environments and mismatched data distributions.
• Existing FRL methods mainly synchronize policy or value parameters, ignoring distributional mismatch across clients.
• Key idea: diffusion priors act as behavior models, giving personalized, data-supported distributions for local policies.
• Instead of averaging policies, Optimal-Transport Mixture-of-Experts aggregates diffusion priors, preserving diverse behavior modes.
• A DICE value baseline provides low-variance, return-aware guidance for local policy improvement.
• Results: beats representative FRL methods in average returns, final-round performance, and worst-round robustness; abstract gives no numbers.
• Novelty: aggregation in distribution space, remaining stable as client heterogeneity increases.

b2gSINMX3R.text:
• Problem: fusing multiple heterogeneous tactile sensors for manipulation learning remains largely unexplored.
• Key idea: MiTaS combines tactile sensors operating at different temporal resolutions for contact-rich manipulation.
• Method: modality-specific convolutional stems plus transformer fusion of RGB camera, GelSight Mini, and event-based Evetac.
• The fused multi-sensor representation conditions a flow-matching imitation learning policy.
• Setup: evaluated on five contact-rich manipulation tasks against vision-only and visuo-tactile baselines.
• Results: MiTaS averages 80% success versus 31% vision-only and 54% visuo-tactile baselines.
• New: multi-tactile co-training boosts visuo-tactile policies over 10% on some tasks, even without Evetac at test time.

9I9DPyr2f9.text:
• Problem: unclear whether natural-language reasoning helps VLMs steer noisy low-level policies in long-horizon robotic manipulation.
• Key idea: train VLMs to reason in free-form language as test-time compute guiding low-level action policies.
• Method R³, step 1: mid-train an off-the-shelf VLM on expert-generated reasoning traces to set reasoning style.
• Method R³, step 2: refine the reasoner with single-step rubric-based RL using offline action data.
• Setup: evaluated on Language Table, a controlled testbed for studying robotic reasoning and manipulation.
• Results: R³ improves exploration and generalization to unseen tasks; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• What's new: free-form reasoning drives actions at test time, unlike prior auxiliary-supervision structured traces.

nXfwmrzXzz.text:
• Problem: zero-shot VLMs lack knowledge of personal routines, so proactive robots default to inaction.
• Insight: daily routines repeat, so a few interactions reveal stable user-specific patterns for proactive help.
• Method: System 1-2 framework, VLM task predictor reads memory plus observation, VLA executes actions.
• Procedural Assistance Memory: finite-state machine over activity phases, per-state rules, and event-driven transitions.
• Reflection VLM revises memory from each day's interaction trace, with no weight updates or retraining.
• Setup: multi-day desk assistance with six pick-and-place tasks; memory-free baselines achieve near-zero proactive recall.
• Results: best precision, recall, and F1; first-fire delay drops from ~5s to 1s; FSM drives gains.

l8hOz8loVg.text:
• Problem: humanoid whole-body controllers ignore manipulated objects, approximating payloads with randomized end-effector force disturbances.
• Force-disturbance proxies miss distributed multi-contact wrenches across arms and torso, failing near payload limits.
• Key idea: train the low-level controller as an object-aware motion prior, with the object physically simulated.
• Single policy imitates retargeted MoCap primitives, yielding human-like motion behind a compact task-space command interface.
