• Reference-free high-level policy, with actions bounded to the low-level data envelope, prevents off-distribution queries.
• Setup: Unitree G1 humanoid performing long-horizon, multi-stage bimanual box pick-and-place.
• Results: one policy generalizes across box masses, sizes, start and goal poses, and recovers from drops.

FVPhDDjumI.text:
• Problem: long-horizon visual manipulation planning needs action-relevant facts, not high-dimensional image details.
• Setting: robot learns only from image transitions: current image, executed high-level action, resulting image.
• Test task: given start and goal images, output a high-level action sequence reaching the goal.
• Key idea: learn image-grounded STRIPS-style world models with sparse preconditions and add/delete effects.
• Method: induce abstract transition graph, learn latent binary predicates, one grounded propositional operator per action.
• Learned predicates are distilled into a visual encoder, enabling classical planning from novel images.
• Results: higher image-to-plan success than visual rollout, latent graph-search and latent-symbolic baselines; abstract gives no numbers.

6T2ebANGy5.text:
• Generalist robot methods like VLAs, offline learning, and RL need huge, diverse datasets, increasingly generated by world models.
• Key claim: world models open a stealthy data-poisoning entry point into the robot learning supply chain.
• Attack hides malicious prompts or compromising transition dynamics inside visibly safe teleoperated datasets.
• The payload stays dormant until fed through a world model, which then generates dangerous synthetic trajectories.
• Evaluated against state-of-the-art action-conditioned and text-conditioned world models, with poisoning shown propagating downstream.
• Results show unsafe or compromised VLA and RL policies despite training on seemingly safe ground-truth data.
• New threat model: unlike classic poisoning, no dangerous trajectories appear in the shared dataset itself.

yeAKwjw5Xa.text:
• Problem: VLA models generalize well but ignore physical contact, failing on force-, texture-, and slip-sensitive tasks.
• Prior tactile approaches use low-dimensional signals, missing high-resolution contact dynamics needed for manipulation.
• Key idea: DreamTacVLA grounds VLAs in contact physics by learning to predict future tactile states.
• Hierarchical perception fuses high-resolution tactile images, wrist-camera local views, and third-person global views.
• Hierarchical Spatial Alignment loss aligns tactile tokens with matching regions in wrist and third-person images.
• Tactile world model finetuning; hybrid digital-twin plus real-world dataset addresses tactile data scarcity and sensor wear.
• Outperforms state-of-the-art VLA baselines on contact-rich tasks, reaching up to 95% success.

o4lQTMHyTc.text:
• Open-world delivery needs mobile manipulators to follow free-form instructions and handle novel objects.
• Dual-system approaches ground language into visual prompts, but low-level controllers break under noise, dynamics, and contact.
• Key idea: use a pretrained flow-matching VLA as the controller, steered by grounded spatial cues.
• The VLA provides a strong manipulation prior; the cue supplies the target information for novel language-object mappings.
• A lightweight adapter is contrastively trained for salient, spatially discriminative cue representations.
• The adapter then predicts a diagonal affine transform over generated action chunks to steer toward the cued target.
• Across tabletop and mobile-base settings, it achieves up to nearly 2x task success with negligible inference overhead.

GRyPwVAxpq.text:
• Problem: benchmarks test physical reasoning or policy execution separately, never the integrated "intuitive manipulation" humans use.
• Intuitive manipulation: combining physical understanding, reasoning, and motor control to adapt quickly to new scenes and rules.
• IMBench evaluates perception, physical reasoning, action generation, and iterative execution as one integrated capability.
• Tasks require inferring physical structure and producing feasible action sequences under explicit constraints.
• Covers contact-rich manipulation, tool use, and multi-stage dependencies: 35 tasks, 14K filtered trajectories, scalable scenario generation.
• Results: VLMs show partial physical reasoning but fail to produce executable plans.
• SOTA VLAs struggle with task constraints and cross-scenario generalization, exposing a missing axis in foundation models.

h26AmTGnfu.text:
• Problem: RL for manipulation is sample-inefficient; random exploration wastes most training on free-space motion, not contact.
• Gap: Disagreement or uncertainty-based curiosity often chases irrelevant transitions like erratic motions and interactions.
• Key idea: Tactile feedback is a natural exploration signal, so curiosity should be anchored to touch.
• Method: TacEx decomposes model epistemic uncertainty across sensory modalities and directs curiosity toward the tactile channel.
• Result: Without prior knowledge or external rewards, the robot discovers contact dynamics, learning to manipulate and grasp objects.
• Result: The interaction-dense data from tactile curiosity gives strong zero-shot performance on downstream optimization tasks (abstract reports no numbers).
• New: TacEx post-trains VLAs pre-trained without touch, substantially improving downstream performance while staying highly sample-efficient.

qEOv7MuWIx.text:
• Problem: high-speed off-road MPC needs precise vehicle dynamics models that stay robust as terrain changes.
• Specializing generalist forward kino-dynamic models needs much real data and often overfits to terrains or regimes.
• OptCar fine-tunes a generalist model with limited real data plus synthetic rollouts from terrain-specific system identification.
• A history-conditioned adaptation module encodes recent state-action observations into a dynamics context token.
• Evaluated in closed-loop MPC at 6 m/s across three terrains and an out-of-distribution cart-pulling task.
• Cuts 6 m/s tracking error about 55% versus fine-tuned AnyCar on vegetation/dirt; most accurate with unseen cart payload.
• With 5 real minutes per terrain, matches a 30-minute road specialist on road, far better off-road.

LqUR3gxKdH.text:
• Problem: simulators' sim-to-real visual gap corrupts policy perception, undermining closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end driving policies.
• Key idea: generative simulation should preserve policy-relevant scene features, not just achieve photo-realism.
• Method: simulator-grounded autoregressive video model distilled from a large pretrained video model via traffic-scenario guidance.
• It varies visual appearance while preserving scenario layout and temporal consistency of dynamic objects.
• New metric FDπ^k: Fréchet distance over scene-context features from public E2E policies, since FID misranks fidelity.
• Results: 1.6x better FDπ^k than strongest prior closed-loop simulator on nuScenes, 4.7x on NAVSIM.
• Navhard-CL benchmark makes NAVSIM interactive with adversarial agents and weather, exposing overlooked policy failures.

FP3mCkMV24.text:
• Problem: humanoid robots playing ball sports struggle to combine professional motion styles with strong task performance.
• AdaPT: an Adaptive motion Planning and Tracking framework that learns tennis serving and rally styles from broadcast videos.
• Hierarchy: a planner generates stylistic kinematic motions, and a tracker executes them with minimal impact on planning.
• Sim-to-real gap: real-robot tracking degrades, autoregressive planning overlooks this, and noisy perception compounds the errors.
• Adaptation: the tracker learns randomized motion speeds, and a learned motion-speed adapter conditions the planner.
• Results: simulation and real-world experiments show professional styles and task performance, but the abstract reports no numbers.
• Novelty: speed-adaptive planning and tracking that bridges the sim-to-real gap for stylistic humanoid tennis from videos.

NZrwlgnR4X.text:
• Problem: fixed planner-to-policy interfaces fail when contacts, balance, or disturbances change faster than high-level updates.
• Formulates "policy orchestration": runtime selection of a feasible policy-goal pair that tracks the planner target.
• Key idea EPO: each goal-conditioned policy learns a composite energy, low energy meaning feasible, accurate goals.
• At runtime, EPO refines each policy's goal, then executes the lowest-energy policy-goal pair.
• Modular: new policies need only their own energy model, without retraining existing policies or a scheduler.
• Simulation: improves the precision-robustness trade-off; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Sim-to-real: same frozen policies and energy models deployed on real humanoid loco-manipulation tasks.

z5Mgc1GGjP.text:
• Problem: real-world RL fine-tuning of VLAs overfits to specific scenes, sacrificing the generality from pretraining.
• Simulation offers diverse scenes, but hand-designing them is costly and labor-intensive.
• Key idea: use 3D world generative models plus a language-driven scene designer to create training worlds.
• Method: generate hundreds of diverse interactive scenes with unique objects and backgrounds for parallel RL.
• Simulation: RL from imitation baseline lifts success from 9.7% to 79.8%, with 1.25x faster task completion.
• Real world: generated scenes plus domain randomization raise success from 21.7% to 75%, 1.13x speedup.
• Ablation: greater scene diversity directly improves zero-shot generalization, showing value of effectively unlimited generated data.

acslhrig33.text:
• Problem: likelihood-based policy gradients need differentiable action likelihoods, limiting robot policies to simple distributions like Gaussians.
• Key idea: use flow matching policy gradients, which bypass likelihood computation, to train more expressive flow-based control policies.
• Method: an improved flow policy gradient objective making the framework practical for training from scratch and fine-tuning.
• Setup: evaluated on legged locomotion, humanoid motion tracking, and manipulation tasks, plus ablations on training dynamics.
• Results: succeeds across all task families, with robust sim-to-real transfer demonstrated on two humanoid robots.
• Finding: from scratch, policies exploit the flow representation for exploration; fine-tuning is more robust than baselines.
• What's new: first practical demonstration of likelihood-free flow policy gradients for real-world robot control.

EsZGt1eIZr.text:
• Problem: end-to-end driving models trained offline on human demos suffer compounding errors and long-tail brittleness.
• Key idea: train end-to-end driving policies via large-scale self-play directly from pixels in simulation.
• Gigapixel: batched simulator rendering simplified bounding-box worlds in perspective view at 50k agent steps per second.
• Self-play DAgger: pixel policies learn via on-policy distillation from a privileged RL teacher, avoiding sample-inefficient pixel RL.
• Sim-to-real: lightweight perception adaptation transfers self-play policies to real-world sensor data.
• Results: competitive performance on HUGSIM and NAVSIM-v2 without any human trajectory supervision.
• New: first scalable pixel-based self-play for driving, with performance gains proportional to self-play training scale.

9ih6YlxhI5.text:
• Flow-based action-chunking policies incur generation latency, causing mismatches at chunk boundaries during asynchronous real-time execution.
• Existing fixes steer the generation process toward the already-executed prefix, modifying the sampling trajectory.
• Key idea: choose the right initial noise so the unmodified flow ODE naturally produces a prefix-consistent chunk.
• Reframes asynchronous inference as a noise selection problem rather than a trajectory steering problem.
• PAINT finds this noise via backward Euler inversion, then builds the final chunk with a repainting rule.
• Training-free: no gradients, retraining, or policy modification required; works with existing flow policies.
• Improves consistency and task success on 12 simulated benchmarks and 6 real single-arm, bimanual, and humanoid tasks.

kGGI0115Rg.text:
• Problem: generative dynamics models enable robot planning, but safe deployment needs detection of policy-induced out-of-distribution transitions.
• Gap: existing methods treat learned dynamics as fixed and attach post hoc support surrogates for OOD detection.
• Failure mode: dynamics locally insensitive to actions make unsupported actions look like demonstrated transitions, hiding real errors.
• Key idea: support-conditioned control-sensitivity regularization shapes the learned dynamics themselves, not just the OOD detector.
• Method: promotes sensitive local response to control changes in high-support training regions, limiting unstable extrapolation elsewhere.
• Setup: vision-based obstacle avoidance, manipulation, and real-robot navigation experiments with closed-loop planning.
• Results: improved OOD detection and safer closed-loop planning; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

VnF3D7ia9Y.text:
• Problem: robot-human handovers must respect task semantics, e.g., offering a knife handle-first for safety and ergonomics.
• Gap: prior affordance-based methods skip predicting explicit, task-specific human hand poses for using objects.
• Challenge: objects support multiple uses, like a claw hammer for striking or pulling nails, requiring variability modeling.
• Key idea: GENESIS-Handover uses VLM image generation to produce diverse task-specific hand-object interaction hypotheses.
• Method: hypotheses are matched in real time to the observed human hand pose, selecting the best handover configuration.
• Setup: interaction proposal module evaluated standalone, then full system deployed on a mobile manipulator.
• Results: in a 12-participant, five task-object study, 83.3% judged its task understanding better than prior state of the art.

A1Wg3RqdsR.text:
• Problem: object navigation in unseen indoor scenes demands semantic search under partial observability with efficient VLM use.
• Challenge: dense VLM control is costly, while symbolic memories disconnect reasoning from raw visual evidence.
• Key idea: Points of Interest (PoIs), sparse decision units pairing executable waypoints with raw egocentric observations.
• Method: VLM selects among frontiers, suspected targets, stairs, and floor summaries; low-level planners handle continuous motion.
• New: verifiable PoI decisions enable an RLVR pipeline that improves local VLMs without manual Chain-of-Thought labels.
• Results: state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on Habitat ObjectNav; abstract gives no specific numbers.
• Also scales with model capacity, transfers to Active Embodied QA via prompts, and runs robustly on real robots.

1zWj66605w.text:
• Problem: social navigation needs human-level reasoning, but VLM end-to-end planners are unpredictable black boxes.
• Existing VLM instruction-following navigation methods are not designed for fully autonomous real-world deployment.
• Key idea: translate VLM social reasoning into an interpretable vision-language costmap instead of direct planning decisions.
• Method: VLM evaluates traversable regions and social agents from open-set perception, encoding social context as costs.
• Robustness: VLM semantically verifies upstream tracking; high-frequency safety check guards against latency before trajectory generation.
• Results: real-world experiments show safe, efficient, socially compliant navigation in unstructured environments; abstract reports no numbers.
• What's new: a framework that both grounds abstract social reasoning and guards safe deployment; code to be released.

kB0KO1Wife.text:
• Problem: World Action Models use large generative architectures, causing high training cost and slow closed-loop inference.
• Key idea: Light-WAM keeps future-video co-training benefits while using a compact, efficient architecture for manipulation.
• Method: compact video backbone with future-video supervision in a downsampled latent space, cutting co-training cost.
• StateFusionActionExpert fuses adapted multi-layer backbone states via learned-query pooling, predicting action chunks in one pass.
• Setup: evaluated on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 multi-task benchmarks with only 0.44B trainable parameters.
• Results: strong LIBERO performance, usable RoboTwin 2.0 multi-task performance, 72.03ms latency, 4.1GiB peak GPU memory.
• What's new: replaces heavy generative action experts with a lightweight single-pass decoder, also improving training throughput.

wKRawikMuG.text:
• Problem: VLAs rely mostly on vision, missing physical feedback essential for contact-rich real-world manipulation.
• Gap: prior sensory-augmented VLAs use one physical signal, ignoring complementary heterogeneous feedback.
• Key idea: MoSS, a modular sensory stream framework that adapts pretrained VLAs to multiple physical signals.
• Method: decoupled modality streams feed tactile, force, and torque into the action stream via joint cross-modal self-attention.
• Training: two-stage scheme freezes pretrained VLA weights early, then integrates new modalities stably.
• Auxiliary task: predicting future physical signals helps capture contact interaction dynamics.
• Results: real-world experiments show combined signals give synergistic gains; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

AO1shrWa8H.text:
• Problem: generative robot policies start from observation-independent Gaussian noise; source distribution choice is underexplored.
• Key idea: LeaP, a learnable proprioception-conditioned diagonal Gaussian source prior over action chunks.
• Method: lightweight MLP predicts mean and state-adaptive variance; generator architecture and solver stay unchanged.
• Intuition: informed yet stochastic start lets the generator refine actions instead of transporting uninformed noise.
• Setup: 15 RoboTwin manipulation tasks plus real-world deployment, compared against four representative baselines.
• Results: 81.6% average success, beating baselines by 6.5 to 25.5 points, with fewer parameters, faster convergence.
• New: source distribution is a reusable design axis, improving both flow-matching and diffusion-bridge generators.

ZDnuAR0GMn.text:
• Problem: robot learning needs dense, instruction-conditioned progress feedback, but labels, demos, or trained reward models are costly.
• Key idea: read pretrained video-language model token probabilities instead of asking it to generate numeric progress.
• Method: given video prefix and instruction, score likelihood the task is completed as a dense reward.
• Training-free: no reward-model training, task-specific demonstrations, or manually annotated progress labels required.
• Setup: new ManiRewardBench with 130+ real manipulation tasks, four robot platforms, plus Open X-Embodiment datasets.
• Results: beats prior training-free VLM rewards on open-source models, competitive with trained reward models on progress metrics.
• Reward tracks instructions, not just prefix position; enables success detection and reward-weighted behavior cloning.

74gh4jCB2a.text:
• Robot learning is bottlenecked by hand-designed rewards, simulation modeling, or action supervision like teleoperation.
• Goal: learn manipulation purely from task observations such as video, via Inverse RL from Observation (IRLfO).
• IRLfO has remained impractical for real robots due to the hard setting and RL method limitations.
• Key idea: online world modeling makes real-world IRLfO feasible; the proposed method is called MPAIL2.
• Setup: real-world visual manipulation learned from scratch, using observations only, without rewards or action labels.
• Pick-and-place reaches 82% success in under 40 minutes, versus 0% for RL and 12% for BC.
• New: first real-world IRL for visual manipulation from scratch, with positive online transfer across tasks.

awVlNORXDS.text:
• Problem: inertial-only preintegration in neural inertial odometry is sensitive to IMU bias and noise uncertainty.
• Key idea: likelihood maximization using accurate trajectory observations as privileged supervision during training.
• Jointly learns IMU bias dynamics via neural ODE plus gyroscope and accelerometer noise covariances.
• Exploits sparse negative log-likelihood structure; noise-parameter gradients computed by forward differentiation.
• Double-adjoint scheme couples discrete invariant-error adjoint with continuous-time adjoint for memory-efficient optimization.
• Validated on EuRoC with improved performance; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Underwater robot experiments show robustness under intermittent lighting failures and visual degradation.

2AOAVWqGC6.text:
• Problem: 3D foundation models give only centimeter-level camera poses on cluttered indoor manipulation rigs.
• On RH20T, COLMAP and RGB-D ICP can degrade rather than improve WorldMirror-v2 initializations.
• Key idea: repurpose diffusion from global pose generation to local residual refinement on SE(3) tangent space.
• Method learns score field of initializer's residual pose errors via tangent-space perturbations of ground-truth rigs.
• Inference follows score field from foundation initialization, with score ensembling, hard-sample mining, confidence-gated fallback.
• Results: held-out RH20T scenes improve from centimeter-level to sub-centimeter, sub-degree Sim(3)-aligned accuracy.
• Calibration gains transfer to downstream multi-view depth fusion; first init-anchored score-based multi-camera refinement.

TPeVwyCt8w.text:
• Problem: HIL-RL propagates terminal rewards uniformly, crediting suboptimal actions that forced human intervention.
• Consequence: overestimated Q-values for the critic, which misguide actor updates toward suboptimal behavior.
• Key idea: PACT uses intervention-induced preferences to recalibrate credit on suboptimal trajectory segments.
• Method: a progress model learned from human demonstrations identifies suboptimal segments for credit correction.
• Human versus resampled policy actions form preference pairs; counterfactual advantage penalizes Bellman targets of suboptimal segments.
• Policy is also aligned directly with human corrective actions in bounded mean space.
• Results: across five real-robot tasks, average success rate improves 24.5% with 1.3x faster convergence.

hr2FYFod4n.text:
• Problem: temporary obstacles blocking graph routes force costly choices between waiting too long or rerouting too early.
• Gap: reactive avoidance and fixed wait-or-reroute rules ignore how long different obstacle types typically persist.
• Key idea: learn class-conditioned survival curves of obstacle clearance time from online experience, assuming known class labels.
• Method: right-censored observations from early reroutes are used, so learning continues even without witnessing clearance.
• Planner: time-dependent graph planner with obstacle memory computes patience thresholds deciding how long to wait per edge.
• Results: simulation time-to-goal within 1% of ground-truth oracle after under 20 observations per class, beating heuristics.
• Real robot: university atrium with people, chairs, bins, tubes; patience thresholds adapted online over 50 episodes.

FYlYM2c6Xc.text:
• Problem: sparse success labels and single binary preferences give weak, ambiguous reward signals for long-horizon manipulation.
• Key idea: annotators define their own natural-language preference axes, like speed, safety, or carefulness.
• Annotators give pairwise trajectory preferences along each axis instead of one overall better-or-worse judgment.
• Method: a language-conditioned reward model maps a trajectory and axis label to an axis-specific reward.
• A reward-conditioned policy is then trained to optimize across multiple human-specified dimensions.
• Setup: four real-world and two simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks; FPL beats sparse-reward and single-preference baselines by 38%.
• New: dense progress signals without subtask segmentation, compositional behaviors, and test-time steering without retraining.

Av4ykyMvpX.text:
• Problem: vision-language navigation policies trained end-to-end generalize poorly out-of-distribution and transfer badly to real robots.
• Key idea: decouple perception from control by aligning observations to a frozen privileged expert's latent space.
• Method: lightweight adapter maps frozen vision-language embeddings into expert latents via supervised alignment, not policy optimization.
• Benefit: expert navigation behavior is reusable across perception backbones and environmental variations, staying lightweight at inference.
• Setup: in-distribution simulation, zero-shot OOD environments, robustness perturbations, and direct TurtleBot real-world deployment.
• OOD results vs behavior cloning: success rises from 49.3% to 80.5%, collisions drop from 45.0% to 15.5%.
• Real world without fine-tuning: 70.7% success vs 60.9% navigation-pretrained baseline and 40.2% behavior cloning.

f3Dic5dJnz.text:
• Problem: fragile objects break under sub-Newton forces; teleoperators cannot perceive contact force during demonstration collection.
• Bottleneck: delayed visual feedback cannot hold the narrow force range needed for stable grasping.
• Key idea: use a tactile reflex controller during data collection, not as a policy input.
• Reflex-shaped demonstrations become a better curriculum for training tactile-free policies.
• ACT matches the teacher's closing profile, reaching 95% stable grasps on the nominal plastic-cup task.
• π₀.₅ gains stability and transfers to an unseen paper cup, but fails 45% under random disturbances.
• New: tactile sensing as a collection-time teacher; disturbance rejection still needs reflex arbitration, with zero failures.

IY6ti85pg0.text:
• Problem: humanoid locomotion over sparse footholds, where small foot placement errors cause catastrophic failures.
• Model-based control is precise but brittle; model-free RL is robust but struggles with constrained motions.
• Key idea: MARCH, model-assisted RL combining simplified-model planning with learned robustness.
• Step 1: simplified models generate a safe reference trajectory over the sparse terrain.
• Step 2: a privileged teacher trains with a control Lyapunov function reward around that reference.
• Step 3: the teacher is distilled into a vision-based student policy for perceptive control.
• Results: better sample efficiency, less curriculum, smoother gaits; Unitree G1 crosses laterally constrained sparse footholds.

jlXzHOkSXq.text:
• Real-time execution via asynchronous inference is critical for deploying large Vision-Language-Action models smoothly and reactively.
• Prior real-time work targets diffusion policies, though autoregressive policies need it more due to slow synchronous rollout.
• Key idea: autoregressive policies achieve real-time execution by adjusting tokenization horizon and applying constrained decoding.
• This guarantees strict latency bounds, enabling multi-trajectory decoding within budget to maximize task performance.
• Evaluated across simulated and real-world environments against an equivalent-level flow-matching policy counterpart.
• Autoregressive policy consistently outperforms flow-matching and completes tasks significantly faster than synchronous inference.
• New: autoregressive policies stay competitive for real-time use, with faster convergence and better instruction-following generalization.

WxBKiMUZtI.text:
• Problem: keypoint tracking lets humanoids reach correct poses without meaningful contact, failing sitting, wiping, pushing tasks.
• Key idea: track explicit part-level binary contact commands alongside keypoint trajectories for humanoid object interaction.
• Method: contact-following rewards plus trajectory augmentation that breaks correlations between keypoint trajectories and contact labels.
• Result: policy decouples contact from keypoint geometry, producing or suppressing contact on command during deployment.
• Setup: simulation across 10 diverse human-object interaction motions; manipulation tasks completed without task-specific rewards.
• Outperforms keypoint-only trackers on contact-relevant tasks; ablations confirm trajectory augmentation is necessary.
• New: contact controllability validated sim-to-real on a real humanoid across 5 different motions.

AAn8ouEHwO.text:
• Problem: RL for manipulation is bottlenecked by brittle hand-crafted rewards and data-hungry, hackable learned reward models.
• Key idea: RARM generates dense progress rewards from a single reference demonstration, with no per-task reward engineering.
• Architecture: DINOv3 backbone with low-rank adapters, temporal aggregator, and asymmetric cross-attention comparator.
• Training: contrastive objective on ordinary videos, done once, requiring no robot-specific data.
• Reward: rollout clips are matched to demo clips; confidence-gated progress change from the matched clip gives reward.
• Setup: 10 simulated tasks across LIBERO and MetaWorld, plus 4 real-world tasks including long-horizon ones.
• Results: best overall success rates across benchmarks, with negligible per-step reward generation overhead.

N77om40jWL.text:
• Problem: sequential task continuation, where one robot acts in a workspace already altered by a previous robot.
• Existing multi-robot cooperation relies on co-training or co-optimization with shared interaction data.
• Co-training fails to scale as diverse embodiments and policies create combinatorially many robot pairings.
• Key idea: ad hoc cooperation between robots that have never operated together, without joint training.
• Method: PAVE lets robots share value functions to communicate environmental preferences to earlier robots.
• A KNN-based uncertainty filter grounds shared values and prevents overconfidence in out-of-distribution states.
• Results: up to 47.7% higher task success than selfish agents, in simulation and real-world experiments.

4IT3fcnny2.text:
• Problem: open-world humanoid traversal needs vision-guided safe foot placement during dynamic motion with natural whole-body behavior.
• SSR: efficient end-to-end framework for egocentric vision-based humanoid traversal, jointly learning surefootedness, symmetry, and natural motion.
• Imagined foothold guidance predicts upcoming swing-foot contacts and scores their support, steering swings toward stable regions.
• Equivariant latent-space symmetry augmentation efficiently induces bilateral coordination despite high-dimensional visual observations.
• Terrain-specific multi-discriminator motion priors encourage human-like behavior across different scene types.
• Real-world tests: varied stairs, wide gaps, high platforms, and long-horizon outdoor traversal; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• New: foothold imagination reduces edge slips; latent symmetry and per-terrain priors scale natural, robust humanoid traversal.

cJGMjQlgz5.text:
• Problem: RL struggles to explore and discover complex strategies in contact-rich, non-prehensile manipulation.
• Key idea: improve RL exploration through smarter episode resets, i.e., better start state distributions.
• Insight: model-based sampling of states on constrained manifolds is efficient, unlike model-based trajectory finding.
• Method: a novel state sampler that explicitly covers diverse contact modes using contact structure.
• Training: constrained sampling resets combined with projected interpolation and curriculum learning for goal-conditioned RL.
• Results: outperforms RL without constrained sampling and alternative goal-conditioned methods; the abstract reports no numbers.
• New: trains universal, non-prehensile, dynamic manipulation policies in contact-rich settings.

40CsfPl2cq.text:
• Problem: contact-rich imitation learning needs costly expert demos, so policies must be spatially robust with limited data.
• Key idea: VISTA, an equivariant visuotactile diffusion policy built for data-efficient contact-rich manipulation.
• Method: vision and tactile inputs are projected into spherical tokens for a shared geometric representation.
• Permutation-equivariant spherical fusion injects tactile contact cues into the corresponding visual spherical directions.
• Fused harmonic features are rotated by end-effector orientation, conditioning an equivariant diffusion policy for spatially consistent actions.
• Setup: evaluated in simulation and real-world robots against strong visuotactile imitation learning baselines.
• Results: substantially better data efficiency and spatial robustness; the abstract gives no specific numbers.

Ti3oK55n1H.text:
• Problem: manipulation policies break across robots, payloads, and sim-to-real gaps, especially in contact-rich dynamic tasks.
• Domain randomization makes policies conservative; system identification needs data recollected per robot or payload.
• TAM: learned module adding residual torque corrections so a real robot behaves like an ideal one.
• Sits between low-level controller and torque interface, using a proprioceptive history encoder plus torque adaptor.
• Policy-agnostic: same weights work for joint targets, end-effector targets, or direct torque action spaces.
• Trained fully in randomized simulation: multi-robot pretraining, then robot-specific fine-tuning, zero real-robot data needed.
• Zero-shot on real Franka with unknown payloads (RL pushing, BC flipping, MPC balancing), beating system ID and RMA.

TlWfBm8jtZ.text:
• Problem: tactile-only blind grasping with dexterous hands is hard due to sim-to-real gap and sparse signals.
• Key idea: calibrate simulator to real tactile contacts, then learn tactile-only policies entirely in simulation.
• Real2Sim pipeline builds a contact-calibrated digital twin that reproduces real tactile signals.
• Layout-aware tactile encoder injects sensor-geometry priors via self-supervised pretraining to enrich sparse observations.
• Object-specific RL experts' successful grasps are distilled into one tactile-conditioned Diffusion Policy for generalization.
• Setup: physical LEAP Hand with distributed tactile sensing, tested on 10 seen and 10 unseen objects.
• Results: 27% real success over 20 objects, no real demos or vision; ablations support pretraining and calibration.

CH33XUEIBO.text:
• Problem: sim-trained assembly policies degrade on real robots due to contact mismatch, misalignment, friction, and force differences.
• Key idea: separate known nominal task descriptors from hidden execution-time contact residuals in a world model.
• Task descriptor encodes clearance, part scale, insertion depth, and task type as the nominal assembly prior.
• Force/contact, proprioception, and action history update a latent contact belief that conditions dynamics, value, and actions.
• Rollouts proceed from the belief state, with no access to future measured force required.
• Sparse rollouts or human corrections calibrate a lightweight residual adapter while the base model and policy stay frozen.
• Evaluated on a controlled axial assembly family; the abstract reports no quantitative results.

14GtmKGuCf.text:
• VLAs fail when object positions or instructions differ from training, limiting spatial and task generalization.
• Language or visual prompting of 2D grounding coordinates does not fix this brittleness.
• Key insight: how grounding is represented and injected matters; 3D points fed to the action head work.
• Method: grounded 3D point, displacement to gripper, injected into action head via adaptive layer normalization.
• Lightweight two-layer MLP module, model-agnostic, with no backbone or pretraining changes required.
• LIBERO-PRO, GR00T-N1.6: task perturbation 31.2 to 77.5, position perturbation 28.1 to 60.2 success.
• Comparable gains on π0.5 show backbone-agnostic benefits, and real-world experiments confirm practical applicability.

QoUwcaTc3d.text:
• Surgical robot imitation learning needs paired video and kinematics, but real-tissue robot action data is rare.
• Phantom demonstrations give accurate action labels but lack the visual diversity of real tissue.
• SurgVIL combines labeled phantom robot demos with open-source and online surgical videos for policy learning.
• Approximate kinematics are estimated from unlabeled surgical videos and used as weak action supervision.
• Evaluated on da Vinci needle pick-up and cholecystectomy cutting tasks.
• Tested across ACT, Pi0, and Gr00t-H policy backbones.
• Adding surgical videos substantially improves generalization to real-tissue and out-of-distribution settings, offering a scalable path beyond phantoms.

QDJCwo9pmt.text:
• Problem: robot failure detectors give per-frame binary scores or need full episodes, unsuitable for real-time use.
• Key idea: frame failure detection as online video temporal grounding over streaming manipulation video.
• Model outputs each failure's temporal boundaries plus a natural-language description as the failure unfolds.
• Method processes video chunk-by-chunk, using a memory bank over previously observed frames.
• Automated pipeline converts robot trajectory datasets into grounding annotations, giving 73% relative localization gain from pre-training.
• Beats strongest online grounding baseline: mIoU 0.232 vs 0.194; failure descriptions reach CIDEr 0.854.
• New: releases generated pre-training dataset and human-annotated benchmark for real-time failure detection and recovery.

xEOer7gykg.text:
• Problem: VLA fine-tuning leaves implicit which scene region the demonstrator found task-relevant at each timestep.
• Key idea: use operator eye gaze, recorded by HMD eye tracker during VR teleoperation, as temporal grounding.
• Method: a ~50M-parameter predictor estimates fixation from RGB and language, rendered as crosshair on images.
• Policy is unchanged π0; no eye tracker or architectural modification is needed at deployment.
• Results: across six real-world bimanual tasks, mean success rises from 26.3% to 56.0%, improving every task.
• Crosshair input beats auxiliary attention loss on the same gaze, adding instruction-conditional attention and stage awareness.
• Real human gaze beats detection and random cues, because it anticipates what engineered cues cannot.

JqZEEaNDLJ.text:
• Problem: robot RL adoption bottlenecked by costly expert engineering for tasks, rewards, and hyperparameters.
• Key idea: HARBOR frames robot RL automation as a harness-engineering problem for LLM agents.
• Input simulator codebase plus task spec; agents automate environment setup through policy training in simulation.
• Method: bounded stages, specialized agents, standardized commands, persistent artifacts, executable gates, reusable knowledge.
• Scales iteration via decentralized parallel trials and experience learning carried across runs.
• Evaluated on 6 benchmarks, 16 tasks: manipulation, locomotion, bimanual dexterous control.
• Results: rewards and tuning match or beat default configurations; practical token, wall-clock cost; real-robot deployment.

JhEwJ56SH3.text:
• Problem: dual-arm grasping of large, heavy objects with sparse graspable regions under partial observations
• Prior bimanual methods assume full object point clouds, which are rarely available in real scenarios
• Key idea: infer hidden local geometry, such as thickness, edges, and clearance, directly from partial point clouds
• Method: convolutional occupancy networks implicitly learn graspability, collision-free contact regions, and object thickness
• Generates force-closure compliant grasp pairs, refined by sampling-based optimization to resolve incomplete-geometry ambiguity
• Evaluation: analytical force-closure metrics, large-scale simulation, and real-world tests on noisy point clouds of novel objects
• Results: robust, physically stable dual-arm grasps under partial views; abstract reports no specific numbers

nzYChkCtvT.text:
• Problem: simulator-in-the-loop refinement works for rigid objects but cloth state and contact are hard to model.
• Key idea: bring inference-time simulator rollouts to real-world cloth manipulation from a single RGB image.
• Simulator: FLASH deformable simulator balances physical fidelity, numerical stability, and rollout speed for data and planning.
• Real-to-sim: synthetic-trained module fuses pretrained visual features with canonical tokens to estimate simulation-ready cloth state.
• Planning: prior-guided MPPI on sparse-mesh rollouts, anchored at an offline-distilled policy trajectory.
• Sparse meshes preserve key deformation and contact while allowing large parallel rollout batches online.
• Real-robot results: higher success and robustness than baselines; abstract reports no specific numbers.

AmQH2hU9Gs.text:
• Problem: in-hand dexterous rotation policies degrade under pose shifts, force disturbances, and object variation.
• Policies must infer object pose, geometry, contact, and slip from partial, noisy observations.
• Key idea: a World Synesthesia Model (WSM) learns compact latent dynamics from proprioception, depth, touch, actions, and rewards.
• WSM latent serves as recurrent task context for an asymmetric actor-critic, not for imagination or planning.
• WSM reconstructs clean depth from noisy inputs, giving a denoised geometric state for real-robot deployment.
• Ablations: clean-depth supervision gives the largest gain; WSM pretrained on nine objects transfers to 49-object policy learning.
• Results: better multi-object rotation, unseen-object and sim-to-real transfer, and recovery from hard poses and pushes.

Wp9ex57Z2k.text:
• Problem: humanoids need alternative locomotion when ground paths are blocked; primate-style brachiation across overhead bars offers one.
• Challenge: long-horizon release-swing-capture sequences, alternating contacts, and whole-body momentum coordination in high-DoF humanoids.
• Sensing gap: no reliable measurements of segment-relative displacement or hook-contact state during deployment.
• SwingBot: a learning framework for continuous humanoid brachiation using passive wrist hooks instead of actuated grippers.
• Biomimetic keyframes make rare release-swing-capture transitions reachable during early RL exploration.
• Recurrent privileged-state estimation supplies compact position and contact latents for deployment.
• Hardware: continuous bar traversal, robust to payloads, pushes, and varied bar spacings; abstract reports no quantitative results.

7tCsPSbYZb.text:
• Problem: visual navigation policies optimize geometric traversability but ignore socially occupied space between people.
• Example: gaps between walking partners or inside conversation circles are collision-free yet socially off-limits.
• Key idea: GRACE explicitly models social relations and group interaction spaces to avoid socially undesirable paths.
• Perception: builds a visual pedestrian-robot graph from RGB, with soft F-formation targets supervising group-aware attention.
• Planning: this social representation guides a visual trajectory generator, finetuned with group-relative reward-weighted flow matching.
• Setup: real-world experiments on a Unitree Go2 quadruped against representative visual navigation baselines.
• Results: fewer group-space intrusions and collisions with competitive efficiency; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

tegLlXBRCU.text:
• Problem: most VLA models map observations directly to actions, so early mistakes compound on long-horizon tasks.
• Key idea: Coarse-to-Control adds explicit planning natively in the discrete action-token space.
• Method: policy first predicts a compact sequence of coarse action tokens summarizing the intended future trajectory.
• Then it generates executable action tokens conditioned on that coarse plan, in a plan-execute fashion.
• Planning and execution share one action vocabulary, keeping plans close to the control manifold and directly actionable.
• Setup: evaluated on LIBERO, SimplerEnv-WidowX, and real-world robot manipulation tasks.
• Results: consistent gains over direct action generation, largest on long-horizon multi-stage tasks; abstract reports no specific numbers.

WvR13cRtRf.text:
• Fixed-frequency controllers force a trade-off between efficient low rates and responsive high-rate feedback.
• High default control rates waste inference bandwidth, increase actuation jitter, and consume extra energy.
• TARC: an RL policy jointly predicts each control action and how long to apply it.
• Optimizes task performance under soft or hard constraints on the number of control switches.
• Evaluated on a high-speed RC car, a Unitree Go1 quadruped, and a simulated vision-language-action model.
• Matches high-frequency controller performance while running at less than half their control frequency.
• New: control rate adapts online, using high-frequency feedback only when the task requires it.

thG2jwuii6.text:
• Problem: scaling robot learning needs data that targets policy failures, not just more data volume.
• Handheld robot-free collection interfaces are open-loop, giving users no feedback from the current policy.
• DAgger-style correction requires deploying imperfect policies on physical robots: costly, unsafe, and hard to scale.
• RoboPocket: smartphone system for robot-free policy iteration using on-device sensing, display, and cloud-side policy inference.
• AR Visual Foresight overlays predicted policy trajectories, letting users spot weaknesses and collect targeted corrections.
• Asynchronous finetuning folds in new corrections, updating the policy within minutes in a DAgger-inspired loop.
• Across diverse real-world manipulation tasks, online corrections achieve about 2x sample efficiency versus scaling offline demonstrations.

DMljKr2f4O.text:
• Problem: designing control barrier functions that are effective, scalable, interpretable, and not overly conservative remains difficult.
• Key idea: learn neural CBFs by approximating the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi value function with a neural network.
• Training combines physics-informed losses with sparse supervision from vertex-restricted control search.
• Control-affine dynamics and polytope control sets maximize the Hamiltonian at vertices, enabling GPU-parallel tree search.
• A residual architecture guarantees the learned CBF never exceeds the specified constraint function.
• Evaluated on 15 systems, it reliably recovers large safe sets where baselines are conservative or fail.
• Hardware demo: a mobile robot safely avoids pedestrians using a VertexCBF-trained neural CBF.

TTFZrb0Hw3.text:
• Problem: humanoid systems often split upper and lower body controllers, behaving like wheeled dual-arm robots.
• Key question: what does a whole-body native VLA mapping language and pixels to all DoFs require?
• Method: systematic one-variable-at-a-time roadmap across teleoperation, VLA model design, and heterogeneous co-training phases.
• Finding: joint-based whole-body teleoperation beats interfaces exposing only part of the humanoid's degrees of freedom.
• Finding: VLAs pretrained on static and wheeled dual-arm robots transfer well to full humanoid action spaces.
• Co-training with HuMI, a humanoid UMI analog, generalizes to new objects and instructions without extra teleoperation.
• Result: OpenHLM beats GR00T N1.6 and Psi_0 on long-horizon tasks using under half the demonstration time.

0HLj8l0bB4.text:
• Problem: VLM-based robots rely on coarse 2D perception, failing at precise 3D geometric reasoning for assembly.
• Key idea: AssemLM, a spatial multimodal LLM that predicts task-critical 6D assembly poses with explicit geometry.
• Inputs: fuses assembly manuals, point clouds, and textual instructions into unified spatial reasoning.
• Method: specialized point cloud encoder extracts fine-grained geometric and rotational features for the language model.
• New benchmark: AssemBench, over 900K multimodal samples with precise 6D pose annotations.
• Results: state-of-the-art 6D pose reasoning; real-robot tests show fine-grained, multi-step assembly success.
• What's new: shifts evaluation from 2D grounding to full 3D inference; code, models, data released.

X2mRYIgshj.text:
• Problem: VLA action spaces trade off clear Cartesian motion intent against stable, directly executable joint-space control.
• Cartesian actions need inverse kinematics, which gives non-unique or unstable joint targets on redundant robots.
• Joint-space actions suit low-level controllers but obscure task-level motion structure and embodiment kinematics.
• Key idea: DualSpace-VLA uses Cartesian motion-intent tokens to guide joint-space action generation.
• Method: intent tokens, supervised by chunk-wise delta end-effector targets, feed a flow-matching joint expert via cross-attention.
• Differentiable forward kinematics regularizes joint trajectories in Cartesian space during training, with no inference-time inverse kinematics.
• Results: beats end-effector-only and joint-only baselines in RoboTwin, real bimanual tasks, and few-shot transfer (abstract gives no numbers).

Am3aGfOlLh.text:
• Problem: VLA models optimize semantic grounding, but manipulation needs geometry-aware spatial alignment and dynamic affordance selection.
• Key idea: GeoAlign uses robot proprioceptive state to guide spatial alignment of geometry features for policy learning.
• Method: post-trains an RGB geometry branch with robot-domain RGB-D supervision, producing geometry-enhanced (GEP) features.
• Only RGB is needed at rollout; depth supervision is used solely during post-training.
• Proprioceptive state queries the GEP feature grid, yielding compact, phase-dependent geometry tokens for action prediction.
• Results: 99.0% on LIBERO, 85.3% on three SimplerEnv-Fractal tasks, 78.8% on eight real ALOHA tasks.
• Ablations confirm both geometry post-training and state-guided querying contribute to performance.

rfRjWMFfvV.text:
• Problem: collaborative mobile manipulation fails from mistimed waiting, yielding, pulling, or releasing, not weak local skills.
• Setting: two bimanual mobile manipulators physically coupled through shared rigid and deformable objects, partner only partially observed.
• Key idea: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation (SAI), a single-teleoperator curriculum for learning coupled multi-robot policies.
• Method: train Robot A with compliant human partner, then Robot B against deployed Robot A policy.
• Refinement: Robot A is fine-tuned using sparse interventions near coordination failures like delay or phase mismatch.
• Results: on real dual-robot tasks, SAI beats independent imitation and ablations in success, synchronization, and yielding.
• What's new: coordination emerges from curriculum structure, without synchronized dual-operator demos or explicit inter-robot communication.

mR4L9LaUGJ.text:
• Problem: VLA models process all inputs at one synchronous rate inherited from vision-language pretraining.
• This mismatches physics: fast sensors change at hundreds of hertz, vision slower, language stays constant.
• Synchronous VLAs oversample slow modalities, undersample fast ones, and cap action rate at the lowest frequency.
• Key idea: decouple temporal processing so each modality updates and retains information at its own sensor rate.
• Method: per-modality latent buffers refreshed at sensor rates, read continuously by the action head.
• New high-frequency modalities enter via gated cross-attention, leaving the pretrained backbone intact.
• Seven contact-rich real-world tasks: 95.2% vs 40.95% success over strongest synchronous baseline, smooth 100 Hz control.

ULCeXiRzJD.text:
• Problem: dexterous hand-object contact is partially observable; vision is occluded, tactile sensors add hardware and calibration burdens.
• Gap: existing policies rarely model how contact cues evolve under actions, making them brittle under contact uncertainty.
• Key idea: treat hand-object proximity, from reconstructed interaction point clouds, as a hardware-agnostic interaction state.
• Proximity cues also provide immersive contact feedback to operators during VR teleoperation data collection.
• Method: coupled forward-inverse dynamics predicts future latents from actions and decodes proximity changes from latent shifts.
• Policy reweights proximity tokens across manipulation phases and uses dynamics-consistency supervision to stabilize action generation.
• Results: higher success and robustness than baselines in simulation and real world; abstract reports no specific numbers.

YQoaLlpDD3.text:
• Problem: learned dynamics models are morphology-locked; an ANYmal-D model fails on a Unitree Go1.
• Even small actuator or limb-length changes force retraining world models from scratch.
• Key idea: condition one generative dynamics model on scale-invariant morphology features, train policies in imagination.
• Method: physical morphology encoder, adaptive reward normalizer, and morphology conditioning in latent dynamics.
• Setup: QWM versus model-free policy given identical morphology information, tested on training and unseen quadrupeds.
• Results: model-free matches QWM on training cohort but degrades on unseen morphologies; QWM transfers zero-shot.
• New: first world model showing zero-shot cross-embodiment quadruped transfer, with no fine-tuning, adaptation, or warm-up.

PJuQx9kBg5.text:
• Problem: multi-expert diffusion planners must handle unseen regions; should they route among experts or adapt?
• Setup: diffusion planner with shared adapter plus per-domain expert adapters, tested on three real-world held-out maps.
• Routing fails: none of eight test-time routing schemes beats static default on fleet-mean lateral offset.
• Even oracle per-scene expert selection reduces mean offset by only 0.9 m, showing limited routing headroom.
• Adapting wins: reward fine-tuning on 20 target scenes with joint replay cuts offset from 12.4 m to 6.9 m.
• Target-region training drives gains; replaying training scenes limits forgetting on original ODDs.
• nuPlan: open-loop offsets improve but closed-loop degrades; two TTA baselines produce degenerate low-offset trajectories.

oKJnHTluoA.text:
• Problem: VLAs conditioned on history, depth, or 4D features suffer geometric drift when evidence isn't motion-consistent.
• Key question: should a VLA remember past frames, or the motion that connects them?
• Key idea: MotionVLA turns a short past-only video window into compact, time-continuous trajectory-field tokens.
• Method: current visual tokens query motion history, retrieving task-relevant motion recoupled into the VLA stream.
• Training uses trajectory-grounded supervision so injected history stays physically coherent and usable for control.
• Results: better long-horizon manipulation, smoother and more direct executions in simulation and preliminary real-robot rollouts; no numbers given.
• What's new: effective VLA memory comes from motion-consistent evidence, not simply more 4D context.

fTx97RpooW.text:
• Problem: post-training VLAs for reliable real-robot deployment is bottlenecked; SFT/DAgger use failures indirectly, RL needs rewards.
• FlowPRO: reward-free offline reinforced fine-tuning framework designed for flow-matching VLA policies.
• RPRO objective pairs contrastive preference optimization with a proximal regularizer tailored to the flow-matching action head.
• Proximal term anchors implicit reward magnitude, eliminating the reward hacking seen in plain Flow-DPO.
• Teleoperated intervention-and-rollback yields naturally paired positive and negative real-robot trajectories from one operator action.
• Smooth Interpolation plus batch mixing densify sparse corrections into per-state supervision while preserving base capabilities.
• Highest success on four long-horizon bimanual tasks versus four baselines; ablations validate each loss component.

MYYKl10JKD.text:
• Mobile dexterous manipulation needs coordinated base, dual arms, and multi-fingered hands, making policy learning very data-hungry.
• Key idea: learn from scalable, tracker-free egocentric human demonstrations despite the human-robot embodiment gap.
• Capture uses a consumer VR headset plus head-mounted stereo camera, recording whole-body motion in everyday environments.
• Novel whole-body retargeting maps human motion to robot base, arm, head, and dexterous hand commands.
• A vision-language-action policy is trained on retargeted human data plus teleoperated robot data.
• Across four real-world tasks, average success rises from 33.8% to 71.3% versus robot-only training.
• Human data improves robot-data efficiency rather than replacing it; full system will be open-sourced.

0rvhGgRYjx.text:
• Problem: robots must navigate buildings to streets in one episode, but benchmarks test indoor and outdoor separately.
• Existing benchmarks often abstract away robot execution, ignoring exit finding, boundary traversal, and kinodynamic failures.
• NavVerse: physics-enabled benchmark for continuous indoor-to-outdoor embodied navigation with executable robot interfaces.
• Scenes: 100 indoor, 50 urban outdoor, and 50 indoor-to-outdoor environments.
• Tasks: ObjectNav, Vision-and-Language Navigation, and new PlaceNav searching for places like restaurants or banks.
• Zero-shot RL, VLA, and modular baselines all struggle; VLAs achieve the highest success, while modular methods are safest.
• PlaceNav success drops from outdoor to indoor-to-outdoor scenes, showing cross-context adaptation remains a major bottleneck.

kGLogzKtYq.text:
• Problem: robot tool use usually assumes a pre-specified tool, failing in scenes with many open-category objects.
• Goal: open-world affordance grounding, deciding which tool to use and where to interact with it.
• Key idea: object parts capture both affordance semantics and geometry, enabling two-level grounding.
• Semantic level: vision-language models select the appropriate tool and identify task-relevant parts.
• Geometric level: vision foundation models ground selected parts into 3D affordance regions.
• New: a benchmark adding tool selection; GROW² beats state-of-the-art baselines on it and existing benchmarks.
• Higher task success than baselines in simulated and real robot tool use; abstract reports no specific numbers.

OckqYiY2QM.text:
• Problem: VLA models run slowly on low-power onboard devices like Jetson Orin, causing high latency and low control frequency.
• Asynchronous inference hides latency but causes perception-execution misalignment and long reaction times.
• Key idea: EagleVLA (named Jetson-PI in abstract) uses foresight-aligned asynchronous correction for efficient onboard VLA deployment.
• A lightweight correction module predicts future environment representation from committed actions, so the action expert acts from that future step.
• Confidence-based scheduling balances VLM and action expert calls; CUDA graph reuse, GPU buffering, and flow unrolling add speed.
• Results: 8.66x control frequency on Jetson Orin, 3.48x on Thor, and +14.8% average LIBERO success over VLASH.
• What's new: future-state prediction fixes async misalignment, and adaptive scheduling cuts reaction time; code on Anonymous GitHub.

xhO9wj1gGt.text:
• Problem: robot co-design usually reruns costly reinforcement learning loops for every new robot design.
• Key idea: reuse generalist multi-embodiment value functions as differentiable surrogates for robot design optimization.
• Method: train embodiment-aware policy and value function across many robot designs, then freeze the value function.
• Design candidates are optimized via value gradients with respect to embodiment parameters, no new RL loop.
• Setup: perturbed single robots to held-out robots across morphology classes, up to 50 training robots.
• Scales to design spaces exceeding 1100 continuous embodiment parameters with a single trained model.
• New: value gradients also pinpoint performance-limiting design and control parameters, enabling design analysis.

gvM7KWEhVI.text:
• Problem: diffusion/flow planners need certified collision avoidance and fast online replanning for real-world deployment.
• Prior safe planners generate full trajectories, perturbing intermediate states, which is costly and causes distribution shift.
• Key idea: align flow sampling dynamics with execution dynamics by sequentially integrating a learned state vector field.
• Safety is certified only for the executed step, using high order control barrier functions.
• Hierarchical network predicts the next position first, then the next physical velocity, improving robustness.
• Evaluated on navigation, racing, and locomotion benchmarks against existing safe diffusion/flow planners.
• Results: lower planning latency and better safety with competitive goal-reaching; abstract reports no specific numbers.

C08KksTfEx.text:
• Problem: robot manipulation is end-effector-centric, while humans exploit whole-arm contact when hands are busy.
• Challenge: choosing arm contact location, non-prehensile interaction, and respecting end-effector pose or safety constraints.
• Key idea: WACL, a hierarchical framework passing robot-agnostic representations to a downstream trajectory optimizer.
• Representations: semantic scene keypoints, reference contact trajectory, and VLM-generated safety-aware path constraints from language.
• Surface-contact optimizer jointly selects contact link, contact point, and joint configuration; only kinematics-dependent stage.
• Setup: 7-DoF real arm, four whole-arm tasks, learned from few bare-hand human demos, no teleoperation.
• Results: 78% vs 33% success over keypoint baseline; new constraints handled without retraining.

L8ATlveWKT.text:
• Problem: robust multi-hypothesis localization must adapt perception and motion models across environments and robot platforms.
• Classical particle filters use hand-tuned models and non-differentiable resampling, blocking end-to-end training.
• Learning-based localizers lack modularity; prior differentiable particle filters were limited to planar, visual, simulated, or single-platform settings.
• MaD-PF: first end-to-end differentiable particle filter for real-world cross-environment SE(3) 3D-LiDAR localization.
• Uses unit dual quaternions with differentiable motion, observation, and resampling modules, systematically comparing submodule variants.
• Proposed improvements boost robustness on held-out datasets and cut observation model latency by 89%.
• Zero-shot RMSE of 0.398 m or better in unseen environments and platforms, beating SotA with 2.5x less training.

U5POjpnj6J.text:
• Problem: most world action models operate in 2D images, missing explicit 3D scene dynamics and cross-view consistency.
• 2D representations also make aligning visual observations with robot actions difficult.
• Key idea: GSWAM jointly models scene dynamics and robot actions in a unified 3D Gaussian Splatting space.
• A Gaussian VAE (GSVAE) compresses 3DGS scenes into geometrically consistent latent representations.
• Scenes and actions share a 3D-anchored space, handled by an anchor-based spatial diffusion transformer.
• Decoupled flow timesteps per modality enable joint scene-action generation and action-conditioned future scene prediction.
• Simulated and real-world experiments: beats representative baselines in action generation and scene prediction; abstract gives no numbers.

wiovp2zRWA.text:
• Problem: compliant dexterous manipulation usually needs costly, fragile external tactile or force sensors, unsuited to low-cost hands.
• Key idea: motor current tracks actuator torque, so it can serve as a learnable tactile-like contact signal.
• Method: learn from motor current and joint states to predict a compliance reference position for a standard PD controller.
• The induced position error produces appropriate grasping force, adapting interaction forces from real-time proprioceptive feedback.
• Setup: multiple dexterous hands; fragile objects, dynamic loads, sustained surface contact, and thin-object retrieval tasks.
• Results: stable compliant grasping, safer and more efficient teleoperation, better downstream policy learning; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: position-based compliance from proprioception alone, compatible with mainstream teleoperation and policy-learning pipelines.

ik1SfLQgZA.text:
• Problem: imitation learning methods are poorly understood under contact-rich, two-player adversarial robot dynamics.
• Platform: KlaskTron, open-hardware adversarial robot game with learned actuator model enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.
• Dataset: 80k real human demo timesteps, 320k symmetry-augmented, up to 5M synthetic PPO expert steps.
• Setup: GPU-native Isaac Lab environment plus diagnostic baselines for standard imitation learning methods.
• Finding: behavior cloning hits a data scaling plateau despite more demonstrations.
• Finding: GAIL discriminator recovers peg-ball proximity (Spearman ρ = -1.0) but its gradient is too flat for PPO.
• New: asymmetric BC-prior × reward-density interaction; shared policy interface makes algorithms directly deployable on hardware.

DgA5zlu7Ck.text:
• Problem: task-space policy actions feasible on one robot may be unreachable on another morphology.
• Existing SE(3) reachability fields are monolithic, wasting costly IK supervision and undersampling near-boundary regions.
• Key idea: decompose full-pose feasibility into global position reachability plus local, position-conditioned orientation reachability.
• Method: dense Position-SDF trained via forward-kinematics coverage with distance-to-boundary targets across the workspace.
• Orientation-SDF uses IK boundary mining only at representative position anchors, cutting supervision cost.
• Results: 85.53% SE(3) accuracy with 0.51x IK budget, +6.45 points over best 1.00x baseline.
• New: differentiable morphology-conditioned margins enable gradient-based pose repair and zero-shot transfer to new morphologies.

uNi5VigrGr.text:
• Problem: flow and diffusion robot policies need fast inference and high-quality demonstrations, which are often unavailable.
• Consequence: suboptimal demonstrations and slow sampling cause poor behaviors and failures under distribution shift.
• Key idea: Optimal Transport Q-Learning (OTQL) post-trains flow policies with RL using the robot's own experience.
• Method: advantage-weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching both steers and accelerates the flow policy.
• Setup: simulation and real-robot tasks with only 50-60 interaction episodes and no expensive distillation.
• Results: single-task success rises from 36% to 86%, and a pre-trained VLA from 38% to 76%.
• What's new: joint fine-tuning and acceleration, cutting inference steps per action by 70%.

Sal8Urvt1F.text:
• Problem: robots struggle to fully exploit bird's-eye-view (BEV) priors and use them reliably during navigation.
• Key idea: transfer the world understanding of image generation models to embodied navigation.
• Method: an image generation model reads language instructions, finds the goal, and paints traversability masks.
• Execution: cross-view localization aligns robot odometry with the BEV map, reducing long-term drift.
• Setup: extensive benchmarks plus real-world tests on quadruped robot and UAV platforms.
• Result: a 285-meter outdoor long-range navigation task completed with only a conventional local planner.
• Novelty: generative foundation models serve as global planners, bringing their generalization to ground and near-ground robots.

Jq0aPlIS34.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation failures are usually detected only after the robot commits to contact.
• Wrist cameras see contact well, but a bad approach may already push, miss, or slip.
• Key idea: ContactGuard predicts a planned action chunk's consequence before contact and aborts likely failures.
• Method: action-conditioned latent world model predicts multi-view visual embeddings, avoiding pixel-level video prediction.
• World model trains on unlabelled trajectories; a lightweight failure probe uses few labelled pre-contact clips.
• Results: beats direct and corrupted-action ablations on real-world contact-rich tasks; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: a live pre-contact abort signal for chunked visuomotor policies, without modifying the policy.

SaMjmUr6xC.text:
• Problem: reachable workspace underpins robot design and operation, but current approximations are slow, imprecise, or morphology-specific.
• Key idea: RAM, a morphology-conditioned implicit neural representation predicting pose reachability across different robot morphologies.
• Acts as a fast, differentiable reachability surrogate that inherently accounts for self-collisions.
• Generalises to unseen morphologies without retraining, unlike single-robot workspace models.
• New public dataset of 3·10^10 samples generated solely from forward kinematics.
• Results: 86% F1 at nanosecond inference, beating baseline by 14% and three orders faster.
• Speeds gradient-based morphology optimisation by 10x and trajectory optimisation by 100x.

2Z9666X2B7.text:
• Problem: humanoids navigating cluttered indoor spaces need whole-body adaptation, not simplified navigation abstractions.
• Key idea: TANGO, first whole-body vision-language-action model for language-conditioned humanoid traversal.
• Inputs natural-language instruction plus egocentric RGB; outputs 29-DoF joint-space actions for whole-body control.
• Data pipeline: global path planning, kinematic motion generation, obstacle-aware editing, RL-based tracking for feasible supervision.
• Learns coordinated arm placement, torso adjustment, and gait modulation for collision-free movement through 3D clutter.
• Simulation: outperforms state-of-the-art VLN and modular humanoid baselines on long-horizon obstacle-negotiation tasks.
• Trained only in simulation; deployed zero-shot on Unitree G1 for robust real-world language-guided traversal.

Z35baC5jBe.text:
• Problem: human robot demonstrations mix efficient and hesitant actions, and behavior cloning imitates all of them equally.
• Fine-tuning generative policies with offline RL critic gradients can amplify critic errors and drift from the prior.
• Key idea: steer a frozen one-step generative policy by reshaping its latent noise, never updating the decoder.
• Method: an observation-conditioned residual noise shaper trained with advantage-weighted reconstruction of demonstrated actions.
• Advantages are detached and scale-normalized, used only as supervised weights, avoiding critic-gradient updates and keeping one-step inference.
• Also new: a rollout-free decoder-sensitivity criterion picks pretrained checkpoints that stay responsive to latent-noise perturbations.
• Sim and real tasks, clean and mixed data: beats frozen base while limiting drift; abstract gives no numbers.

022K2ZIPR6.text:
• Problem: adapting general VLMs to driving is thought to need heavy 3D priors or architectural overhauls.
• Pilot finding: off-the-shelf VLMs adapt well to driving; precise metric depth is the main missing link.
• Key idea: a non-intrusive training framework adds 3D geometric awareness while preserving open-world capabilities.
• Method: automatically built (image, depth, QA) triplets train primary VLM, auxiliary depth, and frozen twin streams.
• Frozen twin uses logit-level KL distillation against semantic drift; depth branch is dropped, adding zero inference overhead.
• Setup: four benchmarks covering 3D perception, driving language reasoning, end-to-end planning, and general multimodal understanding.
• Results: beats SOTA driving VLMs, rivals 3D perception experts, retains general reasoning; abstract reports no numbers.

GeENMbQXhi.text:
• Problem: robot post-training and architecture changes obscure what pretrained VLMs actually contribute to VLA control.
• Obstacle: predicting bare numeric action tokens shifts outputs away from the VLM's pretrained language distribution.
• Key idea: CLAP prepends a natural-language action description before each numeric action sequence.
• Language-action plan causally conditions precise action-token prediction, with no backbone architecture modifications.
• Setup: single-epoch fine-tuning of one VLM lineage at 0.8B, 2B, and 4B scales.
• Results: 2B CLAP reaches 90.8% on LIBERO, +14.9 points over VLA-0, more robust on LIBERO-PRO.
• New: open-weight multi-scale compact VLA family enabling controlled study of VLM-to-VLA capability transfer.

Gpc0nCixhZ.text:
• Problem: collecting multi-robot demonstrations is hard, since one operator cannot teleoperate many robots simultaneously.
• Setting: decentralised, communication-free visuomotor policies running onboard resource-constrained swarm robots.
• Key idea: coordinated tasks often gain efficiency mainly by minimising inter-robot interference, not tight coupling.
• Approach: train coordinated box-pushing policies using only demonstrations from a single teleoperated robot.
• Method: systematic study of dataset design, data collection strategies, and lightweight policy architectures.
• Results: experiments scale up to 40 robots; learning coordination by passively observing other robots proves difficult.
• Contribution: first systematic look at solo-to-swarm imitation, exposing open challenges for multi-robot learning.

1uKIsrjCvt.text:
• Problem: visuomotor policies waste data modeling task-irrelevant visual variation instead of focusing on localized control-relevant cues.
• Existing approaches impose focus via preprocessing, cropping control- or object-centric regions in RGB images or point clouds.
• Key insight: intermediate CNN features already preserve useful localized context, but standard pooling fails to aggregate it.
• FocusPool: attention pooling that weights intermediate CNN features by relevance to the robot's current proprioceptive state.
• Pooled representation captures task-progressive, control-relevant local information and feeds directly into policy learning.
• Evaluated in simulation and real-world experiments: +36.2% success over pooling methods, +41.2% over explicit local-focus methods.
• New: no input cropping needed, and only 5.8% of encoder parameters are trained.

PAtsmTswIr.text:
• Problem: contact-rich teleoperation logs record robot execution (E), leader command (C), or both; policy I/O choice matters.
• E2E policies may discard command offsets that generate contact; E2C keeps offsets but ignores the robot's execution response.
• Key idea: Dual-State Conditioning (EC2C) conditions on both execution and command, then predicts future commands.
• Command-execution mismatch serves as a cue for contact, latency, payload, and operator compensation, often force-correlated.
• Setup: low-cost real robot, with no force, tactile, or motor-current inputs to the policy.
• Results: EC2C beats E2E and a strong E2C baseline on contact-rich, force-sensitive, and dynamic tasks.
• Also new: latency-adaptive inpainting for action chunking, plus analysis of when long histories help or confound.

foRrdaQ3mz.text:
• Problem: zero-shot object navigation without fine-tuning or pre-built maps, in cluttered, occluded real-world scenes.
• Gap: simulation-strong methods degrade in reality; single-scene inference over large unseen regions is brittle and unsafe.
• Key idea: reason at inference time over multiple trajectory-conditioned imagined 3D futures instead of one map.
• Method: a 3D world model predicts hypothetical observations along candidate paths, keeping plausible scene realizations in superposition.
• An adaptive occluder-aware sampler focuses imagination on uncertainty-critical regions; a Future-Aware Value Map aggregates futures for action selection.
• Setup: simulation experiments plus a physical Unitree Go2 quadruped in occlusion-heavy scenarios.
• Results: outperforms strong ZSON baselines in hidden-target discovery and risk-aware waypoint selection; the abstract reports no numbers.

VEsQVsxMMw.text:
• Problem: large-scale, high-quality robot training data is costly to collect and covers few real-world environments.
• Key idea: Compositional Simulation combines classical and neural simulation to generate accurate, realistic action-video pairs.
• Method: a closed-loop real-sim-real pipeline expands a small set of real demonstrations into large, diverse datasets.
• A neural simulator converts classical simulation videos into realistic footage while keeping actions physically accurate.
• Setup: policies are trained on the generated data and evaluated on real-world tasks.
• Results: the authors report a significantly smaller sim2real gap and higher real-world success rates; the abstract gives no numbers.
• What's new: a hybrid classical-plus-neural simulation offering a scalable path to robust real-world robot training data.

JKoP9L6myQ.text:
• Problem: latent action pretraining entangles transition extent and transition mode in a single unstructured representation.
• Key idea: PoLAR gives latent actions polar structure, with radius encoding extent and direction encoding mode.
• Method: temporal gap between observation pairs serves as a weak proxy for extent; larger gaps map to larger radii.
• Geometry: latents are embedded in hyperbolic space, whose volume grows with radius to fit more diverse modes.
• Setup: evaluated with in-task and large-scale pretraining, in simulation and real-world robot experiments.
• Results: outperforms latent action baselines and strong pretrained VLAs; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Takeaway: latent action space geometry is a key design choice for transferring visual pretraining to robot policies.

WeNTfF2Rks.text:
• Problem: long-horizon, contact-rich tasks like GPU-into-PCIe seating need millimeter precision plus generalization to new tasks.
• Classical pipelines are precise but brittle; end-to-end policies generalize but lose precision out-of-distribution.
• Key idea: complex manipulation emerges from composing simple, independent behaviors instead of rigid pipelines or monolithic policies.
• Semantic behavior uses foundation models to extract spatial constraints; predictive behavior tracks keypoints in imagined videos.
• Reactive behavior provides compliant corrections through high-frequency tactile reflexes; one composition operator fuses all outputs continuously.
• Evaluated on 8 real-world tasks spanning everyday manipulation and precision assembly, with no retraining on new data.
• Largest gains in contact-rich assembly and object transfer; robust recovery from manual perturbations during execution.

03qRtmw4qx.text:
• Latent action models learn pseudo-actions from internet video, but reconstruction objectives entangle motion with background and shortcuts.
• Resulting latents leak scene identity, decouple norms from motion magnitude, and weaken transfer and policy supervision.
• Key idea: AC-LAM imposes explicit algebraic structure, requiring latent actions to compose additively over time.
• Additivity holds for rigid-body motion but is violated by many nuisance signals, filtering them out.
• Theory: this single constraint induces identity, inverse, and cycle-consistency, and discourages scene-constant and goal-only offsets.
• A new diagnostic suite shows AC-LAM latents are displacement-calibrated, with markedly less scene-identity leakage than prior LAMs.
• Consistent downstream policy gains in simulated and real-robot tabletop manipulation, in and out of distribution.

mru8iHzSqR.text:
• Problem: RL fails on legged tasks where most exploration episodes terminate early, yielding little gradient signal.
• Key idea: Actuator Dynamics Curriculum starts with high joint stiffness, annealing toward system-identified values.
• Annealing is triggered as completed episode lengths grow, gradually restoring realistic actuator dynamics.
• Theory via cart-pole: higher critically damped actuator frequency enlarges the viability kernel, reducing policy-gradient sample complexity.
• Kernel monotonicity validated on cart-pole; curriculum applied to Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal-to-handstand transition.
