• Handstand fails under fixed identified stiffness but succeeds in simulation across 10 seeds and transfers to hardware.
• New: simulated actuator dynamics as a curriculum axis for termination-bottlenecked, not reward-bottlenecked, exploration.

EAeJdjpDzM.text:
• Diffusion policies generate distributionally valid grasps and trajectories that may still be physically infeasible on real robots.
• This embodiment gap, from reachability, collision, and executability violations, blocks zero-shot transfer across robot embodiments.
• Key idea: frame diffusion guidance as constrained optimization performed at inference time, with no retraining.
• Method replaces the backward-process sampling perturbation with an optimized correction that stays close to the learned prior.
• Supports hard constraints or soft penalties, evaluated on dexterous grasping and dynamic manipulation across multiple robots.
• Matches the feasibility of projection and gradient guidance baselines while better preserving grasp quality and controller executability.
• Task success improves up to 20pp on dexterous grasping and 23pp on visuomotor manipulation over the best baseline.

RRl1xXZLdM.text:
• Precise assembly with multi-fingered hands is contact-rich and sparse-reward, hampering imitation learning and RL.
• Prior work relied on specialized grippers, tool attachments, and environment fixtures to make assembly tractable.
• Key idea: robots should first learn through task-agnostic play before perfecting precise assembly.
• Play2Perfect: RL pretraining on diverse objects and goals, learning grasping, in-hand reorientation, pose reaching.
• Finetuning focuses exploration on final contact-rich, high-precision interactions; studies object diversity, objective, trajectories, goal precision.
• Prior is 33x more sample-efficient than RL from scratch, even with dense multi-stage rewards.
• Zero-shot sim-to-real: 60% on 0.5 mm-clearance insertions, over 50% on multi-part assembly and screwing.

FKKr8jKS29.text:
• Problem: robots grasp scene semantics but cannot predict how articulated objects like drawers and doors move.
• Key idea: MoMa-SG builds semantic-kinematic 3D scene graphs linking semantics, geometry, and kinematics of articulated scenes.
• Method: segments interactions in RGB-D sequences, tracks motion with occlusion-robust point tracking, then lifts trajectories to 3D.
• Novel unified twist estimation recovers revolute and prismatic joint parameters in a single optimization pass.
• Finds contained objects by reasoning over parent-child relations when containers are in identified opening states.
• New Arti4D-Semantic dataset: 62 in-the-wild RGB-D sequences, 600 interactions, three observation paradigms, parent-child and axis labels.
• Evaluated on two datasets with ablations; a quadruped and mobile manipulator robustly manipulated articulated objects in real homes.

PniGejQAdF.text:
• Problem: general-purpose robots need decision-making models that generalize across diverse tasks and environments.
• Most robot foundation models extend multimodal LLMs with action outputs, forming vision-language-action (VLA) systems.
• Key idea: use large-scale video pretraining as the primary modality, since videos capture physical state-action dynamics.
• Authors curate an internet-scale dataset of human activity and task demonstration videos for training.
• First open, foundation-scale video model for robot planning; generates zero-shot video plans converted into executable actions.
• Evaluated on third-party selected in-the-wild tasks and real robots; abstract reports no quantitative results.
• Shows strong instruction following and robust generalization; model and dataset publicly released for reproducible research.

X7QOq3QotA.text:
• Problem: quadruped locomotion policies fail on robots with different mass, kinematics, joint limits, or actuation, forcing retraining.
• Insight: shared critics average incompatible value targets across embodiments, producing miscalibrated advantages that hurt transfer.
• Method: MorFiC conditions the critic multiplicatively on a morphology latent, replacing additive conditioning used in PPO baselines.
• Setup: single source robot with morphology randomization in simulation, trained in about 2 hours.
• Results: zero-shot transfer to seven robots; 1.98 m/s on AlienGo versus below 0.65 m/s for additive PPO.
• Matches or beats scaling baselines that need tens to hundreds of training hours across many embodiments.
• New critic diagnostics: explained variance, advantage sign-flip rate, policy-gradient cosine; real Go1 and Go2 deployment without fine-tuning.

lGOsJtsr5q.text:
• Problem: real-world RL for multi-fingered hands is hampered by high-dimensional actions and costly hardware failures.
• Insight: human-in-the-loop RL discards the safety signal in an operator's decision to intervene.
• Key idea: WHIRL turns binary human interventions into forward-predictive signals for proactive risk avoidance.
• Method: latent world model with dynamics, reward, termination, and novel per-state intervention-probability heads.
• The intervention head shapes the actor, steering the policy away from states likely to trigger human takeover.
• Setup: 16-DoF LEAP Hand, covering convex/irregular grasping, prismatic manipulation, and long-horizon multi-stage tasks.
• Results: 96.7% success on complex grasping and up to 84% less step-weighted operator intervention.

MCTsPd3H0q.text:
• Human robot demos mix successes with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures, degrading behavior cloning.
• Advantage-conditioned BC helps, but thresholded advantage scores and prompt-based conditions weaken the signal.
• ALIGN directly predicts categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space, avoiding noisy thresholding.
• Conditions are injected into a DiT action expert via AdaRMS modulation fused with flow time.
• Evaluated on mixed real-robot datasets: ARX X5 bowl stacking and Franka key hanging with retry-heavy trajectories.
• Success reaches 90.0% and 56.7%, versus 56.7% and 33.3% for the strongest AC-BC baseline.
• Novelty: aligning condition estimation with action expression improves condition fidelity and vector-field separability.

v4QUDwGroQ.text:
• Problem: personalized robots must ground commands like "Find my bottle" by reasoning about object ownership.
• Challenge: ownership is rarely labeled and must be inferred from long-term human-object interaction evidence.
• Key idea: COOL autonomously learns object ownership from everyday observations while maintaining long-term spatial memory.
• Method: agent-based curiosity-driven data collection guides the robot toward the most informative locations.
• Memory upkeep: curiosity strategy also refreshes stale observations, keeping the environment model current over time.
• Setup: evaluated through offline experiments, ablation studies, and real-world robot deployments.
• Results: COOL infers ownership from real interactions, enabling ownership-conditioned navigation and tasks; the abstract reports no numbers.

n0v95NpvyY.text:
• Problem: quadrotor pursuit in clutter must jointly track evaders and avoid obstacles under intermittent visibility.
• Local distance or visibility rewards make policies myopic, causing blocked routes, unsafe maneuvers, poor future capture.
• Key idea: train non-myopic pursuit policies end-to-end through closed-loop rollouts with differentiable physics.
• Global Reachability Value (GRV): training-only value scoring future capture potential, guiding policy toward obstacle-aware states.
• Visibility-Gated Residual Belief (VGRB): Kalman motion prior plus visibility-gated residual predictor estimates occluded target states.
• Simulation: 89.65%, 86.52%, 76.04% capture rates with zero collisions across three cluttered scenarios.
• Ablations confirm GRV cuts myopic route failures, VGRB improves occlusion estimation; validated in Gazebo and real-world.

FFB8qNJwV2.text:
• Problem: chunked VLA control trades smoothness from long chunks against reactivity from frequent, discontinuous replanning.
• Key idea: rolling denoising keeps a persistent action buffer with staggered flow timesteps instead of regenerating chunks.
• Each step denoises the full horizon with the latest observation, executes the cleanest block, appends fresh noise.
• Executed actions are thus refined across multiple recent observations while long-horizon context is preserved.
• Dual decoupling separates sensing, VLM encoding, DiT denoising, and execution for high-frequency, real-time action streaming.
• Evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0 simulation and real bimanual and dynamic tasks across multiple robot platforms.
• Beats frequent-replanning and asynchronous baselines: higher success, lower reaction latency, smoother trajectories (abstract gives no numbers).

dYOnmedjXv.text:
• Problem: dexterous teleoperation depends on retargeting human hand motions to feasible, intuitive robot hand motions.
• Existing methods need hand-crafted objectives, precise calibration, or global human-robot hand shape matching.
• Consequence: prior retargeting needs hand-specific tuning and transfers unreliably across different dexterous hands.
• AnyDexRT: calibration-free retargeting for intuitive teleoperation across human-like dexterous hands.
• Method: self-supervised fingertip correspondence plus few-shot human guidance anchoring task-relevant regions; contact classifier refines pinches.
• Setup: evaluated on diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks against prior retargeting methods.
• Results: better retargeting quality, less manual tuning, more intuitive, efficient control; abstract reports no specific numbers.

xHjEeyHkhY.text:
• Problem: image-based and dense 3D world models drift in shape over multi-step rollouts.
• Cause: they learn rigid-object geometry preservation implicitly, without enforcing object-level rigid motion.
• Key idea: ORD-WM models object-centric rigid dynamics, separating persistent object geometry from pose changes.
• Method: SDF-supervised vector-neuron VAE encodes each object point cloud as 3D vector latent features.
• An action-conditioned dynamics model predicts per-object SE(3) increments, applied analytically to latents.
• Setup: closed-loop model predictive control with real-time replanning, in simulated and real-world manipulation.
• Results: stable, geometry-preserving multi-step prediction and efficient replanning; the abstract reports no numbers.

IbO5qWFXuh.text:
• Problem: dexterous grasping in clutter demands high-dimensional hand coordination under complex object-environment constraints.
• New benchmark: one of the largest grasp simulation benchmarks, around 0.5B annotations, eight hands, ~50K objects.
• Key idea: T(R,O) Grasp++, a scalable diffusion-based framework for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp synthesis.
• Setup: a single model generates grasps for eight different dexterous hands in cluttered scenes.
• Results: 88% average grasp success across eight embodiments, significantly outperforming existing baselines.
• Efficiency: only 0.3s inference latency and over 10x better inference sample efficiency.
• What's new: cross-embodiment dexterous grasping scaled to clutter with large data and fast diffusion inference.

jAbjN3n1jr.text:
• Problem: visuomotor policies rely on external cameras, causing blind spots, occlusion fragility, and calibration constraints.
• Key idea: replace external views with onboard egocentric depth sensing for collision-free motion planning.
• Method: sparse readings from distributed depth sensors fused into a structured, obstacle-aware point cloud.
• Policy: flow matching generative model jointly optimizing goal-reaching and collision avoidance objectives.
• Setup: trained entirely in simulation on over 100K safety-critical trajectories, no real-world fine-tuning.
• Results: zero-shot sim-to-real transfer; beats external-view and voxelized-planning baselines in simulation and hardware.
• What's new: stable, safe motion planning using only egocentric perception, removing dependence on external cameras.

gUSryIAaeN.text:
• Problem: SFT-trained VLA policies drift off demonstration manifold on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks, compounding errors.
• Key idea: reuse autonomous rollouts before human takeover as signed evidence, not just interventions as demos.
• Hindsight keypoint splits rollouts into recoverable chunks to preserve and failure-inducing chunks to reject.
• Human takeover segments provide verified recovery chunks, imitated with standard flow-matching.
• Negative-aware flow-matching: lagged-reference repulsion suppresses failed chunks relative to the policy snapshot that generated them.
• On 14-DoF dual-arm platform, three tasks: success rises from 8.3% to 35.0% over SFT, same budget.
• Ablations: rollout negatives and human recoveries give complementary gains; SFT preservation mainly stabilizes updates.

q1q252TIt0.text:
• Problem: force-aware VLAs treat force as a constant input channel, ignoring when force actually matters.
• Key idea: VLAs need an intermediate force-relevance mechanism deciding when and how strongly force influences actions.
• Method: VLM-based implicit force reasoning uses learnable force-query tokens to produce a force-admission signal.
• This vision-language-grounded signal modulates a separate tokenized force pathway feeding robot action generation.
• Setup: real-world experiments on two robotic platforms across five contact-rich manipulation tasks.
• Results: 20.8% average success rate improvement over the strongest force-aware baseline.
• New: visualizations show phase-dependent force admission, with force gated by task context, not always on.

JWkaXdmqKb.text:
• Problem: perceptive humanoid locomotion fails over kilometer-scale walks due to compounding perception-action errors.
• Causes: lossy dense terrain maps blur critical edges; myopic imitation lacks trajectory-level credit assignment.
• SOLO: end-to-end policy using only one noisy chest-mounted depth camera plus proprioception.
• Query Reconstructor retrieves precise per-cell spatial evidence, preserving sharp terrain edges like stair lips.
• TA-MSE Distillation adds next-state teacher disagreement to RL reward, penalizing actions causing future divergence.
• Zero-shot real humanoid: continuous 1.5 km outdoor walk over natural stairs, slopes, unstructured terrain.
• Results: terrain estimation error cut up to 4x; sparse-foothold success raised from 3% to 96%.

Q53ayGo2IE.text:
• Problem: long-horizon streaming 3D mapping needs accurate pose and geometry under bounded memory and computation.
• Streaming feed-forward models anchor poses to the first frame, causing train-test mismatch and drift.
• Key idea: treat reconstruction as current-centric local measurement prediction, not persistent global-gauge regression.
• Method: predicts window-relative poses and local pointmaps in the current-frame coordinate system at each step.
• Image-only cached pose-query Transformer reuses visual evidence while keeping pose reasoning transient.
• Motion graph, loop-closure reinsertion, and motion averaging fuse local predictions into a coherent global reconstruction.
• Beats streaming baselines on indoor, outdoor, driving, and RGB-D benchmarks; abstract reports no specific numbers.

GeL3GdwSYo.text:
• Problem: agentic Code-as-Policy robots learn reusable skills only after explicit task instructions, staying purely task-driven.
• Key idea: self-directed play as a continual skill-learning stage before downstream tasks arrive.
• Method: RATs, a Robotics Agent Team that proposes novel yet learnable exploratory tasks during play.
• RATs plans, executes, verifies, diagnoses failures, retries, and distills successes into a persistent code skill library.
• Setup: evaluated on held-out downstream tasks in LIBERO-PRO and MolmoSpaces against no-play and random-play baselines.
• Results: +20.6 points on LIBERO-PRO and +17.0 on MolmoSpaces over CaP-Agent0.
• New: play-learned skills plug into other Code-as-Policy agents via retrieval, +8.9 points on RoboSuite without finetuning.

9w3PEC3XLg.text:
• Human hand-object demos offer dense reference motions for dexterous RL, but naive retargeting loses interaction structure.
• Pose-only retargeting causes contact and feasibility artifacts that propagate into downstream RL policy training.
• TopoRetarget preserves task-relevant local hand-object topology using a single parameter set across diverse conditions.
• Builds a sparse interaction graph over hand and object keypoints for interaction-centric retargeting.
• Optimizes distance-weighted Laplacian deformation with directional consistency, kinematic constraints, and penetration handling.
• Best contact precision and alignment on ContactPose; Pen-Spin training success up 40.6 points over baselines.
• Policies transfer zero-shot to Wuji Hand hardware for cube reorientation and pen spinning.

v24DO7JOuN.text:
• Problem: 3D robotic world models struggle with heterogeneous dynamics across diverse object interactions.
• Key idea: route dynamics through rigid, deformable, and prehensile regimes using a mixture of motion experts.
• Method: regime-specific motion experts share one encoder backbone, keeping physics-specific inductive biases in one model.
• Setup: 1B-parameter model trained on Isaac Sim simulation plus real-world robot interaction data.
• Control: integrated with Model Predictive Control to solve diverse manipulation tasks with a single unified model.
• Results: consistently better prediction on rigid, deformable, and prehensile benchmarks; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• What's new: one multi-physics 3D world model yields stronger real-world MPC manipulation performance.

ar3eWq6mh4.text:
• Problem: human-in-the-loop RL for real-world manipulation needs frequent human corrections, making it costly and hard to scale.
• Key idea: UniIntervene, an agentic model that detects unproductive exploration and autonomously steers policies toward high-value states.
• Value estimation: predicts the latent future consequence of each action, then scores its value for stable progress signals.
• Trigger: a temporal value-risk critic intervenes when estimated value shows sustained stagnation or degradation.
• Recovery: retrieves high-value targets from past intervention memory; a goal-conditioned policy outputs executable corrective actions.
• Results: 8.6% higher average success and 57% fewer human interventions than state-of-the-art HiL-RL baselines on diverse real-world tasks.
• What's new: intervention shifts from passive human correction to autonomous, value-aware recovery, enabling more scalable real-world RL.

RAA96LpIxJ.text:
• Problem: dexterous manipulation needs perception spanning pre-contact approach, contact initiation, and post-contact control.
• Key idea: FingerEye provides continuous vision-tactile fingertip feedback throughout the entire manipulation interaction.
• Sensor: binocular RGB fingertip cameras combined with a compliant contact interface for pre- and post-contact perception.
• Pre-contact: close-range visual cues and implicit stereo enable precise approach and object localization.
• Post-contact: marker-tracked deformation of the compliant ring serves as a proxy for contact wrench sensing.
• Learning: real-and-sim infrastructure, policy-interface study, FingerEye Policy with group-structured fusion reducing modality shortcuts.
• Results: across seven contact-sensitive tasks, beats wrist-only policies by 30+ points mean success, sim and real.

JwpvRd730L.text:
• Problem: sudden motor failures severely degrade quadruped locomotion in dynamic, unstructured environments.
• Prior fault-tolerant control relies on explicit fault detection or handcrafted recovery, limiting responsiveness and generalization.
• Key idea: pain-inspired RL where reward constraints force the policy to use actuator-health cues from an ontology-sense module.
• This pushes the robot toward safer, more protective behaviors when faults occur, enabling zero-shot adaptation.
• A failure-probability curriculum gradually raises motor-failure likelihood during training to improve robustness.
• Tested on weakened-motor and locked-joint faults in Isaac Gym and on real quadruped hardware.
• Achieves lower velocity-tracking error than the SOTA reference in all fault categories; abstract gives no exact numbers.

j5QcZcRrda.text:
• Problem: fast quadrotor flight through clutter, where standard cameras suffer motion blur and high latency.
• Event cameras offer high temporal resolution, low latency, and low power, but simulating events is computationally expensive.
• Key idea: Approximate Imitation Learning trains event-based policies without rendering events during online training.
• Method: learn a task-specific representation space from a large-scale offline event dataset.
• Policy is then trained online using only lightweight simulated state information, mapped into the learned representation space.
• Setup: end-to-end network maps single event camera data directly to quadrotor control commands, no standard camera.
• Results: beats standard imitation learning baselines in simulation; real-world cluttered flights reach speeds up to 9.8 m/s.

e9OQ6xsma9.text:
• Problem: humanoid VLAs lose track of task objects across movement, contact, occlusion, and recovery in long-horizon tasks.
• Framed as object-state divergence: state conditioning actions differs from state used to verify outcomes.
• Key idea: Persistent Object Tokenization (POT) keeps role-indexed 3D object records built from RGB-D observations.
• POT-VLA: same object records condition a whole-body action expert and drive geometric predicate checks.
• Result: closed-loop execution where object state is both actionable and verifiable, unlike direct VLA control.
• Unitree G1, eight real-world task families: 71/80 successes versus 39/80 for matched GR00T-N1.7 baseline.
• Being-0-aligned service tasks: 44/50 versus reported 37/50; largest gains on maintained 3D relations.

G6vrRbO3NE.text:
• Problem: dashcam driver alerting must warn early under partial observability while avoiding frequent nuisance alerts.
• Limitation: prior work reduces alerting to thresholded binary risk prediction, even when visual evidence is incomplete.
• Key idea: VLAlert frames alerting as a tri-action policy over Silent, Observe, and Alert.
• Observe acts as an internal evidence-gathering state, deferring uncertain warnings and adapting the next observation window.
• Method: a 4B VLM generates structured safety-evidence spans; pooled hidden states serve as belief representations.
• Setup: new VLAlert-Bench per-tick benchmark plus DAUS, scoring ranking, coverage, false-alert burden, and lead-time utility.
• Results: best overall operating-point utility versus video and VLM baselines; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

qvOl1xOUtn.text:
• Problem: manipulation policies rarely anticipate and evaluate action consequences before physical execution.
• Key idea: one video-action world model unifying policy learning, video prediction, and action evaluation.
• Shared video diffusion backbone jointly predicts future visual latents and continuous action chunks.
• Action-conditioned simulator rolls candidate actions into multi-view futures with dense task-progress scores.
• Trained on ~27,300 hours: teleoperation, UMI-style data, egocentric human videos, rollout and failure trajectories.
• Test-time compute: sample candidates, rank by re-denoising consistency, rectify weak ones via simulator.
• Improves average performance over baselines on long-horizon, fine-grained tasks; abstract reports no exact numbers.

yaYM35u9Su.text:
• Problem: teleoperated demonstrations mix quality, with hesitations and recoveries that degrade imitation learning at scale.
• Prior progress reward models rely on noisy absolute-time labels or costly human subtask annotations.
• Key idea: WARP learns signed relative progress fully self-supervised from successful demonstrations only.
• Method: time-warp augmentations (speed changes, reversals) train WARP-RM to predict normalized elapsed time between frames.
• WARP-BC aggregates per-frame rewards into chunk advantages, upweighting high-advantage action chunks during behavior cloning.
• Setup: bimanual robot folds T-shirts from crumpled starts; dataset quality varied using episode length.
• Results: with lower-quality data, WARP-BC keeps 19/20 success versus vanilla BC's 2/20, with up to 18x throughput.

dhh4gmm3NK.text:
• Problem: reactive humanoid-human interaction remains open; controllers ignore partners or handle only static objects and scenes.
• Challenges: hard-to-design interaction rewards, retargeting losing inter-person contacts, and occlusion breaking close-range perception.
• Key idea: REACT scales humanoid-human interaction learning to large corpora of human-human motion-capture demonstrations.
• Vision-language model detects plausible spatio-temporal contacts; contact-preserving retargeting maps demonstrations onto humanoid-partner geometry.
• Privileged-state teacher with contact reward is distilled into ego-depth student using realistic rendered human partners.
• Generative human-pose-estimation auxiliary loss handles multimodal, ambiguous close-range perception under occlusion and out-of-view partners.
• Real Unitree G1 performs diverse contact-rich interactions, significantly beating an external pose-estimation baseline; abstract gives no numbers.

FLxpmRskLG.text:
• Problem: most robot data collection pipelines lack force/torque data needed to learn active compliant policies.
• Key idea: UME, an upper-limb exoskeleton giving real-time haptic torque feedback during teleoperation.
• Records whole-arm configurations and joint torque signals; low-cost, lightweight, and portable.
• Transparent feedback lets blindfolded operators unsheathe kinematically constrained objects using touch alone.
• Embedded IMU enables mobile manipulation; universal retargeting drives OpenArm, Franka, and X-ARM robots.
• Learned bimanual, whole-body compliant policies achieve high success; abstract reports no specific success-rate numbers.
• Tasks: long-horizon mobile manipulation, force-based box flipping, occluded box pushing, space-constrained tabletop manipulation.

cfzFrOJmKA.text:
• Problem: robot learning suffers from morphological diversity across embodiments and scarce robot data.
• Key idea: treat human interaction traces as a universal "mother tongue" for physical skills.
• Data: 35,000-hour pre-training corpus spanning human demonstrations and 30 robotic embodiments.
• Unified action space maps human hand motion and robot controls into semantically aligned slots.
• Mixture-of-Flow separates shared motor primitives from embodiment-specific action experts within Mixture-of-Transformers.
• Manifold-Preserving Gating handles sensory shift; Universal Async Chunking handles varying latencies and control rates.
• Results: state-of-the-art on LIBERO and RoboCasa, strong cross-embodiment transfer across five real robots.

ddzWaOmWZE.text:
• Problem: VLA models assume static scenes, so latency makes them fail when objects move during execution.
• Key idea: AHEAD, a predict-then-act wrapper that adds a motion-aware latent world model to a frozen VLA.
• Method: small world model forecasts future patch tokens in VLA feature space using optical-flow velocity and acceleration.
• Language-and-motion saliency mask focuses prediction; adaptive horizon halts when prediction uncertainty crosses a threshold.
• Setup: frozen 7B OpenVLA plus only 4.9M parameters; decoder receives predicted future tokens instead of current ones.
• Simulation: 79–97% success across 20 dynamic scenarios versus 31–58% for the strongest baseline.
• Real xArm 7: 29–30/30 on conveyor and rolling-ball tasks, 23/30 paddle, 19/30 projectile catching where baselines scored 0/30.

z5cgS0XgeK.text:
• Problem: VLM-based manipulation policies rely on 2D RGB, ignoring manipulation's inherently 3D nature.
• They also lack 3D alignment across inputs, outputs, robot embodiments, camera setups, and datasets.
• Key idea: aligned vertex maps and vertex spectra lift 2D pixels to 3D via calibration, optional depth.
• Per-pixel 3D inputs and robot actions are expressed in one shared coordinate frame.
• A canonical Bird's-Eye-View frame yields BEV images, giving view-invariant inputs robust to camera pose changes.
• Data pipeline adds temporal alignment of trajectories across robots, human operators, and datasets.
• Abstract reports improved real-world consistency and generalization, but no numbers; code, data, checkpoints promised.

FGyOl5tNGl.text:
• Problem: VLA policies struggle with dexterous grasping among visually identical, densely packed same-category objects.
• Visible object masks as prompts don't guarantee the policy keeps attention on the target instance.
• FOCUS turns masks into training-time alignment signals internalized by the action pathway via self-distillation.
• Mask-derived bias in action-expert cross-attention is distilled into a bias-free pathway used at inference.
• A lightweight progress query token triggers sub-task termination, enabling sequential multi-object grasping.
• Real robot: 67.5% average success, beating four VLA baselines by at least 26.9 points, up to +34.6.
• Generalizes to unseen categories (58.4%) and unseen lighting (60.1%), where all baselines stay below 31%.

sF3YZbbTNX.text:
• Problem: open-vocabulary long-horizon manipulation needs flexible reasoning, multi-object scenes, monitoring, and failure recovery.
• Key idea: Physical Orchestration, where timing of decisions and tool calls matters because the world never pauses.
• Method: VoLoAgent, a VLM in a closed agent loop orchestrating heterogeneous robot capabilities as interruptible tools.
• It plans, monitors, and recovers, steering a VLA/WAM mid-rollout alongside vision models and action primitives.
• Setup: new RoboVoLo high-fidelity benchmark covering common sense, memory/state tracking, complex references, world knowledge.
• RoboVoLo reports task-level success plus failure-mode diagnostics; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
• Results: VoLoAgent substantially outperforms single VLA/VLM and tool-based systems, validated in real-robot experiments.

suRtJLXVxI.text:
• Problem: human videos show rich dexterous manipulation but lack tactile signals crucial for contact-rich robot tasks.
• Key idea: use simulation as a tactile completion engine, recovering contact information missing from human videos.
• Method: reconstruct hand-object interactions from monocular human demos in physics simulation to obtain tactile supervision.
• Policies: train visual-tactile teacher policies, then distill into deployable point-cloud plus tactile sensing student policies.
• Setup: zero-shot sim-to-real on dexterous hand-arm platforms, covering grasping and contact-rich tool-use tasks.
• Results: teacher reaches 65.9% average success over eight sim tasks; real cube picking 53%, table cleaning 23%.
• What's new: table cleaning is not achieved by existing general sim-to-real systems, suggesting a path to learning from Internet-scale video.

BxW31Dilgn.text:
• Problem: generalist robots usually rely on scaling teleoperation data to train end-to-end VLA policies.
• Key idea: a VLM coding agent writes robot programs from a curated perception, planning, and control library.
• Harness packages multi-step perception and action procedures into callable tools, guided by a plan-act-replan loop.
• Visual and execution feedback verify outcomes and trigger recovery from failures during task execution.
• Results: zero-shot, matches or surpasses state-of-the-art VLAs on tabletop tasks and handles diverse mobile manipulation.
• Ablations: larger tool libraries raise average task progress only with the full harness, not alone.
• New: needs no new teleoperation data or VLA tool, offering an agentic axis complementary to data scaling.

trTMmn2U1g.text:
• Problem: natural whole-body humanoid interaction control is limited by costly whole-body teleoperation data.
• Key idea: ZeroWBC learns interaction from human egocentric videos with synchronized whole-body motion and text, no teleoperation.
• Method: generation-then-tracking, where a fine-tuned VLM maps egocentric image plus instruction to future human motion tokens.
• Motion tokens are decoded into continuous motion, retargeted to the humanoid, then executed by a general tracking policy.
• New interaction-oriented tracking reward prioritizes root and key body-part trajectories while preserving natural whole-body motion.
• Setup: static-scene interaction tasks evaluated on a real Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
• Results: diverse scene-aware behaviors without any robot teleoperation demos; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.

LoGyKMEVVc.text:
• Problem: dexterous demos lose fidelity via retargeting, or need costly robot-specific teleoperation lacking intuitive contact-aware control.
• Key idea: wearable interface sharing one dexterous end-effector module between data collection and robot deployment.
• Module integrates lightweight dexterous hand, in-hand camera, and fingertip tactile sensing.
• Palm-side isomorphic glove maps human fingers to robot-hand joints: real-time, retargeting-free, precise control.
• Zero-gap data: matched in-hand vision, tactile signals, contacts, and actions across collection and deployment.
• Eight real-robot tasks: fine-grained, contact-rich, long-horizon, bimanual; policies average 88.75% success.
• Policies generalize to unseen initial poses and transfer across three robot embodiments.

sIYfeRhQrn.text:
• Problem: Hamilton-Jacobi safety analysis scales poorly to high-dimensional robots like humanoids.
• Prior discounted safety Bellman methods rely on fixed one-step updates, limiting value learning quality.
• Key idea: λ-Reachability estimates safety value via stochastic multi-step rollouts with geometrically distributed horizons.
• Like TD(λ), it interpolates between local one-step consistency and long-horizon max-over-trajectory safety targets.
• Unlike TD(λ), the terminal safety value is used only with probability δ, enabling contraction for δ<1.
• Theory: as λ→1, the estimator recovers the undiscounted reachability objective.
• Simulated and real humanoid tests under balance and collision constraints beat one-step baselines; abstract reports no numbers.

oJTM5ysEeJ.text:
• Problem: olfaction is underexplored in embodied AI; prior machine olfaction mostly targets semantic odor perception.
• Key idea: OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation.
• Method: augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS).
• Setup: agents navigate photorealistic indoor scenes using both visual observations and olfactory measurements.
• Tasks: two source-seeking scenarios, early-stage fire localization and invisible gas-leak localization.
• Baseline policy: multimodal reinforcement learning agent integrating vision and smell over time.
• Results: policy substantially outperforms diverse baselines; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

hf8X30fAtz.text:
• Problem: humanoids are trained as solitary agents and cannot physically coordinate with human partners who anticipate and adjust.
• Key idea: Social Humanoid generates socially responsive whole-body robot motion conditioned on a human partner's motion.
• Method: hierarchical system with a high-level motion generation policy and a low-level whole-body tracking controller.
• Shared-codebook VQ-VAE tokenizes human and humanoid motion into one latent space for cross-embodiment generation.
• A Diffusion Forcing Transformer generates humanoid motion tokens conditioned on the human partner's motion.
• Two-phase adaptive retargeting preserves contact, reachability, and body scale, yielding a 260-hour HHI benchmark from five datasets.
• Results: coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interactions in simulation and on a real 29-DoF Unitree G1.

kCeFEyLOuW.text:
• Problem: online RL for flow-based VLAs is hard because multi-step solvers make action likelihoods difficult to access.
• NFT-style likelihood-free updates help, but trajectory-level rewards give noisy, misaligned credit to action chunks.
• Full-space mirrored comparisons ignore robot action geometry, and updates may drift toward suboptimal behavior-sampled actions.
• Key idea: PAWN, a unified NFT-style framework built on structured local preference optimization for flow-based policies.
• Method: lifts solver-step density comparisons into chunk-path scores, yielding implicit chunk-level preference signals.
• PAWN also groups mirrored evidence into SE(3)-aware motion modes and uses conditional pair guidance toward better continuations.
• On manipulation benchmarks, PAWN beats online RL baselines in adaptation efficiency, success, and OOD robustness; abstract gives no numbers.

hFLtQusqPy.text:
• Problem: humanoid badminton demands split-second decisions, precise striking, and whole-body balance against nonlinear shuttlecock trajectories.
• Challenge: human badminton data is scarce and imperfect; pure RL returns shots but yields unnatural, hard-to-deploy motions.
• Key idea: a three-stage hierarchical framework combining human motion priors with task-driven reinforcement learning.
• Stage 1 learns a compact latent skill space from retargeted human badminton demonstrations.
• Stages 2-3 optimize skill composition via RL, then regularize with a context-conditioned adversarial latent prior.
• Real humanoid deployment: multi-skill play with human players, including sustained rallies and jump smashes.
• New: first real-world humanoid jump smash in racket sports; abstract reports no quantitative success rates.

VY6U0drX88.text:
• Problem: autoregressive discrete VLAs decode slowly and largely ignore the temporal structure of action trajectories.
• Parallel-decoding VLAs gain speed but lack explicit mechanisms for modeling dependencies between action tokens.
• Key idea: TBD-VLA applies block diffusion to discrete action tokens for temporally structured action generation.
• Method: action sequences split into temporal blocks; masked discrete diffusion within blocks, autoregression across blocks.
• Unifies temporal autoregression with parallel decoding, improving both temporal coherence and inference speed.
• New: explicit temporal modeling enables asynchronous chunk execution, like Real-Time Chunking, via temporal in-painting.
• Results: significantly outperforms prior VLAs on simulated and real-world manipulation; abstract reports no specific numbers.

c9tCcHtVcS.text:
• Problem: diffusion trajectory models capture multimodal futures, but uncertainty requires costly Monte Carlo sampling.
• This sampling cost blocks real-time control, where robots must quickly assess risk and keep safety margins.
• Key idea: SCOPE, a lightweight module adding control-ready uncertainty to diffusion trajectory models.
• Method: distills score-curvature into a structured precision matrix around each nominal trajectory, avoiding repeated sampling.
• Output: calibrated Gaussian tubes with per-timestep covariances, used as occupancy predictions or exploration guides.
• Setup: pedestrian forecasting, crowd navigation, Maze2D control, and real-world Franka Panda manipulation experiments.
• Results: fast uncertainty estimation and better closed-loop performance; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

dykg3Ed5Wy.text:
• Problem: soft continuum robots lack simulators combining physical grounding, contact handling, actuation, and learning integration.
• Existing soft simulators lack contact or learning support; rigid-body approximations sacrifice physical grounding.
• Key idea: continuum-mechanics-informed discretization places tendon-driven continuum robots natively inside MuJoCo.
• Single MuJoCo pipeline unifies tendon forces, whole-body contact, and dynamics for contact-rich manipulation.
• Validated against a Cosserat rod reference, static and dynamic, plus real TDCR hardware.
• State-based imitation policies trained from sim teleoperation; zero-shot deployment on a 3-segment TDCR on a Franka arm.
• New: claimed first sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich continuum robot manipulation, across two tasks.

59kpavSqlw.text:
• Problem: household embodied benchmarks assume correct human execution, ignoring errors by cognitively impaired people and older adults.
• Key idea: monitor streaming human activity to detect and diagnose structured execution errors as early as possible.
• Method: operationalizes neuropsychology research on everyday action errors into a large-scale embodied AI benchmark.
• Setup: 20,000 paired activity episodes spanning nine neuropsychologically motivated error categories.
• Baselines: supervised sequence models and LLM prompting approaches evaluated as online error monitors.
• Results: all baselines perform poorly as error monitors, often missing when execution goes wrong.
• What's new: first error-aware testbed for assistive agents, exposing a gap in goal-inference and task-completion benchmarks.

EfJCm9am0o.text:
• Generative robot policies (diffusion, flow) capture multimodal actions but imitation learning suffers from imperfect demos and distribution shift.
• Improving them usually needs more expert data; RL finetuning is hard because policy likelihoods are intractable.
• RoboFFT: a forward-process RL framework that finetunes generative robot policies without exact likelihood estimation.
• Method: forward-noise sampled actions, then use weighted score/flow matching loss as surrogate policy ratio for PPO updates.
• Setup: popular generative robot policies on simulation benchmarks, including long-horizon planning and sparse-reward tasks.
• Results: consistent performance gains with better stability and training efficiency; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• New: integrated into a real-world RL framework, demonstrating effective finetuning on physical robot tasks.

yNHgrgATuY.text:
• Problem: action-supervised VLA fine-tuning lets visual structure irrelevant to predicted actions collapse.
• Formalized as residual visual collapse along local action fibers, i.e., among action-equivalent states.
• Key idea: FIBERTUNE preserves teacher-structured visual residuals during training, adding zero inference-time overhead.
• Method: online action probe finds action-predictive directions, filtered out of intermediate visual-token features.
• Residuals are aligned to a frozen visual teacher, with effective-rank regularization against collapse.
• Beats task-loss-only fine-tuning in all six simulation settings across two benchmarks, π0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT.
• Gains: +10.7 pp SR(5) on CALVIN ABC→D; physical SO-101 pick-place success 72.7% to 78.1%.

BXNVzGSYFe.text:
• Problem: learned dexterous grasping relies on tuned contact losses or costly contact-based test-time refinement.
• Key idea: learn grasp priors from large-scale data via flow matching, without contact losses or refinement.
• Grasps represented as all-Euclidean 3D hand keypoints, replacing mixed SE(3) pose plus joint-angle outputs.
• Keypoints share the object point cloud's frame, enabling native spatial reasoning in a simple Transformer flow model.
• Trained with only standard flow-matching loss; scales with data, model capacity, and batch size.
• Dexonomy: 76.3% success, +47.4% over best comparable baseline, 2.4 mm penetration; best on DexGrasp Anything without fine-tuning.
• Fast batched inference at 0.032 s per grasp; real-world deployment demonstrated on 20 diverse objects.

h1yqzSoZ49.text:
• Problem: human videos are abundant, but embodiment mismatch, scene variation, and robot feasibility constraints hinder transfer to robots.
• Key idea: learn reusable object-centric interaction priors from human videos, without target-task robot demonstrations.
• Representation: object-object interaction motion captures task-relevant scene changes while abstracting away embodiment-specific details.
• Method: compose learned interaction priors with robot-side feasibility reasoning and motion planning.
• Same human-derived knowledge adapts across embodiments, scene geometries, and task contexts.
• Setup: diverse manipulation settings, including real-world Franka tabletop and RBY-1 humanoid mobile robot experiments.
• Results: robust interaction-centric manipulation with zero real-world robot training data; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.

HWaigsXLaH.text:
• Problem: general humanoid whole-body control struggles with diverse motions, fast adaptation, and balance in dynamic scenarios.
• Existing methods need task-specific training or degrade when adapting to new motions.
• FAST: framework for Fast Adaptation and Stable motion Tracking, built on pretraining plus lightweight adaptation.
• Parseval-Guided Residual Policy Adaptation learns a delta action policy under orthogonality and KL constraints.
• This enables efficient adaptation to out-of-distribution motions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting of pretrained skills.
• Center-of-Mass-Aware Control adds CoM observations and objectives, improving balance on challenging reference motions.
• Simulation and real-robot tests show FAST beats state-of-the-art baselines; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

GFxjqZVSND.text:
• Multi-modal motion planning needs joint reasoning over continuous motions and discrete mode transitions, e.g., walking then grasping.
• Mixed-Integer Programming fits, but building tractable non-convex formulations is manual and domain-specific.
• M$^3$P-R1 uses reinforcement learning to fine-tune LLMs to write MIP formulations as executable Python code.
• Solver-backed code generation avoids hallucinated direct answers and yields verifiable plans.
• Outcome-driven solver reward teaches composing discretization primitives and cross-modal coupling constraints.
• New LLMM$^3$P Bench: 1,316 problems across 5 single-modal and 8 multi-modal compositions.
• Results: 91.7% single-modal and 80.9% multi-modal success, beating GPT-5.2 by 26.4/40.6 points; 87.5% on hardware.

U3Nmrhun8B.text:
• Problem: pretrained Vision-Language-Action models generalize broadly but lack the reliability needed for real-world deployment.
• Gap: prior RL ignores pretrained priors or finetunes VLAs with poor sample efficiency and success.
• Key idea: EXPO-FT enables stable, sample-efficient RL finetuning that fully leverages pretrained VLA policies.
• Tasks: string-light routing and plug insertion, pool ball striking, flower insertion into wine bottle.
• Challenges: tasks demand high precision, dynamic actions, and robustness to varied initial states.
• Results: perfect 30/30 success on all tasks with only 19.1 minutes average online robot data.
• New: outperforms RL-from-scratch and VLA finetuning baselines; open-source codebase released for broader adoption.

gTazI5D0Fj.text:
• Problem: World Action Models imagine future video at test time, causing high latency unsuitable for real-time control.
• Key idea: distill video diffusion world priors into an action model during training only.
• Method: two-stage distillation of intermediate denoising representations from a video diffusion model into actions.
• Hypothesis: a compressed low-dimensional subspace of video latents suffices to supervise action generation.
• Video model is entirely discarded at inference, leaving a lightweight action-only policy.
• Results: 95.9% average success on LIBERO, plus competitive real-world manipulation performance.
• About 21x faster inference than a representative WAM baseline, enabling real-time robotic control.

nG11dAaFIX.text:
• Problem: retrieve a target from clutter while minimizing removals of non-target objects.
• Challenge: whether an object blocks depends on the chosen grasp and execution stage, not scene clutter.
• Key idea: grasp-conditioned dependency graphs with candidate grasps as nodes and typed approach/lift blocker edges.
• Dataset: single-object intervention tests on 8,687 scene-target samples from 500 scenes, yielding 3,665,775 labeled edges.
• Method: action-centric edge-context model predicts object-grasp dependencies; short-prefix planner ranks blockers, picks grasp, replans.
• Evaluation: stored-label planning, closed-loop MuJoCo rollouts, and hardware trials validating the execution interface.
• Novelty: ties blockers to concrete grasps, separating merely surrounding objects from actual grasp blockers.

PQdtUNzQLj.text:
• Problem: humanoids in human environments face external contacts that disrupt locomotion accuracy and stability.
• Prior work relies on domain randomization, task-specific force objectives, or learned estimators, limiting transfer and OOD robustness.
• Key idea: feed policies a physically grounded, analytical whole-body disturbance observer instead of learned force estimates.
• Observer estimates residual force/torque online from known robot dynamics, without any force/torque sensors.
• Setup: Unitree G1 tested under torso perturbations, standing pushes, and asymmetric hand payloads versus proprioception-only baseline.
• Results: accurate disturbance prediction, stronger robustness, better velocity tracking even on OOD disturbances; no numbers reported.
• New: penalizing inferred lower-body joint disturbances during training encourages lighter, gentler locomotion.

pPrwDHXw93.text:
• Problem: no controlled study shows which modular VLA design choices actually drive performance and latency.
• Setup: fixed SigLIP2-So400m vision and Qwen2.5 backbone, trained on DROID, evaluated on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus.
• Method: 63 configurations varying action head decoder, loss, initialization, inference passes, and per-module scale.
• Finding 1: initializing the action head from final backbone layers adds 7.1 points at zero latency cost.
• Finding 2: the action head is the best module to scale, but only under that initialization.
• Finding 3: returns saturate near current pi-series model sizes, so scaling further wastes compute.
• Result: EffVLA (~3.75B) matches top open VLAs on LIBERO, faster, and transfers to a real SO-ARM101 arm.

s8ZiyIAn3z.text:
• Problem: self-play RL driving policies are robust in simulation but produce unnatural, non-human-like trajectories.
• Key idea: SHIFT fine-tunes a pretrained self-play foundation policy on real human driving demonstrations.
• Method: same PPO with advantage filtering, adding a reward for distance to the human expert trajectory.
• KL regularization against the frozen self-play policy preserves base performance during extended fine-tuning.
• Setup: closed-loop log-replay simulation, with the ego vehicle driven by the policy and other agents replayed.
• nuPlan Val14: ADE 9.4→8.0 m, collisions 6.4%→3.9%, brake taps 29%→20%; beats BC and BC+RL.
• First public-road test of self-play policies: 2.6× fewer safety takeovers (every 0.57→1.46 miles).

mjvsJNQuFV.text:
• Problem: legged manipulators under actuator failures risk falls, since arm-induced CoM shifts and disturbances amplify instability.
• Gap: prior fault-tolerant control targets locomotion only, ignoring coupled whole-body stability and arm reachability.
• Key idea: FT-WBC, a fault-aware whole-body controller with decoupled upper- and lower-body learned policies.
• Fault Estimator predicts faulty joints from lower-body proprioceptive history, with no extra sensors described.
• Posture Adaptation Module converts the arm policy's base posture requests into safe, executable commands given fault information.
• Results: higher survival rate and larger arm workspace under weakening or locked joint failures; abstract reports no numbers.
• Validated in simulation and with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a real legged manipulator.

da5VPQA7G7.text:
• Problem: single-robot RL navigation fails in multi-robot, human-shared spaces under occlusions and out-of-distribution scenarios.
• Key idea: couple uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting with robust multi-robot decision making.
• Forecasting: predicts future occupancy grid maps by fusing spatiotemporal features across robots.
• Policy: constrained multi-agent RL penalizes paths through predicted-occupied or highly uncertain regions.
• Novelty: uncertainty-driven costs let the policy adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shift.
• Setup: multiple Unity3D simulations, in-distribution and OOD, with varied layouts, crowd densities, and rushing pedestrians.
• Results: better prediction and safety than representative baselines; the abstract reports no numbers; real-robot tests confirm robustness.

5cXsYqAjNs.text:
• Problem: long-horizon manipulation needs joint reasoning over abstract task structure and low-level physical interaction.
• Combining VLMs with video generation enables zero-shot planning, but physics and geometry errors compound over time.
• Key idea: NovaPlan, a hierarchical framework that proposes, verifies, and repairs visual plans in closed loop.
• High level: VLM decomposes tasks, generates multiple video rollouts, and filters out dynamically inconsistent futures.
• Execution: hybrid geometric representation adaptively switches between object-centric flow and human hand flow to derive actions.
• Monitoring verifies outcomes and synthesizes non-prehensile corrections like fingertip poking when failures occur.
• Results: substantially outperforms prior zero-shot systems on multi-stage tasks; abstract gives no specific numbers.

xc8asDq7QI.text:
• Problem: tactile policies stay tied to fixed embodiments because tactile signals vary wildly across sensor hardware.
• Key idea: FTP-1, the first generalist foundation tactile policy transferring manipulation skills across sensors and embodiments.
• Method: heterogeneous encoders map image, array, and state tactile signals into unified morphology-aware latent tokens.
• A shared tactile Transformer expert jointly models these tokens across all sensor types.
• Pretraining: ~3,000 hours from 26 data sources, human and robot demos, spanning 21 tactile sensors.
• Results: +17.2% success on seen sensor setups; +31% on two unseen sensor setups, across 5 hardware configurations.
• New: first unified foundation baseline for tactile manipulation; checkpoints, datasets, and code to be released.

vG6UymddY4.text:
• Problem: visual policies from videos and demos fail in contact-rich manipulation needing force and contact feedback.
• Challenge: tactile data are costly to collect and generalize poorly across sensors, robots, and tasks.
• Key idea: policy-agnostic real-world RL adds tactile residual corrections on top of pretrained visual policies.
• Stage one: warm-start tactile-aware learning using autonomous rollouts from the visual base policy.
• Stage two: learn a lightweight tactile residual policy through online real-world interaction.
• Results: four real tasks improve from 5–40% to 85–100% success within 40–80 minutes.
• New: generalizes across contact-rich tasks, visual base policies, and tactile representations without large tactile datasets.

2qcSjfv9pr.text:
• Problem: high-DoF arm-hand dexterity is hard to discover from scratch with RL on multi-fingered robots.
• Key idea: pretrain one policy on generic object reposing, then use it as a prior for downstream tasks.
• Pretrained policy generalizes, solving the reposing phase of downstream tasks zero-shot, but naive RL fine-tuning quickly erodes it.
• Post-training: behavior-cloning distillation, frozen-actor critic warm-up, and conservative on-policy updates to limit policy drift.
• Joint configuration-space Geometric Fabric controller mediates between policy and robot, safely exploiting full kinematic dexterity.
• Teacher distilled into a stereo-RGB student that transfers zero-shot sim-to-real on a 23 DoF Kuka-Allegro.
• Results: solves contact-rich, long-horizon grasping, reorienting, and insertion across diverse initial states; abstract reports no numbers.

8gqhCYKrxR.text:
• Problem: training and evaluating robot policies in the real world is costly and hard to scale.
• SimFoundry: modular, automated, zero-shot real-to-sim scene construction from a single image or video.
• Builds sim-ready digital twins, then edits objects, scenes, and tasks to generate diverse digital cousins.
• Sim-trained policies transfer zero-shot to real multi-step, articulated-object, and bimanual manipulation tasks.
• Across 7 tasks and 5 policies, sim predicts real performance: Pearson 0.928, max ranking violation 0.018.
• Training with object, scene, and task cousins raises real zero-shot success by 17%, 21%, and 50%.
• New: one automated pipeline unifying digital twins, cousin generation, sim-to-real training, and reliable sim evaluation.

rJe0dLlPev.text:
• Problem: footwear changes foot geometry, mass, and friction, degrading locomotion policies trained for a fixed robot morphology.
• Motivation: like humans choosing boots or skates, shoes could expand legged robots' terrain capabilities.
• Key idea: freeze the simulation-trained nominal policy; fine-tune only lightweight, identity-initialized modulation modules on hardware.
• Identity initialization preserves the original behavior at the start, enabling safe and sample-efficient on-robot adaptation.
• SafeBox: a workspace-aware waypoint sampler that keeps online adaptation within a user-defined physical workspace.
• Setup: shoe-equipped Unitree Go2 in simulation, plus real-world tests with the Go2 fitted with human shoes.
• Results: under equal adaptation budgets, SHOES beats FiLM-only, Linear Adapter-only, and residual-RL baselines (abstract reports no numbers).

GseuCgLNtO.text:
• Problem: parallel-jaw grippers are cheap and robust but lack in-hand mobility, forcing large arm motions.
• Key idea: a double-belt finger module upgrades standard parallel grippers while keeping normal opening and closing.
• Adds three in-hand DoFs: object translation, pitch, and roll, driven by soft belts on the fingers.
• Designed for low-cost manufacturing and easy integration, keeping parallel-gripper reliability and precise control.
• Control: adapted model predictive controller enables in-hand manipulation of known objects.
• Lightweight teleoperation interface jointly controls arm and gripper, 10 DoFs total, with minimal hardware.
• Across teleoperation, MPC, and learned-policy tasks, it consistently beats a conventional parallel gripper in dexterity and feasibility.

LOvZujpKxN.text:
• Self-play RL drives well cheaply but converges to conventions incompatible with human drivers.
• Prior fixes like reward engineering and domain randomization are brittle and labor-intensive.
• Key idea, spiced self-play: a pinch of human data anchors self-play toward human-compatible behavior.
• Method combines 30 minutes of human driving with over 60 years of self-play simulation.
• Reward is minimal, encoding only safe goal reaching, with no hand-tuned behavioral terms.
• Results show better coordination with real human trajectories using 2,500× less data than imitation baselines.
• Full pipeline trains in 15 hours on one consumer GPU, revising assumptions about human-data scaling.

AhpH1nGaUp.text:
• Problem: generalist robot policies hold rich skills, but direct commands often fail to invoke them on novel tasks.
• Key idea: Flow Reversal Steering (FRS) maps suboptimal but reasonable actions into nearby generalist behavioral modes.
• Method: reverse the flow-matching policy to recover latent noise for given actions, then regenerate improved actions.
• Use case: converts coarse semantic guidance from humans or VLMs into effective robot actions, improving zero-shot control.
• Distillation: latent noise behavioral cloning transfers gains back into the policy in under a minute.
• Results: up to 95% absolute task success boost across extensive simulated and real-world manipulation experiments.
• New: FRS bootstraps RL with semantic priors, improving tasks where standard reinforcement learning fails.

Unsv9DsbfO.text:
• Problem: robots must imitate learned expert behavior while satisfying safety constraints and objectives specified only at inference time.
• Key idea: treat constrained trajectory generation as Bayesian posterior sampling with a pretrained policy as prior.
• An inference-time, cost-derived likelihood tilts the demonstration prior toward feasible, optimal trajectories.
• Method: extends Feynman-Kac correctors from diffusion models to deterministic flow-matching policies, requiring no retraining.
• Setup: pretrained Diffusion Policy, GR00T-N1.6, and pi0.5 checkpoints on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks.
• Results: plans around non-convex obstacles added at inference and beats base pi0.5 on zero-shot tasks.
• New: unified retraining-free posterior sampler for both diffusion and flow policies (abstract reports no specific numbers).

TscNG5Wcwn.text:
• Problem: quantifying diversity of variable-length, high-dimensional robot demonstration datasets respecting trajectory structure is hard.
• Key idea: extend Shannon and von Neumann entropy using signature kernel Gram matrices over demonstrations.
• Result: model-free entropy and diversity metrics computed directly on demonstration datasets, no policy needed.
• Method: FAKTUAL curation selects demonstration subsets maximizing entropy under a fixed subset-size budget.
• Setup: image and state-based RoboMimic and MetaWorld benchmarks, plus four real-world manipulation tasks.
• Results: consistently higher success than random selection across tasks and architectures; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• New: no rollouts or policy access, negligible overhead, far cheaper than recent robot data curation methods.

YZ4p3WbWKX.text:
• Problem: robots hear spatial language about unseen objects, but metric-semantic mapping ignores this signal.
• Multimodal foundation models reason poorly in 3D and cannot be fused easily with other sensors.
• Key idea: treat language as a sensor producing calibrated probabilistic observations of object locations.
• Language Sensor Model maps utterances plus scene-graph context to Gaussian-mixture spatial distributions.
• Mixture weights capture referential ambiguity; component covariances capture spatial uncertainty within referenced regions.
• VL-Map fuses language predictions with onboard perception in one belief map, tested on VLA-3D and a real robot.
• Only LSM stays calibrated; VL-Map puts ~70% more probability on true targets than the best foundation-model baseline.

uZalcCyrVl.text:
• Problem: humanoid loco-manipulation via visual imitation lacks diverse, high-quality full-body human-object interaction videos.
• Key idea: PRISM amplifies a handful of real videos into hundreds of diverse counterfactual training videos.
• Method: video-to-video generation creates counterfactual human-object interactions with varied objects from few exemplar real videos.
• Contact-anchored real-to-sim pipeline reconstructs human and object motions into physically plausible robot trajectories.
• Setup: single policy trained in simulation, deployed zero-shot on real humanoid using only onboard depth.
• Results: humanoid picks up, carries, drops boxes, barrels, bins, balls across novel instances, sizes, configurations.
• New: counterfactual intra-class video variability enables category-level generalization without real-world fine-tuning.

lorikYEkAx.text:
• Problem: synchronous executors pause between action chunks, which is fatal for dynamic tasks regardless of inference speed.
• Real-time chunking (RTC) enables asynchronous execution by treating chunk transitions as inpainting of committed actions.
• Flow-matching RTC relies on inference-time corrections, needing fine-tuning, heuristic guidance, and extra computation that adds latency.
• Key idea: discrete diffusion policies inpaint natively via iterative unmasking, making them natural asynchronous executors.
• DiscreteRTC needs zero extra code or fine-tuning, and early stopping provides adaptive guidance.
• Evaluated on dynamic simulated benchmarks and real-world dynamic manipulation, using about 0.7x the computation of from-scratch generation.
• Real-world hockey defend: 65% higher success than flow-matching RTC, 30% higher than training-time RTC.

587eUkwa7d.text:
• Problem: latent world models can drop safety-relevant information under partial observability, causing latent-space safe control failures.
• Failure mode one: estimation gaps, where observations never reveal safety-critical quantities like cooking temperature.
• Failure mode two: prediction gaps, where failures are visible once they happen but cannot be anticipated beforehand.
• Diagnostics: mutual-information measure of safety observability, plus rollout-based measure of future safety predictability.
• Mitigations: privileged multimodal supervision for estimation gaps, conformal risk calibration for prediction gaps.
• Setup: Franka Research 3 cooking tasks, two hardware studies with RGB, RGB+Tactile, and RGB+Thermal world models.
• Results: mitigations improve safety under partial observability but increase conservativeness; abstract reports no specific numbers.

P1R9iBKyv4.text:
• Problem: VLA models need 3D spatial understanding to perceive environments and execute manipulation actions reliably.
• Prior work directly aligns VLA features point-wise with pre-trained 3D foundation model representations.
• Finding: direct alignment acts as low-rank regularization, causing severe rank collapse in pre-trained VLA representations.
• Key idea: align pair-wise relationships between features instead of enforcing point-wise feature equality.
• Method: relational representation alignment injects 3D spatial awareness while preserving the VLA's original expressivity.
• Evaluated on public benchmarks, a new spatial reasoning benchmark, and real-world manipulation; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Results: robust performance and strong open-world generalization across diverse manipulation tasks.

LfugZN8AN2.text:
• Problem: little mechanistic understanding of when and why VLA models generalize across objects, scenes, and instructions.
• Key idea: train sparse autoencoders on VLA hidden-layer activations to extract interpretable feature directions.
• Found features for motion primitives and semantic concepts, some general across episodes and causally steerable.
• New metric separates general transferable primitives from episode-specific memorization features.
• Steering validated in LIBERO simulation and on real-world DROID robot hardware.
• Amplifying general/semantic features induces matching behaviors; ablating them destroys performance (abstract reports no exact numbers).
• Steering also controls unpromptable behaviors, showing VLAs learn reusable perception-language-action features across tasks.

RLsVfgv1pS.text:
• Imitation learning is limited by scarce, high-quality demonstrations; heterogeneous data differs in action space or lacks labels.
• Existing co-training methods align heterogeneous sources using heuristic, hand-engineered techniques.
• Key idea: actions with the same environmental effect should share one representation, regardless of source.
• GLAM: paired generative models with a shared latent action space, grounded by consistent future-observation prediction.
• Downstream BC policies map observations to latent actions, then decode them into robot actions.
• Evaluated on five manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world, under data-scarce settings.
• GLAM averages +48% task success over BC and prior latent-action methods, including transfer from action-free data.

iy5oCeLdEF.text:
• Problem: robot imitation learning lacks action-labeled data, while action-free videos are abundant.
• Prior latent-action methods ignore downstream control, yielding latents hard to model and decode into actions.
• Key idea: ELA learns latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and continuous action decoding.
• Method: end-to-end training of latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder together.
• Setup: leverages abundant video plus only a handful of action-labeled demos, in simulated and real-world manipulation.
• Results: consistently outperforms prior latent action baselines; abstract gives no specific success-rate numbers.
• New: lightweight 4M-parameter decoders plug into existing imitation methods without architecture or objective changes.

6RJsxVCnhB.text:
• Problem: ObjectNav robots must find unseen targets in unknown environments, deciding where to explore under partial observability.
• Key idea: imitate human-like search, probing visually promising frontiers while using spatial memory to avoid revisits.
• Frontier-based Human-Intent Labeling looks ahead in demonstrations to label frontiers explaining the demonstrator's future search direction.
• Spatial-visual candidate space: BEV memory tracks explored areas, frontiers, and trajectory; egocentric visual memory adds semantic cues.
• A VLM policy selects among grounded candidates, trained with an Intent-Aligned Objective for consistent, human-like exploration.
• Results: state-of-the-art on MP3D, HM3D-v1 and HM3D-v2 ObjectNav; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• New: candidate-level interface transfers zero-shot to wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid robots without VLM fine-tuning.

Rrnnh3mDaH.text:
• Problem: in-hand dexterous reorientation usually relies on object pose estimation, which fails under heavy hand-object occlusion.
• Pose tracking also needs object-specific supervision, creating a perception-control bottleneck that limits robustness and scalability.
• Key idea: end-to-end visuomotor policy acting directly from RGB and proprioception, with no intermediate pose estimation.
• Method: jointly learns visual features and control via distillation from privileged-state teachers plus auxiliary reconstruction losses.
• New: image-goal conditioning specifies target object configurations with images instead of canonical pose representations.
• Simulation: across diverse object geometries and instances, outperforms pose-based methods and pretrained-visual-encoder policies.
• Real world: one image-goal policy transfers sim-to-real directly across five objects; code release planned.

QGzgVP8RnK.text:
• Problem: fine-grained, contact-rich teleoperation is slow, error-prone, and unreliable, even for experienced operators.
• Key idea: real-to-sim-to-real shared autonomy that adds learned corrective behaviors to human teleoperation.
• Method: a kNN human surrogate, fit from under five minutes of real teleoperation data, models operators in simulation.
• The surrogate enables stable model-free RL training of a residual copilot policy, then deployed on real hardware.
• Setup: simulation experiments plus a 16-participant user study on nut threading, gear meshing, and peg insertion.
• Results: higher success for novices and faster execution for experts, while preserving operator intent versus all baselines.
• New: beats direct teleoperation, expert-prior and behavioral-cloning copilots; yields better demonstrations for imitation learning.

Br2rXixvyN.text:
• Problem: robot foundation model benchmarks are saturated, uncontrolled, or require training on messy open-source datasets.
• MESA: reproducible evaluation framework measuring generalization of language-conditioned manipulation policies.
• Five suites isolate in-distribution performance plus spatial, object instance, object category, and subtask composition generalization.
• MESA-Gen, an improved MimicGen pipeline, generates tasks and demonstrations at scale.
• Released on two platforms: single-arm MESA and BiMESA, the first large-scale bimanual generalization benchmark.
• Seven baselines tested: diffusion policies, VLM-based methods, pretrained VLAs; best scores only 52% MESA, 49% BiMESA.
• MESA rankings broadly match RoboArena scores, suggesting its signal transfers beyond simulation.

SniDOKrnNY.text:
• Problem: pretrained VLA policies give little signal about action reliability, making execution failures hard to anticipate.
• Key idea: SentryVLA, a lightweight runtime wrapper adding reliability scoring to frozen VLA policies.
• Action level: conformalized quantile regression bounds deviation of sampled actions from expert-like behavior.
• Among multiple stochastic action candidates, SentryVLA selects the one with lowest estimated execution risk.
• Monitoring level: Mahalanobis anomaly score on latent execution state flags abnormal states during closed-loop control.
• Setup: simulation and physical robot experiments; abstract reports improvements but gives no specific numbers.
• What's new: post-hoc calibrated reliability for VLAs without retraining or architectural changes.

6pHgTk73zs.text:
• Problem: training generalizable, scalable in-context imitation learning (ICIL) policies for robots remains an open challenge.
• ICIL lets pre-trained policies learn new tasks from few demonstrations, without any retraining at test time.
• Key idea: train ICIL policies entirely on RGB-only synthetic data generated by a high-fidelity pipeline.
• Method: flow-matching transformer policy, plus subgoal prediction of next subgoal images for precise, visually grounded control.
• New: no depth sensing, precise camera calibration, or real-world training data needed, unlike prior approaches.
• Setup: evaluated on 16 unseen real-world manipulation tasks with only one test-time demonstration.
• Results: 79% average success rate, outperforming prior methods; project page at synth-icl.github.io.

wRLEgpRnVR.text:
• Problem: VLA action tokenizers are designed for reconstruction fidelity, ignoring their impact on VLA optimization.
• Key question: what makes a good action tokenizer from the perspective of VLA training?
• Principles from information theory: maximize temporal token overlap, minimize vocabulary redundancy.
• Further principles: enhance multimodal mutual information and token independence for easier autoregressive learning.
• Method: ActionCodec, a tokenizer built on these principles that improves training efficiency and VLA performance.
• Results: SmolVLM2-2.2B with ActionCodec reaches 95.5% LIBERO success without robotics pre-training.
• Architectural enhancements reach 97.4%, a new SOTA without robotics pre-training; code and checkpoints released.

MQdt80qzTP.text:
• Sim2real RL for general robots still relies on per-task priors like shaped rewards and demonstrations.
• Diverse simulator resets with massive parallelism help, but uniform sampling wastes environments on mastered or impossible configurations.
• Result: returns flatten as the number of parallel environments scales up.
• Success Guided Sampling (SGS) adaptively focuses training on configurations within a productive success-rate band.
• SGS keeps improving performance up to 1M+ parallel environments, 16× beyond prior work.
• Locomotion: one policy learns multiple long-horizon agile skills, replacing per-task priors and separate runs.
• Manipulation: first fully-RL solutions to NIST board nut-and-bolt and rod assembly, without demonstrations.

eIwbKQS5pz.text:
• Problem: manipulation policies must be accurate yet fast under tight robot-control latency constraints.
• Gap: diffusion and flow policies treat conditions as auxiliary signals, not evolving jointly with actions.
• Key idea: represent conditions and actions in one shared token space for unified condition-action modeling.
• Method: UCA-Flow sequences observation, timestep, interval conditions and action tokens into a single Transformer.
• Conditions are dynamically reconstructed per generation stage, emphasizing information most relevant for action refinement.
• Training: improved dual-pass supervision over u and v strengthens optimization for one-step action generation.
• Results: +9.3 points success over best baseline; 45.6x faster than DP3, 4.3x faster than FlowPolicy.

tJpI5D27wh.text:
• Problem: learning tactile dexterous manipulation policies for multi-fingered hands remains challenging and data-hungry.
• Imitation learning needs costly multi-finger demonstrations; RL in simulation lacks fast, realistic tactile simulation.
• Key idea: anchor sim-to-real transfer on privileged sensors, bypassing tactile simulation entirely.
• Method: learn a tactile encoder mapping real-world touch into the privileged simulation policy's latent state.
• Setup: compared against proprioceptive sim-trained policies on in-hand rotation and tactile in-hand reorientation tasks.
• Results: 182% improvement on benchmark in-hand rotation; 57% more goals reached in in-hand reorientation.
• What's new: adds real tactile sensing to sim-trained RL policies without simulating touch.

EfkPQTtjky.text:
• Problem: behavior cloning on egocentric human videos entangles transferable task content with human morphology, head motion, style.
• Key idea: World Action Models predict actions plus scene evolution, giving richer, more transferable supervision from human data.
• Hypothesis: good world targets abstract appearance, capture agent-invariant physics, and separate camera motion from environment change.
• Method: EgoWAM co-trains on human and robot data, varying only the world target: Pixel, DINO, 3D flow.
• Setup: fixed backbone, action head, and data mixture; three real-world bimanual tasks with in-the-wild egocentric data.
• Results: WAM co-training scales better than behavior cloning; DINO gives up to 4x OOD gains, 3D flow +20-30% in-domain.
• What's new: controlled comparison of world targets shows pixel prediction transfers weakly; abstract targets matter. egowam.github.io

eGZ6YMFVzU.text:
• Problem: autonomous vehicles must detect rare objects, abnormal behaviors, and long-tail events in open environments.
• Gap: perception-only methods lack context; LLM-based methods are computationally heavy and poorly integrate LiDAR geometry.
• Key idea: SOFA activates costly multimodal reasoning only when anomalies are detected, using an adaptive slow-fast design.
• Fast path: a LiDAR-based anomaly detection module provides efficient real-time perception.
• Slow path: a VLM-based reasoning module adds semantic understanding; Time-to-Collision-driven switching coordinates both modules.
• New dataset: MAQA has 16K anomalous objects with synchronized LiDAR-image data and reasoning-oriented language annotations.
• Results: on MAQA, SOFA beats baselines in accuracy, efficiency, and reasoning; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

HbuX1Fe8bl.text:
• Problem: diffusion sequence predictors denoise monotonically once, so early mistakes across the horizon never get revised.
• Key idea: selectively re-noise locally stable regions while others keep denoising, enabling iterative cross-horizon revision.
• Re-noised segments are refined using context from the whole horizon, letting earlier and later parts revise each other.
• Evaluated against full-sequence diffusion and Diffusion Forcing on planning, policy learning, and unified video-action modeling.
• OGBench PointMaze/AntMaze: 21% relative success gain over Diffusion Forcing, 23% over Diffuser in goal-inpainting.
• LIBERO-10: 56.5% relative success improvement over Diffusion Policy across prediction horizons and history lengths.
• Video-action: better policy and inverse dynamics, especially out-of-distribution, plus the best action-video consistency.

6EN09R3NGP.text:
• Problem: with few demonstrations, diffusion policies oversample dominant behaviors and miss valid but rare modes.
• Prior guidance methods push samples into infeasible regions; RL-plus-diffusion approaches get stuck in local minima.
• Key idea: Feynman–Kac correctors plus a novel guiding potential steer sampling toward promising underrepresented trajectories.
• Discovered trajectories are repaired with sampling-based trajectory optimization to ensure they are executable.
