• Repaired trajectories are added to the training set, and the diffusion policy is retrained iteratively.
• Evaluated across multiple manipulation environments; the abstract reports no specific quantitative numbers.
• New: systematic mining and repair loop that consistently discovers diverse, novel, executable behaviors.

u56Z5KqtkI.text:
• Action chunking, predicting multiple future actions, is key to strong behavioral cloning, but why it works remains unclear.
• Tests three existing hypotheses: non-Markovian expressivity, horizon reduction, and representation learning; each explains only part of the gains.
• Delayed policies, predicting one action from the state k steps back, often match or beat action chunking.
• Delayed policies fully capture the benefits attributed to those three hypotheses in many settings.
• New finding: chunking performs implicit ensembling by learning many temporal relationships, such as a_t|o_t and a_t|o_{t-1}.
• This implicit ensemble behavior improves robustness and generalization over policies learning a single temporal relationship.
• Proposed explicit-ensemble policy class amplifies this effect and significantly outperforms action chunking across many domains; the abstract reports no numbers.

wALhOwQWnx.text:
• Problem: compliant humanoid controllers relax stiffness uniformly, trading away control authority needed for contact-rich tasks.
• Key idea: functional compliance keeps stiffness along task-relevant axes, staying compliant elsewhere, varying by direction and time.
• Method: jointly learns a control policy, with reward shaped by compliant poses, and a force estimator.
• At deployment, the learned force estimator composes variable compliance profiles tailored to each task.
• Setup: three contact-rich whole-body manipulation tasks on Unitree G1: key insertion, book reorientation, cabinet opening.
• Results: matches state-of-the-art motion tracking, beats baselines on insertion and reorientation, ties best on cabinet opening.
• Takeaway: task-specific variable compliance, not uniform relaxation, should be the whole-body control primitive for humanoid manipulation.

h4x4aofBgS.text:
• Problem: robot RL assumes efficient training requires GPU-resident physics, simulation, and learning on one GPU path.
• Key idea: what matters is an efficient end-to-end loop, not which processor runs physics.
• UniLab decouples CPU-parallel simulation from GPU policy updates via a unified runtime for data and synchronization.
• Built on MuJoCoUni and MotrixSim CPU-batched physics backends; supports PPO, FastSAC, FlashSAC, and APPO.
• Evaluated on representative simulation-based robot control tasks under identical hardware configurations.
• Result: 3–10× faster end-to-end training efficiency versus GPU-dominant pipelines on the same hardware.
• New: reduced CUDA dependence, running on Apple macOS, AMD ROCm, and Intel XPU backends.

DpOVq6nE2d.text:
• Problem: real-world generalization of generalist manipulation policies is hard to diagnose beyond demonstrated tasks.
• Key idea: factorize tabletop manipulation into motor atoms and instruction atoms to test skills separately.
• Benchmark: 30 atomic tasks, 24 held-out compositional tasks, paired single-arm and dual-arm robot tracks.
• Method: fine-tune policies on 3,000 atomic demonstrations, then evaluate atomic skills and held-out compositions.
• New metrics: Atomic Score and Compositional Failure Share separate weak atomic skills from poor compositional reuse.
• Results: 2,700 physical rollouts on five policies; instruction grounding works, fine motor, counting, logical filtering fail.
• Strong atomic performance does not reliably transfer to compositions; demonstration and rollout data will be released.

ey3y7lxWY1.text:
• Problem: single global-camera manipulation struggles to capture fine interaction details and task-relevant regions without wrist views.
• Context: multi-camera setups with wrist-mounted cameras have become the de facto standard in visual imitation learning.
• Key idea: end-effector trajectories serve as visual attention anchors that highlight task-relevant image regions.
• Method: diffusion visuomotor policy with a multi-scale visual encoder capturing both broad context and fine details.
• Spatial conditioning samples point-wise features along intermediate end-effector trajectories inside the diffusion denoising loop.
• Results: beats strong single-view baselines and matches multi-camera baselines in simulation; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Real-world tests show precise manipulation and robustness to visual distractors using only one RGB camera.

pLyDkcGbkT.text:
• Problem: robot policy iteration evidence is scattered across local tools, scripts, and expert memory, hurting traceability.
• Key idea: make the full data lifecycle explicit through agent-native governance across repeated policy iterations.
• Method: rollouts, reviews, dataset decisions, training runs, evaluations, and release recommendations become typed lineage artifacts.
• Agents interpret rollout evidence, adapt accepted data to existing training stacks, and maintain data health.
• Agents also summarize cross-iteration state and plan next data collection within explicit artifact boundaries.
• Results: in real-robot manipulation, iteration is faster and more auditable; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• New: lightweight, open-source lifecycle layer designed for different robot embodiments and training families.

JI9u9A9JJO.text:
• Problem: dexterous hands struggle to manipulate articulated objects' joints in-hand while keeping a stable grasp.
• Challenge: joint control couples with free-floating grasp stability; diverse objects and functional grasps are costly to collect.
• Key idea: first category-level articulated in-hand manipulation policy generalizing across instances and initial grasps.
• Data: automated pipeline procedurally generates articulated objects and synthesizes task-oriented functional grasps at scale.
• Method: two-stage training with articulation physics randomization, reward curriculum, and latent representation distillation.
• Setup: evaluated across four object categories in simulation on unseen instances and varied initial configurations.
• Results: generalizes in simulation and transfers zero-shot to 12 real objects with diverse shapes and joints.

S3FVTypVnZ.text:
• Problem: robot datasets are costly and embodiment-specific, hindering demonstration reuse across different geometry, appearance, kinematics.
• Key idea: transfer across embodiments in latent space, avoiding pixel-level image translation entirely.
• Method: render paired source-target observations in simulation; align source encoder to a fixed target encoder.
• Policy trained on encoded source demos deploys directly on target robot via the target encoder.
• Setup: three simulation tasks, two target embodiments, plus real-world xArm-to-Franka few-shot transfer.
• Results: up to 93% zero-shot success; over 30-point mean gain versus strongest pixel-translation baseline.
• Real world: 27/30 Franka rollouts succeed, beating target-only training and pixel-space translation pretraining.

ghx1d6PQUR.text:
• Problem: VLA pretraining on human videos suffers cross-embodiment gaps in visual observations and executable actions.
• Latent action models bridge actions, but misaligned visual features yield inconsistent inputs and domain-dependent latent actions.
• Key idea: HARP aligns robot visual representations to human semantics, producing unified vision and latent-action spaces.
• Data: few paired human-robot demos serve as bridges; abundant unpaired human and robot videos supervise dynamics.
• Method: robot-adapted encoder and latent action model use manipulation cues plus source-relative pair-discriminative alignment loss.
• Policy: human and robot videos supervise vision-language-to-latent-action; lightweight head maps latents to robot commands.
• Results: 4.481 average length on CALVIN ABC→D and +7.1% real-world success over strongest baseline.

9Jm97oFGuA.text:
• Problem: fluent expert demos fail as teachers for fine-grained insertion, stacking, and alignment tasks.
• Cause: experts compress critical alignment and recovery into brief windows, starving models of high-precision supervision.
• Training data ends up dominated by redundant free-space motion rather than the segments that determine success.
• Remedy 1: deliberate demos that slow near alignment and expose corrective micro-adjustments.
• Remedy 2: resampling that upweights key segments around gripper state changes and task-critical transitions.
• Remedy 3: dynamic features compressing short visual neighborhoods, conditioning actions on local motion and alignment progress.
• New: pedagogical data collection optimized for machine learnability; abstract reports no quantitative results.

yMD1ykviND.text:
• Problem: marker-based vision tactile sensors entangle surface texture and contact force signals in one image.
• Prior decoupling uses serial mask-based inpainting, suffering mask-sizing dilemmas, error retention, and no real paired supervision.
• Key idea: DeTac, a dual-branch generative framework extracting clean shading and marker images concurrently.
• Full-image synthesis removes mask dependency, avoiding indentation-induced mask-sizing problems entirely.
• Cross-branch synergistic optimization lets branches supervise each other, preventing error retention.
• New dataset: strictly aligned real-world paired tactile images collected with custom hardware.
• Results: state-of-the-art decoupling; the abstract reports no numbers. It also improves reconstruction and force estimation and generalizes across sensors.

u2oeVtdVX8.text:
• Problem: data-driven locomotion controllers usually need explicit style labels, limiting use of unstructured data and unseen styles.
• Key idea: disentangle style from functional locomotion, giving independent real-time control over velocity and style.
• Method: tailored sampling strategy trains a style encoder that conditions an autoregressive diffusion model generating kinematic references.
• A reinforcement learning controller tracks the diffusion-generated reference on the physics-based character.
• Inputs at inference: a style reference clip plus a joystick velocity command, no style labels required.
• Attention-biasing and velocity command correction improve user controllability and stylization strength.
• Shown on a simulated humanoid and a physical robot with robust real-time control and continuous style modulation.

2Z8xQxrlsY.text:
• Problem: Cartesian end-effector policies ignore robot bodies, failing under whole-body collision constraints across embodiments.
• Key idea: EmbodiSteer, a training-free framework steering embodiment-agnostic diffusion policies toward embodiment-aware deployment.
• Method: lifts diffusion sampling into target robot joint space via forward kinematics and Jacobian-based updates.
• Whole-body collision-aware guidance after each denoising step avoids collisions while preserving learned end-effector behavior.
• Setup: evaluated zero-shot on 9 simulated robots and two physical robots in highly constrained scenes.
• Simulation: 46.1% lower collision rate and 28.5% higher task success versus Cartesian-only execution.
• Real robots: 90.0% collision reduction and 36.7% success increase, with no retraining required.

XJgz1iK29G.text:
• Problem: discovering contact-rich, long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation motions without teleoperation or human motion retargeting.
• Challenge: possible contact interaction sequences grow combinatorially with task horizon and number of scene objects.
• Key idea: LLM-guided evolutionary search proposes and refines sequences of contact interactions.
• Method: candidates are checked by an efficient sequential kinodynamic trajectory optimizer, with pruning to discard unpromising sequences.
• Results: ablations show successful whole-body trajectories on several challenging long-horizon tasks; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• Deployment: RL tracking policies trained on discovered trajectories transfer the motions to a real humanoid robot.
• Novelty: first to discover and deploy long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation skills entirely via automated evolutionary search.

AztNrTzNOf.text:
• Problem: object-centric policies use representations too simplistic for interaction dynamics or too dense to learn efficiently.
• Observation: relational tasks hinge on short interaction phases where relative object motion is tightly constrained.
• Key idea: Foci Policy, an interaction-centric framework focusing on object-object interactions rather than robot actions.
• Temporal abstraction: automatically extracts compact interaction segments from demonstrations.
• Spatial abstraction: skills are relative SE(3) motion between task-relevant objects, invariant to scene configuration and robot embodiment.
• Setup: evaluated on RLBench, COLOSSEUM, and real-world tasks against object-centric and action-centric baselines.
• Results: strong performance with less training data than prior policies; abstract reports no specific numbers.

0HnCTHL4fw.text:
• Problem: VLA robots must learn new tasks sequentially without forgetting old ones in open-world deployment.
• Core challenge: existing lifelong methods favor plasticity or stability; the trade-off remains unsolved for manipulation.
• Key idea: LIFELONGVLA, a cache-efficient lifelong VLA framework using dual-timescale adaptation plus lightweight replay.
• Method: dual-timescale LoRA gating, with a short-term adapter for plasticity and a long-term adapter for consolidation.
• A task-aware gate merges both pathways, giving explicit control over the plasticity-stability trade-off.
• Cache-efficient stochastic skill replay keeps balanced retention signals without storing full trajectories.
• Results: beats baselines on skill expansion and retention on a real xArm robot; abstract reports no numbers.

N1gnyxWW2f.text:
• Problem: dynamic rope throws are unforgiving; one mistake causes delays or unrecoverable failure.
• Key idea: observe a brief, safe wiggle to identify rope parameters before any risky action.
• Method: predicted rope parameters condition a trajectory optimizer for zero-shot goal-conditioned execution.
• New: task-agnostic identification, no large real datasets or iterative real-world refinement needed.
• Setup: real-robot 3D target striking, plus multi-objective lobbing and draping tasks.
• Results: 3.55 cm striking accuracy versus 15.29 cm for uninformed baselines; over 50% lobbing/draping success.
• Generalization: 0.95 Pearson correlation between simulated and real rope dynamics on unseen motions.

1zYrrwoISV.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation methods treat force merely as an extra observation, ignoring future dynamics and feedback.
• Key idea: FAWAM integrates force at three levels: perception, prediction, and closed-loop execution.
• Perception: historical 6-axis force/torque signals are encoded to modulate action generation.
• Prediction: world action model jointly forecasts future actions and end-effector wrenches to model contact evolution.
• Execution: residual correction module refines actions online, using predicted wrenches as reference for real-time force feedback.
• Setup: real-world experiments across multiple contact-rich manipulation tasks against vision-only and force-aware baselines.
• Results: average success rate improves 36.25% over vision-only and 21.25% over force-aware baselines.

ORKJlyLOHv.text:
• Problem: real-world fine-tuning of mobile manipulation is hard due to high-dimensional actions and coupled heterogeneous modules.
• Key idea: HiRe-MoMa learns residual corrections on top of a frozen base policy for stable fine-tuning.
• Policy-agnostic residual adds corrective actions, working regardless of the underlying base policy architecture.
• Hierarchical decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, reducing gradient interference.
• Expert-guided value alignment uses sparse human interventions, under 20% coverage, to reshape the critic and guide exploration.
• Setup: real-world experiments on TIAGo++, consistently improving task performance with only about 30 minutes of online interaction.
• New: among the first frameworks enabling efficient on-robot real-world fine-tuning for mobile manipulation.

U620dzd51N.text:
• Problem: VLA models add proprioception only as late conditioning, so robot state never guides instruction understanding or vision.
• Key idea: use robot state as an active query that decides which visual patches the VLM processes.
• Method: discretize proprioception into VLM-vocabulary tokens, then gate visual patches with state and instruction before VLM computation.
• Finding: proprioception added as passive conditioning leaves performance essentially unchanged; gains come from active, token-form state queries.
• Ablations: VLM-vocabulary tokens outperform learned projectors for encoding robot state.
• Results: keeping only about 12% of visual tokens appears to beat the full-token baseline on CALVIN ABC→D.
• Across CALVIN, LIBERO, and real-world manipulation, ThinkProprio cuts end-to-end inference latency while improving on the matched full-token baseline.

k2QZxbcSbQ.text:
• Problem: learned inertial odometry reduces drift but stays tied to one carrier, failing across heterogeneous platforms.
• Key idea: carrier-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts pretraining-and-adaptation framework for generalizable neural inertial odometry.
• Method: prototype-based router composes carrier-specific expert features, decoding local velocity and uncertainty constraints.
• Constraints feed a history-aware EKF for robust state estimation when external sensing is unreliable.
• Unseen domains: freeze pretrained base model, learn only a new lightweight expert residual branch.
• Edge deployment: router reused to select informative online samples for efficient incremental updates.
• Results: outperforms learning-based baselines, cutting average ATE by 40% and RTE-10s by 34%.

OnGdMFJg2i.text:
• Problem: teleoperated robot hands lack human-like in-hand dexterity such as regrasping, reorienting, and finger gaiting.
• Key idea: TeleDexter, a hand-object co-tracking controller mapping operator intent to learned low-level contact execution.
• Method: trained on consecutive co-tracking subgoals derived from human reference motions, not frame-wise trajectory imitation.
• Hybrid reward couples sparse subgoal objectives with dense tracking rewards across diverse interaction modalities.
• Single-stage RL with random action masking and domain randomization transfers zero-shot to real robots.
• Seven tasks spanning reorientation and long-horizon tool use on two hands: 75% average success; baselines consistently fail.
• Collected teleoperation demonstrations successfully train autonomous policies via behavioral cloning.

ffIOVlfRQN.text:
• Problem: pose errors and communication latency cause spatial misalignment between agents in collaborative perception.
• Prior methods widen local fusion windows, but operator costs prevent extending them to global scope.
• Key idea: CoLA performs global cross-agent spatial semantic matching and alignment with linear computational complexity.
• Global Structure Rectification Module models global structure and denoises features shared between agents.
• Ego-Anchored Gate Fusion module aligns and fuses collaborator semantics relative to the ego agent.
• A patch-level structural consistency loss suppresses severe position jitter during training.
• Beats state-of-the-art under various noise conditions on real and simulated datasets; abstract reports no numbers.

TmKLynfHXr.text:
• Problem: humanoids struggle on unstructured terrain; human-prior methods lack scene context for motion synthesis.
• Root cause: existing dataset pipelines fail to capture human-scene sequences in challenging environments.
• Key idea: EgoHTR dataset of egocentric, scene-aligned 4D human motion over complex terrain.
• Method: open-source reconstruction pipeline fusing egocentric wearables with a portable 3D scanner.
• Data: 55 scene-aligned sequences, over 150k frames, in diverse complex environments.
• Results: state-of-the-art accuracy versus motion-capture ground truth, establishing a benchmark for motion analysis and synthesis.
• Deployment: perceptive locomotion policies trained on reconstructed reference motions, run on Unitree G1 hardware.

4uXhlSOnz5.text:
• Leg odometry assumes stance feet have zero velocity, so accurate contact detection is critical.
• Foot force sensors are often unavailable and miss slippage; alternatives rely on heuristics or contact labels.
• Key idea: self-supervised contact learning from joint encoders and IMU only, with no force sensors or labels.
• Denoising autoencoder learns latent representation of kinematic features; two-component GMM is fitted in latent space.
• GMM posterior gives continuous stance belief, scaling zero-velocity measurement covariance in an error-state Kalman filter.
• Evaluated in simulation and real-world terrain; lowest odometry error versus supervised and probabilistic baselines.
• Finding: higher pseudo-label classification accuracy does not yield better odometry; code and dataset are public.

cCI6zZIcEw.text:
• Problem: manipulation benchmarks assume the robot is the only active agent, ignoring humans sharing the workspace.
• Key idea: treat human activity as part of the manipulation task, not background scene variation.
• HARP-Bench defines four human-present conditions: Cueing, Interruption, Contribution, and Co-presence.
• Paired task variants enable controlled comparison between standard and human-present versions of everyday manipulation tasks.
• Includes an interactive pipeline for collecting demonstrations in dynamic human-present settings.
• Evaluated VLAs, imitation learning, and heuristic policies; all struggle notably under human-present variations (no numbers in abstract).
• Training on HARP-Bench data improves human-present performance; real-world experiments confirm the benchmark's validity.

HATezFmdN5.text:
• Problem: robot world models trained on demonstrations or policy rollouts hallucinate in contact-rich manipulation due to biased coverage.
• Key idea: train action-conditioned video world models on autonomous robot play instead of teleoperation or narrow rollouts.
• Method: robots explore environments autonomously, capturing broad object dynamics and diverse behavioral modes for world model training.
• Setup: compared against world models trained on human-collected data, evaluated on failure prediction, policy evaluation, and RL.
• Results: up to 40% improvement over human-data baselines in fine-grained failure prediction and policy evaluation.
• Results: RL inside the learned world model yields policies with 65% higher real-world success rates.
• What's new: first demonstration of autonomous play as an effective training paradigm for video world models.

w2H90oEzfp.text:
• Human demos like mocap and internet videos miss contact forces critical for forceful robot manipulation.
• ForceBand: low-cost wrist-worn sEMG system turning human muscle activity into force-enriched demonstrations.
• Collected 10-hour multimodal dataset: egocentric video, sEMG, IMU, and fingertip forces across diverse actions and objects.
• EMG2Force model predicts per-finger forces from sEMG and IMU after short user-specific calibration.
• Users then record demos with only wristband and video; EMG2Force labels them with per-finger force traces.
• Over 50% lower force prediction error than vision-based baselines on fine-grained fingertip interactions.
• Achieves 87% success on pick-squeeze-place tasks needing object-specific force across diverse shapes, sizes, weights.

HeUmGQaw3M.text:
• LLM robot planners are fluent but cannot guarantee executable or safe plans; PDDL planners need fully specified problems.
• EvoPlan combines LLM context-reading and plan repair with symbolic validation and mined temporal-logic safety constraints.
• Offline evolutionary search mines one global Signal Temporal Logic mobility constraint from demonstration data.
• Missing negatives are generated via counterfactual perturbations and an LLM violation generator; recovers red-light rules, social-navigation comfort.
• Mined constraints shield a vision-language driving policy on Bench2Drive and two discrete-action navigation policies on HA-VLN-CE.
• Evolutionary PDDL planner beats strong baselines on ALFWorld Text, robust to goal/action vocabulary mismatch (abstract reports no numbers).
• New: constrained execution loop re-plans on waypoint violations, fully on-robot via local open-weight LLM, demonstrated in Gazebo.

uSrlwzdTIC.text:
• Problem: floorplan localization methods rely on dense offline pose databases, coupling accuracy, storage, runtime to sampling resolution.
• Key idea: FreeLoc treats the floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map for online RGB localization.
• Method: on-the-fly floorplan ray querying retrieves plausible pose anchors without precomputed scene-specific databases.
• Diffusion-aided refinement turns retrieved anchors into accurate continuous pose estimates, avoiding discretized pose space limits.
• Sequential: online likelihoods from coarse candidates and refined hypotheses enable histogram-filter temporal fusion.
• Results: real-time inference, state-of-the-art single-frame and sequential accuracy; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Real-world indoor robot experiments validate practical deployability; first fully database-free high-performing floorplan localizer.

RmP7m64fQ6.text:
• Problem: pretrained diffusion/flow policies fail under ambiguous instructions or scene shifts, despite having needed motor skills.
• Cause: imitation learning couples action generation to training-specific semantic and spatial context, breaking under train–test shift.
• Key idea: Vision–Language Steering (VLS), training-free inference-time adaptation of frozen generative robot policies.
• Method: VLMs synthesize programmatic, trajectory-differentiable rewards over grounded 3D keypoints to guide denoising.
• Setup: evaluated on CALVIN, LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-10-R simulation benchmarks plus real-world spatial and semantic shifts.
• Results: up to 9.6x over base on CALVIN, +13 pts over frozen π0.5 on LIBERO-PRO.
• Also +4.3 pts over the best VLM-verifier baseline on LIBERO-10-R, with no policy parameter updates.

FVZKpmPHV8.text:
• Problem: VLAs see one observation per step, which suffices for quasi-static but fails for dynamic manipulation.
• Failure 1, motion ambiguity: snapshots encode configuration, not scene evolution, so moving targets cannot be anticipated.
• Failure 2, state aliasing: similar observations across task phases demand opposite actions, causing jitter and mistiming.
• Key idea: two separable failures, two fixes, adding temporal context as minimal inputs to a pretrained VLA.
• Method: frozen video foundation model motion summary plus compact proprioceptive history, no architectural changes or task supervision.
• Results: Bottle Handover success rises from 44% to 74%; only system succeeding where asynchronous baselines score 0%.
• Ablations show each signal is necessary: VLAs lack temporal context, not capacity, on four dynamic bimanual tasks.

aTDKKvOg7W.text:
• Problem: robot trajectories are costly to collect; egocentric human videos are abundant but hard to combine with robot data.
• Challenge: human and robot data differ in embodiment, action spaces, temporal dynamics, and supervision quality.
• Key idea: ACE-Ego, a VLA pretraining framework that unifies heterogeneous human and robot embodied data.
• Method: unified camera-space actions, embodiment-aware morphology tokens, and temporally aligned action chunking.
• New: a reliability-aware training objective that handles mixed-quality supervision, including pseudo-labeled human videos.
• Setup: 4.53K hours of robot and simulation data plus 1.48K hours of pseudo-labeled egocentric human video.
• Results: state of the art on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop and RoboTwin 2.0, with strong real-world bimanual transfer.

gbchkYm28k.text:
• Problem: humanoids grasping arbitrary in-the-wild objects need precise end-effector control plus generalizable visual scene understanding.
• Monolithic end-to-end imitation or sim2real methods learn both jointly, making them hard to scale.
• Key idea: modular system pairing large vision models for scene understanding with sim-trained end-effector control.
• HERO: residual-aware EE tracking policy, using inverse kinematics to turn residual EE targets into reference trajectories.
• Adds a learned neural forward model for accurate kinematics, plus goal adjustment and replanning.
• Results: EE tracking error of 2.44cm, 5.5x lower than the strongest prior method.
• Real-world grasping of mugs, apples, toys in offices and coffee shops, surfaces 43-92cm high.

uhnmcdamCa.text:
• Problem: VLA action tokenizers trade off compression, latency, and downstream policy performance.
• Key idea: repurpose neural audio codecs, treating robot action chunks as multi-channel 1D signals.
• Method: multi-scale RVQGAN encoder with residual vector quantization and offset codebooks for compact, ordered tokens.
• Mel-spectrogram losses replaced with time-domain and non-mel spectral losses suited to kinematic signals.
• Vocos-style decoder with ISTFT head and adversarial discriminators reconstructs smooth, detailed trajectories.
• Evaluated on LIBERO-10, RoboMimic, and real-world manipulation against binning, FAST, and VQ tokenizers.
• NAC beats baselines on reconstruction error and success rate at comparable or better compression.

gO08puaqia.text:
• Problem: predicting deformable object dynamics under robot manipulation remains hard and unreliable.
• Prior work: per-object material fitting is slow and non-generalizable; end-to-end models violate physics.
• Key idea: couple a differentiable Material Point Method simulator with two feed-forward neural networks.
• Material from Motion infers per-particle elasticity from visual observations, grounding simulation in object-specific physics.
• Residual from Dynamics learns simulator discrepancies, correcting internal dynamics to absorb systematic modeling biases.
• Enables online material identification on novel objects, with uncertainty steering exploration toward least-confident regions.
• On real manipulation sequences, outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

db6WHoqH91.text:
• Problem: robot policies generalize poorly to unseen backgrounds, distractors, and lighting conditions.
• Prior fixes need costly large-scale pretraining or assume flawless real-world object detection.
• RoboAug needs only one image with bounding box annotations to build augmented datasets.
• Pretrained generative models perform precise semantic augmentation, turning one annotation into hundreds of scenes.
• A plug-and-play region-contrastive loss steers policy attention toward task-relevant regions.
• Tested on UR-5e, AgileX, and Tien Kung 2.0 robots across over 35k real-world rollouts.
• Unseen-scene success rises from 0.09 to 0.47, 0.16 to 0.60, 0.19 to 0.67, beating baselines.

Qa1Uu7lc8n.text:
• Problem: generalist dexterous manipulation needs data; real teleoperation is costly, per-task simulation environments and rewards are hard.
• Key idea: learn task-agnostic dexterous skills in simulation, recomposed at test time for diverse real-world tasks.
• Method: a 3D point-track-conditioned "Anypose-to-Anypose" policy moves any object to any desired pose.
• Training: simulation across thousands of objects with diverse pose configurations, covering broad robot-object interactions.
• Deployment: zero-shot real transfer without finetuning, prompted by object point tracks extracted from generated videos.
• Closed loop: online point tracking provides perception and control feedback during execution.
• Results: consistent gains over baselines in sim and real; abstract reports no numbers; generalizes to novel objects, layouts, backgrounds.

oMvcKDFLRA.text:
• Problem: safety-critical scenario generation must maximize adversariality to expose failures while preserving realism.
• Gap: handcrafted heuristics confine generation to known priors; general LLM agents lack simulator grounding.
• Gap: unconstrained agents also collapse the attack-realism tension into single-scalar maximization.
• Key idea: EvoDrive, first automated LLM-based agentic evolution framework for multi-objective driving scenario generation.
• Method: memory-driven actor proposes generator improvements; critics filter implausible ones; self-evolving evaluator routes simulation budget.
• Pareto archive preserves diverse attack-realism trade-offs and guides further evolution through simulation feedback.
• Results on MetaDrive and CARLA: significantly expands Pareto frontier across generators; scenarios improve policy training.

SMKzI5HX9P.text:
• Problem: human-to-robot transfer methods are hard to compare due to inconsistent tasks, scenes, objects, and robot supervision.
• Key idea: H2RBench, a Real2Sim benchmark standardizing evaluation of learning robot manipulation from human videos.
• Method: pairs real human video demonstrations with simulated robot demonstrations under one standardized protocol.
• Setup: four manipulation tasks with diverse interaction requirements, task-specific human demos, and limited robot data.
• Evaluates multiple representative H2R methods, each bridging the embodiment gap with a different strategy.
• Finding: methods differ substantially in how well they scale with additional human demonstrations.
• Sim predicts real performance: Pearson r=0.89, Spearman ρ=0.85, MMRV 0.06 across method-task configurations.

DwRC6la1Kr.text:
• Problem: adapting VLAs to new tasks usually requires costly task-specific teleoperation data.
• Setting: one-shot demo-conditioned VLAs, conditioned on a single demonstration video of an unseen task.
• Finding: existing end-to-end approaches struggle when tasks require precisely localizing small target regions.
• Key idea: SeeTraceAct improves spatial grounding by predicting future end-effector traces with visibility awareness.
• New benchmark: RoboCasa-DC, a released demo-conditioned RoboCasa extension with episode-paired humanoid videos.
• Setup: evaluated on RoboCasa-DC and real-world Franka Panda tasks conditioned on human demonstrations.
• Results: best success in all four RoboCasa-DC settings, +12.5 points average real-world success over baselines.

BV0T1o1ZIL.text:
• Problem: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) often fail at contact-rich manipulation requiring precise physical interaction.
• Gap: prior work adds force-augmented architectures and regularizers, but root causes of failure remain underexplored.
• Key finding: failures split into two distinct modes, precision failures and force failures.
• Precision failures stem from a training mismatch in flow-matching policies.
• Force failures arise from the distinctive structure of force signals.
• Method: FACT combines one targeted mechanism per failure mode into a single approach.
• Results: 66% average success on five tasks versus 41% for best baseline, across ~2,500 real-world rollouts.

cQPnBRGgWM.text:
• Problem: wires and cables are central to industrial assembly but have infinite-dimensional, contact-driven deformable configurations.
• Gap: existing benchmarks are hardware-tied, lack modular assets, or omit industrial fixtures and shared protocols.
• Key idea: WireCraft, a simulation benchmark for industrial DLO manipulation with configurable difficulty and assets.
• Tasks: three families, connector insertion, clip routing, and channel seating, with articulated and deformable DLO physics.
• Setup: released trajectories from simulation and a physical UR5, benchmarking RL, IL, and VLA under shared metrics.
• Results: privileged state-based RL exceeds 82% success in one representative setting per task family, confirming well-posedness.
• Finding: for connector insertion, vision RL, IL, and VLA struggle moving from socket reaching to contact-rich alignment.

dE7KjOl8yu.text:
• Problem: simulators idealize emerging sensors (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, thermal), hiding failure modes that hurt real-world deployment.
• Key idea: VisionSIM treats sensor realism as first-class by simulating each modality's raw physical measurement process.
• Method: unified, physically grounded platform with fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters across conventional and emerging modalities.
• Reproduces LiDAR pileup and glare, iToF phase wrapping, saturation, motion artifacts, and event-camera refractory drops.
• Also models history-dependent emission for thermal cameras, a failure mode general-purpose simulators overlook.
• Setup: identical scenes and trajectories across all modalities enable principled cross-modality comparison.
• Release: open platform plus large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground truth; abstract reports no numbers.

OOCwc3Dn5d.text:
• Problem: action-conditioned video world models look realistic but often ignore actions, limiting controllability.
• Cause: training on successful expert trajectories yields success-biased video players that hallucinate good outcomes.
• Framing: this lack of persistence of excitation is characterized as a collapse in empowerment.
• Key idea: Action Influence Maximization (AIM) biases training data toward state-action pairs maximizing mutual information.
• Method: batch online reinforcement learning collects data that makes actions maximally influence predicted futures.
• Setup: world models trained on robotic interaction data for simulated manipulation and navigation tasks.
• Results: AIM beats expert-only training and outperforms state-of-the-art models trained with 85x more data.

SN5sVBOZ8D.text:
• Problem: manipulation-pretrained VLAs like π0 assume quasi-static arms, mismatching underactuated, highly dynamic aerial flight.
• Key finding: visual representations transfer well to drones, but flight control dynamics do not.
• AirVLA introduces Payload-Aware Guidance, injecting payload constraints into flow-matching sampling without retraining.
• Gaussian Splatting pipeline synthesizes navigation training data to overcome aerial teleoperation data scarcity.
• Evaluated over 460 real-world experiments on aerial pick-and-place, navigation, and long-horizon compositional tasks.
• Results: synthetic data lifts navigation success 81% to 100%; guidance raises pick-and-place 23% to 50%.
• Long-horizon compositional task reaches 62% success, showing pretrained manipulation VLAs can transfer to aerial platforms.

8xaYRUduNe.text:
• Problem: control-space tree search fails on simple quadrotor planning because naive control sampling yields poor geometric coverage.
• Root cause: naive sampling measures pushed through nonlinear dynamics produce highly uneven, poorly dispersed reachable states.
• Key idea: learn a lightweight sampler whose pushforward achieves low geometric dispersion in the local search space.
• Self-supervised training uses a well-dispersed reference map as scaffold, so no external expert is needed.
• Result: the learned sampler makes control-space search work for quadrotors where naive sampling simply fails.
• Produces more agile trajectories in obstacle-dense settings than established trajectory optimization techniques.
• Reach spans roughly thrice the volume of popular motion primitive libraries, and dispersion improves with test-time compute.

5zw401UEGd.text:
• Problem: human demos scale better than mobile teleoperation, but embodiment gaps hinder whole-body mobile manipulation transfer.
• Existing retargeting gives imprecise, inconsistent solutions, causing action multi-modality that stops supervised policies from converging.
• Key idea: WARP, an offline pipeline explicitly modeling embodiment differences to extract precise, unique whole-body robot actions.
• Method: closed-form Shoulder-Elbow-Wrist geometric solver gives exact end-effector tracking while preserving whole-body structural intent.
• Lazy mobile-base control complements the arm solver, yielding accurate, consistent robot trajectories from human pose.
• Results: retargeted trajectories proved highly reliable in open-loop real-world replay; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• New: first zero-shot whole-body mobile manipulation from offline human demos, with no teleoperation action data needed.

39Q3r1h0mD.text:
• Problem: MPC needs analytical dynamics, failing with contacts and other hard-to-model state dependencies.
• Model-free RL avoids modeling assumptions but demands large amounts of interaction data.
• Key idea: learning-based MPC blending local model-based planning with learned corrections.
• Residual dynamics network augments the nominal analytical model, learning missing state-dependent effects from data.
• Learned action-value critic injects long-horizon MDP structure into local iLQR, countering finite-horizon myopia.
• New: GPU-batched iLQR solver runs learned networks in-loop, solving thousands of problems in parallel within a simulator.
• Results: improved closed-loop performance on biased, incompletely modeled tasks; abstract reports no specific numbers.

7KV78k8rcv.text:
• Problem: VLA policies overfit to their training end-effector and fail on unseen grippers or hands.
• Key idea: mask the end-effector out of the wrist camera so the policy never depends on it.
• Masks come free from robot geometry and camera calibration, projected in real time, no generative model.
• Masks are augmented during training to prevent overfitting to the end-effector's shape.
• At deployment, unseen end-effectors are masked and retargeted via two tips using inverse kinematics.
• Cloak-VLA, trained on one parallel-jaw gripper, transfers zero-shot to another gripper and a five-fingered hand.
• Unmasked baselines with the same retargeting collapse, worst on the dexterous hand; source performance barely drops.

3KzmpJQUpy.text:
• Problem: autoregressive VLA policies are hard for users to steer mid-trajectory without retraining or architecture changes.
• Key idea: Token Steering injects low-dimensional user inputs directly into the model's native action-token space.
• Works purely at inference time, with no extra training, finetuning, or modification of the VLM architecture.
• User inputs guide rather than override the policy, preserving learned dexterity, smoothness, and task priors.
• Evaluated on two household tasks: drawer closing after object placement, and state-aware object swapping.
• Success rates rose from 10.0% to 72.5% on drawer closing and 14.3% to 93.8% on swapping.
• New: lightweight, intuitive steering of robot foundation models, improving accessibility for users with limited physical control.

FYNtpa7rwN.text:
• Problem: pretrained manipulation policies fail when unobserved physical properties and dynamics change at deployment.
• Existing test-time adaptation relies on sparse scalar rewards, ignoring rich geometric and dynamic interaction feedback.
• Key idea: SCOUT adapts by continuously revising an internal belief about environment dynamics from action outcomes.
• Method: action-prediction policy and forward dynamics model share a belief latent space.
• Meta-training: inner loop updates belief via dynamics prediction error; outer loop optimizes action selection.
• Deployment: only the latent belief updates from action-outcome mismatches, avoiding catastrophic forgetting during adaptation.
• Results: significantly faster online adaptation on simulated benchmarks and robust sim-to-real transfer; abstract reports no numbers.

0HS0to0eVo.text:
• Problem: locomotion RL often converges to undeployable local optima like vibrating limbs or torso scooting.
• Key idea: steer off-policy RL toward a designer-preferred gait using model predictive controller (MPC) transitions.
• Method: MPC solving the same MDP inserts transitions into the replay buffer; no reward redesign needed.
• Unlike adversarial motion priors: no discriminator, no kinematic retargeting, no auxiliary objective.
• Setup: 2D walker in simulation plus sim-to-real evaluation on a Unitree Go2 quadruped.
• Results: one to two-term reward yields gaits comparable to 21-term shaped rewards and adversarial motion priors.
• Analysis: injected transitions bias actor-critic updates toward MPC-visited states, reaching basins pure RL misses.

WNZ4Dr57JS.text:
• Problem: zero-shot 3D-object-prompted perception struggles in robotics with tricky materials, dense clutter, and slow runtime.
• Key idea: Z3P (titled 3PTv2), one end-to-end transformer for zero-shot detection, segmentation, and 6D pose.
• Method: persistent object tokens replace bounding-box handoffs between separate models, improving runtime and clutter performance.
• Inputs: single- or multi-view RGB or RGB-D images plus a 3D-object prompt, no object-specific training.
• Setup: evaluated on five robotic benchmarks: IPD, XYZ-IBD, ITODD-MV, T-ROBI, and ROBI.
• Results: new SOTA, first zero-shot method beating all zero-shot and object-specific methods on detection and pose.
• Applications: transparent bin picking, sorting, car charging, electronics assembly, positioned as a 3D-perception foundation model.

aILPNAxgHb.text:
• Problem: humanoid robot gaze relies on task-specific controllers, producing rigid, unnatural, unexpressive eye and head motion.
• Key idea: decouple high-level cognitive reasoning from low-level motor control learned directly from human motion data.
• A Vision-Language Model interprets the scene and designates gaze targets that condition the low-level action head.
• Realistic Gaze Transformer (RGT): a Transformer-VAE pre-trained self-supervised on human motion to learn full-head dynamics.
• RGT is then fine-tuned autoregressively for stable long-horizon rollouts under closed-loop deployment on a facial robot.
• Inference: brief motion history plus VLM eyeball trajectory yields real-time 11-DoF eye, head, eyelid, and blink commands.
• New: separating realism from targeting keeps purposeful gaze while adding natural vitality; abstract reports no quantitative results.

uKRtsLLqs6.text:
• Problem: grasping multiple objects dexterously is hard due to data costs, varied layouts, generalization needs.
• MoDex: data-efficient framework, first unified solution for universal multi-object dexterous grasping across spatial layouts.
• Key idea: single-step decision problem learning residual corrections to a reference trajectory.
• Spatially adaptive dual strategy: single-shot grasp for proximal objects, sequential interaction for separated objects.
• Proximal layouts: 64.17% success on unseen objects, significantly outperforming baselines.
• Separated layouts: MoDex succeeds where prior methods struggle.
• Generalizes across robot embodiments, scales, and transfers zero-shot sim-to-real via simulation-trained vision policy.

rAyG2MJka5.text:
• Problem: socially competent robots need joint spatial and social reasoning, but few models unify both.
• HRI data is scarce, making large models trained from scratch impractical for social interaction understanding.
• Key idea: STARS learns event-level relational representations from fixed-duration interaction scenarios modeled as spatiotemporal graphs.
• Method: self-supervised message-passing GNN autoencoder compresses physical dynamics into compact latents per node and edge.
• Setup: linear probing on SEAN Together VR navigation perceptions and SocialNav-SUB social scene understanding benchmark.
• Results: F1 of 0.635 for perceived competence using 1% labels; baselines need up to ten times more.
• New: latent space clusters distinct human action intents without supervision, showing emergent high-level social semantics.

B7gccZTJyE.text:
• Problem: Driving VLAs use language to aid planning, but a language-action gap limits real gains.
• Key idea: verifiable meta-actions, compact language intentions summarizing future ego motion.
• Meta-actions are derived from expert trajectories and checked against generated trajectories via rule-based mapping.
• Method: action-centric supervised training plus data-efficient turn-level credit-assignment reinforcement learning.
• Dense rewards and precise credit assignment explicitly align high-level decisions with low-level trajectory planning.
• Results: new Waymo End-to-End SOTA, RFS 8.060 (2B) and 8.079 (4B); competitive on NAVSIM.
• What's new: a simple meta-action interface reaches SOTA once made verifiable and optimized for alignment.

lSrxDURLdG.text:
• Problem: UAV-UGV teams must plan jointly; UAVs have limited energy, UGVs recharge them but follow road networks.
• Gap: masked diffusion planners assume distributional alignment in scheduling and need differentiable constraints for optimization.
• Key idea: MEND frames collaborative planning as conditional masked generation of parallel, context-aware team action sequences.
• Neuro-symbolic step: logic-induced admissibility indicator reweights learned action distribution, enforcing operational constraints at execution time.
• Error-bounded scheduling: unmask positions with minimal entropy over the constraint-aware distribution, improving plan optimality.
• Setup: evaluated in simulation, on real-world maps, and with physical UAV-UGV robot teams.
• Results: abstract reports improved constrained planning over baselines but gives no specific numbers.

QJI3N7JzBc.text:
• Problem: real-world failures of autonomous systems are rare, diverse, and expensive to find under limited testing budgets.
• Cheap proxies like simulators or related policies find failures, but these often fail to transfer to target systems.
• Key idea: combine extensive proxy evaluations with few target tests to adaptively select which scenarios to test.
• Method: control-variate-inspired residual model corrects proxy failure signals into a local predictor of target risk.
• Support-aware mutual-information objective favors realistic, well-supported regions while expanding coverage across distinct failure modes.
• Evaluated on autonomous driving, manipulation, and quadruped velocity-tracking tasks against random sampling and active-learning baselines.
• Finds up to 2x more failures than baselines, including severe, diverse failures that competing methods miss.

yzejD0WIk9.text:
• Flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles are agile but hard to control onboard under tight size, weight, power limits.
• Platform: butterfly-inspired flapping-wing robot weighing under 30 grams, with nonlinear dynamics.
• Key idea: hierarchical neuromorphic control running fully onboard a roughly $5 ESP32 microcontroller.
• Two lightweight spiking neural networks: one estimates state from raw sensors, one modulates a wing CPG.
• Trained via imitation learning; achieves stable pitch and heading tracking in untethered real-world flight.
• Versus ANN baseline, SNN inference latency drops 36% (1059 to 680 µs), power 18% (0.033 to 0.027 W).
• Claimed first fully onboard neuromorphic autonomous flight control of a flapping-wing robot, without specialized hardware.

lTLiSuIBAj.text:
• Problem: humanoid policy learning lacks data combining broad motion diversity with precise physical states and interaction grounding.
• Internet videos lack precise physics; lab motion-capture datasets are high-fidelity but cover only narrow behaviors.
• HiPHI: a 600-hour high-precision dataset of whole-body human motion and object interaction.
• Motion coverage is guided by FrameNet, a linguistic framework organizing human action primitives.
• Optical motion capture gives sub-millimeter full-body tracking plus mesh-level object trajectories.
• Benchmark suite evaluates motion diversity, interaction grounding, object consistency, and physical AI applications.
• Results: much broader motion coverage than existing datasets while keeping high-fidelity interaction quality.

5m9zSorosa.text:
• Problem: off-road navigation needs terrain costmaps that generalize to new terrains and adapt costs at test time.
• Gap: segmentation methods adapt costs quickly; representation learning generalizes; no existing approach achieves both.
• Key idea: SPACER conditions costmap generation on a user-specified scaled preference context for rapid adaptation.
• Method: training leverages synthetic data so the model generalizes well to previously unseen terrain types.
• Setup: evaluated on large-scale aerial maps for global path planning and on the RELLIS off-road dataset.
• Results: lowest regret across varied preferences in five of seven environments for global path planning.
• Results: RELLIS costmaps achieve up to 13% lower mean absolute error versus ground truth than next-best methods.

6BQ9NdqznS.text:
• Problem: most VLA policies regress actions reactively, ignoring future dynamics, which hurts out-of-distribution generalization.
• Key idea: supervise VLA training with future 3D robot keypoint tracks as embodiment-centric 4D signals.
• Tracks of joints and end-effector come from forward kinematics on proprioception, with negligible preprocessing cost.
• No external trackers or 3D reconstruction needed; supervision is metric, compact, and derived from robot data.
• A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder feeds this signal into the action expert.
• Gradient isolation preserves the pretrained vision-language backbone; the decoder is dropped at inference, keeping the policy interface unchanged.
• Evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0, and real robots, it beats strong VLA baselines, especially under camera, background, and layout shifts.

BWHjoo36Dr.text:
• Problem: cross-embodiment data needs embodiment-agnostic motion representations for training robotic foundation models.
• Prior flow-based manipulation uses sparse keypoint displacements, mismatching the continuous-time nature of motion.
• Key idea: model robot velocity fields directly as probability velocity fields via flow matching.
• Method: Flow as Flow generates dense robot flows efficiently within a flow matching formulation.
• Benchmarks: outperforms representative baselines on standard metrics with roughly 33x faster generation.
• Real world: 9 methods, 13 manipulation tasks, 260 trials each; highest average success rate.
• What's new: first to formulate robot flows as dense velocity fields unified with probability flows.

MTZ4eKUP94.text:
• Problem: offline-trained grasp synthesis stays fixed, degrading under unseen objects, noisy observations, or unmodeled contact dynamics.
• Key idea: continual learning for single-view 6-DoF parallel-jaw grasping in cluttered scenes, adapting during deployment.
• Method: adapts via memory in a learned embedding space rather than finetuning a large parametric model.
• Grasp outcomes update future grasp scores; optional user demonstrations are recalled and transferred as candidate grasps.
• Setup: evaluated in simulation and extensive real-world experiments totaling over 1000 grasp trials.
• Results: matches 6-DoF baselines before adaptation; exceeds 90% success on challenging categories after 50 online attempts.
• New: memory-based adaptation handles deployment shift and long-horizon continual learning with limited forgetting.

0mUj0bXuJh.text:
• Problem: legged locomotion on unstructured terrain needs curricula, but such terrain lacks explicit difficulty ordering.
• Existing heuristic curricula use parameterized terrains, causing overadaptation to near-fixed perceptual patterns and poor generalization.
• Key idea: TACL generates trajectory-level training tasks directly from unstructured terrain maps, without handcrafted difficulty.
• Method: an evaluator learns a difficulty function mapping trajectory tasks to scores for the current policy.
• A sampler proposes new trajectories guided by the evaluator, forming a closed loop matched to the evolving policy.
• Results: 56.3% higher trajectory success than no curriculum, and 18.5% over handcrafted curricula on hardest terrain.
• Up to 39.74% gain over handcrafted curricula when traversing the same obstacle type from diverse directions.

F4IB3mxHbO.text:
• Perception-free E2E driving compresses image patches into compact scene tokens, supervised only by the planning objective.
• This weak supervision leaves the scene-token bottleneck under-constrained, limiting the visual information preserved for planning.
• NTR adds self-distillation masked latent reconstruction, using only scene tokens as memory to rebuild patch features.
• Foundation-model semantic priors bias reconstruction toward driving-relevant structures, without adding explicit perception heads.
• Auxiliary components are dropped at inference, so the deployed planner and its cost stay unchanged.
• State of the art: 8.0461 RFS on Waymo E2E, 94.1 PDMS and 90.9 EPDMS on NavSim1&2.
• Tokens show lower redundancy and higher effective rank; validated on private data and real-vehicle deployment.

bLQynefrlp.text:
• Problem: in-context learning lets text-only LLMs predict robot actions, but bimanual control overwhelms context windows.
• Challenge: high-dimensional joint action spaces and tight inter-arm coordination constraints make few-shot bimanual prompting hard.
• Key idea: BiCICLe frames bimanual control as a multi-agent leader-follower problem between the two arms.
• Method: decouples joint actions into sequential single-arm predictions, with the follower conditioned on the leader.
• Setup: off-the-shelf LLMs, no fine-tuning, evaluated on 13 TWIN benchmark tasks plus 3 real-world tasks.
• Results: 70.5% average success, +6.1 points over best training-free baseline, surpassing most supervised methods.
• What's new: first training-free few-shot LLM bimanual framework, transferring to real hardware without retraining.

XnIdgAtBX7.text:
• Problem: VLA policies break under visual shifts, exploiting spurious domain-specific cues instead of task-relevant structure.
• Key idea: supervise policies with domain-invariant future latents learned from domain-transformed trajectory data.
• Method: Task-Domain Encoder uses contrastive objectives plus Gaussian disentanglement regularization to separate task from domain.
• Policy learning: encoder supplies future latents for lookahead prediction and domain disentanglement during VLA training.
• Counterfactual task-view compositions: DILL reduces shortcut degree while improving out-of-distribution success.
• LIBERO-Plus perturbations: 69.1% average success, +11.4 points over best matched-input baseline, only 12.5-point drop.
• Novelty: latent diagnostics confirm task-consistent structure preserved and domain variation suppressed, unlike prior VLA training.

3M39Fmw8Mx.text:
• Problem: VLA models underuse multi-view inputs, persistently over-relying on the wrist camera across manipulation stages.
• Consequence: no dynamic global-local view adjustment, limiting stage adaptability and robustness in manipulation.
• Key idea: FocusVLA, a stage-aware framework routing attention across camera views by predicted future interaction intent.
• Method: predicts future intent from historical actions, then guides dynamic view routing during action generation.
• Simulation: on RoboTwin 2.0, average success rate improves 10.08% over strongest baseline π0.5.
• Real world: success rate rises from 71.7% to 85.0%, a 13.3% gain over π0.5.
• New: intent and routing modules plug into existing VLA frameworks without modifying core architectures.

2tjuz95jmb.text:
• Behavior Foundation Models give robust humanoid control but only replay predefined motions, lacking reactivity to environment changes.
• Naively cascading generative planners with BFMs fails: tracking errors cause cumulative exposure bias and collapse.
• ReactiveBFM: real-time closed-loop framework coupling a generative motion planner with whole-body tracking control.
• Scheduled prefix sampling curriculum trains the planner on imperfect physical states, teaching error-recovery instead of ground-truth imitation.
• Asynchronous replanning plus trajectory chunking with temporal ensembling resolves planner-tracker latency mismatch, eliminating jitter.
• Deployed on Unitree G1: diverse text-conditioned closed-loop motions and zero-shot moving target reaching with on-the-fly replanning.
• Sim-to-sim under severe perturbations: 93.1% success, outperforming cascaded open-loop baselines by 28.6%.

tU2SHEG4to.text:
• Problem: gravity assistance for combined human-exoskeleton mass is hard to model analytically.
• Obstacles: non-rigid interfaces, unmodeled biological torques, and statically indeterminate closed kinematic loops.
• Key idea: skip analytical modeling and directly learn feedforward assistance torques from harvested data.
• Method: velocity-limited admittance control suppresses inertia, Coriolis effects, and voluntary human reflexes during collection.
• Slow passive yielding yields clean data isolating configuration-dependent assistive torque requirements.
• Results: absolute torque prediction errors below 10% on novel subjects, beating sparse-sensor analytical baselines.
• New: few-shot calibration personalizes profiles for soft tissue, scaling to high-acceleration dynamic tasks.

J5RZyNKq8z.text:
• Problem: robot models pretrained on egocentric human video consistently underperform those pretrained on robot data.
• Insight: the gap comes from ignoring active perception, since head-driven camera motion is treated as noise.
• Key idea: ActiveMimic models human camera motion as a viewpoint action, learned jointly with manipulation.
• Method: recovers synchronized camera and wrist trajectories from a single body-worn RGB camera, then adapts to robots.
• Setup: pretrains on in-the-wild egocentric human video; real-world tests span tasks with diverse active perception demands.
• Results: consistently beats human-video-pretrained baselines and matches state-of-the-art robot-data-pretrained models; abstract reports no exact numbers.
• New: evidence shows active perception emerges from human video pretraining, not robot-specific fine-tuning.

9ccdcInkM9.text:
• Problem: imitation-learned driving planners suffer distribution shift, causal confusion, and compounding errors in closed loop.
• RL alternatives need handcrafted rule-based rewards and massive simulation, limiting practicality.
• Key idea: closed-loop imitation learning using RL purely as an optimizer, not for reward engineering.
• Reward is a trajectory-distance signal derived directly from logged expert driving data.
• Setup: lightweight MLP policy evaluated on the nuPlan Val14 Reactive benchmark.
• Results: 86.51 score, +3.2 over previous best IL planner Flow Planner, with over 15x faster inference.
• Takeaway: training strategy matters at least as much as model complexity versus large generative planners.

rnp2Bj4RUX.text:
• Problem: LLM/VLM task planners lack physical risk awareness, producing unsafe high-level actions for embodied agents.
• Challenge: under partial observability, hazards often lie outside the robot's immediate field of view.
• Key idea: SafeMem maintains a long-term semantic graph memory of open, dynamic environments.
• Method: egocentric observations incrementally build a graph of objects and their relationships.
• An LLM risk predictor checks candidate actions against memory, triggering conservatism-modulated replanning with hazard explanations.
• Setup: evaluated on the IS-Bench benchmark and a real-world robot platform.
• Results: substantially higher safe success rates than state-of-the-art VLM planners; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

tAXtXe4Oqd.text:
• Problem: imitation-trained VLAs are brittle in precise manipulation because execution errors compound.
• Question: can a simulation-only RL policy make real-world VLAs more robust, zero-shot?
• Dilemma: privileged-state residual RL needs distillation, image-based suffers domain gap, real-world RL is costly and unsafe.
• Key idea: object-centric residual RL corrects frozen VLA actions using object poses, which transfer consistently across domains.
• Method: replay real teleop demos in sim to train a sim VLA twin; add pose noise and dropout.
• Results: on five real Franka tasks, success rises from 42% to 76% with zero-shot transfer.
• New: improved rollouts retrain the base VLA for self-improvement without any additional teleoperation.

vQmF2cR04D.text:
• Problem: real-robot data is expensive; human videos are diverse but suffer a human-to-robot embodiment gap.
• Prior work restricts videos to task-aligned settings or transfers only visual representations, ignoring action trajectories.
• Key idea: robotize human videos, converting them into robot-like episodes for scalable VLA policy pretraining.
• Method: pipeline handles heterogeneous videos, inferring missing intermediate signals across varying annotation levels.
• New HuRo Dataset: about 630K robotized episodes and 142M processed frames from diverse human video sources.
• Evaluated on four real-world manipulation tasks; performance scales with the amount of robotized pretraining data.
• HuRo-pretrained policies beat strong foundation models pretrained solely on large-scale purely robotic data.

menElmunwi.text:
• Problem: large-scale geometric optimization distributed across multiple robots or sessions relies on brittle hand-tuned solvers.
• Existing distributed solvers mainly target rigid-body pose graphs, not general matrix Lie group problems.
• Key idea: DeepCORD, a learning-augmented framework for distributed factor graph optimization on general matrix Lie groups.
• Method: unfolds a parallel, accelerated Riemannian optimizer into differentiable iterations for end-to-end learning.
• A self-supervised feedback policy adapts solver parameters to the optimization phase and communication status.
• Setup: real-world SE(3) pose graph optimization and SL(4) projective submap alignment, synchronous and asynchronous communication.
• Results: lower objective values than existing distributed baselines on most benchmarks; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

m94Acp7Al5.text:
• Problem: UAVs following targets in clutter lag behind turns, pick blocked corridors, or trade tracking for unsafe motion.
• Key idea: target following is inherently predictive, so plan using forecasted target futures, not just current states.
• Method: flow-based planner uses predicted target futures as horizon-aligned residual signals to generate UAV trajectories.
• Safety: risk-scored repair of the executable trajectory prefix is embedded directly inside the sampling loop.
• Setup: fixed in-distribution and out-of-distribution receding-horizon simulation benchmarks, plus simulator-facing interface, sensing, and controller stress tests.
• Results: zero in-distribution collisions with highest safe-tracking time; lowest out-of-distribution collision rate and final tracking error.
• Caveat: Future-MPC stays smoother and wins some thresholded out-of-distribution success metrics; ablations show future adaptation improves candidates before repair.

rK0JCfddwK.text:
• Problem: humanoid-object interaction lacks generalized control interfaces and robust closed-loop perception for reliable execution.
• Key idea: Pro-HOI conditions policy on desired root trajectory, using reference motion only as reward.
• Root trajectory serves as a universal interface for planners, enabling simultaneous navigation and loco-manipulation.
• Data: collected deployable box-carrying motions, removing penetration artifacts via Signed Distance Field loss.
• Persistent object estimation fuses real-time detection with Digital Twin to detect slippage and trigger re-grasping.
• Setup: real-world validation on Unitree G1 humanoid in complex, long-horizon box-carrying scenarios.
• Results: significantly outperforms baselines in generalization and robustness; abstract reports no specific numbers.

nIbnBCtz79.text:
• Problem: long-horizon mobile manipulation needs reasoning about localization, scene changes, and task progress, which images alone poorly capture.
• Key idea: condition a vision-language-action (VLA) policy on a spatiotemporal map of both environment and robot.
• SERF map: environment and articulated robot body as neural points in a shared latent space, updated online.
• Updates: object-level rigid tracking moves environment points; forward kinematics moves robot points from proprioceptive state.
• Policy input: map tokens from multiple reference frames and spatial scales give the VLA local and global context.
• Setup: evaluated on BEHAVIOR-1K long-horizon household mobile manipulation; the abstract reports no quantitative results.
• Results: beats image-only baselines, reaches subgoals faster, handles scene-configuration shifts, and recovers from object drops.

ALlLaCTHKQ.text:
• Problem: dexterous cable tracing needs continuous fingertip regulation of pressure, friction, and incipient slip.
• Task: feeding a cable through the hand via repeated thumb-index pinch-and-curl motions.
• Key idea: Touch2Trace, tactile-driven imitation learning without vision or explicit cable-state estimation.
• Method: self-supervised pretrained encoder for 32×32 TacV5 sensor plus lightweight behavior-cloned transformer policy.
• Setup: teleoperated demonstrations, policy deployed at 60 Hz on a Tesollo DG-5F hand.
• Results: versus proprioception-only, distance rises 0.2 to 20.1 cm, success 0% to 93%, zero-shot to unseen cables.
• New: first systematic real-world study of pretraining, control rate, temporal context, and spatial resolution effects.

8MNr0evyJT.text:
• Problem: does humanoid "retarget human motion, then RL-track it" recipe transfer to contact-rich dexterous manipulation?
• Challenge: manipulation has complex contact dynamics and far less tolerance for tracking error than whole-body control.
• Key idea: Regrind, a minimalist retargeting-guided RL pipeline learning dexterous skills from a single human demonstration.
• Method: retarget hand-object motion preserving spatial and contact relations, then train residual RL tracking object-centric keypoints.
• Setup: simulation training with careful system identification, zero-shot transfer to two different real multi-fingered hands.
• Results: fluid, human-like tool use on hardware, including operating scissors and turning a screwdriver; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: systematic hardware study identifying key sim-to-real factors, with practical guidance for retargeting-based contact-rich learning.

994ptkAdnU.text:
• Problem: anomalies in critical infrastructure can cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures if unrecognized.
• Existing detectors need onboard sensors like motor encoders, often missing on legacy hardware or blocked by security.
• Key idea: AWARE, an adaptive world model detecting anomalies using only external camera monitoring.
• Method: estimates system dynamics parameters and predicts future states to flag deviations as anomalies.
• Setup: 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations.
• Results: 26% better anomaly classification than the strongest baseline under noisy camera-only state estimation.
• New: decoding inferred dynamics parameters localizes the degrading motor with 88% accuracy, enabling fault diagnosis.

1j0Hw81jY9.text:
• Problem: fast robot motion blurs images, corrupting online 3DGS geometry and causing camera pose drift.
• Online 3DGS mapping also suffers unbounded Gaussian growth during continuous operation.
• Key idea: analytically integrate each projected Gaussian over exposure time, replacing N-subframe averaging.
• This exposure integration yields O(1) cost per Gaussian for motion blur modeling.
• Hessian-based pruning score bounds Gaussian count; Adam plus online LM jointly refine pose, velocity, Gaussians.
• Matches or beats offline deblurring 3DGS quality while training 15-150x faster on public and self-collected data.
• Runs online at competitive quality using about 20% fewer Gaussians than the online 3DGS baseline.

f5329HhijI.text:
• Problem: diffusion visuomotor policies commit to one action frame, making action distributions needlessly complex.
• Insight: manipulation is multi-frame; end-effector frames suit local actions, base-aligned frames suit transport and coordination.
• MoF keeps one canonical diffusion state, re-expresses it in several task-relevant frames simultaneously.
• Frame-specialized denoisers predict noise per frame; predictions are fused back in the canonical frame.
• New column-based 6D rotation in SE(3) enables exact, differentiable frame transforms on noisy, off-manifold rotations.
• Nine simulated bimanual tasks: best frame is task-dependent; MoF beats oracle frame selection and MoE baselines.
• Two real-world bimanual mobile manipulation tasks: MoF outperforms all constituent single-frame baselines.

aq2hmhW0kU.text:
• Problem: humanoid whole-body manipulation relies on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real RL, both hard to scale.
• Teleoperation needs costly hardware logistics; sim-to-real RL demands complex reward engineering and controlled settings.
• Key idea: HuMI learns humanoid whole-body skills from humanoid-free demonstrations captured with portable hardware.
• Method: hierarchical learning pipeline translates captured human whole-body motion into dexterous, feasible humanoid skills.
• Setup: five whole-body tasks including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation.
• Results: 3x more efficient data collection than teleoperation; 70% success rate in unseen environments.
• What's new: scalable in-the-wild whole-body data collection, no robot needed during demonstrations.

anfRreNqMN.text:
• Problem: slip detectors lack precise latency characterization and fail to generalize across robot platforms.
• Key idea: fuse spatial pressure maps with friction-induced vibration, two complementary tactile slip cues.
• Sensor: TacV5 combines a 32x32 piezoresistive array at 240 Hz and a 3-axis accelerometer at 8 kHz.
• Method: modality-specific encoders, intra-sensor fusion, cross-modal attention, causal temporal prediction at 240 Hz.
• Setup: 1.4M-frame dataset spanning 37 objects, collected purely with a handheld UMI gripper.
• Results: 96.7% Macro F1, under 1.6% false positives, 76% of slips detected within 23.1 ms.
• New: zero-shot transfer to Tesollo dexterous hand across unseen objects, sensor units, and platforms.

msKuD5tWYj.text:
• Problem: parking policies must hit sub-meter slot precision while reacting safely to nearby vehicles, which are conflicting goals.
• Key idea: CoPark, a residual policy learned via multi-agent self-play on top of a fixed offline plan prior.
• Prior keeps slot-frame geometry; residual head learns reactive corrections that data and scripting cannot provide.
• Novelty: partner-threat signal hands longitudinal control to residual for yielding; lateral stays anchored to reference.
• Closed-loop refinement layer corrects terminal errors caused by action-grid discretization.
• Trained on six lots, zero-shot on new benchmark: Dragon Lake Parking and DeepScenario Open 3D.
• Results: about 70-85% success, 3-6% collisions, beating classical, imitation, and large-scale RL; emergent yielding and queuing.

TTJ3uxLcxL.text:
• Problem: observation-action delay, where the correct action depends on events seen long before execution.
• Example: in a shell game, the final scene alone cannot reveal which cup hides the ball.
• Key idea: memory must be separable, addressable, and prospective to directly serve policy decisions.
• Method: Chameleon, a ~60M visuomotor policy writing embodied event memory and retrieving control-relevant traces.
• New benchmark: Camo-Dataset, real-robot tasks with visually ambiguous decision scenes requiring recall of earlier observations.
• Camo results: decision/end-to-end success rises from 22.5%/21.3% to 80.8%/71.3%.
• Public benchmarks: LIBERO-10 87.1%, MemoryBench 97.3%, MIKASA-Robo 75.1%; same-size SOTA, beating larger VLA baselines.

84ea2xeP60.text:
• Mobile manipulators must adapt base placement, manipulation, and gaze to the spatial context surrounding target objects.
• COWBOY: a scalable sim-to-real framework for learning contextual whole-body manipulation, avoiding direct scene-adaptation RL.
• A vectorized environment-aware whole-body controller coordinates base-arm reaching, collision avoidance, and active vision across thousands of scenes.
• Local RL experts learn object interaction in local scenes, then are reused across thousands of full-scene layouts.
• Composed WBC-RL teachers are distilled into one point-cloud policy controlling base, arm, dexterous hand, and camera.
• Zero-shot transfer to hundreds of objects across cluttered tabletops, shelves, drawers, and other in-the-wild scenes.
• Policy automatically adapts base placement, viewpoint, arm trajectory, and grasp strategy to observed scene geometry.

5oNzcK6SBR.text:
• Problem: registering two egocentric RGB captures of the same indoor space taken at different times.
• Head-mounted views are blurry, fast-moving, partially overlapping; classical and learned scene-graph registration methods prove brittle here.
• Key idea: use one pretrained vision-language model for both scene understanding and cross-scan object matching.
• Method: off-the-shelf foundation models lift each RGB sequence into an object-level 3D scene graph.
• Matching uses object-height priors, paired same/different VLM verification, and per-match rigid transform hypotheses ranked by geometric consensus.
• Training-free: no learned parameters, depth sensor, training, or annotated scene graph required.
• Beats geometric and learned baselines on Aria Digital Twin and Aria Everyday Activities; scene graphs transfer downstream.

JydY4anB01.text:
• Embodied LLM controllers aid human-robot interaction, but memory and latency hinder real-time robot deployment.
• Key question: not just how much to prune, but when during multi-phase training pruning should occur.
• BPF prunes during RL, so compression accounts for task supervision and closed-loop feedback.
• BPF-RL prunes iteratively at RL intervals; BPF-SFT/RL prunes during SFT, then continues during RL.
• Evaluated on RobotxR1 driving pipeline with LLM-Pruner, against post-training, SFT-stage pruning, and smaller dense models.
• BPF-SFT/RL gives 1.69x better size-performance trade-off than smaller dense models; up to 27% faster decoding on Jetson Orin.
• Pruning must be evaluated end-to-end, since output token changes affect latency and closed-loop behavior.

dSbtHPqFj9.text:
• Problem: deployed robot policies must learn new tasks continually without catastrophically forgetting previously learned behaviors.
• Common fix: replay buffers of old task data, usually sampled randomly from all prior experiences.
• Key finding: a small subset of old experiences, called Memory Anchors, disproportionately preserves past task performance.
• Method: find anchors where old and new data representations collapse together but require conflicting actions.
• Example: manipulating a familiar object in a new way; replaying old data there prevents destructive overwriting.
• Results: removing 10% of anchors raises forgetting over 4.5x; anchor-enriched replay cuts worst-case forgetting 63% on LIBERO.
• New: principled replay selection enabling real-robot continual learning of highly conflicting tasks.

mzGjyghofG.text:
• Problem: grasping fully occluded targets in clutter requires discovering hidden objects and ensuring safe retreat paths.
• Gap: existing methods mostly handle partially visible targets, neglecting full occlusion discovery and retreat safety.
• Key idea: human-like multi-view "imagination" reconstructs an amodal 3D target model plus target-centric occlusion point cloud.
