• Method: next-best-action loop searches observable corridors, updating the occlusion cloud, removing blockers only when critical.
• Once visible, target geometry is reconstructed and grasps are chosen satisfying feasible retreat constraints.
• Setup: reconstruction validated on LINEMOD Occlusion and GraspNet-1Billion, plus extensive real-world occluded grasping experiments.
• Results: robust discovery, occlusion removal, and safe grasping across occlusion levels; abstract reports no numbers.

dPgz9Kssgo.text:
• Problem: influence functions for robot data curation don't scale to billion-parameter multitask VLA models.
• Key idea: ATHENA, an influence function framework for curating multitask VLA demonstrations at billion-parameter scale.
• Method: exploits Kronecker structure of linear-layer gradients to cut projection cost.
• Rank-r Random Truncated Approximation replaces dense Hessian inversion, giving about 313.4x faster influence computation.
• Global and local interactive influence balance data curation across 50 jointly trained tasks.
• Setup: RoboTwin 2.0 simulation (9.34 hours) and six real-robot tasks (6.90 hours of demonstrations).
• Results: matches or beats full-data joint fine-tuning using 50% data in simulation, 66% on real robots.

hCG12ifteJ.text:
• Problem: VLA manipulation policies are brittle out-of-distribution, especially with limited real-robot training data.
• Key idea: use a large pre-trained world model's generalization to decompose tasks into visual subgoals.
• Method: VISTA is a hierarchical framework with a world model planner and a VLA executor.
• The world model splits tasks into subtask sequences, synthesizing a goal image for each subtask.
• The low-level VLA follows textual and visual guidance, with goal images adding physically grounded details.
• Setup: evaluated goal synthesis and hierarchical policies across extensive out-of-distribution scenarios with unseen objects.
• Results: world-model guidance lifts the same VLA from 14% to 69% success in novel scenarios.

Eb5TKtrt2X.text:
• Problem: in-hand assembly, mating two rigid parts within one dexterous hand, no second arm or fixture.
• Inspired by human finger cooperation, like capping a pen using only the hand holding it.
• Key idea: unified reinforcement learning framework driven by a goal relative pose between the two parts.
• Function-based auxiliary reward shapes finger roles; regularization toward a single human reference pose guides coordination.
• Robustness: domain randomization plus fused historical proprioception and object observations handle occlusion-induced estimation noise.
• One recipe solves Bottle, Syringe, and Marker tasks; sim-trained policies transfer zero-shot with one camera.
• New: in-hand assembly exposes hand morphology demands, offering a benchmark for modern robotic hands.

dngZLI0SlV.text:
• Problem: model-based RL suffers compounding errors, high inference latency, and unstable backpropagation through time (BPTT).
• Key idea: a chunk world model serves as a differentiable training-time evaluator for a chunk actor.
• Policy and world model jointly predict action and state chunks, avoiding recurrent model invocation.
• H-step hypothetical rollouts are generated in one forward pass, directly optimizing value expansion.
• This removes costly, unstable BPTT while keeping dynamics-gradient-based policy updates.
• Evaluated on 19 challenging high-dimensional HumanoidBench locomotion tasks; abstract reports no quantitative results.
• Deployed in the real world for quadruped bipedal walking; code to be publicly released.

H5QWMBcNSU.text:
• Problem: VLA models in open-ended settings forget old skills catastrophically when continually learning new ones.
• Observation: forgetting tracks diffusion of cross-modal dependencies among vision, language, and actions during adaptation.
• Gap: existing continual learning methods fail to preserve these cross-modal information dependencies.
• Key idea: Info-VLA, an information-preserving continual learning framework with dual cross-modal constraints.
• Method 1: Replay Anchor Contrastive Learning uses frozen-teacher anchors to keep representation-space alignment stable.
• Method 2: cross-modal mutual information maximization preserves vision-language dependency structure, balancing stability and plasticity.
• Results: beats existing methods on retention and adaptation in simulation and real-world; abstract reports no numbers.

BKafd0mNwy.text:
• Problem: safe motion planning while mapping unknown environments with limited, noisy perception.
• Neural Time Fields learn arrival time as continuous cost-to-go, but ignore sensing uncertainty.
• Active Neural Time Fields lack safety mechanisms, so noisy observations can cause collisions online.
• Key idea: propagate sensor-induced robot–obstacle distance uncertainty into arrival time via risk-sensitive representation.
• Method: real-time closed-loop planner combining the uncertainty-aware time field with chance-constrained trajectory optimization.
• Results: fewer collisions than deterministic and inflation-based baselines with preserved path efficiency; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: first uncertainty-aware Neural Time Field formulation, also shown working on manipulator systems.

XnyoJXimAK.text:
• Humanoid soccer demands agile locomotion, ball control, and impact-rich contacts across a continuous behavioral spectrum.
• Prior methods either cover few skills or skip motion priors, yielding unnatural, non-human-like behaviors.
• SoccerBot: hierarchical RL using a latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture.
• Policy learning is constrained within this dynamically plausible motion manifold for natural, human-like movement.
• A single task-conditioned policy learns moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking, with fluid commanded skill switching.
• Robustness-oriented simulation design enables zero-shot sim-to-real transfer to the Unitree G1 humanoid.
• New: unified soccer skill set plus human-like motion quality; abstract reports qualitative real-world results, no numbers.

7hdkIcfGRw.text:
• Problem: sim-real co-training for VLAs mostly uses SFT, treating simulation as static demonstrations, limiting real gains.
• Key idea: RL-Co exploits closed-loop interaction in simulation while preserving real-world capabilities of VLA policies.
• Stage one: warm-start policy with SFT on a mixture of real and simulated demonstrations.
• Stage two: RL fine-tuning in simulation plus auxiliary supervised loss on real data to prevent forgetting.
• Setup: four real-world tabletop manipulation tasks, tested with OpenVLA and π0.5 architectures.
• Results: beats real-only and SFT co-training, +24% real success on OpenVLA, +20% on π0.5.
• Also yields stronger generalization to unseen task variations and substantially better real-world data efficiency.

hPz010j4EA.text:
• Problem: generating feasible, semantically appropriate grasps for different robotic hands from natural language instructions.
• Bottleneck: no multi-hand grasp datasets with fine-grained hand-object contact descriptions existed.
• New dataset: Multi-GraspSet, first large-scale multi-hand grasp dataset with automatically annotated contacts.
• Key idea: Multi-GraspLLM uses an LLM to handle variable-length sequences across diverse hands in one architecture.
• Method: aligns point cloud and text features, then flow matching generates grasps from fused semantics.
• Cross-hand latent space enables knowledge transfer; hand-specific decoders output joint angles per robotic hand.
• Results: outperforms prior methods in simulation and real world; LoRA with 20% data matches full training.

JMcC5JoPKD.text:
• Problem: garments' extreme deformability makes generalizable robotic T-shirt folding and unfolding policies hard to train.
• Key idea: large-scale synthetic data alone can train policies that transfer directly to real-world garment manipulation.
• Dataset: 6 robot embodiments, 1K T-shirts, 1K environment assets, 120K richly annotated episodes.
• Asset generation: FoldNet pipeline creates physically simulatable T-shirts with diverse appearances and semantic keypoints.
• Demonstrations: a unified rule-based framework uses semantic keypoints to generate demonstrations across all embodiments.
• Results: visuomotor policies trained only on synthetic data exceed 90% end-to-end real-world success rates.
• New: zero-shot transfer to unseen environments, unseen T-shirts, and arbitrary initial configurations, across multiple embodiments.

L9RkFeuKRc.text:
• Problem: adapting generalist VLA policies to real-world humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation remains hard.
• Humanoids coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual arms; base/waist errors trigger unstable upper-body compensation.
• Key idea: HAF-VLA progressively denoises shared whole-body actions in stages instead of one-pass chunk generation.
• Stages: locomotion and head first, then waist refinement, finally full-body manipulation.
• Builds on pretrained flow-matching VLA, reusing prefix encoder and action expert with learnable stage embeddings.
• New: cross-stage KV-cache conditioning lets later stages refine outputs using earlier stages' action representations.
• Six real-world humanoid tasks: significantly improves existing models; abstract reports no specific success-rate numbers.

PL6UDcy9Eu.text:
• Problem: external and wrist cameras get occluded, limiting close-range, multi-view perception in dexterous manipulation.
• Key idea: put miniature cameras directly on every fingertip of a multi-fingered robot hand.
• Compact vision-enhanced fingertip modules give comprehensive multi-view observations of objects and surroundings.
• Method: diffusion-based whole-body visuomotor policy using third-view camera plus multi-view fingertip vision.
• Fingertip features add camera-pose encoding and per-finger joint-current encoding for alignment and contact awareness.
• Real-world tasks include retrieving objects behind curtains: 56.6% relative success gain over third-view plus wrist cameras.
• New: first fingertip-vision dexterous learning system, trained from human demos; hardware and code fully open-sourced.

zhiG7XB56D.text:
• Problem: SE(3)-equivariant visuomotor policies assume one global rigid transformation governs the whole observation scene.
• This assumption breaks in real manipulation, where the task-relevant region shifts across different objects.
• Key idea: learn a phase-conditioned affordance field (PAF), a per-point score over the observed point cloud.
• The score-weighted centroid becomes a learned anchor, canonicalizing observation and action instead of the fixed gripper frame.
• The PAF score is also appended as a per-point feature, adding local bias while preserving global SE(3) equivariance.
• Simulation: on multiple MimicGen tasks under varying spatial randomization, PAF consistently improves the underlying policy's success rate.
• Real robot: PAF beats baselines on multi-object tasks and stays more robust under lighting variations.

2vsTg6WU2p.text:
• Problem: VLA foundation models are too compute-heavy for robots' power- and space-limited onboard hardware.
• Idea: serve one robot policy to many robots from a shared remote GPU.
• New: first formulation of multi-robot policy serving as an action chunk scheduling problem.
• System: Armory, a batched serving system validated on simulated and real robot fleets.
• Finding: naive batching heuristics work for identical robots but fail with heterogeneous chunk consumption rates.
• Method: heterogeneity-aware scheduler matching batching to closed-loop action chunk demands of each robot.
• Result: up to 18% higher overall system throughput in real-world experiments.

nl8iBTm3Mt.text:
• Problem: neural inertial odometry measurements break under arbitrary IMU mounting rotations, corrupting filter-based state estimation.
• Key idea: learned mean must transform as a vector, covariance congruently as a second-order tensor.
• GINIO: SO(3)-equivariant interface predicting motion measurement and uncertainty obeying these tensorial laws from calibrated IMU windows.
• Last-Frame Alignment preprocessing is provably equivalent to world-frame training, enabling efficient sensor-frame learning.
• Estimator tracks sensor-local states like IMU bias; interface plugs into NIO, AirIO, EqNIO, ResNet backbones.
• TLIO: 2.018 m ATE under rotations versus EqNIO's 76.389 m, using 11.6x fewer FLOPs.
• NanoBench ATE 5.579→1.430 m without external attitude; Fetch unseen remount ATE 8.15→0.50 m without retraining.

ojMvvFKk6t.text:
• Problem: semi-dense matchers predict discrete grid confidences, yielding grid-aligned correspondences needing costly high-resolution features.
• This computational and memory overhead limits real-time matching on embedded robotic platforms for SLAM and navigation.
• Key idea: reformulate semi-dense matching as iterative coordinate-space optimization with recurrent hidden-state propagation.
• Coarse level: Deep Aggregated Transformer refines global correspondences efficiently through recurrent coordinate updates.
• Fine level: lightweight local module predicts sub-pixel coordinate corrections within compact feature windows.
• Results: higher MegaDepth accuracy and over 10x faster inference than Efficient LoFTR on embedded edge devices.
• New: continuous recurrent coordinate refinement offers a scalable alternative to grid-based matching across indoor and outdoor benchmarks.

5XKFwWrW0v.text:
• Problem: robot foundation models need strong out-of-the-box performance across diverse tasks, strategies, and data sources.
• Key idea: train with diverse context conditioning so prompts precisely steer what the robot does and how.
• Prompts combine language commands with multimodal strategy cues, including task-performance metadata and subgoal images.
• This lets training use demonstrations, suboptimal autonomous data including failures, and non-robot data sources.
• Setup: evaluated on many tasks demanding speed, dexterity, language following, and compositional task generalization.
• Results: abstract reports strong out-of-the-box performance and emergent capabilities, but gives no specific numbers.
• What's new: strategy-level steering via rich multimodal prompts, turning heterogeneous and imperfect data into usable training signal.

7BXJJYw05E.text:
• Problem: embodied AI can cause direct physical harm, yet foundation models' physical safety common sense is poorly understood.
• Examples: boxes too heavy to lift, hot coffee handed to children, spilled liquid creating slip hazards.
• Key idea: scalable, continuous physical safety benchmarking grounded in real-world injury narratives and operational constraints.
• Method: generative models turn narratives into photorealistic images and videos showing safe-to-unsafe state transitions.
• Setup: major foundation models evaluated on perceiving risks, reasoning about safety, and triggering timely interventions.
• Post-training teaches models to reason explicitly about embodiment-specific safety constraints given through system instructions.
• Results: interpretable safety thinking traces and state-of-the-art constraint satisfaction; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

gk8bvFSZq3.text:
• Problem: behavior cloning needs massive high-quality expert data, but real-world human teleoperation is prohibitively expensive.
• Key idea: automate expert policy learning in simulation without any human demonstrations, keeping strong sim-to-real transfer.
• Method: diffusion policy behavior prior trained on synthetic data, such as Code as Policy demonstrations.
• RL steers the prior by optimizing initial diffusion noise, with the denoising process kept frozen.
• This keeps exploration on safe behavior manifolds, enabling stable sparse-reward learning without reward engineering.
• Results: up to 85% success on long-horizon manipulation, 90.5% on industrial assembly, beating all baselines.
• Real-world: state-based experts distilled into visuomotor policies via DAgger and successfully deployed on real hardware.

TZM6J864Lf.text:
• Manipulation tasks range from memoryless Markovian to non-Markovian, needing history within or across interaction trials.
• Naively extending observation history in visuomotor policies hurts performance via distribution shift and overfitting.
• Gated Memory Policy (GMP) learns both when to recall memory and what to recall.
• A learned memory gate activates history context only when needed, improving robustness and reactivity.
• Lightweight cross-attention builds latent memory; diffusion noise on past actions adds robustness to inaccurate histories.
• Results: +30.1% success over long-history baselines on new MemMimic benchmark, +26.6% over VLAs on MIKASA-Robo.
• Stays competitive on Markovian RoboMimic tasks; code, data, and in-the-wild deployment instructions to be released.

RdvH11pAfJ.text:
• Problem: manipulation benchmark scores are treated as general capability evidence, yet reflect one fixed evaluation setup.
• Identifies four failure modes: shortcut solvability, statistical insignificance, creeping overfitting, and data-source dependence.
• Key idea: one diagnostic per failure mode to test whether a benchmark validly proxies manipulation capability.
• Audits LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin 2.0 using these four diagnostics.
• LIBERO: 0.09B probe without language encoder nears SOTA; most reported gains lack provable statistical significance.
• CALVIN: randomizing block poses within training range drops performance for every tested policy.
• RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0 fail fewer diagnostics; reference implementations released for authors and reviewers.

aRtb8NIgc3.text:
• Problem: humanoid foundation models outpace evaluation; real-world tests are costly, hard to reproduce.
• Gap: existing simulation benchmarks target table-top or wheeled robots, not whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation.
• Key idea: SIMPLE, a unified testbed coupling MuJoCo contact dynamics with IsaacSim photorealistic rendering.
• Scale: 60 whole-body tasks, 50 indoor scenes, and over 1,000 object assets.
• Data: automated motion-planning trajectory generation plus low-latency VR teleoperation for scalable collection.
• Benchmarks imitation networks, large VLA models, and world action models; sim performance strongly correlates with real.
• New: policies trained on SIMPLE data transfer zero-shot to physical humanoids under similar settings.

fGWkovHMQE.text:
• Problem: most VLA models map observations directly to actions, struggling on reasoning-intensive long-horizon manipulation tasks.
• Gap: existing CoT VLAs lack unified cross-modal reasoning and explicit inverse reasoning from target states.
• Key idea: decompose planning into forward prediction of next visual state plus inverse dynamics to reach it.
• Method: unified autoregressive Mixture-of-Transformers interleaving text and image generation in a single reasoning process.
• Pipeline: forward CoT picks subgoal, forecasts image; inverse CoT reasons spatially over it; action generated last.
• Setup: evaluated on simulation and real-world manipulation benchmarks against state-of-the-art VLA baselines.
• Results: consistently outperforms baselines, especially on long-horizon tasks; abstract reports no specific numbers.

0PThTAIwPD.text:
• Problem: imitation-pretrained VLA policies fail beyond demonstration coverage, so RL post-training is needed.
• Existing VLA-RL trades reliability for efficiency: costly model-free, stale static simulators, unaudited online simulators.
• Key idea: MERL post-trains VLAs with an evolving simulator whose imagined rollouts are trust-calibrated, not uniform.
• Simulator couples a world model with a reward proxy head, updated alongside policy optimization.
• Stage-level trust adjusts imagined-data ratio and rollout horizon according to current simulator reliability.
• Chunk-level trust selects and weights reliable imagined chunks, falling back toward real data when unreliable.
• Long-horizon perturbed manipulation: higher success and efficiency than IL, model-free, static and online model-based baselines.

qxboQ98QN4.text:
• Problem: robots learning human preferences extend sparse binary feedback to unchosen actions using fixed implication rules.
• User study in two collaborative simulations: human implication labels often contradicted the standard fixed rule.
• Using human-provided implication labels substantially improved reward learning with the PIE preference learning algorithm.
• Key idea: IMPLIED treats fixed-rule implications as initial guide, then learns to infer and revise labels.
• Evaluated on recorded human-robot interaction trajectories and a physical robot pizza-making user study.
• IMPLIED predicts human implications better than fixed-rule and LLM baselines, approaching a human-label oracle.
• Lower preference-estimation error and more rational robot actions under combined preference and task rewards.

oX3ErTz3rv.text:
• Problem: teleoperation cost, not model capacity, limits covering OOD object placements, orientations, and scenes for manipulation policies.
• Key idea: cheap, diverse human egocentric video already encodes visual-physical regularities needed for OOD generalization.
• Base model: LDA-1B, a 1B-parameter latent dynamics-action model pretrained on cross-embodiment robot and human ego data.
• Method: post-training co-trains five objectives: policy, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, video generation, joint action-observation denoising.
• Human data feeds all objectives except policy, shaping shared representations while keeping embodiment-specific action heads uncontaminated.
• VLM backbone is unfrozen during post-training, recovering cross-embodiment knowledge lost with frozen-VLM recipes.
• Results: beats robot-only baselines on OOD and long-horizon dexterous tasks across two robots, matching policies trained on more teleop data.

2xR8oasJuM.text:
• Problem: multi-quadruped coordination methods train task-specific MARL policies, failing when new tasks arrive sequentially.
• Goal: learn new coordination skills continually while reusing old ones without catastrophic forgetting.
• Key idea: Conquer, a semantic skill library framing continual coordination as a retrieve-adapt-update process.
• Self-Allies-Goal backbone models own state, teammate context, and goal, supporting variable team sizes.
• Task-level semantic descriptors from pre-execution information retrieve the most relevant stored skill for adaptation.
• After success, trajectory-level descriptors update the library by semantic distance, enabling cross-task knowledge transfer.
• Results: 95.6% final average success in simulation, strong forward transfer, negligible forgetting, validated on Unitree Go2 teams.

CKVUqG4YQf.text:
• Problem: driving VLA models map inputs to controls but ignore their own critic ability to refine decisions.
• Key idea: CriticVLA extends VLAs from acting to judging, using a VLA-based critic to improve trajectories.
• Method: two-stage, theoretically inspired; generate a rough trajectory, then refine via multimodal evaluation and single-step optimization.
• Data: large-scale synthetic dataset of 12.9 million annotated trajectories strengthens critic reasoning and refinement.
• Setup: extensive closed-loop evaluation on the Bench2Drive benchmark against state-of-the-art baselines.
• Results: 73.33% total success rate, about 30% improvement in challenging scenarios.
• What's new: first explicit use of VLA critic capability for closed-loop driving decision refinement.

ODnu3ohjEQ.text:
• Problem: bimanual dexterous grasping lacks comprehensive datasets and strong generative models.
• BiDexGrasp contributes a large-scale bimanual grasp dataset plus a learning-based grasp generation framework.
• Synthesis pipeline: region-based grasp initialization, then decoupled force-closure optimization for physically feasible grasps.
• Dataset: 6351 diverse objects sized 30–80 cm, with 9.7 million annotated bimanual grasps.
• Generator uses a bimanual coordination module to produce coordinated two-hand grasps on unseen objects.
• Geometry-size-adaptive generation strategy handles varied object shapes and scales robustly.
• Simulation and real-world experiments show superior synthesis and generation performance; abstract reports no specific metrics.

1yL1d39r7K.text:
• Problem: learned robot policies need real-time failure detection, but enumerating failures in open-world settings is intractable.
• Visual monitors react to benign background changes; kinematic monitors ignore the environment and miss relational errors.
• Key idea: represent scenes as spatio-temporal graphs over tracked, labeled objects and their interactions.
• Self-supervised: trained only on nominal demonstrations, flagging failures as deviations from learned object-centric behavior.
• Data-rich regime: GnnT, a predictive graph transformer, detects deviations from learned spatio-temporal object dynamics.
• Few-shot regime: TPC, a non-parametric method, checks geometric consistency and object-relation dynamic changes.
• Outperforms baselines on a public benchmark and new relational dataset; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

ST0jumL7Ma.text:
• Problem: VLAs mapping language and vision directly to dense actions weaken pretrained VLM reasoning and break under spatial changes.
• Key idea: H-VLA decouples high-level key-action reasoning from low-level motion generation in a hierarchical framework.
• Key-Action Model predicts structured key-actions as semantic sub-targets; Motion Planning Model generates dense actions conditioned on them.
• Unified Camera-Centric Action Space keeps actions consistent across datasets, robot embodiments, and camera viewpoints.
• Two-stage training: pre-training emphasizes key-action reasoning, fine-tuning emphasizes dense motion generation.
• SimplerEnv: 91% Google Robot visual matching, 84% Google Robot variant aggregation, 81% WidowX visual matching.
• Agilex real robot: gains over best baseline of +10 in-distribution, +52 OOD position, +16 OOD scene/object.

Qgk0k192w6.text:
• Problem: reconstructing occluded 3D scenes in clutter requires both viewing and physically pushing objects.
• Existing belief maps show where scenes are unresolved, not how, relying on costly lookahead or heuristics.
• Key idea: DiVE learns decomposed view-resolvable and push-resolvable visibility maps, revealing what each action uncovers.
• Predictions map to a shared visibility-gain scale, enabling hierarchical choice between observing and interacting.
• A mode-specific policy then selects the concrete viewpoint or push action.
• Simulation: 11.3% higher occupancy IoU on extreme-occlusion shelves, 13.2x faster per step, 19.8x faster planning.
• Zero-shot real-robot deployment recovers 79.2% of initially occluded objects.

PCVxUMrP6N.text:
• Problem: multimodal Diffusion Policies fuse vision, touch, and force as flat features, losing distinct roles and pairwise relations.
• Key idea: ViTaForce learns three paired cross-modal encoders, each anchored to a distinct physical question about contact.
• Inputs: RGB scene and hand-eye vision, dual-side tactile pressure maps, and high-rate end-effector wrench windows.
• V–T encoder learns where contact occurs on the fingers, using hand-eye vision and tactile maps.
• V–F encoder learns when contact will spike, from scene approach cues; T–F separates genuine contact from motion-induced wrench bias.
• Setup: contact-rich assembly tasks such as nut-bolt insertion, with learned representations feeding imitation-learned diffusion policies.
• Results: more efficient policy learning, plus better accuracy and robustness under external disturbances; the abstract reports no numbers.

9kXz22fI7a.text:
• Problem: humanoid imitation learning needs many demonstrations, which are slow and hard to collect via teleoperation.
• Existing manipulator data-generation methods fail on humanoids' high-dimensional arm, leg, and torso action spaces.
• HumanoidMimicGen adapts contact-rich whole-body skills from a handful of source demos to new object poses.
• Interleaves single- and dual-arm skills with whole-body locomotion and manipulation planning for stable, collision-free data.
• New simulated benchmark: nine diverse tasks testing humanoid loco-manipulation across varied scenes and layouts.
• Generates large imitation datasets, enabling systematic study of data-generation and policy-learning design choices.
• Co-training whole-body visuomotor policies with generated data beats real-data-only training by 20%.

AGM5ZQRjOT.text:
• Problem: functional dexterous manipulation needs precise contact, coordinated arm-hand motion, and recovery from execution errors.
• Simulation poorly models contact dynamics, but real-world full arm-hand demonstrations are costly and noisy.
• Key idea: decouple control into a functional hand skill and an arm-hand coordination policy.
• Hand skill handles precise contact; coordination policy controls the arm and decides when to activate the skill.
• Method: hierarchical real-world RL with real-time human intervention and DMP-based data augmentation.
• Setup: six real-world functional tasks evaluated on two different multi-fingered dexterous hands.
• Results: 98.3% average success within one hour of online training, robust to dynamic disturbances.

NzvfxoRvOC.text:
• Problem: RL humanoid tracking policies are agile but struggle to satisfy safety constraints specified after training.
• Key idea: ConstrainedMimic enforces arbitrary runtime constraints on top of learned whole-body tracking policies in real time.
• Method: combines operational space control with control barrier functions using whole-body kinematics and dynamics.
• Constraints act on both the kinematic reference motion and the underlying robot dynamics.
• Setup: motion-tracking and teleoperation on a simulated Unitree G1, with self-collision, obstacle, joint-limit, and CoM-stability constraints.
• Respects current contact mode and tracking objectives, minimally restricting policy capabilities when constraints are active.
• Fully differentiable, runs on CPU/GPU/TPU at up to 300-500 Hz; software to be released upon publication.

cxxUgLuNa2.text:
• Problem: dexterous grasping across object scales needs varied contact modes, from two-finger pinches to bimanual grasps.
• Existing synthesis relies on hand-designed contacts and initialization heuristics, trading off success rate against diversity.
• Key idea: HUGS learns an object-conditioned human grasp prior instead of directly retargeting human demonstrations.
• The prior adaptively proposes contact modes and wrist initializations, then guides force-closure-aware optimization.
• Prior trained on a compact self-collected dataset: 1.8K human grasps over 304 diverse objects.
• Synthesized 3.2M robot grasps over 157K scenes, objects 2–30 cm half-diagonal, two-finger to bimanual.
• Trained models autonomously select contact modes in the real world, grasping objects from screws to large boxes.

9gWuAC6Oum.text:
• Problem: SLAM systems ignore functional relations between objects and interaction elements needed for fine-grained robot interaction.
• Existing functional 3D scene graph methods rely on offline reconstruction, unsuitable for real-time exploration.
• Key idea: Functional-SLAM maintains a functional scene graph continuously and recursively as an online SLAM state.
• Nodes persist via anchor-keyframe geometry combined with functional-context constraints.
• Stable functional edges are committed by accumulating multi-frame evidence through temporal relations.
• Functional topology supplements visual loop closure in repetitive-appearance or texture-degraded scenes.
• Results: much faster than offline methods with competitive accuracy, plus better pose accuracy than peer SLAM.

pENAQ22Jh1.text:
• Problem: long-horizon demonstrations for wheeled mobile manipulators are scarce, costly, and hard to collect at scale.
• Existing teleoperation and wearables suffer cognitive decoupling, poor scalability, and inconsistent action representations across modes.
• SuperSuit unifies robot-in-the-loop teleoperation and active human demonstration through one shared kinematic interface.
• Both modes yield identical joint-space trajectories, so data mixes directly without modifying downstream policies.
• Natural human stepping maps to continuous planar base velocities; an isomorphic wearable arm drives manipulation.
• Shift-invariant delta-joint actions mitigate calibration offsets and compliance without needing inverse kinematics.
• Real-world results: 2.6x throughput over teleoperation, comparable policy success, monotonic gains with more active data.

gqmJ7SIK5Q.text:
• Problem: humanoid RL lacks scalable, easy-to-train compliant force control, limiting forceful manipulation despite agile locomotion.
• Key idea: reinterpret demonstrated motions, in hindsight, as compliant responses to external perturbations.
• Method: adjust only sparse motion goals under perturbation, leaving dense reference trajectories untouched.
• Benefit: compliant interaction emerges naturally without degrading motion tracking rewards; framework is plug-and-play.
• Results: one policy performs wiping, cart pushing, door opening alongside dancing and running.
• Extends seamlessly to multi-agent cooperative transport; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• What's new: a single policy unifying adaptive compliance and agile whole-body humanoid motion tracking.

m0Zqqi9Lfr.text:
• Problem: AI copilots boost performance via shared control, but excessive assistance causes over-reliance and skill atrophy.
• Goal: an embodied AI coach that accelerates human motor-skill development rather than replacing human skill.
• Key idea: scaffold strategically and step back with learner capability, allowing productive failures that drive learning.
• Formalism: coaching as non-cooperative dynamic game; learner maximizes task performance, coach targets independent competence.
• Method: RL combining adaptive shared control with probabilistic models of coach's causal influence on skill evolution.
• Setup: user study with N=33 participants learning first-person-view drone racing.
• Results: significant gains in human learning outcomes over state-of-the-art AI coaching baselines.

cHCwUratwL.text:
• Problem: humanoid soccer demands coordinated balance, locomotion, ball interaction, and skill switching over long horizons.
• Gap: existing humanoid sports methods use task-specific multi-stage pipelines, hindering joint learning of multiple skills.
• Key idea: one command-conditioned RL policy learns and composes atomic soccer skills like dribbling, trapping, shooting.
• Method: skill-specific adversarial motion priors, skill-specific critics, and an object-aware temporal encoder.
• Setup: trained in simulation, deployed sim-to-real on a Noetix E1 humanoid robot.
• Results: robust multi-skill execution and long-horizon composition; the abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• What's new: a unified, single deployable policy for multiple object-interactive humanoid skills and smooth transitions.

8YqfXYof0Y.text:
• Problem: VLA models understand semantics but miss spatiotemporal dynamics of how the world responds to actions.
• Key idea: use privileged 4D information, 3D point tracks, as training-only supervision for world dynamics.
• Method: a lightweight point track head, fed VLA features, predicts future 3D trajectories alongside actions.
• The shared representation absorbs evolving scene geometry, giving action prediction a more physically-aware context.
• Compatible with dominant VLA designs; inference uses the unchanged VLA with no extra inputs or compute.
• Results: +10% on LIBERO-Long and +40% on RoboCasa, plus gains in real-world manipulation tasks.
• New: shows 3D point tracks are effective targets for learning action-world dynamics, backed by extensive ablations.

C96z0RnFh8.text:
• Problem: Variational Automation tasks involve larger object geometry and pose variation than fixed automation, demanding persistent reliability.
• Model-free policies adapt to open-world variation but often fail to close the industrial reliability gap.
• Key idea: combine interpretable robot programming with agentic coding, using graphs as policies.
• GaP's multi-agent coding harness builds directed perception, planning, and control graphs from a Modular Open Robot Skill Library.
• GaP generates internal simulations, rehearsing graph variants in parallel to refine structure and parameters for success and throughput.
• Setup: 8 new open VA benchmarks, 4 in simulation and 4 in the real world.
• Results: GaP significantly outperforms baselines in success rate; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

qMAfkDMTOy.text:
• Problem: perception-based humanoid loco-manipulation needs paired egocentric images, language, and robot-compatible whole-body kinematics.
• Bottleneck: no existing data source provides this complete vision-language-kinematics tuple at scale.
• Key idea: synthesize vision-language-kinematics (VLK) supervision automatically inside 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of real indoor scenes.
• Method: plan navigation and interaction trajectories with privileged scene info, then render matching egocentric views afterward.
• Scale: 48,000 paired trajectories generated with zero human intervention or teleoperation.
• Policy: VLK model predicts short-horizon whole-body kinematic trajectories; a whole-body tracker converts them to humanoid actions.
• Results: sim-to-real transfer on physical Unitree G1 for navigation and single-object transport from synthetic data alone.

NEtxISu52Q.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation needs force, tactile, or audio, but multisensory datasets are scarce and hardware-specific.
• Pretraining policies with every possible sensor is impractical, so new modalities must be added after pretraining.
• Task: multisensory continual learning, adapting pretrained policies to new tasks and sensors without losing original performance.
• Method MuSe: token-level multi-stage fusion, multisensory future prediction, and episodic recall on pretraining data.
• Setup: adds force-torque sensing to a pretrained vision-only policy, evaluated on real-world manipulation tasks.
• Results: strong on contact-rich finetuning tasks and also improves original pretraining tasks; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: a modest multisensory dataset can boost general capability beyond the finetuning distribution.

MWj9u2VZPx.text:
• Problem: building physically stable, visually faithful simulation scenes from real environments is slow and expensive.
• RoboSnap converts a single RGB image into a simulation-ready interactive scene for robot learning.
• Key idea: layered design separating physics-critical interaction area from surrounding visual context.
• Collision-aware foreground assets are refined for stable interaction; 3D Gaussian splatting preserves background appearance.
• Evaluated on DROID scenes and real-robot tasks: reliable trajectory replay in recovered scenes.
• Enables task-specific synthetic data for policy training and shows meaningful sim-real correlation for evaluation.
• New: DROID-Sim, a real-to-sim companion dataset built from 564 real-world DROID scenes.

aPppmSJzb5.text:
• Problem: delayed-evidence tasks, where an early cue vanishes before a later decision, making observations ambiguous.
• Current observation alone is not a sufficient state, so visuomotor imitation policies need memory to act correctly.
• Key idea: TRACE stores task-relevant visual and robot-state evidence in a fixed-size, bounded latent memory.
• Memory is indexed by path signatures, compact order-sensitive features of the executed robot-state trajectory.
• Signatures act as trajectory-conditioned keys for writing and retrieving evidence, not as storage of cues themselves.
• Plugs in via lightweight adapters, leaving policy backbone, action head, and imitation objective unchanged.
• Real-world long-horizon manipulation: beats short-history and recurrent memory baselines; abstract reports no specific numbers.

7jMlaTLtAc.text:
• Problem: deployed robot policies fail, naive retries repeat mistakes, and recovery often needs human intervention.
• Key idea: FAR lets robots learn from their own failures at test time and retry autonomously.
• Failure-Contrastive Preference Adaptation builds preference data from failures, steering the policy away from unsuccessful behaviors.
• Lightweight action perturbations during retries encourage local exploration around previously failed attempts.
• Successful recovery trajectories feed a training loop for continual policy improvement.
• Results: average gains over diffusion policy of 17.6% in simulation and 11.7% on real-world manipulation.
• New: failure cases are exploited as informative data, improving efficiency under reset and timestep budgets.

weyfPS89NJ.text:
• Problem: long-horizon robot skills depend on embodiment-specific affordances, which handcrafted or LLM-sampled task curricula ignore.
• LLM-generated tasks reflect semantic plausibility, yielding curricula that are too hard, redundant, or miss learnable behaviors.
• Key idea: FOSA learns a grounded task generator to discover what a specific robot can actually do.
• Method: a GFlowNet abstract policy builds symbolic task skeletons, each compiled into a simulation environment.
• Low-level policy-learning success on each generated task provides the reward signal for training the GFlowNet.
• Results: diverse, executable tasks near each robot's capability frontier, across heterogeneous platforms; the abstract reports no numbers.
• Distilled into one language-conditioned policy, discovered skills improve performance on unseen complex, long-horizon tasks.

QFFjW11NYa.text:
• Problem: adversarial attacks on VLA robot policies ignore how predicted commands are actually executed by controllers and hardware.
• Key insight: a command-execution gap exists between VLA-predicted task-space commands and what the robot can realize.
• ExecGap: an adversarial patch attack that biases predicted commands toward low-executability directions.
• Low-executability directions are estimated from kinematic inefficiency and dynamically weak actuation of the robot.
• Result: commands become hard to execute effectively, degrading execution and impairing task completion.
• Simulations across multiple VLA policies: larger command-execution mismatch and weaker execution than existing patch attacks.
• Real-robot experiments confirm physical patches induce execution degradation; code to be released upon acceptance.

zr63f3tmyq.text:
• Problem: multi-skill VLA policies under-model which primitive skill to execute and where/how to contact objects.
• Key idea: MAST-VLA, a dual-conditioning framework combining skill-conditioned experts with trajectory-affordance spatial priors.
• Method: skill-conditioned LoRA-MoE adapters in the LLM backbone, guided by skill-query tokens and routing biases.
• Method: predicted affordance heatmaps become patch-level trajectory-affordance priors feeding the action head.
• Setup: CALVIN ABC-D long-horizon multi-skill cross-scene generalization, plus real-robot multi-skill sequence experiments.
• Results: state-of-the-art Avg. Len of 4.65 over five-subtask evaluation sequences on CALVIN ABC-D.
• What's new: jointly conditions skill selection and contact/motion priors, deployable under real perception and control noise.

EL8hXhrhFK.text:
• Problem: humanoid whole-body controllers rely on fixed trajectories or constant teleoperation, limiting flexibility and autonomy.
• Goal: drive a universal humanoid controller in real time through interactive, streaming natural language commands.
• Key idea: TextOp supports on-the-fly instruction changes during execution, enabling free-form intent expression.
• Method: high-level autoregressive motion diffusion model generates short-horizon kinematic trajectories conditioned on current text.
• Low-level whole-body motion tracking policy executes generated trajectories robustly on a physical humanoid robot.
• Results: real-robot and offline tests show instant responsiveness, smooth motion, precise control; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: smooth transitions across dancing, jumping and other behaviors within one continuous text-driven execution.

GX5xey9ade.text:
• Problem: automated robot-demo annotation pipelines lack reliable quality signals; detector confidence poorly predicts label correctness.
• Key idea: SPARC assigns each spatial annotation a reliability score using robot tasks' spatio-temporal structure.
• Annotations include bounding boxes, object trajectories, and manipulation phase labels, generated automatically at scale.
• New benchmark IA-Bench measures grounding accuracy for interacted objects in robot demonstrations.
• Evaluated on 1.7k human-annotated demos across diverse embodiments; beats detection-only baselines, retaining 3x samples.
• Finetuned models reach state-of-the-art grounding and pointing among similar sizes, using no manually annotated data.
• Policies trained on SPARC annotations significantly outperform baselines in cluttered real scenes; code, data, models released.

zYpPmDICVV.text:
• Problem: robust multi-directional humanoid perceptive locomotion on complex terrains remains underexplored, especially while carrying payloads.
• Key idea: RPL, a two-stage framework distilling terrain-specific privileged experts into one multi-depth-camera transformer policy.
• Stage one trains terrain-specific experts on privileged height maps, decoupling locomotion and manipulation skills.
• Distillation adds velocity-based depth feature scaling and random side masking for asymmetric views and unseen terrain widths.
• New parallel multi-depth ray-casting system renders 5x faster, modeling sensor latency, noise, and dropout.
• Real-world: multi-directional walking with 2kg payload on 20° slopes and 22/25/30cm stairs.
• Also crosses 25x25cm stepping stones separated by 60cm gaps, demonstrating robust perceptive humanoid locomotion.

XjyM9If1Tm.text:
• Problem: feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long aerial video suffers cumulative trajectory drift and lacks geographic alignment.
• Key idea: ground reconstruction using public geo-referenced data: orthophoto maps (DOM), elevation models (DEM), and OpenStreetMap.
• Method: split long videos into overlapping chunks; a transformer visual geometry model regresses camera trajectories and point maps.
• Anchor frames per chunk are matched to geo-referenced maps, yielding correspondences and geometric constraints into global coordinates.
• New: test-time training fine-tunes a sparse subset of layers, aligning latent tokens to geographic coordinates.
• This test-time training corrects spatial drift while preserving structure; intra-chunk and global pose graph optimization ensure consistency.
• Results: beats feed-forward baselines by a large margin on three aerial benchmarks; abstract gives no figures; code promised.

VKVM1q9FbN.text:
• Problem: humanoid RL locomotion rarely tackles steep slopes, which demand simultaneous balance and posture control.
• Stage I: learns a blind locomotion prior using a terrain-aligned apparent ZMP regularizer on the local support plane.
• Issue: Stage I policies on steep inclines degrade into inefficient crouched gaits that overuse low CoM for stability.
• Stage II: Biomechanical Slope Gait Adapter conditions CoM-height, joint gait, and swing-leg priors on slope geometry.
• PCA terrain descriptors serve only as critic inputs and reward gates; the deployed actor stays purely proprioceptive.
• Encourages hip-dominant uphill propulsion and knee-oriented downhill braking; new Isaac Lab uphill terrain environments support training.
• Unitree G1 sim-to-real: reduces crouched gaits, enabling blind continuous traversal of outdoor grass slopes up to 25°.

Hi8mV09nOi.text:
• Problem: VLN research focuses on high-level reasoning, memory, and maps; low-level action representation stays underexplored.
• Key idea: predict a language-conditioned flow field over the robot's local visible sector, not discrete actions.
• Continuous trajectories are generated by rolling out the predicted flow field, making actions spatially queryable.
• Data: VLN-CE episodes converted into frame-level sub-instructions with matched action, trajectory, and dense flow targets.
• New benchmark: continuous-time Habitat setup isolating low-level action interfaces, using a shared velocity-command controller.
• Results: beats action-token and action-chunk baselines across planner frequencies under matched encoders and training.
• Zero-shot real-world closed-loop deployment also outperforms both baselines; abstract reports no specific numbers.

rcE4amkjBq.text:
• Problem: manipulation policies treat proprioception as an isolated vector, unaligned with visual tokens.
• Consequence: policies struggle to ground robot state in scenes, often underperforming vision-only baselines.
• Key idea: GeoProp, a lightweight plug-and-play adapter aligning proprioception with vision via explicit geometric grounding.
• Method: projects robot state onto image plane, samples local visual features to build grounded state token.
• Also injects state-derived spatial priors into visual features via FiLM, plus velocity-based look-ahead feature sampling.
• Results across 67 tasks: +9.4% success in simulation, +11.2% real world, only 3% more parameters.
• Takeaway: resolving state-vision misalignment is a simple, high-impact inductive bias for generalist embodied policies.

Ih059VNeWq.text:
• Problem: World Action Models suffer from text ambiguity in cluttered scenes and RGB predictions biased by irrelevant backgrounds.
• Key idea: MaskWAM, an object-centric world-action model using masks as both explicit inputs and predicted outputs.
• Method: a unified Mixture of Transformers jointly handles mask prompting and future mask prediction alongside video and actions.
• Predicting future masks adds object-centric semantic supervision, suppressing visual noise and improving even text-conditioned WAMs.
• First-frame visual prompts, such as target object masks, give precise spatial anchors that reduce language ambiguity.
• Setup: evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world tasks with both language-clear and language-ambiguous instructions.
• Results: significantly outperforms baselines and generalizes to unseen objects; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

cvPjGuUATQ.text:
• Problem: real-robot demonstrations are expensive; simulation and human data scale but each has gaps.
• Simulation suffers a sim-to-real visual gap; human data suffers a human-to-robot embodiment gap.
• Key idea: the two sources are complementary, with sim supplying robot-valid actions and humans supplying real visuals.
• Method: SimHum co-trains kinematic priors from simulation and visual priors from human observations.
• Policy is then fine-tuned on a small real-robot dataset for bimanual tabletop manipulation.
• Results: up to 40% better than the best single-source pre-training baseline in a controlled data-collection study.
• Across four tasks, 80 real episodes yield 62.5% OOD scene success, 7.1x over Real-only.

quVJ7qbQl6.text:
• Problem: fine-tuned robot policies take shortcuts on salient cues instead of grounding language, hurting compositional generalization.
• Key idea: diagnose failures per instruction factor, such as color, verb, object, size, and spatial attribute.
• Formalizes instruction factor bias, meaning policies over-rely on dominant factors as shortcuts.
• Metrics: Factor Dominance Rate for pairwise bias, Factor Dominance Hierarchy for global ranking.
• Across six foundation policies, consistent ordering: color ≥ object ≥ spatial ≥ verb ≥ size.
• Bias-aware data collection reallocates a fixed budget toward under-grounded factors like verb and size.
• Beats baselines in simulation and real robot using half the demonstrations, improving sample efficiency.

8CDEvBQA6x.text:
• Problem: simulation-optimized dexterous grasps often fail in the real world, especially with collisions, clutter and occlusion.
• Key idea: automatically verify simulation-generated grasps on real hardware, with minimal human intervention.
• Method: a multi-camera setup checks physical grasp feasibility where single-view perception typically fails.
• Coverage-preserving grasp selection algorithm keeps the dataset diverse across a wide range of geometric configurations.
• Setup: validated on 100 objects with diverse geometries, producing a large-scale dataset of real-world-verified firm grasps.
• Results: grasps are substantially more reliable than simulation alone and more diverse for highly constrained environments.
• New: an automated pipeline that is more efficient than human teleoperation, collecting more valid and diverse grasps.

FsgXevFLkn.text:
• Problem: dexterous manipulation needs both long-term foresight and fast reactive control during contact changes.
• VLAs lack physical dynamics understanding; World-Action Models suffer high latency from iterative generation.
• LiMA: asynchronous dual-system diffusion framework decoupling slow intent planning from fast reactive execution.
• Slow system generates sparse long-horizon spatiotemporal intent; fast system refines dense high-frequency motion.
• New Latent Schrödinger Bridge Coupling aligns sparse intents with dense actions via entropy-regularized transport.
• Cuts inference latency by 45.8% versus Cosmos-Policy through asynchronous decoupling.
• Six bimanual dexterous tasks: 70.8% overall success, 78.5% average subtask success, robust in unseen scenarios.

c0ygOLwL7i.text:
• Navigation diffusion policies pretrained on single-robot oracle demonstrations generalize poorly to new embodiments and hard scenarios.
• Hard cases like dead ends and long obstacles need reactive behaviors using only onboard local observations.
• Prior diffusion RL post-training gives marginal gains due to intractable likelihoods, unstable gradients, and weak exploration.
• GQRM: data-efficient RL post-training via Q-value reweighted score matching, avoiding unstable diffusion policy gradients.
• Self-bootstrapped exploration perturbs behavior while preserving the pretrained policy prior; group Q-score normalization weights per-state trajectories.
• Distributed online RL across heterogeneous embodiments yields X-NavDP, a cross-embodiment visual navigation policy.
• Success rises from 61.20% to 84.28% in simulation and 10% to 65% on real-world hard cases.

OIhLrULoIq.text:
• Problem: VLAs reason in language but miss physical dynamics; world-action models learn from videos but lack reasoning.
• Key idea: world-language-action (WLA) models jointly predict textual subtasks, subgoal images, and robot actions.
• Method: autoregressive Transformer predicts next-state, combining semantic intentions with fine-grained physical dynamics from a World Expert.
• Meta-queries let world prediction implicitly guide the Action Expert, so it can be disabled at inference.
• Enabling world prediction at inference allows test-time scaling for improved robot control.
• WLA-0 prototype: 2B active parameters, 40 ms per inference on an RTX 5090, evaluated in simulation and real-world.
• Results: state-of-the-art 92.94% on RoboTwin2.0 Clean, 56.5% on RMBench; promising for action-free cross-embodiment video learning.

1HqdYVWaXi.text:
• Problem: dense VLM embeddings are noisy and spatially inconsistent, hurting robots that reason jointly over semantics and 3D.
• Analysis: authors examine spatial structure across recent VLMs, finding intermediate features more spatially consistent than outputs.
• Key idea: ReSiReg reconstructs dense language features from spatially consistent VLM intermediates to improve language-grounded retrieval.
• Method: cluster intermediates into visual prototypes, derive their language descriptors, reconstruct patches as soft prototype mixtures.
• Setup: evaluated on open-vocabulary semantic segmentation and 3D mapping across backbones, plus real-world manipulation scenes.
• Results: improved dense retrieval quantitatively; manipulation scenes show more spatially consistent target activations; no headline numbers in abstract.
• New: compact 25M-parameter dense VLM, much smaller than yet competitive with ViT-B baselines; code and weights forthcoming.

f9grq4Ncx9.text:
• Problem: action-conditioned world models forget or hallucinate scene content hidden by end-effector occlusion and fast wrist-camera motion.
• Prior fixes like longer context, joint-pose retrieval, or field-of-view overlap often miss informative history in dynamic manipulation.
• Key idea: Ctrl-Mem, a memory-augmented, multi-view, action-conditioned world model that retrieves geometry-relevant past frames.
• Core component: W-VMem, a 4D wrist-view-centered memory anchoring past observations to temporally evolving surface elements (surfels).
• Method: surfel rendering and scoring for future wrist poses select informative, non-redundant history frames as generation context.
• Results: more temporally consistent rollouts, beating prior methods under replay-based evaluation; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Policy evaluation strongly correlates with real-world performance, and Ctrl-Mem improves policy performance on long-horizon tasks.

hvArz6F8eA.text:
• Problem: safe human–robot collaboration needs monitors that detect present or imminent robot collisions, not just describe scenes.
• Key idea: "collision grounding" binds vision to robot geometry, viewpoint, layout, human proximity, and motion.
• New benchmark: TouchSafeBench, built in Habitat 3.0 with 2,940 indoor human–robot co-presence episodes.
• Data: multi-view RGB-D, top-down trajectory maps, calibrated cameras, and simulator-derived contact labels.
• Tasks: classify current safety state and warn about imminent collision before contact occurs.
• Results: across three VLMs and nine visual representations, best average Macro-F1 stays below 50%.
• Findings: depth doesn't automatically become collision evidence; robot–scene contact is harder than human-contact risk.

ecN9efL5zs.text:
• Problem: robotics simulation lacks large, diverse, realistic articulated assets like drawers, doors, and cabinets for training.
• Key idea: procedurally generate unlimited articulated, simulation-ready objects instead of relying on limited hand-made asset datasets.
• Introduces Infinigen-Articulated, a toolkit with procedural generators covering 18 common articulated object categories.
• Provides high-level Blender utilities so researchers can build their own custom articulated asset generators.
• Export pipeline brings assets and their physical properties into common robotics simulators.
• Generated assets proved effective for movable object segmentation and training generalizable reinforcement learning policies.
• Also enabled sim-to-real transfer of imitation learning policies; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

E5lvpA2Glx.text:
• Problem: VLA policies generalize poorly because collecting diverse real manipulation data across object appearances is costly.
• Key idea: EMMA augments VLA training with generated videos plus an adaptive training strategy.
• DreamTransfer: diffusion Transformer generating multi-view consistent, geometrically plausible manipulation videos via text-driven editing.
• Edits foreground, background and lighting while preserving 3D structure and geometric fidelity of original scenes.
• AdaMix: adaptively weights mixed real and generated samples by policy performance, emphasizing challenging samples.
• Setup: over 1800 trials across simulation and real robots, including zero-shot unseen visual settings.
• Results: over 92% relative gain versus real-only training in the real world, plus 17% more with AdaMix.

u2dtQWAFQo.text:
• Problem: GMT humanoid teleoperation controllers suffer foot skating, dragging, and mistimed foot-ground contact transitions.
• Kinematic metrics miss this gap; adapting frozen GMT backbones creates a retention-adaptation trade-off.
• Controlled study compares full fine-tuning, residual adaptation, and low-rank updates under matched supervision and budget.
• CA-GMT: contact-grounded foot rewards plus low-rank update of a frozen GMT backbone.
• Results: False Contact Rate drops 0.401 to 0.235, tracking error down 16%, jerkiness down 37%.
• Phase-conditional variant adapting only swing frames reaches FCR 0.199, also lowest on Unitree G1 hardware.
• Low-rank adaptation preserves out-of-distribution tracking better than full fine-tuning and residual variants tested.

Z04KxYWC6V.text:
• Problem: VLA models rely on 2D visual backbones, limiting depth, spatial-relation, and contact-rich action reasoning.
• Key idea: geometry should be organized around task-relevant objects, relations, and affordances, not injected in isolation.
• Method: 3D Semantic-Aware Feature Generator fuses RGB semantics, depth, and instructions into 3D Reasoning Tokens.
• Tokens condition the action head via a FiLM-based geometry-conditioned decoder, directly modulating action generation.
• Setup: evaluated on simulated benchmarks and real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
• Results: better overall performance and training efficiency, with largest gains on spatially demanding tasks.
• New: 100% success on LIBERO-Spatial, a new state of the art and reportedly first to saturate it.

RYXo2ktK1M.text:
• Problem: pretrained VLAs generalize broadly but lack the precision and speed real-world manipulation tasks demand.
• Key idea: expose a compact "RL token" readout from the VLA as an efficient interface for online RL.
• The RL token preserves task-relevant pretrained knowledge while keeping RL lightweight and sample-efficient.
• Method: a small actor-critic head on the RL token refines actions, anchored to the VLA's policy.
• Setup: four real-robot tasks covering screw installation, zip tie fastening, charger insertion, and Ethernet insertion.
• Results: up to 3× faster on the hardest task phase, with significantly higher success after minutes to hours.
• New: enables fast real-world RL fine-tuning of large VLAs, sometimes surpassing human teleoperation speed.

uHhNEb0OSW.text:
• Asynchronous VLA execution predicts next chunks during motion, causing boundary misalignment with already-committed actions.
• Existing delay-aware fixes need retraining, architecture changes, or costly fixed-prefix inpainting that inflates latency.
• FreeBar: training-free plugin casting chunk alignment in flow-based VLAs as barrier-guided action-space constraint.
• CBF-inspired consistency constraint between consecutive chunks, solved in closed form, avoiding backpropagation through action head.
• Progressively tightening consistency bound preserves early generative flexibility while aligning chunks with committed execution stream.
• Tested on Kinetix, RoboCasa, real robots, multiple VLA backbones: 10–15% average success gain over naive async.
• Cuts per-chunk inference latency over 45% versus RTC; robust across latencies, base policies, and hyperparameters.

qx5mPYiXVi.text:
• Offline-to-online robot RL is powerful but complex, making system behavior hard to reproduce and diagnose.
• Core question: how value-function reliability affects value-guided learning across offline pretraining and online adaptation.
• Introduces value-reliability metrics measuring global task-level progress and local action-level preference quality.
• Study spans a full pipeline, 240 hours of pretraining data, and over 3,000 rollout trajectories.
• Reliable value functions let offline RL scale better than quality-agnostic behavior cloning.
• More reliable values stabilize online adaptation by prioritizing high-quality rollout data.
• Achieves 86% on millimeter-precise chip insertion, 84% on block disassembly; framework and data to be released.

WF4X17Al2r.text:
• Problem: unclear whether large-scale human video can teach fine-grained, high-DoF dexterous robot manipulation.
• Key idea: treat diverse egocentric human data as scalable, predictable supervision for dexterous policies.
• Method: Vision-Language-Action model pretrained on 20,854 hours of action-labeled egocentric human video, 20x prior efforts.
• Recipe: large-scale human pretraining, then lightweight aligned human-robot mid-training for transfer.
• Finding: log-linear scaling law between human data and validation loss, strongly predicting real-robot success.
• Results: 54% average success-rate gain over no-pretraining baseline on 22-DoF hand, plus one-shot adaptation.
• New: transfers to lower-DoF hands, suggesting human motion is a reusable, embodiment-agnostic motor prior.

iIanOcE27q.text:
• Problem: robot grasps must be firm enough to hold objects yet gentle enough to avoid damage.
• Challenge: the right force depends on density, elasticity and friction, which are rarely known beforehand.
• Key idea: estimate material properties in real time from visuotactile sensing during the grasp itself.
• Method: estimated properties feed a simulation-built model that predicts the minimum force needed to hold the object.
• New dataset: real fruits and vegetables with measured shape, mass, elasticity and friction.
• Setup: validated on a real robot with a parallel-jaw gripper across a wide variety of objects.
• Results: the system gently grasped diverse objects and adapted to each; the abstract reports no numbers.

42z4ov9nRQ.text:
• Problem: VLAs are mostly Markovian, failing tasks needing memory of past contact events.
• Vision-based memory is computationally expensive and fails when events look identical, like repeated button presses.
• Key idea: FM-VLA uses force history as compact memory for non-Markovian, contact-rich manipulation.
• Method: VAE pretrained on force time-series reconstruction encodes force histories into compact memory tokens.
• Force latents plus short state history condition the action expert as additional tokens.
• Setup: three memory tasks: finding hidden block, pressing button, wiping dish a set number of times.
• Results: over 80% success, minimal inference overhead, significantly outperforming baselines; first force-based VLA memory.

0gwpqWBvhJ.text:
• Problem: learning policy representations from unlabeled multi-policy data, each episode generated by a fixed, unobserved policy.
• Key idea: adapt implicit neural representations from vision to behavior, representing a policy as a state-to-action function.
• Method: an episode-level latent modulates this function via FiLM layers, giving a self-supervised generative prior over policies.
• Enables policy identity inference without labels, by inferring the latent that best explains an episode's behavior.
• New: defines policy-level OOD shifts along state- and action-distribution axes, missed by agent- or environment-level OOD settings.
• Setup: synthetic GRF, Seek-Avoid, MuJoCo, chess, Formula 1, and robotic manipulation datasets.
• Results: abstract reports no numbers; gains are most consistent in continuous settings with longer episodes, more policies, and OOD splits.

qbninLImrj.text:
• Problem: navigation benchmarks reward task success but ignore economic constraints of commercial autonomous delivery.
• Key idea: CostNav scores physical AI agents by cost-revenue, contribution margin, and break-even analysis.
• Method: Isaac Sim collision and cargo dynamics combined with SEC filings and AIS injury report data.
• Setup: seven baselines evaluated, two rule-based and five imitation-learning navigation methods.
• Result: no method is economically viable; all baselines produce negative contribution margins.
• CANVAS (RGB+GPS) leads among SLA-compliant methods at -$28.40/run versus LiDAR Nav2 w/ GPS -$37.34/run.
• New: first physics-grounded economic benchmark; sim SLA compliance closely matches real delivery robot results.

Bshs9HDDiu.text:
• Problem: VLA models generalize semantically but fail on unseen physical motions in novel environments.
• Key idea: World Action Models learn physical dynamics by jointly predicting future video and robot actions.
• Method: DreamZero builds on a pretrained video diffusion backbone, using video as dense world-evolution representation.
• Data: learns diverse skills from heterogeneous robot data, without needing repetitive demonstrations.
• Results: over 2x better generalization to new tasks in new environments versus state-of-the-art VLAs.
• Setup: evaluated in real-robot experiments with closed-loop control on unseen tasks and environments.
• What's new: model and system optimizations let a 14B autoregressive video diffusion model run at 7Hz.

1u6oriJJcU.text:
• Problem: World Action Models predict future frames, but inference-time video prediction adds costly latency.
• Efficient WAMs drop vision at deployment, yet predicted futures stay auxiliary, not guiding policy improvement.
• Key idea: WAM-STEP repurposes the training-only visual branch as an internal imagination module for self-improvement.
• Step 1: calibrate visual branch on mixed-quality rollouts with action-conditioned preference loss for action-following prediction.
• Step 2: freeze visuals, optimize actions via reward-scored imagined futures with policy-anchor group-relative baseline.
• Results: RoboCasa365 success rises 20.7% to 24.0%; real-world tasks reach 62.5%, +20 points.
• New: consequence-to-action feedback without separate world-model simulator or video generation at inference.

93leGzRaPV.text:
• Problem: music-driven dance generators produce expressive but physically invalid motions for humanoid robots.
• Even expert-trained trackers accumulate a feasibility gap over long generated dance sequences.
• Key idea: latent-guided closed-loop system streaming music-conditioned dance directly to a physical humanoid.
• Planner uses diffusion forcing with causal receding noise schedule and cross-modal music-motion alignment.
• Tracker feedback corrects next-token predictions via latent optimization during both training and inference.
• Data: about 50 hours of dance, 30 hours lab mocap plus 20 hours filtered public data.
• Results: continuous, physically plausible, high-dynamic robot dance across diverse music styles and genres.

7UeBDg4KRa.text:
• Problem: text-to-motion pipelines generate kinematics for separate trackers, limiting interactive, closed-loop humanoid language control.
• Key idea: end-to-end closed-loop control that continuously responds to changing text commands while maintaining balance.
• Method: diffusion-based action prior learned from text-labeled humanoid state-action trajectories executes skills directly from language.
• A lightweight residual RL policy atop the frozen diffusion controller improves long-horizon robustness and prompt switching.
• The same diffusion policy serves as a steerable text-conditioned motion prior for downstream task adaptation.
• Results: robust language-grounded skills, smooth interactive transitions, style-preserving downstream control; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• What's new: a unified end-to-end alternative to kinematic generation plus tracking for interactive text-driven humanoid control.

CPY2RsdnjI.text:
• Problem: robot hands and fixed cameras occlude large parts of grasped objects, hindering in-hand 3D reconstruction.
• Gap: existing methods use predefined or open-loop reorientation that does not explicitly target unobserved surfaces.
• Key idea: AURORA actively reorients objects in-hand to expose the most uncertain, unseen regions.
• Method: Ray-GPIS planner estimates reconstruction uncertainty along candidate viewing rays to select next-best views.
• Execution: an axis-conditioned in-hand rotation policy reaches targets; visual fusion builds the 3D model incrementally.
• Results: real-world tests on diverse geometries show higher surface completeness and faster reconstruction than baselines.
• Note: the abstract reports no specific numbers; details are at aurorahand.github.io.

zMbOvWpUUw.text:
• Problem: bimanual dexterous handover between two robot hands is fundamental yet underexplored compared to single-hand grasping.
• Challenge: giver must leave clearance for receiver while both hands manage finger contacts and avoid interference.
• Key idea: DexHandover, a generative "Shape-to-Motion" framework mapping object geometry directly to full bimanual handover motion.
• Data: optimization pipeline generates a large-scale synthetic dataset of physically validated bimanual handover poses.
• Method: two-stage generative model predicts handover poses; RL synthesizes giver-to-receiver motion anchored at those poses.
• Setup: validated in simulation, then trajectories retargeted to robot hands for robot-to-robot dexterous handover.
• Results: abstract reports reliable handover from object geometry alone but gives no quantitative numbers.

pWDT36r945.text:
• Problem: long-horizon humanoid teleoperation needs sustained spatial awareness, which current interfaces shorten.
• Concept: "perceptual horizon," the extent of operator awareness of objects, surroundings, and robot pose over time.
• Existing limits: narrow views, shaky robot-mounted cameras during walking, and head-coupled view control disrupting robot motion.
• SPOT: VR teleoperation combining binocular fisheye camera, wide-field stereoscopic display, free-looking, and visual stabilization.
• Key idea: stereo view rendered on virtual hemisphere, so head rotation explores the view without moving the robot.
• Evaluated on drop recovery, peripheral retrieval, bimanual manipulation, fine alignment, and dynamic interaction tasks.
• Results: improved efficiency, accuracy, recovery speed, and operator workload; abstract reports no specific numbers.

7vjPgJ7x2b.text:
• Problem: free-form language instructions let inattentive or malicious drivers command unsafe maneuvers in driving VLA models.
• New benchmark suite tests safe navigation following, navigation-scene conflict awareness, and robustness to adversarial instructions.
• Finding: existing VLA driving policies fall short on both safe instruction following and conflict awareness.
• Key idea: decouple conflict reasoning from action generation via interpretable conflict prediction before acting.
• Navigation-conditioned world model "dreams" the instructed maneuver to check feasibility before the policy commits.
• Results: state-of-the-art 83.64 Driving Score and 59.82% Success Rate on Bench2Drive closed-loop benchmark.
• Closed-loop language following improves 48.7%; collisions under unsafe instructions drop from 66 to 45 versus prior SOTA.

JbpsGhdjs9.text:
• Problem: humanoid RL relies on costly MoCap data that lacks scene geometry, causing foot slippage and mesh penetration.
• Key idea: learn coupled motion-terrain interactions directly from ordinary monocular video via 3D scene reconstruction.
• Method: 3D vision models segment and reconstruct human trajectories plus terrain and object geometry from video.
• Kinematic-consistency optimization extracts high-quality motion data from noisy visual reconstructions.
• Contact-invariant retargeting transfers human-environment contact features to the humanoid robot.
• Results: robust, highly dynamic humanoid behaviors across diverse challenging terrains; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• What's new: low-cost consumer-grade monocular pipeline replaces MoCap, offering scalable scene-aware humanoid skill learning.

xWoyO2BPcl.text:
• Problem: companion robots lack affective perception; shared movie viewing demands viewer-level emotion understanding from egocentric views.
• New benchmark EgoScreen-Emotion: 224 trailers, 28,667 egocentric keyframes, 18 viewing conditions, 5 annotators.
• Viewing conditions vary camera height, distance, and angle; agreement Fleiss κ=0.34 overall, 0.72 high-confidence.
• Significant FPV domain gap: Macro-F1 drops from 28.06 to 14.64 Raw→FPV, a 47.8% relative decline.
• Method: multimodal long-context model fusing 3-frame visuals, synchronized audio, and narrative summaries.
• Confidence-aware aggregation and label smoothing yield Macro-F1 32.74, 84.3% of human reference, beating Gemini-2.5-Flash (23.50).
• First shared-viewing affect benchmark, validated end-to-end on a physical quadruped; dataset, code, weights to be released.

03zMMFkTXk.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation needs force sensing, but most commodity arms lack costly dedicated force sensors.
• Key idea: learn external joint torques from data instead of adding force-sensing hardware.
• NEXT trains in 1 minute on just 10 minutes of free-motion data.
• NEXT torque estimates are comparable to dedicated joint-torque sensors.
• NEXT enables force-feedback teleoperation on low-cost off-the-shelf robot arms.
• FIRST up-samples pre-contact segments during behavior cloning, beating prior force-aware policies by 14%+ on five long-horizon tasks.
• New: force-aware teleoperation and policy learning without extra sensors; code and videos at jasonjzliu.com/factr2.

4soIQrXqxj.text:
• Problem: grasping policies fail to transfer across robot hands with different kinematics and degrees of freedom.
• Key idea: diffusion-based grasp generation explicitly conditioned on hand morphology for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping.
• Method: grasps from diverse hands mapped into a unified canonical hand representation for shared learning.
• Conditioning: hand kinematics encoded as graphs, combined with object geometry, continuously guide the diffusion process.
• Training: new joint-level loss over the hand kinematic structure constrains generated grasps.
• Setup: new benchmark evaluating grasp generation across robot hands with varied morphologies.
• Results: strong zero-shot generalization to unseen hands; abstract reports no specific numbers.

2vDRocNuih.text:
• Problem: real-world RL struggles with contact-rich industrial manipulation needing micrometer precision, 99+% success, fast cycles.
• Bottleneck: no intuitive, physically feasible interface for collecting demonstrations and interventions for off-policy RL.
• Key idea: kinesthetic teaching via admittance control constrains human guidance to trajectories the robot and policy can reproduce.
• Method: control stack maps low-frequency RL actions to high-frequency torques via a reference generator and impedance controller.
• Reference generator preserves tracking performance while improving contact handling and producing smoother policy actions.
• Setup: four difficult insertion and industrial assembly benchmarks, including a complex datacenter compute tray.
• Results: cycle time reduced 23-48%, human interventions reduced 62-86%, a practical step toward production deployment.

hDNvcoKMXH.text:
• Problem: large dexterous grasp datasets are mostly used only for grasp generation and pick-and-place.
• Question: can grasp data enable functional dexterity in articulated tool use, not just grasping?
• Method: hierarchical imitation learning, with high-level hand sub-goal prediction and a low-level goal-conditioned controller.
• Pretraining: 355k-trajectory dataset built from grasp annotations pretrains the controller, then demo fine-tuning.
• Benchmark: new DexCraft simulation suite with six articulated tool-use tasks needing coordinated finger motion.
• Results: beats end-to-end diffusion policies and from-scratch hierarchical policies; +33.3 points real-world success over DP3.
• Takeaway: grasp datasets serve as scalable pretraining data for contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

HvKifHMHcM.text:
• Problem: VLAs lack consistent 3D geometry linking perception, motion reasoning, and action generation.
• Key idea: unify scene, future motion, and actions in one shared robot-centric 3D frame.
• Lifts pretrained VLM features into spatially grounded 3D scene tokens, preserving vision-language priors.
