• Actionable 3D Trajectory Field predicts how task-relevant scene points will move in 3D space.
• Trajectory field acts as latent reasoning, conditioning a 3D flow-based policy via geometry-aware attention.
• Results: SOTA on CALVIN and LIBERO, competitive on RoboTwin2.0, beats strong baselines on real robots.
• Ablations: gains come from end-to-end geometric consistency, not future-motion prediction alone.

ZAdTLinUnd.text:
• Problem: VLA models rely on 2D image-text priors and miss the 3D dynamics behind physical actions.
• Key idea: use 3D flow reconstructed from RGB video as training-only supervision for VLA models.
• Method: dual-level flow supervision through lightweight auxiliary heads, pluggable into existing 2D VLA backbones.
• Point-level flow forecasts future displacements of task-critical 3D points in the scene.
• TCP-level flow aggregates point motions to align with the robot's tool-center-point trajectories.
• Results: gains in manipulation success, zero-shot robustness and data efficiency, in simulation and real-world tests.
• New: no 3D sensors, no architecture changes, no extra inference compute, since auxiliary heads are discarded.

uizBY3yrgz.text:
• Problem: real robot data is costly; collected tasks often lack diversity in objects, scenes, and skills.
• Key idea: automatically generate diverse, informative manipulation task proposals to maximize value of collected data.
• RoboGene: agentic framework combining diversity-driven sampling, self-reflection quality checks, and human-verified feedback memory.
• Works across heterogeneous embodiments: single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation robots.
• Setup: large-scale real-world collection of 18k trajectories, plus new metrics for task feasibility and diversity.
• Results: generated tasks significantly outperform GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro on feasibility and diversity.
• VLA models pre-trained on RoboGene data achieve higher real-world success rates and stronger generalization.

YTw6LOO9C5.text:
• Problem: fine-tuning VLAs on few robot demos erodes semantic structure inherited from pretrained vision-language models.
• Question: what makes a good action representation? Inspired by mirror neurons, which share intention-level encoding.
• Probing shows semantic structure degrades during fine-tuning, tracking both task success and out-of-distribution generalization.
• Key idea: anchor action representations to a semantic manifold from pretrained encoders during training.
• Method splits representations into shared semantic and private channels; plug-and-play, discarded at inference.
• Deployed model stays unchanged; validated on multiple VLA backbones across simulation and real-world benchmarks.
• Results: up to +18.7% real-world in-distribution success and +21.5% out-of-distribution generalization.

tsWZwXGz5P.text:
• Problem: dexterous manipulation data is expensive, and fragmented hardware prevents pooling demonstrations across robot platforms.
• Shared visuomotor policies suffer visual entanglement, mixing task semantics with embodiment-specific appearance.
• AdvDex: unified Vision-Language-Action framework for scalable cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation learned from human demonstrations.
• OmniShare: large multimodal human demonstration dataset providing high-fidelity priors, bypassing costly teleoperation.
• JAAS action space: canonical SE(3) wrist plus 15 finger joints, unifying human hands, dexterous hands, and grippers.
• Domain-adversarial learning decouples embodiment-specific visual features from universal task skills.
• Physical experiments: beats single-embodiment baselines, with zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation; abstract reports no numbers.

xn8Hwa4hpq.text:
• Problem: tactile representations and policies are tied to specific sensors, blocking transfer across robots and hardware.
• Key idea: learn one shared latent space for resistive, magnetic, and vision-based tactile sensors.
• Method: modality-specific encoders map tactile signals into the shared latent, trained on paired contact data.
• Encoders are trained jointly across all sensor pairs, producing a consistent latent space for every sensor type.
• Analysis: the latent aligns sensors while preserving object-level contact information, per sensor-identity and object classification tests.
• Tasks: pick-and-place, plug insertion, board wiping, and object reorientation, with zero-shot transfer between physically distinct sensors.
• Result: average transfer success rises from 27.5% (vision-only) to 45.9%, a step toward sensor-agnostic tactile manipulation.

xfZJ2GKrZG.text:
• Problem: optimization is valuable for robotics but existing frameworks are too slow and poorly integrated with learning.
• RoboKit: a general-purpose toolkit for parallel differentiable optimization tailored to robot learning.
• Built in a kernel-level language, pairing multi-seed sampling with versatile optimizers for performance and flexibility.
• Well-tuned engineering delivers over 10x speedup compared with prior optimization frameworks.
• Geometry and differentiable rendering are first-class, accelerated via hybrid and coarse-to-fine representations.
• Optimizes 1024 grasps in just 2 seconds.
• Fully differentiable costs enable distilling optimization into policies that run faster while matching or surpassing optimization.

UZnHsKKAAB.text:
• Problem: teleoperated robot demonstrations are expensive, labor-intensive, and hard to scale to diverse scenes and long-horizon tasks.
• Key idea: generate manipulation data autonomously via scene generation, reusable RL interaction skills, and VLM-guided tree search.
• Method: a VLM hierarchically decomposes tasks into subgoals, and closed-loop RL skills execute contact-rich interactions.
• The pipeline collects long-horizon demonstrations with built-in failure recovery and adaptive re-planning.
• Setup: evaluated on the LIBERO-PRO benchmark and on a real Franka robot.
• Results: scales high-quality data, and simulation training improves generalization to novel scenarios; the abstract reports no numbers.
• Novelty: adaptive reasoning over geometry and scene layout replaces fixed sequences of controllers, grasp predictors, and planners.

YrNlVJcApO.text:
• Problem: world-action models train mostly on successful demos, so they rarely predict consequences of bad actions.
• Existing WAMs generate future videos, then recover actions via inverse dynamics or use videos as goals.
• Key idea: CAM, a causal world-action model predicting future video and task progress conditioned on executed actions.
• Action conditioning lets failure rollouts supervise action consequences, so bad actions become valid targets, not discarded data.
• Failure-aware progress predictor learns success and failure outcomes, optionally scoring sampled action candidates at inference.
• Setup: simulated and real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, compared against many existing world-action model baselines.
• Results: CAM beats baselines, improves with more failure data, and reduces success-biased hallucination; abstract reports no numbers.

2nityiXWGJ.text:
• Problem: action-conditioned video world models must either learn robot-specific controller semantics or leak outcomes via logged states.
• Key idea: condition on the middle signal, a nominal trajectory from the robot's own controller and kinematics.
• The nominal trajectory is available at deployment, computed before any scene interaction is observed, so outcomes don't leak.
• Method: render nominal robot geometry plus camera-aware static RGB/depth context as a shared visual interface.
• The video model sees actions only as geometry, learning how objects, surfaces, and occlusions respond, from fixed and dynamic viewpoints.
• Results: beats Cartesian/vector action-conditioning baselines on DROID and RoboCasa-GR1; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
• Ablations confirm nominalization and depth help; probes include counterfactual redirection, held-out embodiments, and human-to-robot video.

2dEfANeQL7.text:
• Problem: scaling humanoid loco-manipulation data via teleoperation or motion capture is costly and physically constrained.
• Key idea: fully virtual pipeline combining 3D assets, simulator scenes, and video foundation model priors.
• Starts from known geometry, camera, metric scale, depth, and robot-proportioned character before generating videos.
• This privileged setup enables metric 4D human-object interaction recovery with less depth ambiguity and morphology mismatch.
• Motions retargeted to humanoid; object-aware latent adaptor and scene-aware tracker handle manipulation and terrain.
• Generates over 20,000 sequences: pick-up, object manipulation, sitting, and terrain traversal.
• Egocentric policies trained only on GRAIL data reach 84% pick-up and 90% stair-climbing success on Unitree G1.

M8NqiSkMDr.text:
• Problem: generative imitation policies output dense action sequences that are hard to verify, repair, or synthesize.
• Key idea: replace dense action head with piecewise Bernstein polynomials defined by few control points.
• Method: generative policy samples control points conditioned on scene geometry and affordance-predicted grasp poses.
• Bernstein properties enable procedural synthetic training data from a single demonstration and analytic safety guarantees.
• Infeasible trajectories repaired by sequential convex projection, minimally adjusting control points, preserving start, grasp, place poses.
• Results: ~82-200x faster wall-clock, ~129x fewer FLOPs per episode, ~10x fewer gradient updates.
• Performance comparable to state-of-the-art, while adding verifiable, repairable, collision-free trajectories via compact parameterization.

uoFfrJHHq8.text:
• Problem: bidirectional-thrust quadrotors enable inverted flight, perching, and sensing, but aggressive inversions remain hard.
• Prior Hopf fibration geometric control struggles with actuator saturation and motor reversal delay, needing heuristic tuning.
• Key idea: RL policies modulate a constant reference trajectory for compact, position-constrained quadrotor inversions.
• Method: separate policies trained for nominal-to-inverted and inverted-to-nominal transitions, compatible with standard tracking controllers.
• Simulation (JAX): 32% lower position RMSE and 57% faster settling than strongest optimization-based baseline.
• Hardware: successful inversions across multiple yaw configurations with position RMSE below 0.35 m.
• New: circular flight in both regimes shows downstream trajectory compatibility; open-source implementation released.

6epaMjDFWZ.text:
• Problem: manipulation data must be semantically meaningful and physically executable; current pipelines usually deliver only one.
• Human demos capture intent but are costly and suffer the human-robot embodiment gap; simulation under-specifies function.
• Key idea: IM-ENGINE uses image editing as an intermediate representation for simulator-grounded embodied data generation.
• Method: edit rendered scenes, recover 3D state via simulator priors and anchor object, refine physically, output supervision.
• Grasping: generate human grasp in image, recover hand-object interaction, retarget to robot hand, physically validate.
• Goal generation: edit scene into desired outcome, recover object pose, refine into valid goals and trajectories.
• What's new: combines generative semantic priors with simulator grounding; abstract reports no quantitative results.

r7ZN8cPEcj.text:
• Problem: hierarchical long-horizon manipulation failures are ambiguous: bad decision, partial observation, or failed low-level execution.
• Supervised learning lacks recovery-state data; RL struggles with sparse rewards and non-local credit assignment.
• Key idea: MAGMA-GEN converts the agent's own ambiguous failed rollouts into validated recovery supervision.
• Method: a privileged coach hypothesizes early decision-level errors and proposes localized corrections or recovery actions.
• Validation: candidates are kept only if re-execution from the same state under matched conditions improves progress.
• Setup: interactive long-horizon manipulation in simulation and on real robots, with evolving task constraints.
• Results: beats distillation and trajectory-repair baselines on task success and recovery; the abstract gives no numbers.

yyitbtz7rQ.text:
• Problem: whole-body policies tracking global end-effector poses fail under out-of-distribution inputs from noise or infeasible commands.
• Key idea: Competence Manifold Projection projects user intentions onto a learned manifold of safely mastered behaviors.
• Hierarchical Manifold Inclusion Framework reduces infinite-horizon safety constraints to an efficient single-step manifold inclusion check.
• Lower-bounded Safety Estimator separates unmastered intentions from the training distribution to define the competence manifold rigorously.
• Implicit Isomorphism Constraint aligns manifold geometry with safety probability, enabling O(1) seamless defense against arbitrary OOD intentions.
• Real-world legged manipulator tests: 100% survival in typical OOD scenarios where baselines fail catastrophically, under 10% tracking loss.
• New: emergent best-effort behavior progressively achieves OOD goals while staying within learned competence boundaries.

iXJWieKME1.text:
• Problem: asynchronous inference latency makes robot actions lag behind real-time environment changes.
• Lag is worst in dynamic scenes, where policies misread and react poorly to fast-moving objects.
• Key idea: predict object flow to synthesize future observations, letting the policy act on anticipated states.
• Flow-based contrastive learning aligns visual features of predicted observations with ground-truth future states.
• Anticipated visual context enables proactive planning that explicitly compensates for inference latency.
• Evaluated on complex dynamic manipulation tasks with actively moving objects; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Results: significantly better responsiveness and success rates; novelty is flow-to-future latency compensation for asynchronous policies.

0o1c1Xxn1m.text:
• Problem: automated open-vocabulary 3D box annotation fails when sparse LiDAR covers only part of an object.
• Consequence: existing VFM-based pipelines produce mislocalized boxes or leave partially visible objects unlabeled.
• Key idea: use image-generated 3D assets as amodal geometric priors for partially observed objects.
• Method: match input images to rendered asset views, aligning canonical geometry with world-space LiDAR points.
• Efficiency: propagates anchor alignments for dynamic objects and aggregates multi-frame evidence for static ones.
• Results: detectors trained on its labels gain 14.1 mAP on nuScenes over strong baselines.
• Waymo: +12.45 mAP at IoU 0.5 for vehicles, showing amodal priors fix partial-visibility annotation.

05nE8s5e7I.text:
• Problem: VLA deployment is bottlenecked by inference latency, especially iterative flow-matching action denoising.
• Prior fixes are one-sided: faster forward passes keep the decoding loop; async execution causes prediction-execution mismatch.
• Key insight: both failures stem from decoding each action chunk in isolation.
• FlashVLA: streaming decoder keeping a buffer of action chunks at staggered noise levels, decoded jointly.
• Chunk-wise causal attention: each forward pass emits one executable chunk; noisier chunks attend to cleaner ones.
• Evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0, and real robots; matches or beats π0.5 under one-step asynchronous delay.
• Up to 20x faster action decoding, 1.83x lower per-action latency, 30Hz control on consumer GPU.

X4i3kSa2kd.text:
• Problem: humanoid teleoperation latency sits near 200ms, matching human reaction time and blocking reactive tasks.
• Root cause identified: position-only PD control in low-level loops creates this persistent latency floor.
• Key idea: scaled velocity feedforward cuts tracking delay about 70ms, with a provably optimal feedforward ratio.
• Control operates directly on SE(3) poses of extremity links, avoiding joint-space retargeting in the loop.
• Closed-form Cartesian mapping with one calibration step adapts to operators with different body proportions.
• Validated in simulation and real world for RL locomotion; supports optical motion capture and VR tracking.
• Achieves 50ms end-to-end latency, enabling ping-pong ball balancing, juggling, and real-time returns.

lHDmYo4bzs.text:
• Dexterous imitation learning is bottlenecked by collecting contact-rich demonstrations that transfer faithfully to robot hands.
• Prior exoskeletons record only human-side data, using free-space-calibrated open-loop retargeting that degrades under contact.
• SEED-UMI's key idea: human and robot both wear the same exoskeleton during collection and rollout.
• Shared joint encoders turn retargeting into paired cross-embodiment supervision rather than open-loop mapping.
• Exoskeleton-mounted wrist cameras see identical mechanisms, enabling policies on raw images without segmentation or inpainting.
• Evaluated on five contact-rich dexterous manipulation tasks against exoskeleton-based teleoperation baselines.
• Achieves 3.0× higher data collection efficiency than teleoperation and 70.0% average rollout success.

wHAVgmIwj3.text:
• Problem: absolute pose regression is fast but hides perspective and scene geometry, limiting relocalization accuracy.
• Key idea: reformulate APR as a geometry-aware regression pipeline instead of direct image-to-pose mapping.
• Method: query image is first lifted into a scene pointmap, giving the regressor geometric rather than appearance-only input.
• Novel Gram-based pose proxy: network predicts a structured Gram matrix encoding perspective constraints and scene geometry jointly.
• Geometry-guided pointmap augmentation synthesizes novel-viewpoint training samples directly in pointmap space.
• Unlike NVS-enhanced APR, augmentation needs no costly rendering or extra neural scene representation.
• Indoor and outdoor experiments: substantially better accuracy with efficient feed-forward inference (abstract gives no specific numbers).

ndhpQ86iXs.text:
• Problem: always-on robots face endless streams where instructions arrive, lapse, and scenes change without reset.
• Gap: current action models assume fixed instructions, no mid-task intervention, and single-step reasoning.
• Key idea: robots must watch live streams for future cues, recall past actions, and act concurrently.
• Method: ARMS adds three lightweight context modules to a pretrained π0.5 backbone, updated asynchronously without blocking.
• Agent-causal self-history logs which arm did what and when, enabling simultaneous dual-arm action.
• ARMS Dataset: staged script auto-labels every module from real dual-arm teleoperation, needing no extra annotation.
• Results: 45% on combined task versus 28% for best VLA/streaming baselines; ablations confirm each component matters.

wMrKZ9eYBg.text:
• Problem: scaling generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by costly embodied interaction data collection.
• Egocentric human videos are abundant but lack action labels; existing annotation methods are noisy.
• Key idea: learn continuous latent actions from human video transitions as implicit policy supervision.
• LAPT-Scale-LAM uses continuous latents, not vector quantization, preserving fine-grained motion and interaction dynamics.
• Perceptual, semantic, and optical-flow alignment signals strengthen transition supervision beyond pixel reconstruction.
• VLA policy pipeline: latent-action pre-training, target-robot embodiment alignment, then task-specific post-training.
• Trained on 23.3K video hours; real-robot success rises 63.3% to 85.0% scaling 1K to 5K hours.

FuxTpvfYnh.text:
• Problem: navigation world models use multi-step diffusion and autoregressive generation, causing high latency in closed-loop deployment.
• Key idea: a lightweight one-step world model predicts all future frames non-autoregressively in a single pass.
• Architecture: 3D U-Net with efficient spatial-temporal attention for fast prediction of future observations under candidate actions.
• Pretraining and random trajectory sampling improve world-model performance when training data is limited.
• Unified planner supports image-, language-, and point-goal navigation via modality-specific scoring and anchor-based trajectory initialization.
• Evaluated in closed-loop experiments in both simulation and real-world environments against state-of-the-art baselines.
• Results: faster generation and strong navigation performance; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

QAHhXvXHtb.text:
• Handheld collectors like UMI use bulky pistol grips, hindering ergonomic, fine-grained dexterous manipulation data collection.
• YUBI: finger-aligned gripper with yielding, finger-driven actuation mapping human finger motion directly to jaws.
• Data system integrates VR-based 6 DoF gripper tracking for high-fidelity bimanual trajectory acquisition.
• Curated UMI-style dataset: 8434 hours, 1.20M episodes, 119 tasks, an unprecedented scale.
• YUBI beats UMI gripper in bimanual versatility, dexterity, and operational efficiency.
• Single policy transfers across UR, Franka, and ELEY robots by simply mounting the gripper.
• Gripper hardware, collection software, and dataset released openly as one integrated reproducible stack.

r2uaBmvWgH.text:
• Problem: scaling VLM planner test-time compute raises latency, tokens, FLOPs with uneven, diminishing success gains.
• Key idea: decide when and where to spend test-time compute instead of scaling it uniformly.
• Method: DIRECT routes each prompt using multimodal scene context to allocate compute adaptively.
• Studies three scaling axes: chain-of-thought depth, model size, and memory history.
• Setup: VLABench and RoboMME benchmarks, plus physical Franka arm in DROID setup.
• Results: router matches or beats stronger model's success at up to 65% lower average latency.
• New: different scaling axes give distinct capability gains; routing improves success-cost Pareto frontier.

O7LrmASsJS.text:
• Problem: humanoids struggle with fast, stable locomotion over diverse unstructured terrain using only reactive proprioception.
• Key idea: end-to-end perceptive parkour policy mapping depth images and proprioception directly to joint actions.
• No external localization or mapping needed, simplifying real-world deployment on hiking-style terrain.
• Foothold safety: Terrain Edge Detection plus Foot Volume Points reduce catastrophic slippage on terrain edges.
• Flat Patch Sampling generates feasible navigation targets, mitigating reward hacking and stabilizing training.
• Validated on Unitree G1 humanoid, robustly traversing complex terrains at speeds up to 2.5 m/s.
• Training and deployment code to be open-sourced, requiring minimal hardware modifications for real robots.

kBoTnjRw4s.text:
• Problem: humanoid whole-body control policies are trained per robot, isolating motion experience across embodiments.
• Key idea: decouple embodiment-independent motion representation from embodiment-dependent physical execution.
• Shared motion backbone learns human-motion semantics from multi-robot rollouts; lightweight robot-specific modules handle execution.
• Robot modules condition on each robot's proprioception, dynamics, and action space.
• Human motion, robot reference motion, and sparse VR input are unified into human-centered command tokens.
• A causal Transformer with historical context models temporal structure for shared motion understanding across robots.
• Tested on nine simulated humanoids and differently sized real robots; motion representations transfer with robust execution.

gn0kBXdK0G.text:
• Dexterous manipulation suffers from visual occlusion and complex contact dynamics that challenge existing vision-language-action models.
• Prior tactile approaches use homogeneous fusion, lacking adaptive tactile integration and explicit physical dynamics modeling.
• DeCAL unifies understanding, imagination and action generation in one physically-grounded dexterous VLA model.
• Mixture-of-Transformers architecture assigns specialized experts per capability while enabling efficient information flow among them.
• Adaptive Visuo-Tactile Fusion uses contact-aware gating to dynamically regulate when and how tactile information is used.
• Visuo-Tactile Latent Co-Imagination jointly predicts visual and tactile dynamics, instilling implicit physical world knowledge.
• Achieves state-of-the-art 71% average success and 83.4% progress success, generalizing well to unseen scenarios.

H7b56xK590.text:
• Problem: VLA policies rely on vision, missing local contact state needed for contact-rich manipulation.
• Key idea: learn how tactile readings should modulate actions in rare, risky near-failure states.
• Avoids large-scale tactile pretraining and extensive real-world contact exploration by training in a real-aligned simulator.
• Stage one: sim-real co-training on mixed trajectories warm-starts tactile-conditioned actions in a pretrained VLA.
• Stage two: simulation RL with verifiable task rewards, plus supervised real-data loss anchoring deployment distributions.
• Zero-shot real-robot transfer without privileged simulation state or online real-world RL.
• Four bimanual contact-rich tasks: average success 72.5% versus 50.0% baseline.

aITDcHSCTW.text:
• Problem: video-world-model policies see short observation windows, making long-horizon manipulation non-Markovian when past events matter.
• Key idea: MemoryVAM adds episodic memory so actions and imagined futures condition on full episode history.
• Recap-Cue module: Perceiver Recap Compressor turns per-frame CLIP embeddings into compact memory tokens.
• Lightweight Cue Gate estimates task completion from memory and language; tokens feed video backbone and action decoder.
• Training uses video prediction, delta-reconstruction auxiliary loss, and episode-boundary supervision, with no per-frame progress labels.
• Works with UNet and DiT backbones by changing only the cross-attention injection interface.
• Results: LIBERO-Mem success 5% to 42.5%; real robots 78.3% counting, 80.0% spatial recall, 75.0% sequential tracking.

KdaClHHEUt.text:
• Problem: current VLAs ignore touch or use static tactile encoders, limiting agile, human-level dexterous manipulation.
• Root causes: scarce diverse tactile data, no standardized evaluation, VLA architectural limits, static tactile encoders.
• Dataset: open-sourced 100-hour tactile-rich dataset, collected via data-efficient recipe prioritizing elementary motor primitives.
• Key idea: variable-rate Mix-of-Transformer architecture exploits high-frequency touch while preserving existing VLA capabilities.
• Encoder: novel temporal tactile VQ-VAE captures dynamic touch signals rather than static tactile cues.
• Setup: evaluated on 12 tasks requiring delicate force control and deformable object manipulation.
• Results: over 30% higher average success rate than the strongest baseline, enabling tactile-reactive dexterous policies.

qH1h7UkK0k.text:
• Problem: robot policies replay demonstrated trajectories but fail to imitate the demonstrator's underlying intent.
• Key idea: The Imitator Game benchmark, levels L0-L3, progressively widening the gap between human demo and robot scene.
• Pinpoints where trajectory replay stops working and genuine task understanding becomes necessary.
• IG-10K: 20,000+ paired human-robot episodes, 50+ tasks, 6 domains, real and simulated, all four levels.
• Imitator Arena: open platform for blind A/B human evaluation of robot imitation.
• Nine SOTA models hold steady L0-L2 but collapse at L3, where functional substitution is required.
• Video-conditioned beats caption-conditioned, yet all stay below 13% zero-shot; 10-demo fine-tuning gains grow with pretraining.

nYkpEYmvbg.text:
• Problem: VLM-based navigation generalizes well but lacks spatial awareness for reliable path planning in complex scenes.
• Key idea: estimate egocentric 3D occupancy from RGB video as an intermediate representation for navigation reasoning.
• Method: continuous latent occupancy compressed into one compact spatial token, avoiding dense volumetric inference overhead.
• S2A-Align: two-stage training, first on ground-truth occupancy, then on self-predicted occupancy to close train-inference gap.
• Setup: large-scale dataset with 4.2M occupancy annotations spanning diverse scenes and navigation tasks.
• Results: SR +4.6% R2R-CE, +5.3% RxR-CE; MetaUrban collision cost cut over 4x.
• Also 90.9%/91.0% zero-shot SR on InternVLA-N1 point-goal benchmark, plus robust real-world obstacle avoidance.

LHLnvoAEhr.text:
• Problem: low-cost mocap gloves and markerless trackers show user-, fit-, and session-dependent biases that degrade teleoperation.
• Key idea: few-shot, fine-tuning-free calibration from a small set of paired raw and target hand poses.
• Method: a HyperNet conditioned on paired examples predicts LoRA-style updates for a frozen MANO hand-estimation module.
• Per-user calibration becomes one feed-forward step, preserving MANO's geometric prior and the compact estimator's efficiency.
• Setup: trained on InterHand2.6M with synthetic drift augmentations, tested on augmented sequences, real glove data, and teleoperation.
• Results: beats uncalibrated input and standard baselines in calibration efficiency, hand-state accuracy, and teleoperation (abstract reports no numbers).
• What's new: hypernetwork-generated LoRA adapters replace per-operator or per-session optimization for dexterous teleoperation calibration.

G2Ja89f1e8.text:
• Problem: teaching quadruped robots new navigation skills in clutter is data-hungry, and social cues vary across users.
• Key idea: users physically lure the robot with a teaching rod, like dog training.
• Robot then follows high-level gesture and verbal commands; speech specifies action, gesture specifies spatial target.
• Method: reconstruct each demo scene in simulation, inject perturbations, and learn recovery to expand limited data.
• Policy is conditioned on both gesture and speech, which jointly outperform either modality alone.
• Results: 97.15% sim success across six cluttered scenarios, using under one hour of real demonstrations.
• Adapts to new users with under five minutes of interaction (+22.23% sim success), and runs on real hardware.

AY4totylcx.text:
• Problem: behavior cloning gives VLA models only positive supervision, never signaling which actions are instruction-inconsistent.
• Offline RL could add corrective signals but usually needs costly rewards or curated non-expert robot data.
• Key idea: successful expert demonstrations alone yield dense negative supervision via instruction relabeling.
• Method: pair expert actions with mismatched instructions to synthesize counterfactual instruction–observation–action tuples.
• An adversarial discriminator learns an instruction-grounded reward for offline RL, with no extra rollouts or annotations.
• Results: beats a strong SOTA baseline on LIBERO-PRO object-position and task perturbations; abstract reports no numbers.
• Also outperforms baselines on a real TX-G2 robot, showing denser supervision can complement collecting more data.

6DFI1qPxPg.text:
• Problem: humanoid parkour policies fail on highly challenging terrains unseen during pre-training.
• Key idea: real-to-sim-to-real framework using rapid test-time training (TTT) on each novel environment.
• Stage one: pre-train an end-to-end perceptive policy on diverse procedurally generated terrains.
• Stage two: quickly fine-tune on high-fidelity meshes reconstructed from real-world captures of the target terrain.
• New: efficient feed-forward RGB-D geometry reconstruction pipeline balancing speed and fidelity for test-time training.
• Results: capture, reconstruction and fine-tuning take under 10 minutes on most tested terrains.
• Humanoid traverses wedges, stakes, boxes, trapezoids and narrow beams with robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

8FGH4qAdNB.text:
• Problem: VLA policies fail on long-horizon manipulation when task-relevant cues become occluded or unobservable over time.
• Prior memory methods suffer information bottlenecks, dual-system latency, or redundant unselective visual buffers.
• Key idea: EventVLA, an end-to-end VLA with sparse visual evidence memory of task-critical events.
• Visual anchors retain initial and short-term context; Keyframe Evidence Memory (KEM) stores sparse task-critical keyframes.
• KEM predicts future keyframe probabilities from VLA latents, preserving transient evidence before it disappears.
• New benchmark: RoboTwin-MeM, a diagnostic suite for non-Markovian manipulation tasks with interactive visual evidence.
• Results: +40% average success over state-of-the-art memory-augmented VLAs on 17 simulated, 4 real bimanual tasks.

MQlY5j6pnd.text:
• Problem: visuomotor policies assume static targets, but real objects move, like parts on conveyors or swaying fruit.
• Key idea: split moving-object manipulation into predicting the object's future pose and reaching that predicted pose.
• Method: SIDO displaces objects to counterfactual future positions and morphs demonstrated action chunks accordingly.
• Morphed actions preserve hand-object relative pose, yielding a goal-conditioned policy trained only on static demonstrations.
• Deployment: an object pose predictor supplies the future position the goal-conditioned policy should reach.
• Setup: three simulated tasks (Mug, Square, Stack), five motion patterns, and two real tasks (Gantry, Peachtree).
• Results: higher moving-object success than baselines, with static-object performance preserved and no dynamic demonstrations needed.

tXUfbhgQg2.text:
• Problem: collision-free path planning needs free-space representations that are both scalable and provably safe for optimization.
• Explicit convex-set unions give hard constraints but scale poorly; implicit representations scale but lack guarantees.
• Key idea ILD: jointly learn an invertible mapping and a union of convex polytopes in latent space.
• Planning runs over latent convex sets; the invertible map decodes paths, preserving feasibility after refinement.
• Visibility-Guided Sampling (VGS) keeps the learned convex sets connected, enabling paths between regions.
• Across 2D, 6-DoF, and 14-DoF tasks: better coverage, connectivity, success; zero false positives after refinement.
• Shown real-time on a 14-DoF bimanual robot; test-time refinement handles scene changes on a 6-DoF arm.

wt25SMJmEq.text:
• Problem: dexterous grasping fails to generalize across robot hands with differing geometry, topology, and kinematics.
• Key idea: scaling both diversity and quantity of hand embodiments improves generalization to unseen morphologies.
• XDex: a unified cross-embodiment grasp synthesis framework trained across many heterogeneous robotic hands.
• Dataset: largest, most diverse multi-hand grasp dataset to date, with 1,000 robotic hands and 7k object scenes.
• Method: embodiment encoder jointly captures geometric and topological hand features.
• Representation disentangles three factors: object geometry, hand embodiment, and grasping pose.
• Results: beats prior methods in grasp quality, consistency, and diversity, and generalizes to unseen real-world hands.

WaIPZtSrpq.text:
• Problem: robot manipulation data is accurate but narrow; scalable ego-centric human data often lacks motion precision.
• Key idea: collect large-scale in-the-wild ego-centric manipulation data with millimeter-scale motion accuracy for robot learning.
• Method: Oracle Suite wearable kit with auto-labeling and validation pipeline for accurate motion capture.
• Dataset: over 1,000 hours of multimodal demonstrations spanning hundreds of skills and real-world scenarios.
• Annotations: calibrated views, 3D hand/wrist trajectories, depth, masks, task/sub-task language, vision-language supervision.
• Setup: preliminary real-robot co-training study plus main pre-training study in RoboCasa and on real robots.
• Results: ego data helps narrow robot data; verified annotations beat larger unverified ego data; fully open-sourced.

ntHuqgjrgs.text:
• Problem: video-based World Action Models are costly, model action-irrelevant details, and accumulate long-horizon imagination errors.
• Key question: do world action models really need video generation, or is image editing enough?
• Key idea: ImageWAM repurposes pretrained image editing models as a better-matched prior for robot action prediction.
• Editing models only a current-to-target frame change and grounds instructions to localized visual differences.
• Method: flow-matching action expert conditions on editing KV caches; target frame never decoded at inference.
• Results: beats standard VLAs and matches competitive WAMs in simulation and real world, without extra policy pretraining.
• Efficiency: 1/6 the FLOPs and 1/4 the latency of video-based WAMs; caches attend to task-relevant regions.

HmdwOezjlQ.text:
• VLAs often ignore language, following visual shortcuts from dataset biases: counterfactual failures on under-observed instructions.
• Failures include repeating well-learned behaviors and picking frequently seen objects regardless of the instruction's intent.
• LIBERO-CF: first counterfactual benchmark, assigning alternative instructions to visually plausible LIBERO layouts to test language following.
• Evaluation shows counterfactual failures are prevalent yet underexplored across state-of-the-art VLAs.
• CAG: dual-branch inference contrasting a standard VLA with a language-unconditioned vision-action module during action selection.
• Plug-and-play: no extra demonstrations, architecture changes, or pretrained model modifications; works across diverse VLAs.
• π0.5 gains 9.7% language following (15.5% with VA); real-world success rises 17.2%.

dkaxE3v6uu.text:
• Problem: long-horizon sidewalk navigation for delivery robots and wheelchairs, using only a single monocular RGB camera.
• Imitation learning alone suffers compounding errors, poor social compliance, and weak counterfactual reasoning in complex situations.
• FlowPilot: mapless navigation policy using anchored flow matching to model multimodal sidewalk navigation behaviors.
• Pre-trained on large-scale robot fleet data, then aligned via human-in-the-loop preference learning on intervention data.
• Preference tuning (FlowPilot-HP) needs only a small amount of human intervention data to improve social compliance.
• Simulation: FlowPilot reaches 42% success rate and 66% route completion; real-world tests span diverse sidewalks.
• FlowPilot-HP cuts IR by 40.0% and NIR by 52.1% versus the base model; code release planned.

eioQ9vJ6Oj.text:
• Problem: humanoid parkour over sparse footholds and narrow, discontinuous terrain remains an open challenge.
• Such terrain demands precise foothold selection, effective vision use, and consistent alternating steps during fast transitions.
• Key idea: end-to-end perceptive parkour policy using only onboard depth sensing, no external mapping.
• Saliency-guided temporal perception combines a foothold saliency prior with gated memory across frames.
• Gated memory retains task-relevant depth features, enabling reliable foot placement from partial observations.
• New alternation loss adds symmetry regularization, encouraging natural alternating gaits and robust traversal.
• Results: significantly higher success rate and foothold accuracy in simulation and real world; abstract gives no numbers.

aGLO1l8SNB.text:
• Problem: humanoid parkour policies complete tasks but suffer harsh landings, edge contacts, and unstable stance contacts.
• Insight: humans regulate foot-terrain interaction via tactile feedback; most humanoids lack rich sole tactile sensing.
• Key idea: TactileStep brings sole pressure sensing into humanoid locomotion control for softer touchdowns, stabler support.
• Method: tactile simulation aligned with real pressure insole, so policy learns hardware-available contact features.
• Training: tactile and motion cues identify foot-contact phases; phase-aware rewards encourage safe landing, stable stance.
• Setup: evaluated in simulation and on Unitree G1 humanoid across diverse terrains versus strong perceptive baseline.
• Results: up to 48.8% lower peak touchdown force, 30.1dB less impact noise, 23.8% more stance contact area.

xcDyj95l5P.text:
• Problem: humanoid motion tracking policies suffer training-deployment gaps from real-world disturbances and inaccurate simulation.
• Key idea: fine-tune policies online using a neural dynamics model trained on real-world robot data.
• Data collection: low-frequency reference perturbations with adaptive intensity balance safe deployment and exploration efficiency.
• Model: history-based proprioceptive dynamics model in Euclidean space via differentiable forward kinematics, no MoCap needed.
• Fine-tuning: policy updated directly through backpropagated model gradients, yielding high data efficiency.
• Setup: physical validation on Unitree G1, showing rapid real-world adaptation to various perturbations.
• Novelty: first online, MoCap-free fine-tuning framework for humanoid tracking policies; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.

7BCkvvmpuj.text:
• Problem: depth sensors and monocular models fail on transparent, reflective, specular surfaces, hurting robotic deployment.
• Prior fixes rely on preprocessing, auxiliary modules, or fine-tuning, adding redundancy and over-specializing models.
• Key insight: sensor-induced supervision bias, where models inherit sensor failures from biased real-depth labels.
• OptiGeo: bias-aware training using a clean-geometry teacher and residual-trimmed alignment to rehabilitate real supervision.
• Small transparency-targeted rendering set serves as a compact clean-geometry source, not a large fine-tuning set.
• With only 30M parameters, beats 300M monocular and billion-scale multi-view models on transparent-scene benchmarks.
• Remains competitive on zero-shot depth and boundary sharpness; real-world navigation cases confirm practical efficiency.

0ua1KHFIUD.text:
• Pre-trained robot policies need fine-tuning for new environments; RL helps but depends heavily on reward quality.
• Sparse rewards lack process feedback, hand-designed rewards are costly and biased, foundation-model rewards ignore control.
• HiRE is a training-free framework that edits foundation-model rewards by contrasting successful and failed trajectories in hindsight.
• It finds "trap states" scored high-reward that lead to failure, and undervalued states that lead to success.
• HiRE penalizes trap states and boosts rewards for critical successful states, making semantic rewards control-aware.
• Works with any foundation representation and any RL algorithm, at minimal extra computation.
• Reportedly beats other reward recipes in fine-tuning performance and efficiency; the abstract gives no numbers.

656PH9MVla.text:
• Offline pretraining alone leaves generalist robot policies brittle under real-world distribution shifts and long-tail failures.
• Learning While Deploying (LWD): fleet-scale offline-to-online RL for continual post-training of pretrained VLA policies.
• Closes the loop: deploy, pool fleet rollouts and human interventions, improve policy, then redeploy.
• Distributional Implicit Value Learning (DIVL) gives robust value estimates from heterogeneous, sparse-reward fleet data.
• Q-learning via Adjoint Matching (QAM) extracts improved policies from flow-based VLA action generators.
• Tested on 16 dual-arm robots, eight real tasks, including grocery restocking and 3-5 minute long-horizon tasks.
• Single generalist policy reaches 95% average success, with the largest gains on long-horizon tasks.

tQRHDxUApa.text:
• Problem: dynamic grasping must predict where and when contact will occur, not react to current poses.
• Key idea: contact-relevant rigid-body SE(3) state is a compact, task-sufficient abstraction for proactive grasping.
• Method: object-centric forecast-then-select framework predicts future SE(3) trajectories from short pose histories.
• A reachability-aware interception selector picks feasible contact states under kinematic and timing constraints.
• Setup: trained in randomized physics simulation on primitive shapes, transfers to real objects via recovered geometry.
• Results: success rises from 24.5% to 62.0% in simulation, 15.3% to 67.3% in real-world tasks.
• New: 15 ms forecaster, far faster than dense visual future prediction, enables real-time catching and interception.

7ymfgWpcWw.text:
• Problem: collecting large-scale vision-based tactile data is costly due to diverse contacts and sensor-instance inconsistencies.
• Existing simulation and free-form generation produce unrealistic tactile signals that transfer poorly to dynamic real-world tasks.
• Key idea: generate tactile images grounded in physical priors, namely contact force and contact pose.
• Method: two-stage controllable generator conditioned on a single reference tactile image, force, and pose.
• Synthesizes realistic samples across different sensors while capturing task-relevant variations for data augmentation.
• Evaluated on object insertion, imitation learning, and object weighting, including real-world robot experiments.
• Augmented datasets consistently improve downstream performance; the abstract reports no specific numbers.

mHCqiRUiHi.text:
• Problem: large Vision-Language-Action models are too memory-heavy for deployment on edge robotic devices.
• Key idea: design for efficiency at training time instead of relying only on post-hoc compression.
• BitVLA is a fully native 1-bit VLA where every parameter is ternary: {-1, 0, 1}.
• It builds on the public 1-bit LLM BitNet b1.58 2B4T and is trained as a manipulation policy.
• Quantize-then-Distill compresses the vision encoder to 1.58-bit, guided by a full-precision teacher for representation alignment.
• Evaluated on simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks, it matches the full-precision OpenVLA-OFT baseline.
• It reduces model memory 11.0x and end-to-end latency 4.4x, enabling manipulation on memory-constrained robots.

3hsq75Gmr9.text:
• Problem: accurately predicting deformable object dynamics for robotic manipulation remains challenging for physics-only and learning-only simulators.
• Key idea: PGRD, a hybrid simulator combining physics-based and learning-based approaches via learned residual corrections.
• Method: optimizable spring-mass simulator backbone plus neural network predicting residual corrections to physics predictions.
• Velocity-based formulation ensures stable simulation; sliding-window transformer captures temporal dependencies across time steps.
• Setup: evaluated on diverse real-world deformable objects against purely physics-based and purely learning-based baselines.
• Results: PGRD more accurate than both baseline types; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• Applications: MPC manipulation planning, including language-conditioned generated goal images, and Gaussian Splatting action-conditioned video prediction.

XA0dFQQlqP.text:
• Problem: vine robots navigate confined spaces well, but hysteresis, tether effects, and deformation make them hard to model.
• Consequence: these modeling difficulties limit conventional planning and control approaches for soft growing vine robots.
• Key idea: a data-driven, vision-based control framework for what the authors call the first autonomous vine robot system.
• Setup: 19 cameras distributed along the body give whole-body feedback on robot state and surroundings.
• Method: an end-to-end visuomotor policy learned from demonstrations efficiently aggregates distributed camera inputs for closed-loop control.
• Robustness: the policy tolerates inaccurate robot state estimates and imprecise actuation, common issues in soft growing robots.
• Results: robust branch steering, slope climbing, unsupported terrain traversal, precise reaching, and maneuvering through confined spaces and obstacles.

rQZHMVTYYy.text:
• Problem: MLP robot policies treat observations independently, missing interactions among physical variables.
• Insight: power, inertia, contact, slip, and compliance depend on products of observable signals.
• Key idea: PRISM makes polynomial interactions among observations explicit, learnable, and compact via factorized polynomial modules.
• RL: keeps the MLP backbone, adding a gradually activated element-wise polynomial function after it.
• Imitation: replaces linear proprioceptive conditioning in Diffusion Policy with an end-to-end polynomial layer.
• Results: beats standard and capacity-matched larger MLPs on humanoid locomotion and contact-rich manipulation; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: sensorless compliance emerges without force, tactile sensing, contact labels, or admittance control.

Q6xWLHyg6x.text:
• Problem: VLAs are closed, hardware-expensive, slow when reasoning, and not reliable enough for real deployment.
• Key idea: MolmoAct2, a fully open action reasoning model improving MolmoAct along five axes.
• Backbone: Molmo2-ER VLM, trained on 3.3M embodied-reasoning samples with a specialize-then-rehearse recipe.
• Data: 720-hour bimanual YAM dataset, the largest open bimanual set, plus filtered DROID and SO-100/101 subsets.
• Method: flow-matching action expert grafted onto a discrete VLM via per-layer KV-cache, plus open OpenFAST tokenizer.
• MolmoAct2-Think re-predicts depth tokens only for changed regions, keeping geometric grounding with far lower latency.
• Results: beats π0.5 across 7 benchmarks; Molmo2-ER beats GPT-5 and Gemini Robotics ER-1.5 on 13 benchmarks.

F5KmQJCC8X.text:
• Problem: raw-action diffusion policies mix scene understanding and trajectory generation, struggling with precise multi-arm coordination.
• Key idea: Latent Diffusion Policy (LDP) runs flow matching in a deliberately shaped latent action space.
• Method: an observation-conditioned CVAE encoder absorbs scene understanding, concentrating each observation's conditional action distribution.
• Benefit: the flow model learns a smoother velocity field, easing learning from limited demonstrations.
• Temporal modeling: per-token diffusion forcing in training, with staircase inference sampling to fix distribution mismatch.
• New metric: reconstruction FID (rFID) predicts downstream task success from latent space statistics alone.
• Results: substantially outperforms DP3 on coordination-heavy RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and transfers to real bimanual robots.

HBHR1GxaS0.text:
• Problem: why generative behavioural cloning diffusion planners can stitch sub-trajectories into new behaviours is poorly understood.
• Key finding: shift equivariance and local receptive fields are the two key enablers of compositional generalization.
• These properties explain data augmentation, data scaling, and inference choices in existing diffusion-planning BC methods.
• Method: Eq-Net, a new diffusion planner backbone built around equivariance and locality for compositionality by design.
• Setup: Eq-Net is trained and evaluated exactly like a vanilla diffusion planner, purely via generative BC.
• Results: much more diverse trajectories than existing diffusion backbones (abstract reports no specific numbers).
• New: trains only on short sequences yet generates consistent long-horizon plans, enabling reliable stitching without offline RL.

Xgth4qBOmb.text:
• Problem: safe RL for VLAs needs costly real-world exploration or hand-crafted safety functions, neither scales.
• Key idea: SafeDojo learns safe VLA actions through imagination inside an interactive video world model.
• World model predicts action-conditioned futures; ResNet success classifier estimates per-step task progress from imagined frames.
• Lightweight safety head predicts per-step contact probability from latent context and proposed action chunk.
• Decoupled reward and safety cost balanced via Lagrangian-based constrained GRPO under explicit safety constraints.
• Evaluated on SafeLIBERO and real Franka; beats inference-time safety, model-free and model-based RL baselines.
• Over 7% average safe-success gain across 21 tasks; first model-based safe RL framework for VLAs.

c5oiL7JqbQ.text:
• Problem: humanoid motion foundation policies assume reference motions already fit the robot's terrain, which often fails.
• Human demos specify intended behavior but not footholds, clearance, body height, or contact timing on robot terrain.
• Key idea: Perceptive BFM keeps raw human motion commands but uses local terrain perception to adapt contacts.
• TCRS synthesizes terrain-consistent references via foothold construction, swing optimization, root reconstruction, collision repair, multi-point IK.
• Blind teacher tracks adapted references; raw-reference student learns via target-frame action alignment distillation.
• Student: identity-gated Transformer with residual terrain pathways initialized to preserve tracking prior, correcting only when needed.
• Single real-robot policy handles locomotion, acrobatics, and teleoperation on stairs, slopes, sparse supports, and grass; abstract reports no numbers.

keuUzk1RSd.text:
• Problem: bimanual policies must adapt arm roles to scene, but demonstrations often have uneven arm-role distributions.
• Fixed left/right action spaces don't specify how behaviors should transform when roles swap between arms.
• Key idea: decompose paired arm features into swap-symmetric and swap-antisymmetric components.
• Symmetric part captures shared coordination; antisymmetric part captures role-specific distinctions that flip with role assignment.
• Components recombine as residual updates, a plug-in module with no new inputs, objectives, or role labels.
• Evaluated on multiple bimanual tasks with balanced and imbalanced role distributions, compared against corresponding base policies.
• Improves robustness across role configurations, with notable gains on underrepresented ones; abstract reports no specific numbers.

xOhVCWilYJ.text:
• Problem: hierarchical VLM robot systems use sparse points or boxes, inadequate for region-level grounding.
• Example: instructions like "place near the bowl" specify feasible regions, not single target points.
• Key idea: RoboMAP uses adaptive affordance heatmaps as language-conditioned interface between reasoning and downstream modules.
• Method: predicts dense score maps for continuous, object-free regions, guiding segmentation, grasping, and control.
• Training: synthesizes heatmap supervision from points, boxes, and robot trajectories, avoiding manual dense labels.
• Results: best reported accuracy on three of four spatial grounding benchmarks, with 0.04 s grounding-stage forward pass.
• Real robot: 82% success over 50 dual-arm trials across five tabletop tasks, plus cross-embodiment demos.

kpX1KOfNI5.text:
• Problem: egocentric occlusions and high-DOF whole-body coordination hinder humanoid grasping in unstructured environments.
• Key idea: HuG hierarchically couples active perception and whole-body action for autonomous object discovery and acquisition.
• Active perception controls viewpoint, maintaining a recursive spatial belief of the target to resolve visual ambiguity.
• Affordance-aware alignment uses learned reachability priors to choose kinematically feasible, dynamically stable whole-body postures.
• Whole-body grasping policy is distilled entirely from large-scale synthetic data, with no real-world training.
• Results: zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a real humanoid; abstract reports no quantitative numbers.
• New: coordinated perception-action markedly improves grasp reliability and generalization across diverse spatial configurations.

l0bwpzWRKy.text:
• Problem: embodied foundation models need massive data; human demonstrations scale well but suffer an embodiment gap.
• Key idea: model human intention via gaze as a mid-level representation for cross-embodiment transfer.
• Gaze encodes high-level task semantics and is tightly coupled with low-level actions, bridging humans and robots.
• Robots internalize human intentions from human data, needing no robot-side intention annotations.
• Method: Chain-of-Thought inference predicts intention first, then actions, exploiting intention-action synergy.
• Setup: long-horizon, fine-grained manipulation across diverse embodiments, in simulation and the real world.
• Results: consistently beats baselines and generalizes to unseen settings; the abstract gives no specific numbers.

5TiiTY1fK3.text:
• Problem: end-to-end robot policies typically use raw past observation sequences as memory, which fails in long multi-stage tasks.
• Robots need memory at multiple granularities, from long-term task progress to short-term occlusion handling.
• Key idea: combine multiple modalities so each captures a different level of abstraction.
• Method: MEM pairs video-based short-horizon memory, compressed by a video encoder, with text-based long-horizon memory.
• Setup: vision-language-action policies on real-world long-horizon tasks like kitchen cleanup and grilled cheese preparation.
• Results: MEM policies complete tasks spanning up to fifteen minutes.
• New: memory lets policies adapt manipulation strategies in-context, beyond conventional observation-history memory.

Nfz7oM0Vwz.text:
• Problem: mobile manipulation suffers from tightly coupled base-arm control and poorly allocated attention under shifting viewpoints.
• Key idea: infer latent motion intent to dynamically reweight multi-scale perceptual features for stage-adaptive attention.
• Geometric-semantic structured alignment strengthens cross-modal correspondence for more robust multimodal perception.
• Decoupled coordinated flow matching action decoder explicitly models joint base-arm action generation, easing optimization.
• Setup: evaluated on three ManiSkill-HAB scenarios without privileged information, plus real-world mobile manipulation tasks.
• Results: success rate gains of 28.2%, 26.1%, and 23.6% over state-of-the-art methods.
• New: intent-driven perception plus structured coordination; outperforms baselines in real-world mobile manipulation too.

oq5Byppu7Q.text:
• Problem: humanoid depth perception fails partially and intermittently in real deployment, breaking perceptive locomotion policies.
• Prior unified methods switch between perceptive and blind sub-policies, wasting information in partially corrupted depth.
• CAP: a single-stage policy whose world-model encoder learns to denoise, reconstructing clean depth from corrupted input.
• A co-active proprioceptive variational encoder supplies depth-free body-state information alongside the perceptive world-model latent.
• Training couples a depth-noise curriculum with world-model feature dropout, spanning the full perception-quality spectrum.
• Simulation: matches or beats perceptive baselines with good depth; degrades more smoothly than binary-switching baselines.
• Unitree G1 indoor-outdoor trials show robust walking under occlusion, real-sensor corruption, and outdoor depth artifacts.

P8H2WZH2Tw.text:
• Problem: egocentric human-video representations capture perception, not prediction of upcoming manipulation motion.
• Key idea: forecasting future 3D hand motion as pretraining teaches both manipulation and motion dynamics.
• Method: SFHand autoregressively predicts hand type, 2D box, 3D pose, trajectory from streaming video plus language.
• Architecture adds an ROI-enhanced memory layer for temporal context focused on salient hand regions.
• New dataset EgoHaFL: 247K clips, 3.95M frames pairing 3D hand poses with fine-grained language instructions.
• Results: state-of-the-art on simulation and real-world manipulation, up to 13.4% higher success rate.
• Also leads 3D hand forecasting with 35.8% lower ADE than baselines; code and data to be released.

JiMWz6U93i.text:
• Problem: large VLA foundation models have high inference latency, breaking real-time control loops in dynamic environments.
• Key idea: asynchronous framework decoupling slow semantic reasoning from fast reactive execution, inspired by hierarchical control.
• Large foundation model runs on remote workstation, providing high-level guidance to the robot.
• Lightweight onboard Edge Adapter continuously refines actions at high frequency using latest observations.
• End-to-end finetuning plus trajectory re-weighting prioritizing dynamic interactions bridges the asynchronous stream domain gap.
• Evaluated on real-world vision-based navigation with communication delays up to 6 seconds.
• Achieves 40% higher success rate than state-of-the-art baselines, combining VLA semantics with edge reactivity.

wBzyyPlFs6.text:
• Problem: urban sidewalk navigation is hard due to complex layouts, dynamic pedestrians, and long distances.
• Gap: no unified benchmark exists for quantitative, reproducible evaluation of visual navigation models on sidewalks.
• Key idea: SidewalkBench, a GPU-accelerated sidewalk navigation benchmark built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
• Scenes: diverse high-fidelity environments, both procedurally generated and real-world scanned.
• Pedestrians: reactive, event-based behaviors with flexible, efficient animation for realistic evaluation.
• Setup: 9 models tested on 330 unit-test, 800 pedestrian-reactive, and 105 long-horizon scenarios.
• Findings: pedestrian interaction and long-horizon robustness are key bottlenecks; synthetic sidewalk training data looks promising.

HuFkyUA5RR.text:
• Problem: robots recover from failures reactively but rarely learn abstract knowledge to avoid them later.
• Training a separate RL recovery policy per failure mode is highly inefficient and does not generalize.
• Key idea: ReSYNC discovers and refines relational predicates from failure-recovery experience to support abstract planning.
• Method: incremental dual learning; RL learns recovery skills, then concept learning invents predicates explaining them.
• Turns local recoveries seen in training into global failure avoidance on unseen long-horizon test problems.
• Results: across four simulated domains, ReSYNC outperforms strong baselines by over 50%.
• New: first to jointly learn skills and concepts from failures; sim-to-real non-prehensile manipulation demonstrated.

nBDd4rVq5Q.text:
• Problem: injecting low-dimensional robot signals into pretrained video diffusion latents for World Action Models
• Key idea: signal injection is a distribution-alignment problem, not a formatting detail
• Probe: frozen VDM denoiser reconstruction error shows frequency-domain packing fits the prior better
• Method: MetaWAM packs all signals into disjoint DCT bands of one unified meta-frame
• No added modules or architecture changes; slot-aware routing supports policy, world-model, and value prediction
• RoboCasa: 68.9% success, one meta-frame replaces per-signal frames, 39% lower inference latency
• Real world: 85.0% success on three Franka tasks

c7BvD59RpP.text:
• Problem: end-to-end visual RL for visuomotor control is compute- and memory-hungry, needing many rendered environments.
• Key idea: Stochastic Decoupled Policy Gradient (SDPG), a lightweight on-policy visual RL method.
• Method: estimates policy gradients via random perturbations of trajectory rollouts.
• Efficiency: needs orders of magnitude fewer batch-rendered environments, cutting compute and memory overhead substantially.
• Setup: trains diverse visuomotor policies end-to-end in a few hours on one RTX 4080 GPU.
• Results: on visual MuJoCo, consistently beats baselines in training time, memory usage, and rewards.
• New: realistic visual benchmarks for dexterous manipulation and challenging locomotion, plus sim-to-real transfer on physical hardware.

rYkaehgzzO.text:
• Problem: VLAs generalize poorly under distractors, appearance shifts, and similar tasks given coarse instructions.
• Key idea, S2: train the executor through a cleaner interface with more specific language and less visual input.
• Specify More: keep the original instruction as the goal; relabel trajectories with refined trajectory- and subtask-level language.
• See Less: an explicit visual evidence budget forces acting from task-sufficient evidence, without region or mask annotations.
• Off-the-shelf VLM planners can supply the detailed guidance through in-context learning.
• Setup: eight real-robot tasks on TX-G2 (AgiBot G2-compatible) and HSR, compared against pi0.5.
• Results: mean subtask success rises from 54.2% to 79.0%; goal-preserving guidance beats instruction replacement in ablations.

sdujBb3P4e.text:
• Problem: VLA driving models are far too slow for real-time control, with bottlenecks spread across four pipeline stages.
• Stages: visual encoding, language prefilling, reasoning-token decoding, and flow-matching action prediction each waste compute differently.
• Key idea: FlashDrive co-designs algorithms and systems to accelerate all four stages simultaneously, not one in isolation.
• Methods: streaming KV-cache reuse across overlapping frames, plus diffusion-based speculative decoding for low-entropy reasoning tokens.
• Adaptive denoising step caching spends compute at sharp endpoints; CUDA Graphs and kernel fusion add system-level gains.
• Results on Alpamayo1.5-10B with W4A8: latency drops from 716 ms to 159 ms, a 4.5x speedup.
• Accuracy cost is about 0.07 m minADE6@6.4s, ADE@6.4s improves, enabling real-time VLA driving on consumer GPUs.

uMgOYXmgn2.text:
• Problem: humanoid locomotion policies must stay stable under sensor dropouts while capturing long-term temporal dependencies.
• MLP policies lack temporal memory; Transformers are too computationally heavy for high-frequency real-time control.
• Key idea: RoboDreamer uses Mamba's selective state-space model for efficient long-horizon temporal modeling.
• Randomized temporal masking during training teaches recovery of missing observations and prediction of future states.
• Predictive capability enables action chunking, generating multi-step actions per inference pass for smoother control.
• Results: outperforms MLP and Transformer baselines in robustness and efficiency; abstract gives no specific numbers.
• New: maintains stable locomotion under masked observations while supporting real-time high-frequency humanoid deployment.

sIe2LX2HaF.text:
• Problem: robotic food cutting involves high-contact, topology-changing interactions with deformable, elasto-plastic objects.
• Real-world data is costly and wasteful, since each trial damages or destroys the food.
• Simulation helps, but physics and perception sim-to-real gaps compound quickly during cutting.
• Key idea: DexNinja, a differentiable real2sim2real engine turning few real demos into dense training data.
• Method: reconstruct objects from real trajectories, randomize mass, geometry, and friction under category-level constraints.
• New: custom differentiable simulator couples robot dynamics, tactile contact, and deformable cutting to augment episodes.
• Results: augmented data improves sim-to-real food slicing and generalizes to unseen strawberry shapes and sizes.

c4Z0Y8gvnI.text:
• Problem: sim-to-real transfer is widely believed to require real-world data or task-specific fine-tuning.
• Key idea: sufficiently large, diverse synthetic data alone enables zero-shot real-world manipulation of rigid objects.
• MolmoBot-Engine: open-source procedural data generation pipeline across robots, tasks, and MolmoSpaces environments.
• MolmoBot-Data: 1.7 million expert trajectories covering articulated object manipulation and pick-and-place tasks.
• Policies: Molmo2-based VLM with flow-matching head, a pi0 replica, and lightweight edge-ready MolmoBot-SPOC.
• Setup: Franka FR3 tabletop tasks and RB-Y1 mobile manipulator for doors, drawers, cabinets, pick-and-place.
• Results: zero-shot tabletop pick-and-place reaches 79.2% success across 4 settings versus 39.2% for pi0.5.

Zts11nHGLq.text:
• Problem: world model planners fail on long-horizon tasks due to compounding errors and exponential search.
• Prior hierarchies need task-specific policies (hierarchical RL) or low-dimensional states with known dynamics (classical MPC).
• Key idea: HWM does hierarchical MPC directly on visual world models trained only via next-latent prediction.
• Multi-timescale world models share one latent space; long-horizon predictions become subgoals via latent matching.
• An action encoder compresses primitive action chunks into latent macro-actions, keeping long-horizon search tractable.
• Real Franka pick-and-place from one goal image: 70% success vs 0% for single-level planning.
• Simulated push and maze tasks: better long-horizon performance with up to 3x less planning compute.

DzAZfcPUiP.text:
• Problem: tasks like food prep and surgery need force-sensitive contact and have subjective, continuous success criteria
• Example task: knife peeling, where quality is hard to quantify and rewards are hard to design
• Stage one: force-aware data collection and imitation learning yield a robust initial policy across object variations
• Stage two: preference-based finetuning with a learned reward combining task metrics and human feedback
• Data efficient: only 50 to 200 peeling trajectories needed per setup
• Results: 100% same-produce success on cucumbers, apples, potatoes; finetuning improves performance by up to 40%
• Zero-shot transfer to held-out produce: 50% zucchini, 90% pear, 80% daikon radish

PEWWDUL10X.text:
• Problem: VLA generalist policies struggle with complex spatial or semantic tasks, clutter, and precise manipulation.
• Key idea: OmniGuide steers VLA action sampling using guidance from diverse external models.
• Guidance sources include 3D foundation models, semantic-reasoning VLMs, and human pose models.
• Method: express guidance as differentiable energy functions with 3D attractors and repellers shaping sampled actions.
• Setup: simulation and real-world tests on π0.5 and GR00T N1.6, covering collision safety and human demonstrations.
• Results: significantly higher success and safety rates; abstract reports no specific numbers.
• What's new: one unified framework matching or beating prior methods built for single guidance types.

MWHlzlo4UD.text:
• Problem: real-world manipulation methods are hard to reproduce and compare across labs and platforms.
• Static datasets cannot evaluate interactive manipulation; simulation misses real-world complexity.
• Key idea: stochastic challenges, reproducible real-world tasks sampled randomly from a shared distribution.
• Random task samples mimic the rigour and surprise of hidden test sets.
• Robots in different labs are compared by success rates over samples from the same distribution.
• Implemented as a novel mobile manipulation benchmark, comparing two robots tested in two labs.
• New: a general benchmarking paradigm enabling system-level innovation and cross-platform comparability, like YCB objects.

qKU6lifnPU.text:
• Problem: VLA policies tie actions to fixed sensor sets, failing when sensors break or embodiments lack them.
• Key idea: treat action generation as context-conditioned sparse computation via conditional routing of experts.
• Sensor availability gates modality-specialized experts, enabling graceful degradation under missing sensors without retraining.
• Task intent routes action-side representations to task-relevant experts, improving multi-task and long-horizon specialization.
• Setup: depth as representative auxiliary sensor; evaluated on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, real dual-arm manipulation.
• Results: beats dense-action-generator ablation and strong pretrained VLA baseline, including zero-shot on unseen scenarios.
• New: exploits depth when available yet stays robust without it; abstract reports no specific numbers.

w3g5PWur7i.text:
• Problem: long-horizon mobile manipulation suffers compounding errors and capacity interference between locomotion and arm control.
• Gap: VLAs handle short tasks; hierarchical agents have rigid sub-task mapping, inflexible replanning, no continuous learning.
• Key idea: MobiAgent, a dual-loop framework linking robust deployment execution with continuous, annotation-free policy self-improvement.
• Inner loop: VLM receding-horizon planning and visual reflection compose atomic skills for dynamic error recovery.
• Skills run on specialized flow-matching experts sharing one VLM backbone, boosting reuse and reducing capacity interference.
• Outer loop: autonomously segments, verifies, and clusters rollouts to discover skills and fine-tune the library.
• Results: +22.5% success over SOTA monolithic VLAs on BEHAVIOR-1K, plus robust real-world error recovery.

hJv9yhbgxR.text:
• Problem: pretrained VLAs struggle to keep long-horizon visual history with high-frequency updates while staying efficient.
• Prior work uses external memory management, limiting either memory horizon or policy reactiveness.
• Key idea: Native Memory Compression reuses the VLA's own vision encoder to compress frames.
• Each historical frame per camera view becomes one token appended to the VLA input sequence.
• Training: memory tokenizer supervised by frozen VLA, then VLA unfrozen for task-specific fine-tuning.
• Results: simulation success rises from 32.4% to 84.0%, up to 98.7% on real robots.
• Low latency and GPU memory, and competitive with prior methods using only 20% of training data.

Q4ehHMIPmb.text:
• Problem: long-horizon embodied agents struggle with partial observability, fragmented spatial reasoning, and poorly integrated memories.
• Key idea: brain-inspired RoboMemory unifies Temporal, Spatial, Semantic, and Episodic memory for planning and interactive learning.
• Method: a comprehensive embodied memory system plus a dynamic spatial knowledge graph for scalable, consistent updates.
• Setup: evaluated on EmbodiedBench with Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Ins as backbone, plus real-world robot trials.
• Result: raises Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Ins average success rate by 26.5 percentage points on EmbodiedBench.
• Open-source backbone with RoboMemory performs comparably to strong closed-source VLM agents.
• Real-world trials suggest cumulative learning by reusing accumulated experience across repeated task attempts.

Tjg1ZvCdXU.text:
• Behavior-cloned policies learn undesired modes from demonstrations, like handing over a knife blade-first.
• Data curation needs original demos for retraining; inference-time steering adds substantial runtime overhead.
• MoRE (Mode Redirection) "unclones" unwanted modes via a short fine-tuning step on policy weights.
• A temporary mode classifier's redirection signal is distilled into weights; a retain loss preserves desired competence.
• Evaluated on eight simulated and real-world tasks with Diffusion Policy and π0.5 VLA backbones.
• Improves average deployment success rate by 43 points over the original mixed-mode policy.
• Beats adaptation and steering baselines, nears filtered-data retraining, with zero inference-time overhead.

WBGnJHRIso.text:
• Problem: humanoid soccer shooting needs whole-body stability, high-impulse ball contact, and accurate targeting simultaneously.
• Motion tracking RL is stable but rigid; task-reward RL struggles to discover valid kicks from scratch.
• Key idea: RoboNaldo uses a single human-kick reference as scaffold, gradually shifting optimization toward shooting performance.
• Three-stage curriculum: stable kicking prior, then stationary free-kicks at random positions, then moving-ball shooting.
• Locomotion-command and kick-trigger interface, driven by heuristic planner in training, swappable for other high-level controllers.
• Simulation: 50% lower free-kick shot error and 2.96x shot velocity versus prior baselines.
• Unitree G1 with onboard perception: 0.73m/0.86m error from 3m; ball speed 13.10m/s, 59-71% of professional shots.

334wtBsPIG.text:
• Problem: contact-rich manipulation policies must decide what visual and tactile information to encode, and when.
• Key idea: touch deserves representation budget only in phases where contact makes it action-relevant.
• Method: PA-VMMIB suppresses tactile latents before contact and reallocates rate to touch during precise contact.
• Theory: action-conditioned multimodal bottleneck yields water-filling allocation, equalizing marginal rate-distortion slopes across active modalities.
• Prediction: tactile activation threshold scales as 1/λmax of tactile Fisher; smooth sensors give finite-width crossover.
• Setup: Linear-Gaussian checks, MuJoCo+TACTO simulation tasks, and Franka+DIGIT physical peg-in-hole experiments.
• Results: +26 points over vision-only at 4 mm clearance, converging to vision-only at 8 mm.

eRpTR7EEC1.text:
• Problem: robots must move cameras to inspect, reveal occlusions, or match user intent before acting.
• Gap: language-conditioned camera motion is underexplored as a first-class action, unlike navigation or manipulation.
• Task: given RGB observation and free-form intent, predict relative SE(3) target camera pose for next view.
• Data: mines multi-intention supervision from egocentric video, pairing intents and observation-gain descriptions with target poses.
• Method: LIME combines auto-regressive observation-gain text output with a continuous flow-matching pose head.
• This jointly predicts what the next view should reveal and represents multi-hypothesis target views.
• Results: abstract reports no numbers; LIME learns active camera control from passive human video across robotic tasks.

bsjuF5klA3.text:
• Problem: long-horizon precise manipulation data mixes useful actions with detours, hesitations, failures, and imperfect recoveries.
• Key challenge: identify which action chunks advance the task instead of uniformly cloning or discarding trajectories.
• Idea: GR-BC builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations, rollouts, failures, and human interventions.
• Method: reverse graph search gives minimal steps-to-success; chunks are weighted by how much they reduce this potential.
• This reuses recoverable failure segments, treats interventions as recoveries, and down-weights regressive chunks within successes.
• Iterative offline post-training appends new rollouts to the graph; no reward model, critic, or progress predictor needed.
• Across four precise tasks and three VLA backbones, GR-BC beats single-round SFT, reaching 91% success.

3jf63cW3cJ.text:
• Problem: SFT-adapted VLA models learn where success lies, but never where reliability breaks down.
• Key idea: reframe robust adaptation as Failure-Boundary Learning: discovering, localizing, and shaping success-failure boundaries.
• Method DLS builds a real-grounded prior from few real demos plus simulated co-training.
• Discovers failure boundaries at scale through on-policy rollouts in digital twin simulations.
• Semantic progress localization uses privileged simulator states to pinpoint where failure occurs, beyond binary labels.
• Directional shaping reinforces successful flow denoising directions and suppresses failing ones, without likelihoods or critics.
• Real-robot results: beats SFT and online RL, especially under randomized initial states and unseen visuals.

Qu7v3GmYDU.text:
• Problem: VLA models are expensive at inference; redundant visual tokens inflate compute during robot control.
• Existing pruning criteria come from generic VLMs, using vision-text attention or static semantics.
• These fail to track stage-wise manipulation, where relevant objects and interaction regions shift over time.
• Key idea: predicted actions reflect short-horizon task progress, so score tokens by influence on actions.
• Method: training-free ACE back-attributes actions to visual tokens via gradient-weighted relevance for stage-aware pruning.
• Results: up to 39.0% fewer FLOPs; π-series gains 1.7–2.0% success, 1.33× LIBERO, 1.36× real-world speedup.
