• OpenVLA-OFT stays competitive with 1.57× simulation and 1.55× real-world speedups; code is publicly available.

YnMZwXZ68A.text:
• Problem: driving policies scoring high in open-loop evaluation often fail when deployed in closed-loop simulation.
• Diagnosis: the OL-CL gap stems from two causes, observational domain shift and objective mismatch.
• Observational domain shift is largely recoverable with adaptation; objective mismatch is the primary, structural gap.
• Many OL policies learn biased Q-value estimators that ignore reactive agents and temporal compounding errors.
• Method: a Test-Time Adaptation framework that calibrates observation shift, reduces state-action bias, and enforces temporal consistency.
• Results: TTA mitigates planning biases and scales better than baselines; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
• New: exposes blind spots in standard OL evaluation protocols that miss closed-loop deployment realities.

dFblf2sS7M.text:
• Problem: VLAs need large video-action datasets, but real robot teleoperation data is scarce and costly.
• Existing methods recover pseudo-actions from generated robot videos, treating synthesized pixels like real demonstrations.
• Key idea: generated videos preserve task geometry (where) but lose control signals (how), the Asymmetric Preservation Principle.
• Method: GRA supervises only the VLA vision backbone with future 2D end-effector waypoints from generated videos.
• Waypoints come from human videos via pose estimation, retargeting, simulation, and calibrated projection, feeding an auxiliary 2D head.
• Action head trains on real demonstrations only; waypoint loss anchors spatial representations during fine-tuning.
• Real-robot results: beats pseudo-action baselines at matched data budgets (the abstract reports no specific numbers).

PLNJ3a6Yht.text:
• Problem: humanoid ladder climbing is hard due to sparse footholds, whole-body coordination, and sensitivity to perception errors.
• LadderMan: unified system for robust humanoid climbing across diverse ladders plus manipulation while on the ladder.
• Stage one: hybrid motion tracking learns multiple climbing experts from a single reference motion.
• Stage two: experts distilled into one depth-based visuomotor policy via hybrid imitation and reinforcement learning.
• Vision foundation models bridge the sim-to-real depth gap, enabling zero-shot transfer to real humanoid hardware.
• Separate dual-agent manipulation policy allows stable teleoperated manipulation during climbing.
• Results: robust climbing across many ladder geometries; abstract reports no quantitative success rates.

NHE9q2cz1n.text:
• Problem: robot foundation models use single-step or short-history visuomotor context, limiting long-horizon and adaptive behavior.
• Key idea: integrate Test-Time Training into VLA policies, using fast weights updated by gradient descent as memory.
• Fast weights compress history into weight space, scaling context to 8K timesteps without growing inference latency.
• Training recipe: sequence action forcing plus truncated backpropagation through time to scale training context length.
• Unlocks one-shot imitation from human video, on-the-fly improvement, perturbation robustness, and stronger multi-stage task performance.
• Real-robot results: 87% gain over single-step baseline; only method completing five-minute, ten-stage assembly task.
• New scaling axis: 8K-context pretraining beats 1K-context pretraining by 62%, first steady closed-loop gains from context.

n31eEof0k3.text:
• Problem: VLA policies struggle with long-horizon manipulation due to multi-step, progress-dependent tasks and compounding execution errors.
• Key idea: LoHo-Manip decouples a task-manager VLM from a short-horizon VLA executor for long-horizon instruction following.
• Manager runs receding-horizon, predicting remaining plan: subtask sequence with explicit done/remaining split as language memory.
• Manager also outputs a visual trace, a 2D keypoint trajectory showing where to go next.
• Executor VLA conditions on the rendered trace, turning long-horizon decisions into repeated local "follow the trace" control.
• What's new: implicit closed loop; failed steps persist, enabling replanning without hand-crafted recovery or visual-history buffers.
• Results: gains in long-horizon success, robustness, and OOD generalization in simulation and real Franka; abstract reports no numbers.

oias4zZRUn.text:
• Problem: quadrupeds know few gaits; animal-based motion data needs cooperative animals and fragile cross-species retargeting.
• Key idea: Uni-Mo removes animals entirely, reframing motion data scarcity as a generation problem.
• Pipeline: LLM proposes motion prompts, video diffusion synthesizes robot behaviors, videos are lifted into 3D trajectories.
• Identity Consistency Loss enforces cross-frame appearance coherence, making drifting generated videos reliably extractable.
• Lifted trajectories train tracking policies deployed on a real Unitree Go2 quadruped.
• Releases Quad-Imaginarium: 7488 language-annotated motions, 18.5 hours, spanning acrobatic and performative behaviors.
• Results: 96.7% real-world success on 392 sampled motions; 97.6% simulation success across full dataset.

yPkDKkOD11.text:
• Problem: robot embodiment strongly affects manipulation performance, yet design is rarely optimized alongside motion.
• Task: generate full robot designs that track human-demonstrated end-effector trajectories while maximizing user-defined rewards.
• Key idea: Transformer Transformer, a diffusion transformer trained on RoboTokens, unifying embodiments, states, and actions.
• One architecture spans wheeled bimanual, quadruped, and humanoid designs, serving as generator and cross-embodiment controller.
• Learned as a reward-agnostic dynamics model; Dynamics Self-Guidance converts predictions into values steering design diffusion.
• Zero-shot optimization of unseen rewards and trajectories, beating evolutionary baseline in performance and runtime.
• Fabricated optimized ALOHA design reduced tracking error by over 70% versus the original hardware.

CtcahYuPBL.text:
• Problem: vision-only VLA policies struggle with contact-rich tasks like insertion, where touch is critical.
• Real-world tactile data is costly to collect, and no unified evaluation platform for visuo-tactile policies exists.
• Key idea: UniVTAC, a simulation platform for scalable, controllable synthesis of informative visuo-tactile contact data.
• Supports three commonly used visuo-tactile sensors within a single unified simulation framework.
• UniVTAC Encoder: trained on large-scale synthetic data with designed supervision for tactile-centric representations.
• UniVTAC Benchmark: eight representative visuo-tactile manipulation tasks for systematically evaluating tactile-driven policies.
• Results: encoder raises average success by 17.1% on the benchmark and 25% in real-robot experiments.

k9EjTLL8bA.text:
• Problem: in long-horizon tasks, visually plausible VLA actions fail when earlier subgoals remain incomplete.
• Key idea: "historical support", a criterion asking whether task history justifies a candidate action now.
• Method: frozen base VLA plus lightweight post-policy assessor that scores and reranks candidate action chunks.
• Assessor outputs sparse per-candidate evidence masks, giving interpretable traces of supporting history.
• Training uses wrong-history and missing-evidence counterfactuals, sparsity and faithfulness losses, no dense evidence labels.
• Results with frozen 0.5B base: 98.1% LIBERO, 83.3% SimplerEnv-WidowX, 84.0% real-world long-horizon success.
• Ablations show support reranking beats generic sampling and policy-confidence reranking, especially on long-horizon tasks.

58liP3p4hu.text:
• Problem: tendon-driven, muscle-actuated robots suffer nonlinearities, friction, and hysteresis, blocking sim-to-real policy transfer.
• Key idea: learn a neural actuation model, use standard rigid body simulation for arm and environment.
• Method: Generalized Actuator Network (GenAN) learns from joint position trajectories, no torque sensors required.
• This makes actuation model identification applicable across a wide range of robots.
• Setup: PAMY2, a four-DoF tendon-driven arm powered by pneumatic artificial muscles.
• Results: goal-reaching, ball-in-a-cup, and table tennis policies trained entirely in simulation, deployed successfully on hardware.
• New: claimed first successful sim-to-real transfer for a four-DoF muscle-actuated robot arm.

jnEHLRyWTZ.text:
• Problem: dynamic, contact-timed, dexterous tasks are hard or impossible for human teleoperators to demonstrate.
• Behavior cloning stalls without expert data in this infeasible-demonstration regime.
• Key idea: GLIDE infers task-specific failure points and turns them into executable guardrails.
• From a task description, guardrails use robot state to filter teleop and policy commands.
• Guardrails constrain failure-prone actions and refine iteratively using closed-loop dataset feedback.
• Data-collection efficiency rises from 0-10% to 70-90% on tomato, marker, and wine tasks.
• Guarded deployment lifts tomato plate transfer success from 0% to 60-70% using mixed-quality demos.

USXQ0bDfAz.text:
• Problem: humanoid interaction skills are bottlenecked by scarce realistic data and task-specific reward engineering.
• Key idea: HumanX compiles monocular human videos into generalizable humanoid interaction skills without per-task design.
• XGen: anchor-centric pipeline generating physically plausible robot interaction data from video, then augmenting it for diversity.
• XMimic: interaction-prioritized learning framework acquiring generalizable skills from seconds of demonstration.
• Setup: basketball, football, badminton, cargo pickup, and reactive fighting; 10 skills, zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1.
• Results: fadeaway jumpshots without external perception; 10+ consecutive human-robot passing cycles from one video.
• Over 8x higher generalization success than prior methods, offering a scalable, task-agnostic path to interactive skills.

2vx7I6aRPS.text:
• Problem: robot foundation models need real-world post-training, but heterogeneous deployment data resists stable policy updates.
• Data sources: demonstrations, human corrections, and autonomous rollouts, all mixed during deployment.
• Key idea: Trust-Region Flow Matching Optimization (TRFO), one RL objective unifying all experience types.
• TRFO uses signed advantages to attract high-value transitions and repel low-value ones within a trust region.
• Method loop: collect on-robot data, estimate values via distributional TD, update with TRFO, redeploy.
• Setup: precise, contact-rich bimanual manipulation tasks, with policy improved across successive real-world iterations.
• Results: consistent monotonic gains in success rate and throughput on all tasks; abstract reports no exact numbers.

r27erS063s.text:
• Problem: long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation needs robust meta-skills plus seamless closed-loop chaining with autonomous recovery.
• Explicit interaction representations are precise but hard to plan; implicit skill embeddings lack interpretability for composition.
• Key idea: contact flow, combining key body trajectories with time-series binary contact signals as a shared interface.
• Low-level CF-Track policy learns a unified library of loco-manipulation skills by tracking contact flow.
• High-level CF-Gen heuristically synthesizes future contact-flow sequences, enabling composition and autonomous failure recovery.
• Significantly outperforms prior baselines on meta-skills, multi-skill chaining, and long-horizon tasks; abstract reports no numbers.
• New: VLM integration for semantic task decomposition, e.g., arranging scattered boxes into a heart shape.

dKRgZYcdRV.text:
• Problem: Action-to-Action flow matching policies degrade under spatial out-of-distribution shifts and visual distractors.
• Cause: strong reliance on historical motion priors plus entangled global visual representations.
• Key idea: SlotFlow, an object-centric flow matching policy for robust visuomotor manipulation.
• Method: decouples observations into semantic "what" and geometric "where" representations for policy conditioning.
• Semantic features suppress background correlations; geometric features ground actions in shifted object configurations.
• Setup and results: tested in simulation and real-world manipulation; abstract reports robustness gains but no numbers.
• What's new: object-centric conditioning adds robustness while keeping A2A flow matching's low-step inference efficiency.

jeNVGuJQrb.text:
• Problem: foundation-model visual features emphasize global semantics, missing temporally sensitive cues needed for robot control.
• Training robot encoders from scratch is costly: robot data is scarce and pretraining is computationally heavy.
• Key idea: SPARK, a simple post-training method adapting pretrained foundation models to robot control.
• Dynamics-aware abstraction: compact features preserving temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure.
• Knowledge preservation: patch-level alignment with the original foundation model retains useful pretrained semantics.
• Results: consistently higher success rates and generalization than vanilla foundation models across multiple robotics benchmarks; abstract gives no numbers.
• Gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation, offering a cheap alternative to robot-specific pretraining.

drlpFld34L.text:
• Problem: dexterous manipulation is bottlenecked by the high cost of collecting large-scale robot demonstrations.
• Opportunity: egocentric human videos offer scalable, diverse manipulation behaviors but face visual and action gaps.
• Key idea: EgoEngine converts egocentric human RGB videos into high-fidelity, robot-usable dexterous demonstration data.
• Visual bridge: replaces the human with a robot in video, preserving scene context and temporal alignment.
• Action bridge: generates task-aligned, executable robot action trajectories that satisfy feasibility constraints.
• Setup: validated in simulation and on real robots; the abstract reports no quantitative success rates.
• New: claims first zero-shot visuomotor dexterous policy learned from human videos, without real-robot demonstrations.
